other then that enjoy the chapter :) Please dont forget to Rate, Vote ,Fav, Follow it helps me alot :) ---------------
In 2136, after Hope had landed, Terraforming was almost immediate and things were going successfully. They used a process known as ‘Bubble’, which would require several people in astronaut-like suits to venture around with a mechanical tank known as ‘Growth’. Growth was designed to create a large Dome of energy that would mimic earth's atmosphere, act as an insulator, and deflect all harmful rays and radiation.
Growth also had a second use. It could be filled with a chemical that was infused with synthetic particles and Microscopic nanobots after the Dome was created and it be used to infuse the special particles and nanobots into the soil of mars.
The nanobots, which contained a chemical known as I-20, would use the particles as an energy source for a chemical reaction with I-20 that would allow a near-instant or accelerated growth of fertile land that could be used for farming.
After continually repeating the process for five years, mars started to look as if it had been cured of its desolate past. Civilisation began to spring up near Hope, which had landed prior to the Terraforming. By 2148, Earth received the first of its shipment of supplies. However, Earth itself had not remained idle. The people were trying to help in any way possible. The supplies were indeed needed, though.
In 2159, technology had advanced even further, allowing light speed travel, and by 2464, the human race had gone galactic. Hundreds if not thousands of planets were being colonized. Brink had formed into the main technology dealer of the newly formed EUF (Earth United Forces) which lasted for centuries to come.
Of course, not everything transpired perfectly. With newly inhabited worlds under the EUF’s control, people on distant planets demanded autonomy and wars were fought on a planetary scale. With war came crime and looters and with that came criminal organisations.
Even as newly terraformed planets were made, new species of creatures were found in some environments. They were not dubbed as aliens, as they were not as sentient as humans, but life in itself other then humanity was the latest thing for at least a decade.
Unfortunately, with the spread of humanity, narcotics and illegal contraband sprung forth like never before and it became nearly impossible to deal with it in trade routes. Had it not been for the heavy EUF presence and their warships designed by Brink, there would have been chaos. Brink was profiting quite well.
In fact, after a few supply runs to earth, they had even paid off the Australian government, which was no more. Earth had formed into one single hierarchy who also lead the EUF with an appointed Overseer and under him were the judges. Judges could overthrow the overseer if they unanimously voted to do so.
Under these judges were the generals and commanders of the EUF's forces. These individuals were not plentiful. Only a handful was ever around at any given time in the EUF's centuries long history. In the year 2999, a certain individual had just graduated from one of the EUF's academies (which numbered in the thousands now, due to humanity being so widespread).
Avrin Sygin became an exceptional soldier. In his first battle on Iosa-II, he infiltrated a crime den and, from the inside, ended every single one of those 234 lives using their own life support against them as their hideout was on a non-terraformable volcanic planet.
He had made it so the life support system, instead of removing the carbon dioxide and putting it outside, had would bring the extremely toxic gas inside. Without so much as a drop of blood being shed, he had gained the rank of Lieutenant.
Avrin went on to do extreme feats, from obliterating crime organisations to saving platoons of captured EUF soldiers. In 3007 he was promoted to a commander of the EUF. Unfortunately for him, it was also the year the Ziox virus mysteriously appeared from one of Brink's under-the-radar facilities that was experimenting with recoding human DNA in search of giving people superhuman abilities without the need for cybernetic implants. They wanted to be gods and the EUF didn’t even know.
Unauthorized duplication: this narrative has been taken without consent. Report sightings.
That being said, the Ziox virus went on to take the lives of billions. If you thought the black plague was bad, it was a sneeze compared to the Ziox virus. This was due to humanity being so widespread and constantly on the move. One person would infect someone on one planet while setting off a chain reaction. Before the symptoms kicked, people would move to other planets for trading or visiting and the process would be repeated.
The EUF had to cordon off sectors and enforce them heavily. Refugees were either destroyed in their small ships if they did not listen or contained on single planets used as sick bays.
In 3010, the worst ever case of Ziox virus occurred on Votera Prime with 99.9% of the population infected and cordoned off. Of course, people began protests and things became violent. The one looking after the cordoned sector was none other than Avrin.
He knew the kill rate of the Ziox virus was perfect, with some cases being cured with no treatment. You either had the luck to win a lottery a year straight or you didn’t – that was the chance of being randomly cured.
Avrin figured that these people were as good as dead and what made matters worse, due to the entire population being infected, he could not risk soldiers down there to police it all. It was a bad situation, as the people of Votera Prime were starting to flee to the planet's ships. The planet itself was earth-like to begin with, very popular, rich in resources, and had quite a reputation.
Avrin, instead of taking the chance of seeing these people flee, decided to end it and save them the misery. He used a super weapon equipped only to flag ships that EUF commanders possessed. Its nickname was ‘the Meteor’. It was an Ionic Burst Covered in layers of assorted unstable particles with a dark matter core.
Avrin used it on Votera Prime and the giant mass of energy plunged into the capital of the planet – Marleth, a sort of resort city near the ocean. The burst exploded sending a shockwave of flame and lightning across the surface of Votera and destroying everything it engulfed in a near instant. No one was safe unless they were deep, deep underground as the radiation sunk beneath the planet’s surface as well.
Arvin’s own crew turned against him an hour after he had destroyed everything on the planet and set off a chain reaction. Unfortunately for him, the moment he pulled the trigger the cure had been discovered.
Avrin had gone from zero to hero and now he was less than zero. Killer of millions, overthrown by his crew, locked away, sentenced to death. Unluckily for him, he had no son or family to pass on his name. He was the last of his bloodline. He was thankful though that he would leave no one behind to be persecuted for his own actions.
------------ (The Present: In the unknown realm) -----------
Avrin opened his eyes slowly after his somewhat rest. It had felt like a dream within a dream as he remembered taking those lives and how his own crew turned on him for his actions.
"It seems it will haunt me for a while – if not for the rest of my life. I’ll have to find a way to stop it. I’d rather not think about those shitty memories again." He frowned to himself and stretched, even though he felt weird doing so. It was all in his mind, after all. But he felt extremely refreshed, as if he had been healed and was now even stronger than before.
“I need to find a way out of here.” He looked around, trying to remember that vine-like magic that had engulfed him. Sitting in the open void, his legs crossed, he let his body float randomly. He didn’t know what was up or down –there was no gravity.
Avrin blinked as a crack appeared in the open void that leaked a white light. He was not so dumb as to not approach. It seemed to be healing, but every now and then, it would crack again and turn a bit larger.
"Bingo...."

chapters.title: Chapter 19 Infiltration.
chapters.content:
This message goes out to the guests ^^ im glad that my FF can attract unregistered users i know this is to much to ask. but if you register on RR you will find your words can not just reach me but other author's. we could use your support. id be glad if some of you could register and rate/vote and more importantly Review as im interested in your thoughts :). Enjoy ch 19 
---------
During Avrin's mindful rest, Neriel had spent the night plotting what he should do and decided that a grand master level shapeshifting spell would work wonders. Myra was powerful with Moonwing, but only when she used it was she more powerful than an angel. This gave Neriel a chance to scope things out.
Using shapeshifting, he managed to take the identity of an elf he saw guarding the entrance of the forest city. This way, he would be able to enter while the guard was far in the distance. A blue light engulfed him and poured a through the glassless windows as he transformed. He was now a 5 foot and seven inch tall elven male in basic leather armour and standard equipment.
He used another grandmaster level technique to form a summoned weapon over which he cast an illusion so it would appear the same as the spear the guard had held. It was a standard wooden spear with spirals covering it the tip of it, four spiky curves, and an intricate nature pattern on the end.
He looked around to confirm no one had seen what he was in the process of doing. When he was sure he was alone, he then used a spell called Phase Walk which was a master level spell that allowed him to distort what he was walking through, almost as if it was ethereal, which allowed him to part through. This was on the tip of being a grandmaster spell due to it requiring a lot of concentration, but for an angel it was at least as much as he required.
He left his home from behind since he knew it was most likely heavily guarded from the front. Not enough were there for him to detect their presence, but enough so they would not be able to see him using magic or leaving a sort of presence on the edge of his ability to find life. It was harder since there were hundreds of people in the streets, even at night.
He smirked to himself as he took the narrow vine opening and followed it until he reached an opening to leave. From he jumped down and began his search for information.
As an angel, which were referred to as the chosen ones by some people in the other races, he was widely respected and feared. But in situations like these, if he was to ask around in his normal appearance it would arouse suspicion, as powerful as he was.
He was no match for a large group of sylph warriors and mages, especially since some were at a master and even grandmaster level. He also knew he had no chance against either of the two leaders: Syranna & Myra.
So it only made since that a covert operation was the way to go. As he entered the crowd of sylphs, he admired how peaceful they seemed. They were truly a lovely creation and were indeed his favourite, even more so then humans who he actually despised somewhat.
As he wondered around the area that was close to the near instant flash energy he had felt earlier, he started to feel a speck of energy that was identical to it. Angels were second to none when it came to detecting traces of magic – or magic at all really. What confirmed his suspicions was the area appeared to be well guarded.
As he approached a large vine wall covered in trees and bushes, he put on an act and called over to a single, nearby guard. The guard didn’t even hesitate as Neriel was dressed and looked like someone he knew.
The guard rushed over, following Neriel around the corner. As the guard came closer, Neriel raised his hand and used a master level stun spell that knocked the guard out cold.
Neriel then used a same level spell called ‘Binding Reigns’ which was produced ethereal chains to bind a target to the ground and not allow them to move an inch. After Neriel confirmed the elf was no threat, he used the same shapeshifting spell as before and took the stunned guard's appearance. Neriel then went on to the front and what seemed to be an entrance in the wall of vines.
He passed through easily as no one was aware that he was an intruder. The closer he got, the stronger the presence of deity magic became. That was until he reached the entrance of some ancient ruins. As he stood in front, he was stopped by two guards who had armour that didn’t even compare to his.
They wore what seemed like plate mail with intricate designs, half capes and hoods, and each brandished a short sword on their waists and a lance in their hands, which they sued to block Neriel.
"What are you doing here? Who released you from duty?" one of the guards demanded.
Neriel just smiled and laughed. “I apologize sir. I was just checking to see if everything was ok." Unfortunately, Neriel was not such a good actor and the other guard, who was more trained then Neriel, swung his weapon towards the angel. He had obviously picked up that something was wrong.
Stolen from its rightful place, this narrative is not meant to be on Amazon; report any sightings.
Oh no, Neriel thought before raising his hand effortlessly and grabbing the spear as he raised a brow. "How dare you?" he demanded in an echoing voice, releasing his shifted form. The guards’ eyes widen in fear. Even they knew that Neriel was an angel who was stronger than them. Neriel also revealed his wings, which were white and quite large – each nearly more than half as tall as his own height.
Neriel used his weapon and own power to deflect the other guard’s weapon who seemed to have come to his senses and tried to hit him with the back of the tip. He also jammed his fist into the guard who had first attacked him and still seemed to not comprehend what was happening.
In nearly two seconds after revealing himself, he had beaten two guards at a master level. Neriel returned to his near emotionless state as it didn’t seem like anyone else was around. There were quite a few trees and bushes blocking the sight. But he didn’t know how long he had until someone noticed.
He entered into the ruins and was greeted by the same candle light as Myra before. The presence of the deity magic was stronger than before. He hadn’t felt someone like this since right after the demon war.
Neriel noticed the many cells and the guards inside who turned to look at him. He was greeted by surprised looks as they questioned to who he was. But he didn’t respond, he just went through them using his superior power and knocked them all out.
The prisoners also seemed to fear the angel and crept back into the darkness of their cells. But then one had reached out and grabbed the keys of the fallen main guard and began opening his cell.
Little did Neriel know, he endangered the elven city and caused an annoying skirmish. With all guards dealt with, he reached a large stone door. He touched it, but grunted quietly as he realised it was unique and most likely crafted by someone more powerful than him.
"A way to open this,” he muttered. “There has to be a way." He touched his hand against it again and began to channel his energy into it, trying to overwhelm it. Even though he knew it was hopeless, he was motivated by his promise to Abbadon.
Little did he know, that the door reacted to only the most divine. Moonwing was part of a sigil crafted by Septim, and he was an angel crafted to be more celestial than anything else other than a deity. The door responded to his divine energy. Not as quick as to Moonwing’s, but after channelling his energy enough, it began to rumble and open.
As it opened, he widened his eyes as he was met with the force of intense magic that stunned his senses. Little did he know, this room was meant to conceal all traces of the etilith shield. And since the door was opened, it overflowed his senses.
"Incredible! This is truly magnificent." He walked in while speaking, admiring the power the shield emitted. He was trembling with excitement and anxiousness. He went over and touched the flowing and ever changing rainbow like shield as he felt its immense power.
Why do the sylph have something like this? he thought to himself. He then noticed something inside the shield covered in what stone vines. "What is that?" Little did he know, it was someone capable of changing Seleria itself and one day rivalling and surpassing the gods.
Neriel knew this shield had a magic circle, just by the look on the ground, but he had questions. Why did the sylph have this? Why did they keep it a secret and lie to him? Who gave it to them? And most importantly, what was inside?
He then began to hear roars and yelling. It was faint, but his sensitive ears could pick it up. He also felt the faint magic over the etilith shield. It seemed like there was combat going on.
"Oh dear. It seems like those prisoners somehow got free. No doubt those two will show up now. I’ll have to summon Lord Abbadon." He knew he had no chance against them and it was his only hope.
His magic weapon lost its illusion and began to trail along the ground in the shape of a spear of white gold with unnatural designs. The spear left a glowing mark as Neriel trailed it in a pattern. He was forming the shape of a summoning circle. He had one shot, as this was the highest grandmaster level spell he could use at the tip of becoming hero level. He would waste all his remaining energy by doing this.

chapters.title: Chapter 20 Angel lord.
chapters.content:
so good news seems il be able to keep my promise after all :) checked my email and i had this with a "be careful!!" message hehe. please dont forget to rate/vote and help Spectral Regalia make it into the top 10!! other then that. 4 more chapters until the end of Volume 1 ^^ other then that. enjoyChapter 20 Angel Lord >: ) ------------
Neriel knew the risks. Even if he was to attempt such a spell, he wasn’t sure if it would work considering the materials of the room were meant to hide mana traces. He didn’t know if that would affect the spell in some way.
He finished the main diagram of the magic circle that consisted of a one complete circle on the inside and a semi-circle on the outer left side; a somewhat half ring. He then began to draw a smaller circle linking the semi-circle and the full circle. This was a careful process. He had to make sure everything was done right.
He felt he was not as fast as he could be. Could it be because I’m nervous of the two sylphs? The thought annoyed him. Imagine! To be worried about creatures lesser then him. He didn’t hate the sylphs, but didn’t think they were better than him. The knowledge that they had weapons forged by the god Septim made him even more nervous.
He was around 97% complete with the circle. Twenty-four minutes had passed and things had become eerily quiet outside. He figured that the prison riot had all but been crushed.
“I need to hurry up. All I need to do now is channel my mana into it." He began to do so and the summoning link started to take place as the magic circle began to glow brightly. Unfortunately for him, he was about to taste pain quiet clearly.
In a moment, a figure appeared next to his side like a lightning bolt, catching him off guard. As if in slow motion, his head began to turn but not before the figure rammed its fist into his hip, sending him tumbling towards the wall and smashing into it leaving a clear impression of his form. He coughed out blood and gasped.
"Haha. You’re here earlier – sorry – later than I expected." The figure looked annoyed but was grinning savagely. It was the elven maiden, Syranna, brandishing her sigil bow Eclipse, which had allowed her powers to be modified to combat so she could take the angel off guard, otherwise it would have been incredibly hard for a sylph even as trained as her.
"I apologize about being late then. It seems someone let out the vile creatures and they had to be taken care of." A vein was popping on her forehead, as she knew it was Neriel who had done so. However, she was unaware that the incident had been an accident.
Neriel fell from the wall and caught himself in a pained kneeling position, one hand on his waist and emitting a white light. It was obvious the light was a healing spell, but he was sure he’d broken a couple of his ribs. So this is the power of a sigil. No..more so it is half the power of one, he thought. That is truly monstrous. There is no way I can defeat her I’ll have to improvise. He considered his options but it didn’t seem like Syranna wanted to wait for him as she drew back eclipse and aimed it.
"I can’t let you out of here alive, dear angel. It would risk the order and peace of my race."
Neriel glared at her. "Of your race? You sylph have been hiding something and keeping it away from us. I can feel that shield’s power. Whatever is inside it must be something important."
Syranna made a tsk sound with her mouth and drew the mana string that had formed on Eclipse. A mana bolt that was stronger than what she had used on Avrin began to take shape, but a voice called out to her. Myra. "Syranna! That’s enough! I’m sure violence can be turned into something reasonable." Syranna was sceptical.
Avrin had been nothing but bad luck. She wanted to deal with the angel and then, if she got the chance, go for Avrin next. "Myra, I can’t agree with you. He has seen it and it puts us at risk." She spoke calmly, but her face betrayed the tension that lay beneath the surface of her skin.
Myra sighed quietly. She didn’t have a counter argument. In fact, she was more inclined to battle the angel and capture him – but it would cause problems. Unfortunately, the talking had given Neriel time to use a master level magic called White Out.
Using this magic, he engulfed the entire room in a bright light that had come from a sphere of mana. It exploded immediately after it was formed, while they were distracted. Neriel rushed over to the magic circle but not before memorizing its location and shutting his eyes tightly.
As he reached the spot, squinting his eyes to confirm, he decided to try a different approach – a more dangerous one. He placed one hand on the etilith shield, which gave him a sort of mystical feeling, and then placed his other hand on the magic circle and began to use his body as a conduit draining the mana of the etilith shield. His body burned in protest.
His body was not built to hold such magic. Cracks formed on his skin and light flooded from his eyes and mouth, but he kept steady as the magic circle began to grow brighter than it would have if he had used his own magic. He hadn’t used this before because he wasn’t sure of the effects but he was in a dire strait and it was better than nothing.
While the white out spell slowly dispersed, Syranna was covering her eyes. Myra had used a quick mana shield that blocked the effect to a degree, but only enough to buy her a few seconds to realize that he was draining the etilith shield's mana for the obvious summoning circle she spotted.
Ensure your favorite authors get the support they deserve. Read this novel on the original website.
"Oh no!" Myra whispered. Having no choice, she raised Moonwing and used a shockwave to blow Neriel away from the circle. It was too little too late. The circle was engulfed in a dome of green and blue mana about three meters wide and four meters high.
Myra knew she had no time to waste and began to chant a powerful mana bolt to try and disperse the summoning. Of course, she knew she only had a few seconds. Neriel, on the other hand, was now unconscious several meters form the circle. Syranna, however, had recovered and had the same idea as Myra.
Myra was using a different approach. A large blue arrow began to form, emitting electricity. One of the many pros of Eclipse was it was able to use any of the elements as an arrow. In this case, electricity seemed like it would do well in damaging the summoning.
A large sphere of mana began to emit from the tip of Moonwing. It was a few feet in diameter before she released it with a large whooshing sound. At the same time, Syranna's arrow was let forth, making a piercing howl as both attacks were sent forth.
At that moment, a large presence of mana was felt within the circle and, as if understanding the situation from the two large attacks, the being from within slashed downwards from within the circle, sending a large mana shockwave outwards as both attacks collided. It distorted the mana flow in the air and emitted a light similar to white out. The energy flow reached the etilith shield which damaged it greatly, but it was still holding.
The being that had countered both sylph leaders’ attacked began to show himself. It was adorned in white robes, similar to an oriental Chinese outfit and large white wings which had some sort of armour at the bony area. The being had shoulder-length blonde hair and a circlet on his forehead with a deep crimson gem.
His light blue eyes would make any female fawn over him. He had a fair build that seemed a bit muscular, but athletic. He was roughly five foot, four inches and was wielding a large sword that had a dominating aura emitting from it. The gods themselves would crave such a weapon.
Neriel slowly looked up as he was moved by the shockwave and it woke him slightly. He weakly moved onto his hands and widened his eyes with a pleased feeling. "L...lord Abbadon." He couldn’t have been happier as Abbadon’s presence guaranteed he would survive.
Myra glared nervously as she was dealing with who she figured to be the single most powerful warrior on Seleria. Syranna began to sweat slightly and tightened her grip on Eclipse.
"Abbadon," Myra said, He gazed around and she saw a pained expression cross his face as he caught sight of the injured Neriel. What made it more frightening was that he was ignoring them. Could it be he hadn’t noticed yet or he simply didn’t see them as a threat?
"Neriel, are you ok?" Abbadon was clearly worried about his fellow angel.
"I’m fine, my lord. Please, look behind you. I’m sure you are aware, but that—" Before he could continue, Abbadon interrupted.
"From what I can see, you put yourself in a dangerous situation. I will have to decide your punishment later." Abbadon frowned, which made Neriel sulk quietly. He hadn’t expected to be lectured.
The lecture put Syranna somewhat at ease. "If you are done, we would appreciate it if you would leave and never return to this forest again." Anger laced through her words.
Abbadon turned and emitted a powerful presence at Myra and Syranna who felt it immediately and stepped back, brandishing their weapons again. "Moving on, it seems Neriel was right. Whatever this is behind me, it surely belongs to a deity.
Judging by the feeling of the mana, it is an object of lenaya." He sighed quietly. "Not only that, there is something inside of it which needs such a powerful object to either protect it or keep it sealed.
The magic around it is a vine spell that has been petrified, so I’m guessing you’ve sealed something in – something you don’t want out." Myra was shocked at the whole situation. Standing before her was a being to be reckoned with. His knowledge of magic and situations was unmatched.
"You also injured an angel – a harbinger of peace. I cannot let that go unpunished, even for sigil wielders." At this stage, both the sylph leaders knew this would end in a fight.
Myra faced Moonwing towards Abbadon. "It hasn’t been recorded that sigil wielders had faced off. Do you truly wish to make us fight when these weapons are for combatting dragons?" Myra tried to change his mind.
Abbadon gave a menacing smile and raised the strongest blade ever created, the great sword Twilight, and pointed it between Myra and Syranna, gesturing that he would take them both on. "A weapon is used to kill or protect. In this case, I will use mine to give judgement."
---Previous Chapter Next chapter

chapters.title: V1: Chapter 21 Ready...Set...Battle
chapters.content:
First of all Credits go to Zeratul For Pring how do you guys find it as feedback is needed :).
Please note id like to ask people to always check up on the updates page as there is always info on the front of it  twice a week. there will be another pred chapter By Zeratul released soon.

P.S most important thing regarding this and the next release is asking how the grammar is for this chapter. also dont forget to thank zeratul O.O!! ------------Syrana wasted no time preparing a dark arrow as she waited for him to make the first move as it would justify her retaliating. Myra still wanted to resolve this matter without combat however Syrana had forgotten that this type of battle would destroy this area and endanger the sylph. She didn’t want Abbadon to realise this and put them in a difficult position.
Abbadon then gave them a choice. "If you truly want to avoid conflict, I am not without fairness." Though Abbadon said those words, he was reluctant to start battle as Neriel would be caught up in the crossfire but at the same time he couldn’t let this go since he was interested in the shield and what it held sealed. Myra cautiously eyed him without lowering her guard while taking in his words and deciding on a course of action.
It seemed that she was slowly starting to regret taking Avrin in as it brought bad luck quickly. How could she have foreseen a force capable of combating a dragon, better than anyone else, would come to the slyphs.
"What is it you want Abbadon? … Surely you aren’t thinking we will give up the Etilith shield so freely to you. Since it is made by Lenaya it is rightfully ours." Myra fastened her grip onto moonwing as if preparing for a violent response.
"That is true." Abbadon calmly spoke "Although to my knowledge, I am not aware of something like this existing. So it must be a hidden gift, possibly under the noses of the other gods." Abbadon like the elves wanted order and peace but not for the forest but the entirety of Seleria.
So a god favouring a race was something he could not allow as it was not fair and tended to ruin the balance. "But i can see that is doing no harm. In fact I’m more interested in what is inside."
Abbadon was possibly the most careful and cautious humanoid on Seleria. The way he pointed out facts in such intense moments was something to be jealous of. One would think that it was no wonder that he was appointed leader of the angels and tasked by septim often.
"That is none of your business!" Syrana blurted out angrily. "That’s quite rude of you to talk in such a manner, my dear maiden." Abbadon responded to her. "She is right however, you angels have no reason to go snooping around. We are doing no harm and have no intention of doing so." Myra followed.
"Well then you won’t mind if I take a look?" Abbadon placed his hand against the shield trying to disarm it, but it was indeed much too powerful for him to do so in an instant. "I see, truly a powerful object of a deity. I would have no hope of trying to turn it off without spending months fiddling with it." He complimented Lenaya in a tone that would suggest he is capable of still doing so to the goddess he did not follow.
"How dare you!!" Syrana called out in anger. She was quite smart herself as she understood his compliment was also a comment to how he could undo the goddess' work. "Syrana wait!!" Myra called out  but it was too late the dark arrow bolt had fired with a fierce precision.
Even if Abadon was an angel wielding a sigil it would still hurt if he did not counter. He used his angelic speed imbued with some of his own sigil weapons strength and managed to tilt his body to the side as the arrow shot straight past him. As he turned to dodge his hair swayed in the air but the arrow had cut a few strands which made him widen his eyes in surprise.
Even if the sigil's power was half the strength it was no doubt still strong enough to injure or even kill him if he underestimated either of the two.
The arrow struck the Etilith shield as it was quite strong causing the shield to shake violently but it still held strong. Afterall, it was capable of sustaining much more as well as drawing its energy from the forest.
Abbadon noticed the shield was quite durable and smiled. "I see it’s quite powerful. I wonder ..." He slashed across the air sending a mana blade wave towards the shield that seemed to block the main portion of the attack but the part of the wave that hadn’t hit the shield went on and hit the walls of the ruin, causing it to tremor greatly as debris fell down around them the remnant wave continued to pass through, causing a slight tremor around the area.
Abbadon did not know it drew its power from the forest which is why he had attacked. Although there was the possibility of him still doing so. Myra on the other hand knew if things went out of hand the forest would suffer if they continued with such attacks.
"Stop!!" myra called out being the only one who knew the magic circle enough even more so than syrana understanding the consequences. Syrana took Abbadon’s attack as a sign of battle and then began to barrage him with quick mana arrows with no elemental attunement.
Love what you're reading? Discover and support the author on the platform they originally published on.
Abbadon was more careful than before he wielded Twilight as if it were a normal sword. His angelic strength lessening the weight that would cause a man to wield it with both hands but Abbadon seemed to be blocking or splitting the arrows in half.
"I’m sorry my dear maiden but if that is all you have then this won’t be much of a battle." Abbadon spoke blatantly, taunting Syrana who seemed to grin taking that challenge. She began to pull the mana string back quite far as a mana arrow formed that looked more like a spiral spear than an arrow. Each spiral consisted of two colours red and green. She would then fire the spiral like an arrow that screeched through the air with ease leaving a mana trail as it did.
Abbadon eyes twitched for a moment before using twilight to block it. The spiral arrow did not break instead it was pushing against the flat side used to block against it and was spinning like a drill. "I see a drill arrow?"  Abbadon spoke. Myra grinned "Not quite ..." The arrow would then explode over abbadon's blade, entangling it with vines that had thorns around it.
Abbadon was quite surprised. This was also his first combat lesson with a weapon capable of competing with his own. "Interesting, but not good enough." Abbadon grinned  as he underestimated Syrana's arrow. "You know, for an angel as intelligent as yourself. You sure tend to overlook things." Syrana spoke followed by the vines surrounding Abbadon’s blade glowing red before exploding in a pillar of flames.
The flames themselves seemed violent and bursted upwards  20 meters, hitting the ceiling and causing more debris to fall as well as a diameter of a few meters that managed to collide with the shield again causing it to wobble and weaken before it replenishing itself from the forest.
Syrana gazed proudly, making a fist as she jumped slightly and raised her hand. "Got him!!" Neriel called out in a slight despair. "M-My lord!!" The flames were then blown away as if it was nothing. Revealing Abbadon underneath with a few scorch marks on his robe and a few scratches on his flawless skin. This left Syrana with a speechless expression and Neriel with a sigh of relief.
Abbadon smiled as he pointed his blade at Syrana. "I guess it’s my turn now. Please try not to die." Syrana knew he wouldn’t take it easy on her, and as if not waiting she fired off another Arrow attuned with nature and fire towards Abbadon.
"I don’t think this is a skill suited for Twilight but I suppose it should do." In a moment he jabbed his sword forward as if wielding a rapier which caused a sonic boom like motion to sway around the hilt. The movement of the skill caused a mana strike that would pierce forwards to be shot towards Syrana. It collided with her arrow as they both struggled for a brief second before Abbadon’s attacked pierced right through and towards Syrana.
"Damn it." Syrana spoke as she prepared herself, not having time to dodge the attack that was a few meters away before exploding against something that seemed to form out of nowhere. What was left was a gaian shield that was falling apart due to the attack. Behind it was Syrana who covered her eyes and myra in front of her holding moonwing towards the attack that had been blocked.
"S-Syrana we need to work together if we are to have a chance." Syrana was thankful that her friend had come to help her and nodded giving a firm smile. "Nice of you to join us priestess, I suppose this way it will be more fun. Neriel."
Abbadon spoke. "Y-yes my lord!" Neriel came to attention and Abbadon then spoke. "I no longer think it is wise to reuse that object. I noticed the magic circle containing it. I want you to try and disable it." Neriel's eyes widened with worry. "B-but I don’t have the energy."
Abbadon chuckled quietly. "That is fine. I’m sure you will figure something out. Whatever is in that shield is worth having an object crafted by a deity to guard. It truly must be something valuable. Unfortunately, I have become quite curious and I do not think I can come out of this unharmed."
Before Neriel could reply, flame arrows had come towards Abbadon who raised his hand creating a shield similar to a gaian shield but with a divine touch. Using his own angelic power as well as the strength of a full sigil weapon they were effortlessly deflected.
He then continued with his own attacks as he slashed vertically then horizontally a few times in quick succession. Sending mana waves towards the two who seemed to dodge or hide behind a gaian shield that would crumble after being hit by a few of these attacks.
"Come my dears. Let us battle to our hearts content." Abbadon showed an enjoyable look as it had been centuries since he last enjoyed a battle and decades since he enjoyed one with opponents capable of killing him ...

chapters.title: Chapter 22 To Be What i Should Be.
chapters.content:
Credits to Zeratul for Pring. please again dont forget to ask us how the grammar is. btw please know for those that dont read the Updates thread that chapter 24 is the end of volume one and ch 25 is the start of vol 2.  can we get a rating of 80 for a bonus chapter release >:)  you guests need to put in the effort now and register mwuahahaha!! -------------The prison like ruins were trembling heavily to the extent that the forest above shook with the force of the attacks the sigil users sent against each other. The sylphs above who were detaining the prisoners, who attempted to riot, considered it dangerous to be in the area and were quite worried as they wondered what was going on. Surven who was organizing the sylph's as he was in charge in case Syrana and Myra were not around also knew something was wrong.
"I knew that boy was trouble." He spoke to himself before calling out "Please everyone it is dangerous here! Move all the prisoners away and keep everyone away from here!!" He called out as he gazed at the entrance to the ruins, seeing it shake violently as he began to sweat a little. The elves wasted no time in moving as they would do their best to try and assist for the sake of their people and the forest.
Meanwhile underneath, Neriel who would turn around occasionally to see Abbadon attacking Myras shield, as well as deflecting blocking or avoiding Syrana’s arrows seemed to be enjoying himself. Considering the stakes, Myra on the other hand looked quite worried and Syrana was just pissed off. He felt somewhat glad that it wasn’t Abbadon who seemed to struggle. To the contrary, it felt like he was still holding back.
He pressed his hand against the circle on the ground as he pressed another hand onto the shield. He still remembered the pain and agony from the last time he tried to channel its energy into him but this time he had a plan. He made an adjustment to the edge of the mana circle Lenaya had created for the sylphs and it seemed out of place. It was a magic circle that emitted a white faint glow.
Neriel began to channel a small portion of the shields mana into his own circle while being careful not to rush it like he did when summoning Abbadon. But it seemed to still hurt him quite a bit as he felt his own mana going crazy as if a foreign body had entered him.
But the white circle began to glow a bright color and the etilith shield itself began to distort violently. As bolts of what appeared to be green lightning hit all over the place. one even shooting out towards Myra who had a gaian shield up and took notice.
"N-not good." She spoke seeing the lone angel tampering with her goddess’ gift. Syrana on the other hand gave a more violent response, wasting no time firing a charged lightning arrow towards Neriel. He barely turned in time to see her do so as he gave a worried look.
As the arrow was released Abbadon came and slashed it before it reached the halfway mark as he grinned while looking at the two sylphs. "Whatever you are doing Neriel keep it up." He said with a smile.
"Y-yes my lord." He continued to which Syrana and Myra went on the offensive as Abbadon was now protecting Neriel. He was at a disadvantage this time as he was facing two opponents. The lightning was a somewhat god send (no pun intended) as the bolts that went crazy would occasionally fire towards Syrana and Myra giving him a chance to go on the offensive. But the bolts would also tear at the ruin’s walls.
They all knew it most likely would not hold up for long. The magic circle of the etilith shield began to distort slightly as the shield itself bended violently. This time, bolts would fire inside of it hitting itself as it would only add to weakening it.
The true loser was the forest which seemed to be suffering quite largely. The trees would begin to wither and the grass itself changed color. This made the sylphs on the surface panic and Surven who was also panicking struggled to keep order.
Myra felt something was wrong and the forest was weakening due to the strain. The etilith shield was a wonder that would negate attacks from the inside which made her surprised at the time Avrin was able to use his own ability. But when tampered with from the outside it was vulnerable.
Which is why there was a need to heavily protect it. "Stop it!!!" Myra spoke as she was now enraged and began to charge a violent mana sphere that was easily at hero level as her eyes began to flare with a mana aura that emitted from her body. The mana sphere began to build up and seemed like a miniature sun. This made Abbadon and Syrana quiver with a slight fear.
If you discover this tale on Amazon, be aware that it has been stolen. Please report the violation.
"M-Myra" Syrana said worryingly. Abbadon on the other hand was taking up a stance as Twilight began to glow for the first time a light blue. "I see you decided to get serious. Then I shall take it up a notch." Myra fired the Mana bolt that would be capable of decimating a village with ease. Probably not the best idea in such a space but Abbadon was there to counter it.
He would thrust his mana imbued Twilight in the same way he had done with Syrana but this time was different as he said "Vorpal Thrust". A beam of energy covered in a sharp spiral fired towards the mana bolt as they both collided but it seemed like Abbadon’s full sigil was the victor yet again as it caused the mana sphere to implode as it let out a powerful shockwave that managed to luckily deter the trajectory of the thrust that pierced upwards into the ceiling.
As the sharp energy beam pierced into the ceiling, it fired into the tree line piercing through a large ancient tree with ease and continuing further into the sky that managed to even pierce a hole through the clouds. The beam then slowly vanished into the endless sky as if it would reach the heavens itself.
At that moment a few bolts of lightning hit against the petrified vine prison that Myra had put onto Avrin. Every time it tried to heal itself, the unstable mana lightning from the tampered shield would continue to damage it.
Little did they know that this had given Avrin the chance to escape. The petrified rock crumbled a little. Inside the spell that had kept Avrin’s mind asleep, had left a spot for him to escape due to outside interference. Avrin gazed at empty space that had several cracks that opened wider and wider. "This is my chance." Wasting no time he rushed through it into the white light that seemed to be his escape.
In that moment two things were recognized. Avrin was now awake and back into his own consciousness and he was greeted by a fierce battle that was raging on. He was in the middle of it. "Not good." He quickly began to analyze things. He came to realize something as he had time to think. It seemed he tried to change his personality in this new world and became dumber and less driven. As if he had no cares.
When the truth is his past self was required for survival. His instincts from his past world kicked in as he looked around "Sylphs fighting … against a winged being?" Avrin quickly spoke as he looked around some more.
"The shield is twisting … and shooting lightning everywhere?" He continued and saw another winged being that seemed to be the cause of the twisting. "Another one. Their purpose is unknown?" Avrin grinned to himself as the petrified rock revealed only his glowing eyes. Neriel looked past the shield to see a deep blue emitting from a crack in the rocky vines which sent a shiver down his spine as if gazing at a devil. "What i-i-is that?"
Avrin smiled as he let a quiet breathe out. "It’s time I stopped playing around and start thinking of tactics. Obviously them engaging in combat allows me to freely escape, but how." He looked around and placed his hand onto the ground in the tight narrow space.
"Perfect, but I don’t have long judging by the current state of that shield nor do I want to be caught up in it imploding" He spoke quietly to himself as he figured that is what would happen if it had been tampered with for too long.
Avrin when entering this world had been too careless and too driven by his own needs, forgetting his past training and mindset. But what dawned on him was that there were beings who were more powerful than him and could do away with him whenever they needed. He also remembered his past when he was betrayed by his crew.
As he focused his dark matter onto the ground he spoke to himself as it reassured him. "To survive in this world I need to be cautious and analytical. If a tactician thinks two steps ahead I need to think 4 steps ahead. i will never allow myself to be in such a state unless it is within my plans. I will take the weak man I was and I will build on to become the man i need to be."

please dont forget to reccomend spread the word of this ff aswell as rate/follow/favourite other then that enjoy the bonus chapter -------------While the fighting raged outside of the etilith shield as well as the angel Neriel trying to stop it, who seemed unaware of what the danger could be if it was indeed intended to implode. Avrin had dug several feet into the ground as it seemed as if it were melting downward. He intended to dig down and hide himself. He had thought of a theory. There was not one bit of mana in his body, therefore he had hoped they would not be able to detect him after everything was said and done.
At first glimpse he knew from the way they were fighting that he didn’t have a chance and figured they have some sort of ability to detect mana. So if he were able to hide himself underground and reseal the entrance of the hole it would be as if there was nothing there. But he had a couple of problems.
The first was that should the elves win, they do know that there is something inside of the prison that held him. So they would be suspicious. The second was that should the angel-like creatures win, he had no idea how smart they were or anything about them. It was truly a risk. Avrin continued at this pace as he was now nearly 2 meters into the ground as the dirt turned to clay, which seemed to turn into a different layer as there were some roots that were quite thick in the ground which he also had to go through.
Meanwhile Abbadon seemed to be taking the fight a bit more seriously as he stepped up his offensive against the two sylph leaders, but it also seemed Syrana was irritated at not being able to press forward. She was used to overpowering her opponents easily, but here in front of her was a being stronger than her who still seemed to take it easy on her. Myra on the other hand was more worried at Neriel’s progress and the gift granted to her by her goddess Lenaya.
Myra suddenly began to chant as she gathered mana into Moonwing. "Oh, goddess of life, godess of our people. Please grant your priestess some of your power in my time of need. Spreading wild, entangling roots, the ecliptic moon and its lover the sun." Moonwing began to emit an intense power as it began to emit its aura signifying that it was indeed a Celestial weapon. Although this caught Abbadon’s eye.
"That will be quite dangerous." He mumbled to himself before bringing back Twilight in a stance that showed he was about to use his own ability to interrupt Myra. "Thankfully it seems like me, you’re not taking this fight seriously. After all, many lives would be lost." He also knew he had to hold back for Neriel’s sake and he was not as careless as to bring the sylphs above into the fray as that would indeed anger the goddess Lenaya as well as make his own goddess think twice of him.
"Reverie Tempe-..." Before he had finished speaking, he was interrupted with a volley of elemental arrows from Syrana who showed a smug grin. She continued her merciless barrage as smoke began to build up from where Abbadon stood completely covering his location.
As the smoke passed a shield had revealed itself as it pulsed with magic. "Divine Shield" The power of his shield imbued with his powerful angelic powers as well as his sigil’s power was more than enough to stop Syrana’s attack. As he prepared to slash towards her a glow of energy reflected in his direction as he turned to face it.
He was greeted by a hero level skill known only by Myra. He would be lying if he said he had seen it before so he didn’t know what to expect. He kept his shield up as he intended to meet it dead on, having no choice considering that behind him was Neriel. If he moved Neriel would surely die.
"You damned fairy." He snickered. Myra had finished her spell thanking syrana in her mind for buying her time. It seemed Abbadon had stopped right before he attacked her friend as myra pointed Moonwing with the prepared spell towards him.
She spoke as he seemed to ready himself as Myra did so. "Lenaya’s Thorn" A beam of green light shot from the tip of Moonwing as thorns and mana like flowers had formed from the beam as it seemed to fire towards Abbadon’s shield.
He gasped as he knew his divine shield would not be able to handle a constant stream of magic. He had a better chance of attacking the beam itself. In a quick change of mind he lowered his shield forgetting that Syrana was still there.
He had made a mistake but in the meantime he gripped Twilight with both hands and held it in front of him as the thorn like beam collided with the edge of the blade, causing it to emit a white and green light as a screeching sound echoed throughout the now somewhat destroyed ruins.
A case of content theft: this narrative is not rightfully on Amazon; if you spot it, report the violation.
Abbadon found himself pushed back slightly. He had felt annoyed he had to hold back significantly but decided it was ok in this case as long as he would do so to stop this attack. At that moment Syrana began firing arrows towards Abbadon. He had looked towards the shield wanting to see its progress. But luckily caught a glimpse of the attack as he held his right hand out casting a semi circular divine shield while still taking the attack of myras head on.
He was now facing a two pronged attack. "Gah!" He felt himself struggle with his limited power. "You sylphs … truly ... a..are strong together … your weapons may be a half power … but working like this … you can even match me when we are all holding back." 
The percentages of powers being released were 60/60% for the sylphs while Abbadon was only using 30%, being a full sigil wielder it was more then enough to compete.
He then had an idea as he smirked to himself in a show of agile skill seeing Syrana take a slight break to find a better point to attack him. He jumped his power use up to 40% and deflected the beam towards the etilith shield 9 meters above Neriel as the beam collided with the shield as well as neriel’s distortion.
It was all it could handle before the dormant lightning bolts that had seemed to stop prior had now awakened and gone berserk as they shot out rapidly. One of the bolts hitting Syrana who was just about to land hitting her left thigh as she gasped in pain and fell down rolling around.
This made myra stop her stream for both the shield and her friend Syrana who she rushed to help. Abbadon gazed at the shield as he hit some stray bolts that came towards him. Neriel seemed somewhat safe as they didn’t shoot down near him.
"It’s too dangerous to continue." He rushed over to Neriel and grabbed him by his cloak and tugged him away while skillfully drawing a mini teleportation circle on the ground. He spoke as he gazed at the two sylphs who seemed to gaze back.
"I apologize concerning this situation but it seems this has gotten to dangerous. … Whether there is something in there or not I will be above to protect your city. I am not as blind as to realise this could be bad. I recommend you hurry and return too." Before either of the two could reply a phase of light engulfed both Neriel and Abbadon who vanished as the circle that had been drawn by the tip of Twilight was also gone.
The shield was now unstable as the radiant color turned red and black and lighting cut away in every direction. Myra had to cast her own gaian shield to stop stray beams. "Damn it, this situation ..." Myra called out angrily. Syrana slowly got up as she was emitting a small healing pulse at the burn mark left on her thigh. "Myra we need to go quickly. He might not be enough ..." She stood up and took her hand as she tried to lead her away but was met with resistance.
"And leave Avrin in there? It’s true he brought us to this situation but its also me who trapped him. He will surely not survive." Syrana sighed as she had little care for Avrin and didn’t want to argue.
As Syrana was larger and physically stronger, she lifted Myra up onto her shoulders and ran off as she screamed for her to drop her. Her concern for Avrin was brought only because it seemed like it was too late to save the etilith shield and the thought of it reminded her of him.
Meanwhile Abbadon had already begun chanting as the fairies began to cast their own magic to try and help while all the other residents were held away to hide in shelters. It seems the etilith shield’s power had caused a freak lightning storm with purple coloured clouds that fired red lightning bolts which seemed quite powerful.
"Holy goddess of light, mother of the celestials, heed my call for your servant has need of your powers. The protection that desires the shield that guards the heavens. Bulwark of Light!!" A powerful aura exploded around the ruins which also seemed to dig into the ground as if forming.
Avrin who had found a hidden tunnel that seemed to be another connection to the ruins had continued to run across it as he had changed his mind regarding filling in the hole due to his discovery here.
He used his augmented eyes to see in the pitch black darkness of the tunnel that didn’t seem to have anything in it. Only a steady stream of water and large roots. He panted heavily as he was not exhausted but sweating as he had also noticed the shield going crazy as he felt rumbling from the lightning bolts inside the ruins as well as the ones outside.
"What … an interesting situation. … Well, it could be worse." He smiled to himself as he tried to cheer himself up. He blinked as he saw a light emit from the floor and ground of the tunnel a yellowish light was seeping through forming a sort of shell as it was going upwards as if intending to connect.
He chuckled to himself  "Oh, no you don’t."
