chapters.title: Chapter 44 Swamplands.
chapters.content:
Special release courtesy ofDraconis for his quick pring and the fact that i couldnt leave you guys hanging for a cliffhanger hopefully this one is less. Please Rate/Follow/Favourite. and also enjoy :) this special release
-------------
As Avrin waited worryingly at her words, they had finally come out “What I want from you, Avrin, is to know what your ability truly is…” Avrin blinked. It wasn’t what he expected as he had thought it was something perverted. But this seemed to be even worse in a manner of speaking. “Syrana, that’s a little…” Before he finished, she huffed and cut him off “What’s wrong? Surely the information is something you need?..”
Avrin titled his head “But it isn’t equal to the information you want...Besides, what would you do with it. Something like that, I don’t trust you with. I’m sure you would use it against me in a heartbeat, so I have no desire to tell you..”
Syrana grumbled and eyed him, as if showing him a poker face. “Fine..I suppose you are right..” Avrin only rolled his eyes as it was obvious that he was right. Syrana continued to speak. “Very well then, how did you end up in the forest to begin with Avrin? Why were you destroying it and killing the creatures?..”
Avrin blinked, this was a good opportunity for him to clear things with her. “Fine, I'll tell you. Maybe this will ease tension between us.” He went over and sat down again. Syrana doing the same opposite of him.
He began to tell her from the start of his journey about how he was executed and the reason why and how he was reincarnated. But he left the part regarding God and anything to do with his power out. In fact, he had only told her that he had been given this body and awoke in the forest with only his past memory of his universe.
He then told her about his struggle to survive and get used to his ability without giving her too much information. Only the basics. Syrana, as if like a sponge, absorbed everything. She was hesitant to believe him at first, but felt as if he were telling the truth. Her gaze towards him seemed to be less aggressive as he continued on.
Avrin spoke “From there, I was attacked by both groups of creatures...I had no other choice but to fight and protect myself...In the end I killed them all and captured one that I experimented on, I admit. Though that was probably not the best of ideas…”
Syrana huffed. “You’re telling me.. Regardless, it seems your actions were justified. But to experiment with that vile dark magic on a captured creature is heartless”
Avrin chuckled and grinned “I already said I regretted it. Stop rubbing it in...Besides, in the end it ran off..I made it stronger but I guess its clan did not agree…” Syrana blinked as she gazed at Avrin who seemed to be annoyed and a little sad.
Avrin spoke again “The creature came back to me covered in the blood of itself and its kin..They didn’t accept it back and tried to kill it...In the end, when their leader tried to kill it, I felt obligated to help it. At that point I already felt regret. It reminded me of my past and it angered me. So in return for them killing it when it came to me with hope, I killed them.“ Avrin showed a dark menacing gaze at the fire as he remembered it.
Syrana quietly gazed with awe at him and spoke “I’ve no comment for your actions...I can feel your regret towards it, so I will forgive you for now...But this changes little between us...Even though the Neophat is alive…”
Avrin blinked as he looked up at her. “A..Alive?!” A near innocent smile appeared on his face which made Syrana blush faintly and look away as she replied “Y..Yes, but its arm had to go...Such a vile thing couldn’t remain in the forest..”
Avrin blinked. “Why would you!! If it was alive it surely must have been near death..” Syrana turned and gazed at him and replied. “So I thought as well….But it seemed like the arm, after being removed from the body, liquefied and then went over the wound on its chest as if it recycled itself and was sentient...We took it back and locked it away for safety and to try and heal it, but…”
Avrin was amazed. It seemed that regrowing an arm seemed to have an even better effect than he imagined “Incredible, I never realised it was that useful”.. Syrana stood up and roared. “Useful?!! You interfered with the laws of life! After it healed itself the wound on its chest healed quickly and that dark magic spread around its body. It broke out of the cell and ran away, we tried tracking it but it left the forest before we even put a group together”
Avrin tilted his head and smiled. “I’m glad that it’s alive. I would like to meet it again someday and make it up to the creature. If it doesn't try to kill me” Avrin chuckled slightly but Syrana only sighed and gazed at the fire.
Things seemed a bit quiet now that things have been explained. It was somewhat awkward. But Syrana spoke out. “Ehm...Avrin, if your story is indeed true, then I apologise for half of why you were sealed away…” Avrin tilted his head and snickered. “Only half?..” Syrana then glared and shot daggers at him. “I’m sure if you were left alone, than the entire forest would be like that Leophat..”
Avrin only chuckled at her dumb reason, before speaking “Since your so forgiving and apologetic for tonight, do I get one for you admiring me while I was bathing?” He grinned and stared at her as if she were a sort of criminal.
Syrana only stood up as if protecting herself “N...No, I was just..checking to see if you were up to something and also intended to see how strong you had gotten…” Avrin spoke “Well as you saw, I'm quite happy to say I'm significantly stronger than I was before.” He then stood up and approached her as he sat beside her, gazing at her.
Syrana blushed slightly and tried to scoot away slowly, but seemed to somewhat enjoy him being near her. Even more so for the fact that things have been somewhat cleared up. “A..Avrin, what are you..?”
He spoke before she got the wrong idea. “A deal is a deal Syrana. Please let me see the spirit stone now.. “ Syrana made a dull look as she had thought he was making a move on her, but held her left hand out to him as she formed the inactive stone.
Avrin began looking at it closer. “Incredible, so it forms using mana...I don't think I would be able to mimic its creation to the point of its usefulness...Syrana, who invented the spirit stone?” Syrana, feeling somewhat obligated to educate Avrin considering he was still new to Seleria, began to speak in a sort of teacher tone. “The spirit stone was invented by a good friend of my fathers. His name is Albert L.Grym, a human archmage”
Avrin smiled and gently emitted a nebula mist over the spirit stone which made it turn dark. Syrana quickly brought it back into her body as mana “What were you planning?!!” Avrin blinked and placed his hands on his lap as he gazed as if he did nothing wrong. “Uhh, I was just examining its structure to see if I could create one of my own…”
Syrana was quiet before speaking “It’s impossible. The spirit stones must be obtained in a capital city from one of the mage guild branches there. Made specially from an ore that is capable of being turned into mana and being absorbed into the body..But I know from your words that your ability has to do with creating things” She grinned slyly.
Avrin stood up and dusted himself off “You’re smarter then you look. I should give you more credit for deducing that...But I won't say anything else unless you answer this. Is it possible for me to meet this Albert L. Grym” Avrin spoke eagerly, awaiting her reply.
Syrana chuckled and shook her head. “I’m sorry to say that he died a century and a half ago” Avrin looked somewhat sad and Syrana wriggled her nose and cleared her throat and spoke “But his bloodline lives strongly. Last I heard, one of his kin is the leader of the mage guild and continues his families study of spirit stones and more”
Avrin’s face lit up happily again as he smiled and bowed. “I thank you for that.” Syrana spoke again “Well give me a clue Avrin. Was I right or wrong?..” Avrin regained his posture and blinked “Oh, your deduction” He smiled “you’re right to a degree. Creation is one aspect of my ability. But that is all I shall share. Anyway, Syrana, I’m feeling tired so I shall rest. I’ll leave first watch to you”
Avrin chuckled as Syrana gave an angry pout as she had been tricked. But remembered something as she spoke while Avrin was about to enter the tent. “Avrin...For Ayame, she indeed has feelings for you, but she is young. I know you beat her badly and I take it the reason she feels attracted to you is only because she lost to you. That being said, please do not harm her mentally. She is important to me”
This story originates from a different website. Ensure the author gets the support they deserve by reading it there.
Syrana spoke a rare emotional side of her which made Avrin smile and speak “This is rare for you to be asking in such an emotional state.” He teased as Syrana glared. Avrin continued “But I’ll say this. I’ve no interest in a relationship for now. I want to focus on establishing myself in Seleria. I just have no interest. Besides, I would have no confidence in protecting someone I loved in a world with monstrous people.” Avrin smiled softly as turned around to enter, but words made him blink.
“Avrin...You know not all females are weak and fragile, needing your protection.. F..For instance, if we were to be together, I am more then capable of looking after myself. I’ve done so for centuries…” Syrana spoke as if hinting at her feelings. It seemed she had grown more fond of him after tonights events.
Avrin, with no hint of a romantic emotion, gazed at the tent. Away from her. “Syrana, after what has happened between us, I am still very angry...It is also too early as we have only now become on such a talking basis. Besides, I’ve no interest in someone who longs for my body alone.”
Syrana spoke out as if to explain it was different now that she had gotten to know him, but he continued to speak before her, as if to give her a bit of hope to improve relations, as it seemed to be more beneficial now. “But I'm sure maybe someday you will impress me. But until then there is a lot of anger for me to vent caused by you and your people.”
Avrin entered the tent as Syrana gave a saddened look, not uttering a word as she hugged her knees while gazing at the fire. As the night went on without a hitch, Avrin had woken up refreshed, and before eating, had entered a Pulsing Dragon state for a good hour, which energized his body even more so. As he got out of the tent Ayame and Syrana had already begun to pack their things. The fire pit was cleaned up as if it werent even there. Most likely due to Syrana’s respect of the forest.
Avrin spoke “Have you both gotten your things from the tent?..” He spoke firmly. Ayame nodded and Syrana replied with a ‘yes’ Avrin then raised his hand towards the tent as it began to disassemble into dark matter and absorb into his hand. Ayame and Syrana both gazed with awe and curiosity as they were amazed.
Syrana especially as she had wanted to learn more about Avrin’s ability. She was snapped out of her mini trance as Avrin spoke while he finished absorbing the tent quickly. “Syrana, do you think we could arrive before these 2 days are up?..”
Syrana was silent as she gazed at Ayame who seemed to smile back at her as her mind seemed to be cleared. Syrana spoke “If we leave now at full speed for a few hours instead of walking, I’m sure we could reach Langs lair in 16 hours, cutting the time down more than half”
Avrin turned and gazed at Ayame. “Ayame can you handle it?..” Ayame was silent as she looked at Avrin then shut her eyes and nodded as she spoke “I’ll consider it stamina training. If I can’t keep that pace up then I can’t be considered a White Dragon shinobi..”
Avrin nodded and got his own things that he had placed down as he absorbed the tent. “Very well. Lets go.” As the 3 of them finalized everything, they left quickly as they rushed through the forest, like lightning shooting through quickly. Although Syrana and Avrin had held their speed back for Ayame. Avrin in the past had been slower than her, but those couple of years of training made an astonishing leap for him. But he knew he still had a long way to go.
They continued on for 5 hours and Ayame was starting to feel fatigue as she slowed down. They stopped on a mountain path. Syrana pointed to a large mountain engulfed in greenery, with large trees sticking out of it as well as several clouds being split by its height.
Syrana spoke “Lang’s lair is located there, although we will have to be careful. There are creatures that worship it like a god that will protect the surroundings even against us. Especially the orcs”
Ayame shivered with disgust. ”Urgh..Or...Orcs...I hate them” Avrin didn't know how to react. He had never seen an orc before, but was eager to meet one and test his combat prowess. “Syrana, how strong are orcs exactly?” Avrin spoke as they rested for a bit for Ayame who seemed to be eating a sort of muffin/cookie made from the fruit like paste that Syrana made and cooked.
Syrana spoke knowledgeably. “Orcs at the most are as strong as a knight only because of their brute strength. Other than that they're not social to outsiders. They have Shamans for magic and can be quite tricky. And they do vary from area to area, so it will be hard to say. But I'm sure regardless, these orcs will pose no real threat to us as long as we keep our guard up”
Syrana had begun speaking to Avrin in a less harsh tone, which Avrin seemed to be pleased with. He had gotten quite sick of her past way of speaking and would not deal with it if it continued on. That being said he still intended to get revenge on her. And Ayame he was forgiving after he settled the score. After they had rested for a half hour and ate they made their way down the mountain path and entered a denser part of the forest that seemed almost swamp like as there were frog like croaks as well as chirping and the sounds of insects as well as a faint fog.
Ayame held her nose and spoke “Argh..T...That stench..” Syrana was used to worse as she had been in battle with countless dead bodies and blood ridden ground. As for Avrin, who had been to many different planets in his universe as well as battlefields, he was no less used to it then Syrana.
Syrana chuckled and spoke “It’s the natural gas of the forest. When the insects and plants decay and go back to the planet, they combine with the water and release this gas that acts as a sort of fertilizer for the plant life. Which in turn acts as food for the insects and the insects to the animals and so on”
Avrin was intrigued by Syrana’s view of natural habitats. He spoke softly “You're quite attuned to nature Syrana. I see Sylphs are truly children of nature.”
Syrana huffed and shut her eyes as they continued. “As children of Lenaya” She corrected and continued on “We must love all her creations. Even places like these..”
As Avrin nodded, they continued further. Avrin had augmented his left eye for safety as he had a feeling something was up. Syrana only gazed with curiosity at him as she saw his eye change. Avrin then raised his hand, signalling for them to slow down. He whispered.
“200 meters ahead of us there is quite a lot of humanoids. Easily more than a hundred.” Syrana only gazed at him with shock as she spoke “H..How can you see that?” Avrin only smiled and then grinned “Just one of my abilities. Besides, I want to know is it ok if we kill them. Or are you going to hound me for attacking?”
Syrana only glared at him “We won't attack them if there is no reason. We will go around. Regardless, they are creatures that live in the goddess Lenaya’s boundless gifts”
Avrin rolled his eyes slightly while Ayame made a sigh of relief and regret. It seemed she wanted to fight and relieve frustration but was also glad she didn't have to meet an ugly orc.
As the 3 continued on, Avrin used his augmented eye to navigate away from the orcs. At that moment, a child like scream roared out. With a heroic intuition Syrana rushed in the direction to go see if a child was in danger. Ayame had also followed after her.
Avrin only sighed before his augmented eye widened slightly in the direction they went off in. He could see a group of 3 humanoids with weapons that seemed to be large and somewhat muscular, and a small child like creature. But what he saw wasn’t the 3 of those humanoids attacking the child. It was the 3 of them trying to defend it from a large creature.
Avrin spoke softly as he looked at the creature. “That looks nearly identical to a…”

chapters.title: V2: Chapter 45 Long Awaited Encounter.
chapters.content:
Full Pr Credits to Draconis who made this release possible.  here is a special release for all of you as it seems you cant get enough some more words of encouragement i dont think there is a cliffhanger in this one? XD enjoy ch 45
Please dont forget to Rate/Follow/Favourite -----------------
Avrin spoke softly as he looked at the creature. “That looks nearly identical to a damn bear.” Avrin sped up to go catch up with Syrana and Ayame with a sigh of frustration as they were meant to keep to themselves. He cared not for the trivial matters of orcs or if there petty offspring perished. It seemed he almost instantly got used to considering orcs as pests.
Avrin made his way into the clearing just in time to see Syrana jump towards the orc child that seemed somewhat bulky. She had perfect timing, as a moment sooner and the creature would have had the child in its grasp for a snack.
The child made weird high pitched grunting sounds that would be considered funny to Avrin had it not been for the situation. Ayame didn't hesitate to counter the bear creature as she jumped up and kicked towards its large bulky forearm.
Ayame’s strength was indeed formidable as a large ‘Bang!’ like sound echoed slightly the moment her kick landed, sending the bear creature back several steps. It even seemed shocked at the sudden turn of events.
Avrin stood his ground as there was no need to get his hands dirty. In fact, he was more interested in the creature rather than rescuing the child. The creature, although resembling a bear, had  a larger mouth span and sabre like teeth sticking out of the sides of its jaws.
Almost like an alligator. It had a dark green fur color but also had a sort of mane that ran around its back and downwards. Its size was easily nearly 2 and a half stories tall.
For the average warrior this may seem like a deadly opponent, but he knew Ayame herself could match it equally if not better. But he also knew the creatures attack was no pushover. One hit would definitely give Ayame a run for her money.
Ayame and the creature battled. The creature giving her a barrage of claw slashes knowing its prey had escaped for now and seeking vengeance on Ayame who attacked it. Ayame countered by slashing at its thick fur with her kunai that seemed to give it a somewhat nice cut, but nothing deep.
It was surprising, it shouldn’t have cut at all, as Avrin had noticed on the way here, using his augmented eye, that the spears of the orcs trying to save the child couldn't penetrate its thick coat of fur.
Syrana moved the child to the orcs who seemed somewhat skeptical of her intentions but did not hesitate further to look after one of their young. Most stories depict orcs as ruthless savages who care only for their own well being, but it seemed like the variants here seemed to show otherwise.
Syrana turned and spoke to Ayame in a loud voice. “Ayame, stand aside..” Ayame blinked for a moment as she was enjoying the battle but frowned and then did as her teacher asked, stepping aside. All while Syrana had unsheathed Eclipse and pointed it towards the bear.
Syrana then fired an elemental arrow with little power as she did not intend to kill the creature, only show that she was superior. The arrow wielding physical properties as well as the force of the air skimmed faintly across the swamp, emitting a faint screech before plowing into the bears gut, knocking it back several meters as the bear creature rolled around letting a roar of agony as The ground shook with its anger and pain.
But this creature seemed to be smart and knew Syrana was more powerful of a predator and decided to retreat for today, as it left somewhat limping and battered, its tall figure vanishing into the shadows of the swamplands until not even its thunderous footsteps could be heard.
Syrana sighed slightly and Eclipse began to reform back into mana in the form of the sigil before going back into her right hand. Ayame, with a confident smile, approached her. “Teacher, you truly are something to be able to take such a creature out without even trying.” This compliment made Syrana smile as she felt satisfied with her student’s words.
Syrana then blinked as she spotted Avrin walk over to a spot where some of the creatures blood from Ayame’s attack was. Avrin leaned down and gazed at the blood which had a sort of blue pigment with his augmented eye, picking up traces of something he hadn't expected to see.
“Well this is worrying…” He rubbed his head and focused his hand over the small blood stain as the particles of what he had noticed with his eye sprung up. They were none other than dark matter particles. Forming only half a centimeter in diameter in total from a blood stain of 8 inches but still considered nothing for the creature that had lost it.
“Hmm” The blood stain had lost its blue pigment and turned red as if influenced by the dark matter, but Avrin soon absorbed the dark matter into himself as if it were nothing. As he thought to himself “-It’s most likely in these lands. I didn't expect I would be so close to it-” Avrin seemed cautious as he looked around, but maybe he was just over thinking things. But he couldn't deny the fact that there was dark matter in that creatures blood.
Syrana, who approached Avrin curiously, spoke “Why do you look like you're about to be ambushed?” Avrin stood up and gazed at her. “None of your concern. Now if you're done playing hero we have lost time to make up” He spoke firmly, clearly wanting to leave this area.
Syrana glared and huffed at him. “Why should I? While you were looking at that blood stain the orcs are welcoming us to stay with them for helping rescue one of their children.” Avrin clicked his tongue quietly. He then pondered the fact that maybe he shouldn't avoid it and just hope it comes to him, that way he can settle things.
“Do as you wish…..” Avrin spoke calmly as he walked off in the direction of where the bear creature had come from. This made Syrana speak quickly “Where are you going!?” Avrin replied, annoyed at her nosiness “Why Mother, I am going to go scout ahead. Is that wrong?” He clearly had something bothering him as just yesterday he seemed friendlier.
This change irritated Syrana who ignored him and went off towards the orcs, before getting out of earshot, she spoke “We will be back here by tomorrow. I know you're more than capable of handling yourself here, but try not to kill anything...Life here has a circle it follows”(PR Note: IT’S THE CIRCLE OF LIFEEEEEEEEEEEE)
Avrin didn’t reply as he vanished in the same dark shadows the swamplands depicted. He had been following the mana trace the bear had left, he clearly wanted to know how dark matter got into it.
----Syrana/Ayame’s Side---
As they both went with the orcs, they were led to a somewhat decent sized settlement that seemed to be made from the trees of the swamp as well as materials of creatures.
For protection, there was a wall surrounding most of the settlement, and it was layered with wood and shells as well as several spike like traps for the larger creatures that felt as if they were interested in attacking the settlement.
“T..Teacher, it smells funny” Ayame desperately wanted to hold her nose but Syrana told her otherwise. “Don’t be rude. This is mostly the swamp, there is little place for their fecal matter to go” But those words seemed to make it worse for Ayame who seemed to be ready to vomit.
Syrana ignored it though as she was led by the 3 orcs as well as the child female orc who seemed somewhat chubby wearing makeshift leather clothing that was somewhat ragged.
If Avrin were to be here to describe it, he would easily say it was the most detestable sight he had seen for a long time. Ayame and Syrana had both entered a large hut in the back of the settlement that was against a sort of hill that seemed to also act as protection.
They did well to ignore the gazed of the curious orcs that thought them food or prisoners. One of the orcs began to speak in its language to another that was dressed in what seemed to be a shamans outfit with several furs adoring its body as well as a skeletal remnants of a skull of some poor creature.
This orc also had a wooden cane that seemed to be crudely carved, but one could tell by the smell of the herbs and mystical feeling of the hut that this was indeed an orc Magi. Every tribe of orc had a Magi. They were the leaders, being the most knowledgeable and powerful they lead their people to live and not perish.
The orc began to speak to Syrana in broken Human dialect. “Elf saved youngling...This orc thanks you…” Syrana smiled softly and replied “I cannot let a child that hasn't lived its life perish from this world.” The orc, which seemed to be a sort of female that was aged, spoke “Thank you again Elf...Your people always...treat us normal...never bad…”
Syrana nodded and replied “We Sylph in general believe in equality of all the races. But I’m curious, that arktos subspecies should have plenty of food near where its lair is. Surely your people have not attacked it with provocation?”
You could be reading stolen content. Head to for the genuine story.
The Magi shook her head quickly and stamped her cane down as she growled randomly “The creature lurks closer near our lands...And it comes with many.. others...They are hungry...Something scared them….makes them move away...As if there home isn’t their home… Might Lang save us…” The Magi sighed as she went back to her seat covered in pelts and sat down.
Syrana began to think carefully to herself as she wondered what in this swamp could possibly scare a creature that could be considered one of the apex predators. Even among others, it isn't scared of them.
She then blinked as she remembered the way Avrin acted, as if he knew something was wrong. She gritted her teeth. “He was hiding something..urgh… It’s too late, I'll just have to wait for tomorrow..”
The Magi smiled “Elf...you stay here with us. You and your friend...You help us, you are our guest now...Stay as long as you like…” Syrana smiled at her and bowed. “I’m truly grateful for your hospitality. We will only remain for a night as we have a place to be.”
As the arrangements were made, they began to settle down in a makeshift hut that could be considered VIP treatment even though it looked like a rundown shack.
-----------Avrin’s Side------------
He had been walking for a good 30 minutes and saw the bear creature had found a meal. It had managed to catch and kill a sort of horse like creature that also resembled a buffalo. It’s colours seemingly blending into the swamp.
Avrin did well to hide himself at a fair distance and stay in the branches of large trees, as he didn't want to alarm the creature. He wanted to observe it a bit longer, just to satisfy his curiosity and put his worries at ease.
As the creature was eating, a rumbling sound echoed. A large gorilla like creature with one eye that resembled a cyclops that was bulked up had smelt the carcass and was drooling. Starving and mad.
The bear, seeing another apex predator, both roughly the same size, began to roar and growl towards it, as if telling it that this was its food and for it to piss off. The gorilla like cyclops which was covered in thick white and blue fur with his front side covered in what seemed like scales, only roared in reply. As if telling the bear to take a hike.
As the bear stopped eating, the two creatures circled each other. But Avrin cared not for their fight as it was petty. He turned around, intending to leave, when a large ghostly like roar echoed  around the area. It was menacing and filled with bloodlust and madness.
This would have not bothered Avrin as he would consider it another predator, but what caught his eye was how the bear and the gorilla creature both froze as if petrified. They began to back off quietly, as if trying to not make sound and draw attention before they both got far enough from the corpse, that even the bear left behind. Both creatures started running until they vanished.
Avrin stayed quiet before he heard rustling sounds in the direction of where the roar had appeared from. A black glowing blur shot out from the bushes near the swamp to the corpse of the dead creature and began feeding on it as if not caring if it was for anything else.
Avrin’s eyes widened with a nervous excitement and curiosity, his left augmented eye could clearly see something not of this world. It had been something he knew he had seen before and had met before. He chuckled softly as he regained his composure and jumped out of the tree line into the open around 30 meters from the creature.
He then called out to it as it was eating, ignoring him as if thinking he was a nobody. That was until his voice called out. “It’s been quite a long time since we last met creature. I didn’t expect that such a change would occur with just an arm replacement..”
The creature stopped. It had been through pride then anger and met fear, only to be tortured and be freed to be rejected and then nearly killed. The creature moved its mouth from the carcass as the blood of the dead animal lingered around its mouth as well as the shadowy like mane that glowed with static somewhat.
It had been years since they last met. It’s body was different compared to before. It was larger but also thicker and looked more muscular. It’s mane was longer and was as if it reflected the night sky, with black static pulsing through it.
It’s eyes being a pure glowing purple with red crimson pupils. It’s tail swayed back and forth, seemingly as if it had the strength to tear a man in half. It gazed at Avrin quietly. It seemed almost awkward.
Avrin cleared his throat and spoke “What’s wrong? Don’t you recognize your master, creatu-...” Before he could finish the creature that he had tortured for the sake of an experiment lunged at him with lightning speed, with ferocity, and with revenge. This creature was none other than the Nemean/Leophat Avrin had captured and thought dead.
Avrin blinked as the creature was indeed incredibly fast. But compared to his current state, it was only 20% faster than Ayame using her speed ability.
Avrin jumped up as the Leophats claw crushed towards where he had formerly been. Avrin grinned as he kicked downwards, stomping the creature into the ground, causing a small crater that shattered with the force.
“I’ll have you know I myself have gotten stronger. You have grown an attitude, hopefully this shows you who’s boss again…” Avrin spoke somewhat smugly before blinking with surprise.
The Leophat didn’t look harmed at all. In fact, Avrin felt a tough resistance from its fur that was definitely mutated due to dark matter. The Leophat grabbed Avrin, taking advantage of his surprise, and swung him around. Throwing him towards a nearby boulder.
Avrin, regaining his composure at the right moment, managed to regain his balance eventually. Gracefully kicking softly at the boulder and landing on the ground. “Your durability is stronger. I can’t take you lightly...But this is good..I get to experiment again on you. But this time I’ll be using a technique I’ve been itching to try..”
Avrin indeed had intended to try techniques taught in the manual, although he currently had no intention of killing this creature as it had too much importance to kill so easily.
The Leophat roared with pride as it felt it was stronger than Avrin, as it lunged quicker than before. Almost 15% faster. Which made Avrin smile widely with surprise, but not enough to shock him further. Avrin emitted his dark matter into his legs, using a part of the Pulsing Dragons meditative focus to help the effort.
He kicked his right foot in a crescent shape with a significant force at an angle the manual had spoken of. The force of the semicircle, resembling a crescent, forced the ground to cut open slightly before causing a slight vacuum of air to explode out. Blowing the leophat away slightly, disturbing its attack.
Avrin then frowned. “It seems all I can do is kick hard and quick enough that the air is blown away. I think it is acceptable though for my first try.” Avrin gazed at the Leophat which seemed to stop dead in its tracks, but held no fear in its eyes. This creature seemingly experienced a lot. It only stopped because it was cautious, and not fearful. It still intended to fight Avrin and Avrin knew this.
Avrin gazed quietly at the creature before reaching up and removing his cloak as he fixed his gauntlets slightly “Very well, I’ll humor you...I’ll show you the difference between us..I’ll only use my current physical strength to overpower you and show you that the gap has not shortened between us, but only grown. And once that happens, I look forward to keeping you as a pet” Avrin smirked as he fixed his gauntlet.
But those words, the Leophat understood, as the mutation not only made it more powerful, but also smarter. It knew Avrin was mocking it even if it didn’t know what he was saying. It roared and vanished in a flash as it appeared behind him, the dust kicking from where it left to the trail of where it arrived behind Avrin. Both it’s arms and claws slashing downwards towards Avrin.
Avrin, who still fixing his gauntlet, had his face hidden in a menacing shadow as the top half of his face was dark, other than his pupils. He ducked as he had seen the Nemean move at that speed, but Avrin was faster. He had spent years training and he would not be showed up by this creature he empowered.
But as he ducked, he used one of his own counter techniques. His left foot curving upwards like a bullet, smashing into the jaw of the Leophat. The force of the blow seemed to cause a slight quake near them as the Leophat was shot several meters in the air and knocked back.
Avrin slowly regained his stance. Lowering his leg and raising his body up in a proper position. “Although you have gotten stronger, you remind me of how I used to be when I got my power… Unrestrained and thinking that you can take the whole world”

chapters.title: V2: Chapter 46 Agreement.
chapters.content:
Full credits to Draconis for pring so i wasnt going to release a ch today until the artwork was done but i was convinced in rrs chat by some readers and i felt bad. *sighs* even when i dont try to make a cliffhanger it seems its in my writing style well no point fighting it il just write how i always do. :)
Please Rate/Favourite/Follow/Enjoy ch 46 :) 2 more chs till end of volume 2 ---------------
“But just like me you’re going to have to learn the hard way” Avrin spoke in a normal tone towards the creature. The creature growled towards Avrin as it stumbled slightly, a sort of crack visible under its chin. As if it were a shell.
Avrin, who prepared himself in a defensive stance, extended his left hand forward and his right hand back as well as his left foot forward and right foot back. Making sure his feet were firmly planted on the ground.
The Nemean rushed towards him again, unleashing a barrage of ferocious slashes that seemed to send dark energy waves every time it slashed. This made dodging a hassle for Avrin. If he were to get hit by one it would definitely hurt, especially since he wasn't utilising any dark matter abilities.
But he used this as practice. He had not gotten to spar with anyone other than Shimaru during the duration of his training and this made things easier. Shimaru was significantly faster than the Leophat.
But Avrin didn't let up. First the creature unleashed a right slash with each claw emitting a dark matter wave capable of skinning the ground itself to a degree and plowing into a tree. Then came a tail swipe which sent another dark matter wave which Avrin had to jump to avoid.
“You're just a bundle of ferocity… Quite scary..” Avrin, who kept his composure in the fight, has the mindset determined to how well he could focus and continue to avoid. As the creature slashed upwards with its left hand, while avrin was still in the air, 5 more dark matter waves pulsed towards him.
“Urk..Not good.” Avrin covered himself in an arm cross guard as 2 of the waves hit him, causing a slight explosion which resulted in a minor vacuum of air. 
Avrin fell to the ground but regained his balance with one hand planted on the ground. His arm guards and gauntlets were torn up. His arm itself seemed slightly burned as steam emitted from it. The creature roared towards him as if telling him it was capable of defeating him.
Avrin seemed irritated. He hadn’t made any moves  to attack yet because he wanted to see how well he could focus on a strong opponent as well as see the creature’s potential. The Leophat seeing Avrin was seemingly barely scratched rushed towards him at high speed, appearing above him with it’s fists balled up as it smashed down towards his body.
Avrin, seeing this, didn’t hesitate to quickly back flip away in the air. Narrowly missing the attack of the creature. As the Leophat’s hands collided with the surface of the ground, the ground itself shook violently and rubble shot up as a 5x5 meter diameter, messy crater was formed.
Avrin landed back on his feet as he judged that the creature indeed had strength capable of hurting him. But he still wasn’t going seriously. Otherwise he was certain he would defeat it.
“You got quite a strength improvement” Avrin let a smile escape his lips as he spoke again while gazing at the creature standing in the rubble that came back down like rain. “I’ve decided I’m going to keep you. You’re going to come in handy as an ally”
The creature roared again, seemingly not out of breathe. Its crack like wound on its chin had also seemingly healed which impressed Avrin. The creature rushed towards Avrin on all fours, emitting a trail of dark energy that seemed to give a ghostly sound.
“Play times over…” Avrin spoke firmly as he held his right hand out and extended his fingers to their maximum length and also gave space between them as if like claws.
As the Leophat got within a meter, it felt a shiver run down its spine as it looked at Avrin who seemed to be emitting a powerful killing intent. Before the creature could dodge, it was too late. Avrin had dashed forward and plowed his palm as well as finger tips into the abdomen of the Leophat.
The force transferred through its body. As if time had stood still, a burst of air emitting from its back, shooting a couple of meters before going silent. The Leophat was sent shooting like a star towards the tree line, hitting against tree trunk after tree trunk until it had toppled 3 before collapsing onto the ground.
Avrin made his way to it, opening and closing his right hand “Thank you for that. I’ve been meaning to test the Dragon Claw ability as well. Hehe “ Avrin gave a soft laugh before stopping, looking at the Leophat that was struggling to get up. Avrin could see its chest had the same shattered look as the chin but it had broken to pieces revealing black fur underneath.
“Hmm... I see. So that’s an augmented form of yours. That explains a lot” Avrin moved towards the creature and extended his right hand again. It was time for another experiment. He began to will the dark matter of the creature to come to him only enough to weaken it. And it was done. As if like ash, the augmented shelling of the leophat began to come off the creature, letting a wail of dissatisfaction, trying to get away. But Avrin, having full control over dark matter, was just too superior for it.
It had no chance of escaping. Especially from this range. After 15 seconds it had lost 90% of the augmented shelling and was now panting on the ground. The creature had a dark purple main with black fur surrounding its body. It looked less humanoid and more like a lion from earth to a degree. It was indeed less scary than its augmented form.
Its fur was also thicker than the usual version of a Leophat. It also had a large scar like wound on its chest where its heart was located.
“Indeed it is you. It seems you’ve mutated quite significantly. Well done” Avrin spoke in praise for the creature to have survived and become like this. Although Avrin was still cautious as the creature was still panting for air. Avrin got a stick and started to poke it, as if playing with it. “If your resting, I’m trying something now. It might work it might not”
Avrin, while smiling, approached the creature and placed his hand on its head after confirming it was exhausted and injured. “Good news. Is if this works it’s going to make things a lot easier. Bad news. It may hurt like hell for both you and me” Avrin, smiling, began to emit his dark matter.
What he was doing was transferring knowledge to the creature. It was incredibly hard for him, considering it felt like his brain was going to explode. He also knew the creature was struggling to move around, but Avrin clenched his hand over its head, forcing it into the ground as it began to dig in slightly. “S..Stop moving damnit” He gave a frustrated look.
Avrin was only intending to transfer languages. This alone made him feel like vomiting, which is why his left hand was absorbing mana from the surroundings. After a minute of resisting, the creature seemed to have fallen unconscious. Avrin, who was sweating slightly as well as panting from the pain and exhaustion, felt a sort of deja vu.
After 20 minutes, Avrin had fallen on his butt. His face pale but behind his skin it was as if there was static under it. He gave a tired expression as if he hadn’t slept for weeks, and his mind was unfocused. “Tr..Transferring knowledge….Nev...Never again…” He had vowed to himself he would not put himself through that misery and hassle unless in return he got something of value that he would accept.
“Hey...You awake?...Can you understand me?” The Leophat murmured, as it was as exhausted as Avrin, and slowly opened its eyes. Its chin resting on the ground as its mouth opened and began to speak. “Aru….Ehru…”
Avrin gave a bewildered look. This creature’s tone was different, but it seemed to have trouble speaking. “Put some effort into it. Say Avrin. Go on” The creature, seemingly having no choice, spoke “Ari...Arun….Aerun…..Avan...Avrun...Avrin...Avrin”
The creature blinked in surprise. It actually managed to speak. Not only that, it seemed to have knowledge popping up in its head slowly but surely. It understood this knowledge was words, language, letters, and so on.
It forced itself onto all fours and spoke “Spaeek...Am..spaek…..Spek...Speak….Am speak...I speak...I am speak...I am speaking….” The creature roared loudly, seemingly forgetting that it just had a battle with someone who put it through misery.
Avrin had been absorbing the mana around the area and the color in his face was returning and his fatigue fading. “Very good.“ He smiled to himself. “What else can you say?“ Avrin spoke as if trying to get the creature more excited. This way he could use it against it.
Stolen story; please report.
“I am.. Uhhh... I am a Leophat.“ It continued on proudly. “I am strong. I am a warrior. I am a hunter.” Avrin was also excited. Not only for the creatures, sake but for the reason that he seemed to have succeeded. Unfortunately, he felt that if he was to transfer anything advanced it would possibly kill it or Avrin, as his mind was something he needed to train more. As well as it depending on the mind of the person. Avrin spoke “Yes, you are a Leophat. And what do Leophats eat?”
The creature spoke as if like a child “Meat. Leophats eat meat. We love meat” Avrin grinned and spoke “Very good. And what is your name?” The creature stopped and gazed at Avrin, as it realised he was there. As it had time to think regarding his question, and then knew it was him “You. Turn me into a monster. Get me rejected by my tribe. Get me almost killed. I want revenge”
Avrin shook his head and sighed. “You dumb creature. Are you intending to fight me when you have already lost? Can you not tell I was holding back?”  The Leophat roared slightly as it echoed around “I am hunter. With this power you forced on me, I have no fear”
Avrin knew the creature was right. He wondered if that transfer had also somewhat suppressed its emotion of fear. It was truly a useful tool. Although he could kill it or beat it to death, which he would enjoy, he decided to try and reason with it as it was the best way to build a relationship.
As Avrin sat cross legged, he spoke to it. “You are telling me I have wronged to you? Your tribe got rid of you because your arm was different. What good is a tribe that doesn’t look after its members?”
The creature was silent for a bit, but since it had gotten more intelligent it tried to argue. “My tribe….follow laws...no choice...but to run. Your fault… I was normal”
Avrin chuckled softly and rubbed the back of his head. He would then try a better argument as the creature was indeed right. “What I just gave you is unimaginable power. You are 5 if not 10 times stronger than you were before. Your wounds heal quickly and you can learn to eat mana so you never starve. You will live for hundreds if not thousands of years and your power will only grow.
And I am 100% certain that one day, given time and effort, if you follow me as my pet I will help you become equal if not stronger then a dragon. If not the gods themselves”
Avrin spoke as if to coerce it. The creature was quiet as it grunted and growled. “You lie..Yyou torture me and injure me….Why I believe you?” It spoke in a sort of deep broken english. Little did either know the language they were speaking was indeed proper english. Anyone who came across them wouldn’t understand a word they were saying.
Avrin clicked his tongue quietly and shrugged. “You tried to kill me, I was trying to defend myself. Isn’t there a law in the forest? The strongest survive. Didn’t I do what I must to survive? And in the end, I didn’t kill you. Right?”
The creature roared with anger “You still injure and torture me. My tribe almost killed me...And pointy ears take me away…” Avrin chuckled and raised his finger as if lecturing. “Who do you think killed your tribe for you to help you. Not only that. The pointy ears also took me away too. They almost killed me. So we are even.”
The creature had no way to believe him so it stayed quiet for a bit and Avrin spoke again. “Haven’t you had fun so far, living in these lands with your new power? I bet it feels good beating up creatures that would usually kill you with a stroke of there hand.”
The Leophat indeed acknowledged this. Usually it would take 10 or 15 of them to take down the bear creature or the gorilla creature. It was indeed seduced by the power. But it continued to stay quiet. Avrin smiled and stood up as he stretched.
“If you stick with me and become my pet, I’ll make you stronger. And one day, there won’t be an animal on this world or a living soul that won’t fear you. Even the dragons will become a meal for you. All I ask is that you be my pet”
The Leophat growled. “I am hunter.. I am no pet...I get stronger by myself..” At this moment, Avrin offered again “Very well hunter. Become my servant. Then you are not a pet but you still obey my commands. Do you think people who see you will let you go for long? They will be worse than me. They will cut you up and do worse experiments and you won’t live. at least with me you will be safer.”
The Leophat, having new found knowledge, knew that this statement was true. It felt this power was different and its body felt strange. At one stage after it healed, it began vomiting a sort of transparent substance that was blue, and from that day onward its body felt as if it wasn’t connected to mana anymore, but something else.
“You speak true...But why I need follow you. Why I need listen you. Why not be ally” Avrin huffed. At least progress was made. He went over to the creature and gave it a pat on the back. “Remember this carefully. This power to begin with was mine alone. Consider yourself lucky I even allowed you to live. Now what is stopping me from killing you and making a deal with another creature? Merely the time and effort..”
This was 50% true and it made the Leophat cringe slightly. At this point, its body had released the fear emotion as the threat was indeed enough for it to surface. The Leophat, feeling fear for the first time in years, didn’t know how to react other than nod in agreement. The other 50% that Avrin hadn’t told it, was because he felt an attachment towards the creature. It had been the first one he tried many experiments on and it and he almost died on the same night.
“Ok… I listen.. I servant of Avrin. And Avrin teach me eat mana and grow stronger to eat dragon” The creature began to drool as it imagined what sort of taste dragon meat would give. This made Avrin back away as he felt it a little weird, but funny. He cleared his throat and spoke.
“Very well. Considering your new form, you are no longer a Leophat.” This made the creature almost teary as it growled with annoyance. “What am I if not Leophat?...” Avrin began to think and then grinned. “Your race is a variant of Spectral. Therefore your race will be Nemean. A Spectral Nemean. Yes I like that” Avrin began to rub his chin with satisfaction.
“Spectral Nemean. Haehe.” The newly named Nemean seemed to also like the name, as it had a sort of tough, strong feeling to it, and it was also unique. One of a kind, until it had kin. Avrin then called out “That’s not all. I need a name for you. I’m not just going to call you Nemean from now on. Do you have any?”
The creature, now slowly becoming accustomed to Avrin, was now healing slowly. Avrin as well, was still absorbing the mana. The area was starting to become infused with dark matter and giving a ghostly feeling. As if the space was twisting. But to Avrin and the Nemean, this was like home.
“Name...I need..name..Why I need name?” It asked curiously and Avrin spoke. “Dragons have names because they’re all different and very powerful. Later on, if there are many of your kind, how will I tell the difference and tell you apart? If you are one day to match dragons, you also need a name.”
Knowing that this made a lot of sense, the creature was satisfied with his answer and nodded before speaking “Master, I don’t know names...Please give me name. Please give. I want to be powerful like dragon.” It spoke, almost as if begging, to which Avrin nodded and took advantage of.
“Very well. A name for you. The first of your kind as well as a being of immense power. Your name will be Asura, because just like them, you seek power and you compete. In this case compete with dragons. You are the first Spectral Nemean, Asura” Avrin spoke as he had stopped absorbing mana and had folded his arms with satisfaction.
“Azara..Azura….Asura. I am Asura. Haha, Asura Asura Asura. I am ASURA!” Asura also roared with satisfaction. Avrin seemed to have convinced him that it was indeed a worthy name. As the creature began to calm down, it went over to Avrin and embraced him in a tight hug. Avrin blinked as he coughed a bit. This creature still had significant strength and it was overly excited. “S..Stop Asura. Besides, there is a problem…”
Asura blinked and let Avrin go as it spoke in a growl “Who cause problem?! I will fight and defeat problem!!” Avrin laughed softly. Asura was indeed dumb, but also entertaining. He then began to think. Rubbing his chin again.
“The problem is. I wonder how I’m going to explain this to Syrana…”

chapters.title: V2: Chapter 47 Feelings Of Advancement.
chapters.content:
Here is ch 47 of spectral regalia :) i know some of you have pmed me regarding the artwork begging for pieces of info. but before that Id like to thankDraconis who pred this ch and made this possible please take the time to give him some rep for his efforts :)  as for the artwork il add it at the end as treatment for the cliffhanger :)
Please Rate/Follow/Favourite/Enjoy reading ch 47 :) ----------------
Avrin gazed at Asura as he kept thinking. Asura was in a sort of hunched position as a lion would be but it looked somewhat weird considering his body shape was that of a hulking humanoid. Avrin then spoke “Asura, for now you are to remain here. Do not bother attacking the creatures that are dominant here as well as the orcs.
If you need to eat then kill and eat. Do not do it for fun. I am tending to something and I think it better if you do not appear for now”
Asura gave a soft growl as he spoke “But I like hunting and fighting… Why must I remain quiet..This is my territory now.” Avrin frowned “Do not delude yourself creature. When I return, me and you will be leaving this demented swamp. I also refuse to allow a Spectral creature to live in such conditions.”
Asura was somewhat confused. He felt Avrin was denying him lands but also felt Avrin had something bigger in store for him so he nodded. “Ok master..I will go to my lair and rest..How will I find you again?”
Avrin began to think to himself. “Good question. We will meet in this area in 2 days. Just emit your energy and I will surely discover you. We are attuned to each other now”
Asura frowned slightly as he began to walk off. The swamp had gotten quiet. The birds that were chirping as well as the other creatures and insects turned and looked “Master, why must I go now? You promised me. I hope you keep your word”
Avrin chuckled softly “Don’t feel rushed. It isnt the time yet and there are people who would be afraid of you. Like the orcs”
Asura began to think as he nodded and walked off while talking to himself “Orcs... Oh yeah, they tasted funny“ His voice began to drift as he continued to talk to himself before his figure vanished into the tree line.
Avrin continued to gaze in that direction before dissipating his augmented eye “That creature is going to give me a lot of problems in the future. I can feel it…Nothing heavy discipline won't fix.
Besides I should get ba-” Before he finished he felt the presence of a figure behind him. He turned to see it make its way out. “Hmph...There you are..” The feminine voice spoke out. It was none other than Syrana.
Avrin began to walk past her. “If I remember correctly, I could have sworn I said I would return tomorrow. Were you hoping to catch another glimpse of me bathing? Sorry to say but I wouldn't bathe in these waters even if they were the last liquid on Seleria.“ He joked but this made Syrana turn red with embarrassment and clench her hands.
“I..Idiot. I came to let you know that I discussed things with the orcs. It seemed that the creatures of this area have been unsettled and I came to warn you about it.” Avrin blinked and then gave a sly grin as he stopped and looked at her.
“You were worried about me then...Well don't I feel honored.“ He gave a soft chuckle to which syrana huffed and folded her arms under her breasts, causing them to lift slightly. Any normal man would be drooling by now.
“I was being cautious...Besides, I have better things to do then save you so I took the easier way of warning you.” Avrin turned around and began walking off in the direction they had both come from. Syrana also following. Avrin spoke “No need. I've already handled the matter anyway.”
This made Syrana tilt her head curiously as she spoke “What do you mean? You met the creature responsible?” Avrin nodded before speaking “More or less. What would you say if I just happened to meet the leophat from the forest”
Syrana stopped. Her footsteps were somewhat noticeable before, but Avrin felt them quiet down. He also stopped and turned to look at her. He was surprised at what stance she had taken, Eclipse had already been drawn.
“Give me its direction Avrin… A creature like that shouldn't exist...It's an abomination..” Avrin glared at her. “By saying that you are also stating that I'm also an abomination...That creature now has the only affinity with me. Besides, I've already discussed things with it.”
Syrana continued to glare at him before turning around, making her way to where Avrin was before. Avrin had felt she had finally reached a point in becoming too overly aggressive but Syrana spoke “That may be so, but if left alone, who knows what damage it can do to these lands..It can put the natural balance off” Avrin didn’t intend to fight with her.
He knew she was most likely stronger than him so he decided to try a different approach. As disgusting as it was for him. He approached her and as he got in within range, Syrana turned around, feeling something wasn't right. Avrin slipped his arms around her and embraced her as he held her against his chest tightly. His lips softly brushing against her cheek before her head was cradled against his shoulder.
“Syrana, please realise...That being, the only one of my kind, can be lonely….This creature now has a relation to me...I will take full responsibility, so please for now just back down…” Inside his mind and heart Avrin was throbbing with weirdness and a mix of emotions. He had to allow his body to somewhat release some emotion to make it feel more dramatic.He hadn't felt such emotions in a long time. It had possibly done better than he hoped for.
Syrana was quiet for a moment and as Avrin moved his head back, he saw that she seemed to be gazing at him, her face as red as a cherry as she began to stutter. “I...U...Uh...W...I….W..Wha….I….” Avrin, for the first time, smiled, as he felt she was indeed somewhat cute this time.
He spoke again. “May we please head back. In 2 days when we return...The creature and I will leave these lands and I will tend to it..Ok?” Syrana began to nod quickly before pushing herself back after regaining her composure. She was quiet for a bit longer before sighing and clearing her throat.
“V..Very well...It’s your duty to..look after it...When we return it leaves with us…” Avrin nodded. He was starting to feel that using words was often better than combat.
As the two of them left they returned to the orc village. Avrin had moved his hood back on to cover his appearance and was met by curious orc eyes. His stomach somewhat churned with disgust. “It seems the orcs really have taken a liking to you..” He spoke softly as their gazes indeed showed respect towards her.
“It’s a good thing. Doing positive things with power can lead to this, Avrin” Avrin gave a quiet chuckle “You're starting to sound like Myra convincing me to do good”
Syrana blinked “Oh? She tried convincing you. Hah… All I know is if your powers are used for evil, I, as well as others, will hunt you down Avrin..Remember that I have seen what you're capable of. Regardless of your story, I'm still cautious…”
Avrin felt she was telling the truth. It seems that telling her a part of how he came only seemed to affect their relation to the point of her not being as aggressive. She was still a Sylph with responsibilities who has lived for centuries. She was honed. The only thing she had no experience with was romance, judging by her reactions.
Avrin just wanted to retrieve the sky metal and leave this nasty place. As they approached a home like hut that seemed better than most but still kind of run down, Ayame was outside with some female orc warriors sparing with them. It seemed she was giving them a run for their money.
An orc wielding a sword slashed towards Ayame’s back while Ayame was facing another orc only to have Ayame back flip onto the head of the orc who slashed towards her and then go down kicking the creature in front of where it was facing. It let a sort of pig growl sound.
Another orc closed in from the side with a large spear. Ayame saw this from the corner of her eye and did a quick side step before cutting downwards across the shaft of it with her kunai. Like butter, the wooden spear was cut in half. It seemed Ayame enjoyed showing off, although it didn't seem like she was taking this seriously.
Her movements were done in a somewhat relaxed fashion. These orcs, although warriors for many years, had no concept of martial arts or swordsmanship. They just made weapons and randomly attacked until something died.
“You guys are too sloppy with your movements. You’re just attacking and hoping for the best. You need to keep an eye out and find a weakness. Don't just rush in take advantage of your opponent” Syrana grinned as Avrin and her watched from the side. Ayame, although preaching, was indeed not practicing it as she hadn't noticed the two watching her.
As a smaller chubby female orc wielding a shield charged towards Ayame who seemed ready to counter, Syrana spoke up. “Ayame why are you picking on helpless orcs?..” Ayame blinked turning her head before she felt a large force push her. And moments later she was face first in a nearby pile of mud where pigs were kept. One of these pigs came up to her and started to sniff curiously.
Ayame groaned as she moved her head up as her outfit as well as her face was covered in mud. The orc that shield rushed her was dancing proudly as well as the other orcs cheering at her, the one who felled the tyrant. Ayame growled a bit before gazing at Syrana.
“Teacher! not fair!! You did that on purpose!!” Syrana was laughing while Avrin gazed at Ayame from the side. “Ayame, I never knew you liked mud baths.” He spoke as if to rub it in.
You might be reading a pirated copy. Look for the official release to support the author.
Ayame clenched her fists as she stood up and stomped off to find the bathing area. While cursing at them both under her breath. Avrin then began to make his way towards the building and spoke. “I’m going to go meditate for a bit then rest...Let me know if anything happens or when we are going to leave. Other than that, I don't want to be disturbed…”
He spoke firmly. After giving Asura knowledge, it seemed absorbing mana only helped as a short time solution. It was truly a risky move to pull at his current level. It was not an ability one could do wide spread. He needed to refocus his mind to make sure everything was in order and then rest.
Syrana, gazing at him, had saw his attitude go from embracing to solitary quickly. She wondered if something was wrong with him and what he and that creature discussed. She had no idea he was exhausted mentally.
She brushed it aside as she decided she would go speak to the magi again. She felt it was necessary to state intentions. This may even lead them to supporting them somehow. Ayame went off to bathe and Syrana went to see the magi. Avrin, in the last room, in the makeshift home, which was not very tall but somewhat long, and was leaning against the wall for support.
As he entered a Pulsing Dragon meditative state his mind blocking everything out. But something was different. His aura had been violent and through countless years of meditation it began to slowly concentrate into a sort of stable flame.
An average shinobi would take 20 years of training to reach a stable state where there aura emits like a flickering flame. A genius possibly 10-8 years to reach this state. Shimaru himself had taken 13 years. But Avrin had reached it in 2 years. Something unimaginably impressive.
Shimaru hadn't told him this but he was deeply impressed and saw more value in Avrin. But Shimaru was also a master. He knew giving Avrin a big head would not help his training, so he just observed to see which path he would go down. Giving Avrin the manual was as far as the spur of the moment Shimaru had gone.
In the case of Avrin being a genius, he wanted to see the results and what would happen. He had observed Avrin during the years of his training and knew Avrin seemed to not use any mana. In fact, Shimaru couldn't really feel a mana like aura from Avrin even though energy was visible. He couldn't detect it other then with his eyes. It was strange.
Avrin’s visible energy was a dark color. Almost menacing. Like evil in appearance but it had no feeling whatsoever. It was silent. Almost enigmatic. It scared Shimaru. It was like he was looking into a new sort of abyss.
Avrin’s Pulsing Dragon meditation had reached a turning point. Something had triggered it to evolve and advance. The possibility being his ability used on Asura as well as his intense mental fatigue, his aura had all but nearly vanished. A coating around his body of this energy was all that remained as he began to give a black/purplish glow. But after a few seconds, opinions would change.
A pulse emitted from Avrin’s body as it spread silently in the room in a spherical shape. Engulfing the entire room before stopping. This pulse was not forceful nor destructive, which is why it didn't pass the solid objects. Instead it also coated them in this energy.
In the room, the objects were usually makeshift charms and tools as well as spare equipment and dusty relics, the home being reserved for VIPs was used as a storage since no one had used it for years.
These objects now coated in this matter aura began to float as if gravity no longer applied to them. As if they were no longer bound to the laws of this world. As if this entire room had become Avrin’s personal playground.
Several hours passed as the room was silent with nothing but the glow from Avrin’s Pulsing Dragon and the objects floating motionlessly in the air. Avrin’s mind was starting to recover and he was starting to feel rested. And this continued on for 3 more hours until Avrin had begun to slowly break out of his meditation.
His eyes opening before widening slightly as the objects had lost the coating of dark matter and fell to the ground making large clanging sounds. Avrin tilted his head before standing up. “So I wasn’t imagining it. I knew something was different. I’ve reached the next stage of the Pulsing Dragon... The 3rd level…But it’s strange that I cannot determine it properly.
My path has been different since the second stage, but it seems like my path has proven more effective than previously thought.”
He spoke to himself as if summarizing things. He stood up and stretched as he felt his mind was more at ease. He also felt he didn’t need to rest, but he was somewhat hungry and had an urge to eat. He placed the sack at his waist onto the ground as well as the enchanted sack and began to get rations out and eat.
As he ate he began to ponder some thoughts. He hadn’t had time to think about. After he meets Lang and retrieves the sky metal he planned to take Asura with him. He would go back to Shimaru to finish off his training and from there he wanted to try his luck at an academy for Weaponry.
As far as the White Dragon clan was concerned they focused only on assasin like weapons such as kunais and shurikens as well as other tools. At most they had only one weapon which was sword like and it was a curved blade. Almost like a scimitar, which didn't appeal to Avrin. He was disappointed considering he expected such a clan to have katanas.
But he figured the method for developing tamahagane was not known, which benefited him. He didn’t know how to forge it but he could hopefully one day find out how.
Avrin was indeed mostly interested in the sky metal, something that not even the gods seemed to know how to smelt, and was incredibly rare. Scattered around the world. What would Avrin do with it. What would it be like? Judging from Syrana and Myra’s secret conversation, he would also have to keep his guard up, as that metal seemed to have a will of its own.
It only meant forging something from it would only make it more powerful as well as valuable. He wanted to know the sky metal origins, and as much as he could about it this way. It may help him understand how to control it better as well as find more. It would prove useful to him. Defensively as well as offensively, to forge equipment from it.
Avrin continued pondering these things as well as his future down the line as well as bringing up information he had from the books he absorbed as if to confirm that the knowledge was still around. He had no idea if it was temporary, for a duration of years, or was permanent. It didn’t hurt to double check or even triple check.
While having time for himself, things outside seemed to become a bit more loud. As if festivities were going on. It was also close to midnight. He figured the only one of the 3 other than him up at this time would be Syrana as Ayame always liked to sleep before midnight unless training for something.
But that would prove wrong tonight. He heard a knock on the door and a sweet nervous voice but also a familiar one. “Avrin..May I please borrow a bit of your time?” It was none other than Ayame. And for some reason she seemed awfully kinder today.
He was even quiet for a moment, wondering if it was some imposter, but he figured she had reasons. He spoke. “Come in..” The crude door handle as well as the door that seemed to barely fit its frame began to open….
