----Ayames P.O.V---
She was relaxing in a round tub that seemed to be forged quite lazily as there were several dents as well as cracks in the metal interior, as well as the exterior, of the large single plate that was used as a makeshift bath.
Of course the only positive thing was the fact that privacy was given. The orcs were indeed dumb to a degree but the female ones also enjoyed their privacy.
The large bath tub, spanning 5 meters in diameter with a 2 meter length, was rested on a makeshift foundation of rock that seemed to be mixed with some sort of material to harden it like cement. Although it had a disgusting dark green color that made it unappealing.
The bath was more like a mini hot spring considering the area even had its own ceiling and the steam had all but gotten rid of sight for a couple of feet. Ayame was leaning against the uncomfortable metal edge with one of the face towels she had packed with her against her forehead.
She was grumbling to herself as she had all but been cleaned from the mud she was knocked in.
A sigh escaped her lips as she gazed blankly. Something indeed was on her mind. She began to recall her past up until events.
--Ayame Age 6---
A young boy was knocked onto the makeshift tatami mat as he was knocked out. With several individuals sitting crosslegged on the side lines as well as adults giving an awe like expression.
In front of the boy who had just been defeated was a young Ayame with a grin on her face. Her fist extended in front of her, balled up. She spoke “That’s what you get for underestimating me..Just because I’m a girl it doesn’t mean I can’t beat you!”
As she approached the boy to wail on him some more a voice wrung out. “Ayame, enough…” It was none other than her father Calias. Ayame gave a sort of pouty look while clenching her hands.
She turned and bowed to her father before heading off. She had been underestimated by the other students even though she was the clan leaders daughter. They had never seen her as an equal.
She was the only female kunoichi that had shown promise. the other female ones were treated worse and she had often tried to stick up for them.
She grumbled as she walked off to the forest just outside the estate and leaned against a tree as she curled up against her knee. “Why can’t they treat me like they treat each other…”
-------Ayame age 11--------
Practicing in the dojo with her fellow students as they were being taught the basics of the Pulsing Dragon meditation. Ayame was training with 12-14 year olds. The clan was indeed large as there were 16 students in this group alone. This was only one estate which was the main.
There were a couple other branch estates meant to house the excess students and families. Then again, the White Dragon clan, at one stage, had thousands of members. But everything changed when the demons attacked.
Ayame was in the front listening to her grandfather Shimaru, who was explaining the Pulsing Dragon meditation. “The Pulsing Dragon is something our clan alone has discovered capable of sharpening your senses as well as molding your mana to allow your body its full capabilities.”
As he went on to talk, adding that it would be disastrous if one didn’t train after using the meditation or even did it past their limits. There were several students behind Ayame who began to speak.
“Ayame thinks she’s so tough just because she’s the clan heads daughter…” One student whispered to another who then replied “Pfft girls shouldn’t be shinobi. They have no sense of honor and should just use their bodies for us true warriors..”
Shimaru, being an incredibly skilled master, picked this up. But Ayame, being closer as well as somewhat trained, also heard it. She got up in a fit of rage and stomped over towards both of those boys.
“You think my body is something you guys deserve!!! Here is a piece!!!“ Her fist, lacking technique, had plowed into the chest of one of the boys who was sitting cross legged.
He was not as skilled as Ayame and was caught by surprise and worry. He was sent skidding back several feet as his body twitched a bit. He was indeed in pain even though he was unconscious.
Ayame turned to the other boy in her rage and punched towards him this time, using technique. If it had hit directly it would indeed cause serious injury.
But at that moment Shimaru had appeared using his incredible speed and softly caught her small fist he spoke firmly “Ayame...The White Dragon does not allow internal fighting between members unless it is to spar. What you have done has broken several rules… You are suspended from this lesson until I allow you back. Go back to the main building and train in its dojo until you reflect on what you have done..”
Shimaru had to show no favor even to his own granddaughter whom he loved like his own daughter. As tears welled up in Ayame’s eyes she tried to show no fear in front of the others and then ran out thinking even her grandfather was against her.
But she didn’t realise Shimaru had also punished the two. He had given them a stricter punishment, having them train but also assist in the manual labor the female maids would have done as if to show them equality. Not only that but when their parents found out they were punished further.
------Ayame age 14--------
She smiled happily as she had found someone to consider her master at age 12. This was none other than Syrana who had visited several years ago on good will. In Ayame’s eyes Syrana had a powerful and tough aura about her that made her feel like this is the women she wanted to be like.
Syrana was currently showing Ayame some of her own survival and combat techniques. Shimaru had not minded. In fact he found it positive for her to look up to Syrana as a figure she could become like.
As Ayame was sparring with Syrana, trying to hit her using the knowledge she had of the White Dragon, Syrana was effortlessly dodging.
“T..Teacher, you’re too fast! Give me a chance!” Syrana only gave a sly grin as she replied “Ayame, in combat you can’t ask your enemy to give you a chance. They would only laugh.”
Ayame had removed a kunai from her hip belt and stabbed it towards Syrana, knowing she still could probably not hit her, and she was right.
In fact Syrana had stepped forward and used a hand movement to hit the kunai out of her hand as well as lecture her. “You need to grip your weapon better Ayame. Otherwise you will easily be disarmed.”
Ayame began to growl quietly while Shimaru was laughing at her misfortune. Even he knew he couldn’t win against Syrana who was a Sigil wielder. At most he could match her strength and skill without her using her Sigil. He was indeed faster than her as well, but once she used it he had no hope of winning.
Ayame began to listen more to Syrana and began to try and mimic her movements. Syrana would also allow Ayame to get closer and nearly hit her as if to motivate her to let her know she was getting closer to catching her.
“You’re so close Ayame“ Syrana smiled happily. It was like she had a little sister. She couldn’t consider Myra as a  younger sister, more so an equal. A best friend.
Ayame was enjoying her life thus far with Syrana’s presence, but it wouldnt last long. At age 16 Syrana had to stop visiting because many things had come up she needed to tend to and she had not responded to Ayame.
-----Ayame age 16---------
She had matured to become beautiful and was currently in her room trying on kimonos until her older sister Izanami stepped in and spoke ”Oh dear younger sister...Are you trying to find some man to make your own?” Izanami gave a smirk as she approached Ayame.
Her hands then slipping over, as if exploring her body. “Your curves have not fully matured. Unlike myself” Izanami pressed her fairly large bust against Ayame’s back as if to show off.
Ayame blushed heavily with embarrassment and anger as she pushed her sister back and roared out “Not everyone can be as seductive as you!! Just because you have many lovers it doesn’t mean I myself am worried.. All I need is one! Now out out outtt!!!”
Izanami blinked, somewhat surprised at her sisters frustration, before being pushed out of Ayame’s room before she turned. The door slammed shut. “Hmph!.. Never appreciated. I was going to give advice to you..” Izanami walked off to find something else to do.
Ayame put on a blue kimono with a white flower decorative pattern with gold lining across its buds. She also began to experiment with looks. Trying for a more traditional appearance.
As Ayame walked out, feeling confident in herself, she had made it a goal tonight over the years to try and find a partner as it was the annual Dragon Festival. A festival that commemorates the move to this continent and the safety of the White Dragon clan, who had escaped certain doom.
For the younger adolescents it was used to find lovers and was a night of romance for them. Several of Ayame’s female friends had found dates, and even though Ayame was not asked by anyone she still wanted to go around and enjoy it. Maybe she would find someone. Although she was tough and more tomboyish she was still a young girl who wanted to experience romance.
Ayame walked out of her room to see the 5 year old Amias holding a wooden toy, gazing at Ayame. Amias then gave a shifty grin and pointed at her as he blurted out. “Wild girl!” A nickname given to Ayame by him because he had often seen her temper in action against many males. As if she were a wild creature.
Ayame only growled as her signature vein appeared on her forehead and she gave a soft donk on Amias’s head. “I am not a wild girl…” She pouted and walked off while Amias gave a teary look while rubbing his head.
The festival outside, which included members of the other 2 estate branches, was quite large with a few hundred individuals dressed in traditional clothing consisting of hakamas and kimonos as well as unique styles of clothing not seen anywhere else on Seleria. Then again, none of these styles were.
There were even several Sylph who had visited with Myra and Syrana before who made friends here and visited. But Syrana was not included, neither was Myra, as they tended to their own matters.
As Ayame made her way around she was full of confidence. She visited makeshift food stands that sold traditional White Dragon food. Such as red gill fish battered with a chestnut flower and then coated with a sweet fruit flower sauce.
Ayame began to indulge on these delicacies one after another. There were several boys who passed her laughing as one whispered “Look, it’s Ayame. It seems she couldn't get a date..And is eating her problems away, haha” While another whispered. “Shh, she will hear you. Didn't you hear what happened years ago..Besides, let’s hurry. Our own dates are waiting.”
Ayame cleared her throat and sighed as she shook her head slightly, as if trying to ignore them. She forced a faint smile to which the shopkeeper gave her two more and spoke “Don't let those bums get to you Ayame. Here, these are on the house” The man gave a hearty laugh. Before Ayame gave  a proper smile. She was glad to know some people were on her side.
She nodded and thanked him before leaving. She walked around but it wasn't long before her heart began to tug painfully. Everywhere she went she spotted couple after couple. People she knew who agreed with her views were now with partners. Ayame felt betrayed, but that betrayal was sadness and jealousy in disguise.
The night went on with a fierce happiness for everyone other than Ayame whose mood went downhill to the point of her going out of the estate and leaning against the tree she had been to many times before.
Curling up against her knee with a sad frustrated look in her eyes. She then shut her eyes as she tried to relax and block everything out, but it seems fate had other plans for her.

Syrana only got closer, before gazing at the orcs and bowing. Then she spoke “Thank you. Please let the magi know we may or may not pass through the village again.”
The orcs looked at each other then nodded after making a sort of pig like sound, before heading off. Avrin was the first to enter the cave system without hesitating. He wanted to get this over with, but he didn’t get far before a large deafening roar echoed. Followed by a voice.

Silence followed before that intense ominous feeling could be felt. The swamplands were silent and they all knew it was loud enough to make the orc village quiver with fear.
Avrin spoke “Don’t come near me....” This was more so for Ayame’s sake. He knew that Shimaru would be angry if she was hurt or more, so he had to save face for his teacher.
The feeling was more intense than the calm before the storm. It started good, but then that feeling made one more nervous as time went by. Many things running through the persons head. Avrin spoke to Syrana “Both of you, leave now…..”
Avrin had an incredible sense that he would either be killed or be near death when this was over. And that was only the best outcome. Syrana spoke “We are in this together. Even for you.
” Syrana took steps closer while Ayame watched. That was before the cave system began to move. Sounds being heard coming towards them like a tidal wave.
Avrin’s eyes augmented before he gazed down. It was as if mana had taken the form of tendrils. It was compact. But it was heading like water. And, in this case, when it had reached close enough, one shot out like lightning towards Syrana who obviously couldn’t see in the pitch darkness, but felt that something wasn’t right.

At that moment he pushed Syrana out of the way before the large vine pierced through his back and through his stomach. blue blood seeped from the sides of his lips.
Red blood meant that the injury was something he could handle, and his dark matter only needed to recover at its average pace. Blue blood signified a major injury. It was when his internal dark matter engine, so to speak, had felt the force, and his ability, imbued with his red blood.
Just like how humans have plasma. This is an added conditional part of his ability that puts his recovery at a speedier state. Syrana fell to the ground as she was pushed to the side by Avrin, to which she gazed up in shock “A..Avrin” she spoke as the tendril stood like a spike from his stomach, linking into the darkness of the cave.

He knew the injury itself wasn’t life threatening for someone like him. And if he was to be killed, the dragon would of done so long ago. He only felt anger, because this is the second time he had been engulfed by vines. He hated them and had bad memories. He spoke to Syrana.

Deep underground, 4 minutes had passed. Avrin was now dangling in the main chamber where Lang was, uncovered from his mummy like wrapping. His arms were bound as well as his legs, while the tendril still impaling his stomach remained. The blue blood trail across his lips also remained.
Avrin was panting slightly, regardless of the injury not being enough to kill him, it hurt like no tomorrow. His body was truly a marvel to be working even after a few organs were injured. The voice of Lang rang out, engulfing the entire cave system.
“Your body…” The tendril wiggled a bit, which made Avrin gasp in pain, his eyes twitching a bit. Before Lang spoke “No mana… No life force...Only something else...Something monstrous..”
Avrin, quietly panting, replied. ”S..Surely I cannot be all that bad... “ He tried to make a joke. He knew, regardless of his position, he shouldn't anger this dragon further.
Lang growled a bit before replying. “Liar...You corrupt these lands with your presence…” The tendril impaling him wiggled again, as if torturing him. Causing blue blood to seep from his wound as well as his organs to shudder, which in turn made him cough up more blood.
This was starting to become more painful than his execution. His training as a soldier and general as well as this bodies ability stopped him from crying. In fact, any normal person would be dead the moment they were impaled.
“That...w..wasn’t my intention..I….was...looking for you…” He managed to get out, regardless of the pain. His eyes shut slightly as he was feeling it now. Lang spoke again, as if curious. “For me?...To fight me, creature?...”
Avrin immediately replied before the dragon got the wrong idea. “S..Sky metal….Please..give me...the sky metal..” At this point in time, Lang could feel he wasn’t lying. After all, it had a sort of link to his body and could also see his expression. Who would lie in this state. She also knew Avrin didn’t seem like a threat right now.
“Hmmm, yes...I do have it...That ominous metal I keep bound away...Why do you want it..Why should I give it to you?..”
At this point the tendril slowly moved back out of Avrin’s stomach, to which he emitted a faint dark matter to cover the wound as a sort of bandage to let it heal better.
This made Lang curious but cautious. Avrin spoke. “I would like it...Because I am a greedy person..” He smiled as blood ran down his lips a bit more. He dared not lie at this point. After all, he didn’t really have a better reason.
This made Lang laugh slightly as the cave shook a bit. His honesty at this stage made it amusing. She had never known someone to be so open about their negative quality. Avrin spoke again.
“I can offer...something not of this world....”

chapters.content:
Full Pr credits to Draconis who made this possible please give him some rep for his troubles :) Poll results are in with avrin giving a staggering lead *cough* now that wasnt expected was it ? *sarcasm* XD. so iv updated the information part of the google doc adding avrins new abilitys aswell as charecter information you guys may find interesting to read.
that bieng said iv added another poll for the sake of making spectral better i take my readers insight seriously and allways try to adjust how i do things. please take the time to answer a few of my questions.
1-What does spectral Lack?
2-What could be improved?
3-What do you want to see more of?
4-are you liking how its turning out so far?
lets see if spectral can get 10 ratings for this ch :) btw guys thank you for helping me achieve 5th place it means a lot ot me it also means spectral is on the best rated on the front page. :D
dont forget to rate/favourite/follow/enjoy ch 49 :D
---------
Lang gazed at Avrin with interest. What could he offer her that she wanted. She wasn’t like most of her kin that enjoyed riches and unique treasures, she was comfortable with what she had being a servant of Lenaya and a guardian of the swamplands. Her voice echoed with ferocity, as if thinking he was trying to preserve his life with nothing to offer.
“What could you offer me? An insect like you who can only corrupt, what could you get. From another world you say?“ Lang began to chuckle her hearty dragonic laugh, causing the system to rumble slightly “What lies you spin creature..”
Avrin frowned as he leaned up, slightly clutching his stomach as it began to heal, the pain fading slightly. Thankfully his body had also gotten more durable with training so it was common for his healing to be better if he was doing nothing but focusing on recovering. Of course such an injury still required attention and focus.
“I can see you love nature mighty dragon. What if I could offer you something. A plant never before seen on Seleria.. A plant so rare and beautiful even you could not reject it.”
Lang became quiet as she began to think. Her nostrils were emitting a somewhat hot steam as she focused her eye on Avrin. “And you say you have such a flower?”
Avrin grinned. “With my ability I’m able to summon a flower from another world and bring it here. It would be the only one of its kinds and I dare say not even the gods of Seleria would have one.” He began to spin his strategy towards this dragon.
If things went well he could twist lies and get out of here not only alive but with the metal. “This flower glows with the energy of another world and when it blooms its scent is enough to calm even the gods themselves. I’m sure if Lenaya were ever to appear you could offer this to her as a gift and possibly receive her blessings?”
Avrin was truly a spinner of sharp words. He had a plan and there was no way in hell he was going to let Lang get away with what she did to him. He never forgets someone who has irritated him.
Lang glared at him with her single eye as she was still laid down in that mossy hill that was her figure. “Very well creature..If you can bring me such a flower...I shall let you live..And, if it’s as you speak, I will let you take the Sky Metal”
Avrin nodded and spoke “To summon this flower, I need to borrow some mana from these lands. But do not let that deter you, my ability only converts mana.
I am also able to take the corruption away as if it were never there. Do I have your permission?” Lang  growled quietly as she stayed quiet for a few moments.
“Very well creature. BUT, if I feel that you have tainted my lair..I shall devour you…” The threat was all but real, Avrin would have to be careful. There was no way he was able to create life right now.
Synthetic organic material was different to something that was still alive. But there was one thing, one weapon he remembered that was used in dense jungle like battlefields. It wasn’t deadly but it was a deterrent that was amusing.
Avrin raised both his hands as he began to emit nebula mist that began to create a rectangle 2 meters wide and 5 meters tall. As the rectangular mist became denser, until one couldn't see inside of it, he shut his eyes and began to put the image into his head.
He wasn’t confident in creating most casual things as they required an understanding of what made them. But when it came to weaponry, especially ones that he found interesting, it wasn’t hard for him to visualize it and put it in his head.
Of course, with training came the ability to focus better and block things out, allowing him to visualise his creation better which also meant the speed and dark matter used would be more efficient.
Lang gazed curiously at Avrin’s ability. It was something she had never seen before, and what's more is she couldnt feel an ounce of mana or energy emanating from it. This caught her interest, but also worried her. The thoughts running through her head were “-Just what is this creature and the ability he wields. Is he truly able to create life from another world?-”
20 minutes had passed. Avrin would usually be done, but this was his first attempt at doing something like this. He had to be careful with the minor details and especially what it was.
He also had to keep thought on the dark matter waste as to not anger Lang. He had to reabsorb it and recycle it back into the nebula mist, which proved efficient.
A total of 48 minutes had passed before Avrin opened his eyes, panting slightly and lowering his hand. He was somewhat exhausted, having to juggle between focusing on creating the flower as well as keeping an eye on the dark matter waste and also his healing which slowed down due to expending effort on the two other things. His voice spoke.
“Mighty Lang, it is complete.” While Lang’s eyes widened, as if to focus, Avrin raised his hand as the nebula like cage dissipated. It revealed a large flower nearly 2 meters tall as well as a half meter wide.
The flower had a base that seemed to go inside the dirt to cover the synthetic base that wasn’t natural. The flower itself was beautiful. It had large petals that were semi opened and were glowing several colors as if it were a mini light show. Blue, green, red, yellow, all sorts of colors. Of course this was something Avrin tampered with. The usual color was a faint blue, but he needed it to be flashy.
It emitted a faint peach and lemon scent that seemed refreshing and had a long bud in the middle that had some frills. The entire bud itself was glowing white, toning down, then glowing white again as if pulsing. It was truly a beautiful flower.
“T..This is…” Lang’s voice echoed with shock, a powerful echo, and what followed was rumbling emitting from the system as Avrin struggled to keep balance a bit. The hill that was Lang’s body lifted up as the mighty dragon had moved half its body up.
It was menacing. Saying it was 9 stories tall would be a good guess, but Avrin had a feeling at full height it would be around 15-16 stories. Not to mention the length.
He had no intention of fighting such creatures until he had gotten stronger. Lang’s footsteps echoed and caused the ground to rumble and press under her weight as it got closer to Avrin and the flower bit by bit. He was somewhat worried, but had a feeling it wasn’t needed. It seems from a glance he saw her interest in the flower itself and not him.
This was a good sign. Little did Lang know that the flower wasnt the only thing he had formed. After he completed it, a small control a couple of inches in diameter appeared on the edge of the cage. It was a simple design but its signal could reach several kilometers. It had several buttons but only one of them worked.
Lang’s voice wrung out as she examined the flower close up. The dragon’s body was covered with several varieties of plants and vines. It seemed she had slumbered for several hundreds of years for it to grow so much. “Creature, this flower….It is truly beautiful. I must have it. It’s mine. I want it…”
Avrin smirked. Dragon or not, she had spoke that she was different to her kin in the greed respect, but it seems that was just a matter of her not having anything to be greedy about until now. “Very well mighty Lang. But in return, will you keep your promise? Let me live and allow me the Sky Metal?”
Lang stopped for a moment as it glared down at Avrin, the dragon emitting a large powerful aura that felt as if gravity were pressing on him. “Creature, why should I keep my promise to you… There is no doubt you are up to no good. Wanting that object, even matching it with your life..”
A greedy and perceptive dragon. Avrin thought quietly, it was time to spin another strategic lie. “Mighty Lang..the truth is.. if I do not return with the metal as a gift for the demon ruler than my life is forfeit to begin with. Please won’t you allow me to take it? It is nothing more than a gift to put on show.”
A simple and effective lie. Avrin held an emotionless fierce look, as if showing a face that he wasn’t lying but needed a bit of pity.
Lang pondered this before speaking “Hmmm…” Her eyes focused on him closer, until he felt her somewhat steaming heat from her nostrils blow against him like a mini furnace. “Very well creature….It doesn’t seem like you are lying...The demon continent is far...and you have travelled far to try and get this metal you need...And you also used your unique and intriguing ability to create a beautiful flower to please me. I shall grant you your life and this metal you seek…”
Lang’s eyes emitted a quick flash of green as her mana shot towards a corner of the room behind where she was resting. A large vine encasing that Avrin hadn’t noticed before, due to the presence of the dragon, was emitting a faint dark mana. The vines sprung towards Lang and Avrin until it reached between the two. As the vines retracted, the ominous dark mana grew stronger and stronger.
Until what rested on one vine was a large chunk of a strange metal. 2 feet wide and 1 foot tall, give or take parts of it that seemed to be dented in. It had a metallic look.
Reading on this site? This novel is published elsewhere. Support the author by seeking out the original.
The metal itself was strange, it had several lines across it that pulsed slightly, as if they were veins. Pumping what seemed to be a fluid that was glowing red. In all honesty, Avrin felt it was more of an egg that was deformed rather than a metal.
It was somewhat disgusting and he wasn’t looking forward to touching it, but his efforts until now were for this. As he approached the metal he started to have a weird feeling, as if the metal itself was trying to get him closer and closer.
The moment his hand was a few inches from it, his pupils began to change slightly. From the light azure blue to a purplish black. Lang had saw this and then growled slightly before vines wrapped over the metal again, as if like cloth.
“Creature...You are not to touch that metal while in these swamplands...It has a strange effect on you. When you are away from these lands, do as you will…”
Avrin shook his head slightly as if snapping out of a trance. He then realised that the metal indeed had a somewhat hypnotic power to it. Even for him it was somewhat strong. “Ah..Thank you mighty Lang..” Before he took the vine wrapped metal, which seemed to block its effects, he remembered Ayame and Syrana were outside.
And at that moment large rumbling was heard as the cave system shook with force. “Who dares attack my lair…” At one stage, an arrow as if like a shooting star fired in between Avrin and Lang through the thick vines that protected the entrance.
Avrin wriggles his nose a bit. Could that idiot be anymore careless. Before things went wrong he needed an excuse and a dark grin adorned his face. It was time for revenge. And not only 2 birds, but 2 birds and 1 lizard with one stone.
“Mighty Lang, please allow me to leave a side entrance of sorts. The ones who are attacking your lair are after this metal for their own purposes…..” Lang gazed at Avrin, and a small jet of steam emitted from her nostrils again.
“This is the only favor I shall grant you creature...You may leave while I attend to these intruders…” From the side of the system, vines moved, revealing a second entrance to which Avrin wasted no time heading towards it with the large vine covered metal. He emitted a nebula mist around it to left it up. And surprisingly it wasn’t heavy. In fact, it was as if he was carrying nothing.
As Avrin left through the side entrance, at that moment the large vine barrier protecting the first entrance blew open, a gust of dust and smoke kicking around. While the 2nd entrance closed with Avrin through it.
Avrin chuckled quietly “Sorry Ayame and Syrana, I have no doubt that there is a chance you both may die, but for this hatred of mine to settle, revenge is in order..” Indeed, he had not forgiven either of them. He had felt like he was made a fool out of. From her nearly killing him to Ayame underestimating him and annoying him.
Indeed at this stage they may have seemed like wanting to befriend him, but with his emotions locked he cared little. He also reassured himself that Syrana would most likely get them out alive with her Sigil.
He heard rumbling from underneath the cave system as well as roaring. He felt two large manas collide. One obviously from Lang and another from Syrana infused with the Sigil. Little did he know that such a powerful mana collision would be felt from thousands of miles away, Shimaru and Myra also feeling it.
Back at the estate, Myra smiled as she sat down to have tea with Shimaru. She spoke softly “It seems you really have taken a liking to Avrin, but can that really be a reason to trust him so easily with your techniques?” Myra worryingly spoke.
“Ho ho ho! You worry too much. Do not worry, someone who has been given so much and has such dedication surely has a sense of honor. I know he wouldn’t use it for evil” Shimaru spoke. But in the end he truly had no idea.
It was then that two large manas were felt by them. Myra was the first to react. “G..Gah...t..this power...Lang and..Syrana!!??“ She spoke with fright as she stood up. Shimaru also giving a nervous look.
“Incredible...This is the power of a dragon and a half Sigil wielder…” His eyes filled with envy, fright, and respect, at their power…
“But why..Why is she fighting Lang?…” She bit her lips and furrowed her brows with worry. “Was it Avrin...I’m sure he schemed something” Shimaru gazed at her. “Lets not jump to conclusions Myra...We can only trust in them..”
Avrin had been running at his top speed for quite awhile now. It was about the time. Asura was waiting at the destination and Avrin had no need to hold back since Ayame wasnt with him. He shot like a bullet through the tree lines while clutching onto a vine that had a nebula mist covering it for worry that the mist couldn’t keep up.
As he reached the clearing he saw a black figure devouring a small carcass that resembled an animal similar to an antelope. “Asura!” Avrin called out to which the creature turned to look at Avrin, it’s mouth covered in blood and filled with meat as it mumbled. “Ahh master?”
“Were leaving now!” Avrin demanded to which Asura stood up, knowing that something was going on. Previously the meeting between Avrin and Asura had taken place before Myra and Shimaru had realised the mana. And it was then that Asura gasped in fright as he felt the powerful force. “S..Strong…” he spoke with awe.
“Now Asura! We are leaving now!” He spoke to which Avrin continued on with Asura, abandoning his kill poutfully, both of them now shooting through the tree line. Avrin’s face revealed a smile. He was excited, not only did he have the metal but he would get those 3 bitches back.
“All those times you irritated me, all those times you showed anger towards me, and for the time you nearly killed me. I hope you carve this into your mind and heart” Avrin pulled the control from a small pocket in his clothing and pressed it right as Asura and Avrin had entered the clearing where the swamplands met the mountainous plains.
Inside the the cave system Syrana was battling Lang. “Where is he!!!” Syrana yelled while Lang was roaring, vines shooting towards Syrana who fired off powerful fire element arrows that decimated the vines. Lang and Syrana both had to hold back to a degree as to not let the cave fall on them both.
Lang was the most disadvantaged, not wanting to ruin her lair. “Elf!! How dare you attack my lair!!“ Lang roared while slashing its mighty claw towards Syrana.
It seemed like a falling comet emitting its own sound. Syrana imbued an arrow with earth affinity mana and fired it towards Lang’s claw, blocking it with the force to equal it. Of course Lang was still holding back. They were indeed somewhat equal in terms of power since Lang held back more than Syrana.
“None of your concern, elf. How dare you try to go after my property!!” Ayame was hiding behind a boulder, nervous and afraid, but also angry at herself for being of no use, clutching her fists.
Syrana had told her to hide, in worry that she may die, and she had no choice but to listen.Then again, with two power houses going at it, it was a reasonable choice.
“Where is avrin!!” Syrana yelled with anger in her eyes. Although she still couldnt see eye to eye with Avrin after hearing his story, she felt for him somewhat. He was alone in this world, trying to survive, even if some actions he made weren't the best, she would try and help him.
“The demon creature has taken the metal away from your thieving hands!” Syrana’s eyes widened as she stopped for a moment. “W..What?..” At that moment, Lang emitted a shockwave from its mouth that blew Syrana back towards the cave, causing her to gasp and cough out some blood before falling to her knees. But she cared not, and spoke.
“He took the Sky Metal? Than you didn’t kill him?” Lang stopped attacking for a moment before speaking. “The demon is returning to his lands with the Sky Metal for his ruler as a gift...Like I promised him”
Syrana was quiet, as she felt anger well up. She had known then she had been fooled by Avrin. “Lang...I’m sorry to say but it seems we were both fooled…” Lang blinked in surprise as she gazed cautiously at Syrana. “Fooled?...What do you mean elf...Speak now!” Lang demanded.
Ayame raised her head as she looked to see them both stopping as if they had come to an agreement. She approached Syrana quickly to tend to her, Lang gazing even more cautiously. Syrana, ignoring Ayame, spoke “Avrin isn’t after the Sky Metal for the demon king.. He is after it for himself. He tricked you. He was my companion, I was to make sure the Sky Metal wasn’t evil, and fall into his hands if true.”
(PR Note: I tried)
Lang was quiet for a moment. She knew this elf was a Sigil wielder, and knew they loved Lenaya as much as she did. Why would she lie to her. Lang then gazed at the flower Avrin made. “T...That creature…” Ayame also felt the atmosphere. Avrin had indeed played them all. But why would he?
It was then that Syrana and Ayame realised Avrin’s vendetta towards them. He had planned this all along. “T..That bastard...When I get my hands on him..” Syrana spoke while clutching her fists against each other.
At that moment, the flower bud began to glow black as the petals and the flower itself extended open, the 3 of them paying attention to it, wondering what was going on.
The flower, now bloomed, revealed that the interior of it was mechanical, and it seemed the petals and bud were all synthetic organic material. But that wasn’t all.
There were pipes sticking out from the main body of the flower and the bud began to glow brighter and brighter, emitting a screeching sound that made Syrana and Ayame cover their ears in pain. Even Lang roared in agony.
As the flower then began to glow brighter and brighter, as if ready to implode, the purpose for which Avrin intended it to be used for had started….

chapters.title: V2: Chapter 50 What Comes Next
chapters.content:
Full Pr Credits to Draconis whoaaaaaa those comments you guys are so divided on the issue that i just felt compelled to release a special chs for you guys. hopfully this clears the air regarding some things.
Please Rate/Follow/Favourite/Enjoy ch 50 -------
The synthetic flower, which was truly a weapon used in battles where plant life was plenty, had several stages. The first stage, as the flower began to glow brighter and brighter it flashed, emitting a blinding light as if the sun had been in that room for a couple of seconds.
Caused by a chemical reaction. This was done by the bud. It had 3 layers, each layer housing 3 different chemical compounds that are released when the layers are retracted by activating the trap. This causes an intense chain reaction that puts flash bangs to shame.
That was not all. As Lang and the 2 others were blinded and dazed by the light, struggling around, Lang hitting against the cave system causing rubble to fall, Syrana cursing Avrin under her breathe, with Ayame joining in both sharing a new found hatred towards him.
The second stage activated, the pipes sticking out of the body of the flower released a green gas that began to cover the cave. Square meter by square meter.
The tactic for the first two stages was, the first stage blinded and confused the enemy, while the second stage took advantage of the discord and released as much gas as possible. As the gas filled up nearly a half of the cave system.
The the final stage activated. The body of the flower began to charge up, as if a reactor, emitting static before it released an electrostatic shock coloured red.
The tactic from the second stage to the 3rd stage was, the gas used was actually a super, super conductive gas, and the bolt used was a mimicry of a lightning bolt with paralysis capabilities.
The bolt of lightning spread quickly through the gas clouds, engulfing the room with Lang roaring, bumping against the rocky walls, causing debris to fall, barely missing Syrana and Ayame.
The bolts of lightning had hit the 3 of them. Both the Sylph and Human screaming in agony before falling down onto the ground, paralysed.
Although Lang, with her lung capacity, had inhaled a large amount of the gas and seemed to take it heavier than them both. Not only was her outside shocked, but the inside as well. One could even see the lightning from outside of her. Lang gave a large high pitched roar before falling down onto the floor with a large thump.
With steam emitting from the knocked out dragon, and the limp bodies of the knocked out Ayame and Syrana, the lair was quiet. The vines connecting to Lang had seemed to shudder away. The flower trap rested there silently, as a memento of Avrin.
Avrin and Asura, who were now quite far from the swamplands, had begun to head towards the estate. Although at top speed, with their stamina, it would take less than a day.
Avrin was currently smiling, as if a burden had been removed from his shoulder. But with these actions, he knew Syrana and Ayame would most likely hunt him down. Not to mention Lang, who would probably decimate a city looking for him.
Although he couldn’t stop grinning. “Master, you have been smiling ever since you pressed that thing… Why?” Asura asked as he felt nervous to see Avrin gazing and smiling like that. Avrin replied quietly as the two bounced across the landscape like bullets.
“One day, years from today, I’ll tell you all about it.. Right now, let me enjoy this happiness quietly” Avrin indeed wanted to enjoy it silently.
Asura only shrugged as he continued on across the landscape. Several hours had passed since that incident. With the swamplands connection to Lang temporarily severed, the creatures had gone crazy as they did as they pleased.
The orcs had trouble trying to protect themselves and even had to fortify their village. The magi was jumping up and down, cursing the fact that she allowed the outsiders to go to Lang.
In the cave system, Syrana’s body twitched a bit as she struggled to get up “Nn…” She mumbled and coughed a bit, feeling like her entire body had been stabbed by pins and needles. She looked to the side to see Ayame laying there motionless.
She worryingly shook her, thinking the worst, before Ayame mumbled and opened her eyes. “M..Master..w..what happened?..” Syrana gazed with a faint smile at Ayame before putting the events together.
“Avrin…” A powerful glare adorned her face. It was now her turn for revenge. As Syrana helped Ayame up, they looked at Lang to see that she was still out cold.
“Ayame..Let’s go before Lang wakes up. I doubt she will go easy on us…” Ayame nodded as they both headed out. The vines no longer seemed to be restricting them, as if lacking energy.
Avrin and Asura had neared the estate and could see it down the mountain path they took. Avrin stopped to gaze and frowned slightly. “Probably not a good idea to go…” Avrin looked around before forming a void sphere in his hand.
Of course, Asura backed away, remembering how that attack had killed the other gorilla like creature. Avrin focused on the sphere for a moment, enlarging it to one foot in diameter and filling it up with nebula mist.
He aimed it directly at Shimaru’s home, using his augmented eye to get a better focus, and then fired off the unique sphere towards it.
“Hopefully he gets that. Asura, lets go.” Avrin spoke happily. “Master, where will we go?..” Asura curiously asked as the two began to head north. Avrin let a smirk adorn his face as they travelled.
“I heard there’s some interesting things going on in the central continent. Why don’t we go see if we can improve ourselves there.”
Avrin again smiled as he began to think. “-First, it’s best if I gather some information. Right now I have no real idea what I’m doing.
I should take it easy for a few years until my knowledge of this world is sufficient enough for me to come up with a plan-” Indeed, Avrin knew nothing about what to do. Being a god was easier said then done.
“-What’s the rush? I’ll enjoy things for a bit-”  He then gazed at Asura who had his tongue sticking out as the wind blew against his face. It looked like he was enjoying this, as if taking a pet out for a walk.
The day had gone on with much to consider. Myra had rushed over to the swamp lands, meeting up with Syrana and Ayame. Ayame began to explain what had happened, and while Myra was listening, her face seemed to give different sorts of expressions.
But in the end she had laughed “It seems Avrin not only got the best of both of you, but also Lang.” Myra chuckled. “Myra, this isn’t funny…. We know his true intentions now…” Syrana angrily spoke but Myra seemed to think otherwise.
“Hmm... Well I wouldn’t be so sure. You’re both alive afterall. From what you told me, it seems that he used an object he is familiar with, and one effective enough to even defeat Lang.
I’m sure he had the capability to kill the 3 of you with something he could create, but he didn’t. I’m sure he had no intentions of killing you. But you are right to a degree Syrana.”
Ayame sat down with Myra using healing magic against her, as Syrana was tending to herself. Myra spoke “That metal... He must have really wanted it.
To go through that much. I can’t help feel there is a hidden agenda.” Myra contemplated different reasons why Avrin would do such a thing while Syrana saw it as her going back to hating him.
“That bastard...It really hurt...I felt like my insides were burning. I don’t know if i can taste anything either..” She pouted. In the distance, a thunderous roar echoed across the swamplands, causing the birds to scurry and Syrana and Myra to quiver slightly. “W..Well I guess Lang has woken up..” she nervously laughed.
Syrana on the other hand, had a more serious approach. “Let’s leave. I doubt Lang, as dedicated as she is to these lands, would leave. At the very most, she will hold an eternal grudge against him. But I don’t think we are ever welcome here again.” She sighed before the 3 of them continued off, back towards Shimaru’s estate.
Myra, having met Syrana at the borderline between the swamplands and the mountainous plains, and Avrin who was long gone, there was Shimaru left in his dojo, gazing at a strange sphere that had broken through his roof.
It had Avrin’s doing all over it, but it just glowed there. He gazed at it for a few moments quietly before touching it.
The sphere began to condense for several minutes until it had taken shape. It had formed the secret manual for White Dragon techniques, but on top of it a was a note that didnt seem to form right, as it was torn slightly and somewhat distorted in the words of this world.
It read: “”Sorry...Time…..myself….explore…..back…..someday..” Shimaru let a sigh out as he gently placed the note down. For clan members, they were forbidden from going outside without permission. This was to preserve their ways and techniques, but Avrin.

he knew he could never keep locked away. Avrin must have did something truly terrible for him to not even return and say goodbye. Shimaru closed his eyes for a moment before taking the manual and putting it inside the corner of his hakama.
And he then entered a Pulsing Dragon to clear his mind. 2 days had passed before Myra and Syrana had returned with Ayame. Having taken longer for her sake. The 3 of them were currently inside Shimaru’s dojo, who seemed to be at a loss.
“Ayame, you left without permission…” Shimaru spoke softly. “Forgive me grandfather…” Syrana then spoke up, as if to cover. “I hope you can forgive me Shimaru, it was not Ayame’s fault. It was I who allowed her to continue.” Shimaru sighed, rubbing his forehead. Myra then spoke.
“I think such matters are important, but something else needs to be discussed first. Avrin is missing and with him, the Sky Metal. Which seems to be important, as for him to go through all this effort for.”
Ayame spoke before Syrana did. “Why would he betray us like that….We were starting to get closer to him. All this for some stupid metal?..” Syrana patted Ayame’s head, who seemed to be near tears. Avrin was her first true love, so it had hit her the hardest.
“Dont worry Ayame, I plan on finding him myself and dragging him back for answers” Syrana aggressively spoke. “No, I don’t think there is any need to do that“ Shimaru softly spoke out. Myra instead of Syrana spoke “Shimaru, you speak as if you know something we don’t?”
Shimaru gave a faint smile as his arms lifted “Not at all. More of an assumption. Whatever Avrin must have planned, I’m sure he had a good reason. He is unknown to all of us” Both Syrana and Myra looked at each other.
When Ayame was sleeping, they had both found out that Avrin had told them about himself. They felt a bit bad considering he hadn’t told Shimaru anything, but Shimaru was somewhat right, they figured.
Avrin, who comes from another world with no ties or attachments, must have planned something for himself here. They could only hope it wasn’t evil. But considering the object he was after, Myra figured it may be something bad.
As they had finished, both the Sylphs decided to stay the night there. As they also attended dinner with Calias, who had returned without Amias. Syrana was outside on the 3rd floor of the mansion leaning against the wooden railing with a somewhat sad look.
She pictured the night she met Avrin and how she nearly killed him, which made her smile. And then how he was kept locked up, and her fight with Abbadon, which made her give an annoyed look. Then their meeting again at the estate, which made her feel uneasy.
That night, when she tried to test his abilities, only to glance at his body. This caused her to wiggle a bit and blush. From Avrin explaining his story to her, to how he pushed her out of the way from that vine which would have injured her greatly.
“Why Avrin...We were starting to get to know one another...Why is it you went as far as to include me and Ayame in there...We could have both died and you didn’t seem to care...Has the hate from those times I was aggressive kept the revenge in you hot..” Syrana, starting to blame herself a bit, heard a voice that reassured her it was fine.
“Don’t blame yourself Syrana. Avrin must have had this planned since the beginning. He most likely used you as well as this estate as a stepping stone. But that doesn’t mean he is bad. Some people will use others even if they have no intention of killing them.
That pain though, can often be worse than the usual betrayal.” It was none other than Myra who spoke to Syrana.
“I wonder what he is doing...Grr, I’d love to hit him across the head a few times” Syrana clenched her fists, waving them in anger. Across the elven lands, a nearly 6 days worth of normal travel time, Avrin and Asura were resting from their travel with no restraint. Currently eating.
Avrin gazed at Asura, who seemed to be eating the carcass of a sort of Warthog with 5 horns protruding from its head. Avrin just gazed in disgust at his so called servant. Then smiled. He might as well build relation with this creature. Considering the circumstances, he knew he was going to be with this creature for a very, very, very, long time.
“Asura, want to try a burger?” Asura blinked as his mouth was full of raw meat and blood, mumbling as he spat out some food. “Bwargur…?”
Avrin nodded. “From where I come from, it’s a sort of food everyone eats. It has a circular disk of cooked meat with sauce, pickles, and other things.”
Avrin smiled as they sat near the fire. Who would guess that this demon looking creature speaking to this monstrosity were in fact unique individuals of the strongest race. So to speak.
“Whrats ar priwkle?..” Asura spoke, mouth still full. But Avrin just chuckled softly. “It can be many things, but in this case, its a vegetable thats fermented in a special way.” Asura gave a disgusted look as he backed away from Avrin a bit and cleared his mouth, swallowing a large chunk of meat.
“Master, please don’t make me eat any thing like that…” It seems Asura was starting to speak better. His english was somewhat broken, but it seems to Avrin it needed a bit of time to sync.
Avrin grinned. “Give it a try. You will like it. If you eat too much meat, it can’t be healthy” Asura growled quietly. “I refuse!” Avrin frowned then smirked.
“Well I was going to reward you with a meat that no one has ever eaten before, but I guess that’s fine.” Asura’s ears perked up at the sound of ‘meat’ and ‘no one has ever eaten before’.
“Meat...Master, I seem to have...changed my mind. Please let me try it” Asura gave a sort of smile that seemed more like a face that was ready to tear something apart. Avrin then nodded and began to create the ingredients. Of course, he used raw ingredients. As if to make it more meaningful.
Creating a pan and placing it over the hot coals of the camp fire, he formed saltless butter and placed it in, waiting for it to melt. Asura began to drool a bit at the smell alone. Avrin then formed the meat patty, but Asura snatched the first 2 out of his hands, eating it raw. Giving a satisfied look.
As Avrin formed 2 more, he began to cook the patties on the pan, as the sizzling was something that made the stomach rumble. Asura was leaning close to the campfire.
Enough that he had forgotten he was to close and placed his hand in the embers. Surprisingly, he hadn’t noticed for at least 20 seconds, until the heat finally go through and it hurt him. He making a sort of howling sound that made Avrin laugh.
As the cooking continued, Avrin had formed the buns, the tomato sauce, as well as the pickles, giving extra to Asura’s serving. He then put it together. The burgers themselves were a bit larger than usual. He offered one to Asura, who gazed at it cautiously.
“Master...this isn’t an experiment, is it?” Avrin began to think. “Hmm, I dont think so really..” He had wondered how his food creation had progressed. The dried rations had tasted the same regardless.
As Asura picked up the burger, nearly dwarfed by his large claw engulfed hand, he placed it in his mouth. Eating the whole thing in one bite. He was quiet for a moment before giving a straight sort of poker face.
Avrin seemed worried, wondering if he liked it. He spoke before Asura did. “Don’t look at me like it’s poison. Surely it’s not that bad.” As Avrin took a bite, he blinked before smirking.
“This is pretty good...It doesn’t have the synthetic taste at all...I never really thought I would be able to get rid of it“ He spoke out with pride. Before he could take another bite, Asura pounced towards his hand, trying to grab the burger.
“Mine!! It’s mine! Give me it Master, I eat more than you!!” Asura was drooling as he gazed at the burger, craving more of it. Avrin struggled as he somewhat wrestled about with the creature. “Greedy beast... You had yours!” Avrin spoke with a laugh as the two struggled about for it.
Tomorrow was indeed a big day, as their journey to the central continent would finally begin. Avrin had hoped that by going there he would be able to find more of a meaning in seeking godhood.
Little did he know though, that a couple of meters away from him, the vines protecting the outside world from the Sky Metal were almost completely dissolved by it whispers, emitting quietly from the metal as the veins surrounding it began to pump more of that liquid.

chapters.title: V2: Chapter 51 Truth & Emotions
chapters.content:
Full Pr Credits to Draconis here is your release for the day guys enjoy :)Lets see if we can get 10 Ratings for spectral :D Please Follow/Favourite/Enjoy ch 52
-------
Avrin had decided to rest. He could not be bothered in creating a tent and decided to just use the large carry sack as a pillow. He felt no need to be cautious around Asura, in fact it seemed Asura had more or less put the past behind him due to the potential rewards he could reap.
Asura was currently gazing over the horizon, the dark night sky showering the world of Seleria with the light of the stars. The air so fresh it would be something even the top diplomats of Avrin’s universe  would crave.
The sound familiar to a sort of cricket as well as other insects and birds putting their young to rest, not excluding the animals and creatures doing the same to their own kin.
Asura’s intention was to keep on guard. He felt that his master was in quite a rush to leave the swamplands, and after he felt that large mana surge he knew his master had made someone angry. So Asura was more so nervous rather than cautious.
Avrin quietly fell into a sleep, but his dream was more or less something he found unwelcoming. An image of Syrana’s dismembered body crushed against the wall with blood dripping down her face. And Ayame under a light foot, being crushed under Lang’s weight as it roared in anger.
Avrin had started to feel regret towards his actions in his sleep. When Ayame had suddenly been crushed by Lang, letting out a scream of agony, he woke up panting heavily. He had only slept for 20 minutes before waking up again. He clenched his teeth and gazed at the ground, his heart beating quickly.
Asura turned to gaze at Avrin and spoke “Master, what's wrong?” Avrin sighed as he rubbed his face “Something is wrong with me...I feel the need to follow what I believe is best for myself...Yet I feel like I'm showing little care to those around me..” Indeed, Avrin’s personality had just done a 360 from his revenge filled self to a regretful mindset.
Avrin wondered why his mind was becoming crazy with different personalities. Surely it had nothing to do with any mental issue. That was when he realised something, his eyes opened as he remembered.
“Yes that’s right...He said I could control my emotions. Could it be something to do with that...Am I subconsciously blocking things out while other emotions surface for my self preservation.”
Avrin, being as perceptive as he is, which also served as a trait which allowed him to become a general, had hit the nail on the head.
His body had indeed blocked out emotions that it felt were of no use to him in his attempt to achieve what he wanted. It merely allowed the more beneficial emotions to surface and allow him to happily get the 3 of them in his trap and leave without issue.
It also showed that he had little thought of returning to the estate, but that was also an issue in general. He took in a deep sigh and then let the breathe slowly leave his lungs.
“This may cause problems if I let my emotions continue to run rampant...Just when I thought I had them in check, they went haywire without me realising it.”
Avrin had felt like an amaetur. He had trained for several years and felt he had made progress, but a martial artist also relied on emotions to keep their mind in check. Avrin might as well be an expert with a temper problem, which would indeed affect his combat ability.
“Asura, I'm going to meditate for a bit. If anything happens let me know.” Asura only nodded before continuing to gaze off into the distance. They were currently in a densely packed forest area with little clearings. It seemed the Elven continent was indeed an abundant source of nature with forests being common sight.
As Avrin had found a small clearing about the size of an average room, he sat down, crossing his legs before placing his hands on his lap, shutting his eyes as he began to enter a Pulsing Dragon.
Blocking everything out, his mind seemed to relax his body and calm his nerves before it drifted away, as if his body was still on Seleria but his mind was floating in space.
As he entered the Pulsing Dragon, just like what had occurred inside the home in the orcish settlement, his body emitted a faint pulse which went for several meters and began to coat surrounding objects with dark matter, which seemed to nullify their gravity.
Asura’s ears perked slightly as he was able to feel the dark matter Avrin emitted. A trait he had learnt ever since becoming like this. But he paid no mind to it only spoke praise of Avrin. “Master sure is strong..No wonder he beat me..”
Asura was not the only thing to pay attention to Avrin. The Sky Metal had finally managed to burn the last of the vines surrounding it in silence. Avrin hadn't realised it due to his worry, and Asura had figured it was a small animal nearby, but he cared not to hunt as he was full and also went by Avrin’s words to not hunt if he didn't need to.
The Sky Metal seemed to slowly melt into a liquid like goo before it made its way towards Avrin. It was also then that Asuras ears perked up and he turned around only to see the metal was now gone from its position. He growled quietly as he stood up and began to look around, using an augmented eye of his own.
His eyes both widened as he spotted the metal emitting a black and red metallic mana as it headed towards Avrin. Asura rushed towards it, but the metal had reached Avrin from behind.
At that moment, Avrin had felt its presence due to it being so close. He quickly opened his eyes only to then dodge as the metal pounced towards his meditative location before slowly bubbling up and reforming.
“What sort of metal is this...It’s a lifeform…” Avrin spoke out to which Asura made its way into the clearing. Avrin clicked his tongue. “Asura, didn’t I tell you to keep a look out.” Asura gave a soft hmph. “Master, I thought it was a small animal…”
Avrin sighed before nodding. “Don’t destroy it. I need it intact. In fact just stay where you are and let me handle this.” Avrin gazed at the metal which seemed to stand a meter tall with a base that seemed like a slug.
“Sorry, but I’m not your meal. Or whatever it is you’re after. In fact, I’m going to show you that you’re now mine.” Avrin mocked, to which he rushed towards the metal and emitted a nebula mist around it as if to construct a prison.
But something unexpected happened. The metal seemed to absorb the nebula mist and its color went from black and red to purple and a sort of crimson red. “Not good..” Avrin realised. But the goo like metal then shot a spike like tendril which pierced Avrin’s leg.
The speed was incredibly fast and surprised him. The pain surged in his leg as blue blood began to seep out from the wound. But that wasn’t the worst.
Avrin felt as if the metal itself was absorbing his energy. Avrin feeling his strength leave slightly. Asura knew something was wrong and defied his orders jumping towards the metal and slashing against it, but the metal seeming to have gotten bigger due to it slowly absorbing Avrin’s energy only caught the creature in a vice like appendage and threw him towards a tree that then collapsed at the force of him hitting it.
Avrin tried to remove the tendril like appendage, but it had pierced through the ground and didn’t seem to budge. “Not...good...I guess the only way to do this is to beat you at your own game…” Avrin, feeling as if the particles making up his body were quivering, had raised his hand and began to absorb the metal.
It was now a game of who could eat the other quicker, and Avrin seemed to be winning. He felt his strength recover as the metal began to shudder into pieces. That turned into dust which inturn turned into a blackish energy that Avrin absorbed. It seemed to screech quietly.
The Sky Metal had retracted its appendage and in one moment, created a large spiral like spike that pierced towards Avrin’s chest like a bolt of lightning. And it had caught Avrin off guard while he focused on absorbing it. The metal had used its remaining energy to pierce into his chest and straight into the dark matter heart.
The only expected result that followed, was an intense pain from having his chest pierced. But as soon as the spike touched the dark matter heart, the heart itself emitted a pulse that coated across the metal and in a near instant had absorbed it, or more so slurped it up. 
The narrative has been stolen; if detected on Amazon, report the infringement.
The Sky Metal liquified and hovered for only a moment before it was sucked forcefully into the wound in his chest and devoured by the dark matter heart/the core. At which moment a surge of energy rushed across Avrin’s body, his wounds steaming before vanishing. A terrible pain sweeping across his skin and his organs.
The very fabric of his being felt like he was being torn apart. It was a similar feeling to de-particlisation. He fell to his knees wailing in agony as Asura rubbed its head after recovering. It discovered Avrin’s position and rushed towards him as it spoke “Master, what’s wrong?!!”
“AHHHH!!!!..” Avrin roared out as his pupils turned purple and red, the same color as the Sky Metal. At that moment, thoughts rushed into his mind as if it were the memories of the metal itself.
First darkness, then a bright light. This scene to someone would be an enigmatic one, as if it had a prophecy like meaning, but Avrin knew it too well. It was the same scene God had showed him. It was the birth of this universe.
An object engulfed in a mana like fire which seemed like an egg that pulsed out, collided with another similar object, emitting a thundering cosmic bang. But what occurred up and close was something Avrin hadn’t seen before when God had showed him.
The two objects were indeed potential gods that had collided with one another and were not compatible, but as their souls were torn asunder, their dormant and potential energy had molded into each other and formed a thick metallic like substance that shot outwards towards the darkness of space.
The scenes then ended there, as Avrin gasped for air, sweating greatly and panting incredibly fast as he clutched the ground. Trying to piece together what had just happened. But the answer was obvious.
When two gods who weren’t compatible during the birth of this universe collided, their bodies and souls would be torn asunder, but their dormant potential energy would mold into a sort of celestial metal that would be unmatched. This was what the people of this world know as Sky Metal.
Sky Metal was nothing more than the energy of two gods who had perished during this universe's creation. Truly a secret not only people but the gods themselves would kill to have. This Metal’s importance had just skyrocketed to a whole new level.
Avrin’s face showed one of frustration and delight. His eyes widening as he wondered about the possibilities of such a thing. As he raised his hand to try and reform the sky metal, or more so a fragment, his heart began to ache as if not allowing him to.
What he didn’t know was that it hadn’t truly been devoured, it had been stored inside the core and was undergoing a sort of layer metamorphosis. Avrin had no idea that his dark matter core was sentient to a degree.  This was all information he would not find out for quite some time.
Avrin stood up weakly as Asura helped him. “Master...What was that?..What happened?..” Avrin couldn’t really be bothered to explain, he only silently spoke “Take me back to the campsite...I need to rest…”
Asura complied, as he did as Avrin wished. After that, Avrin had slept for the entire night without so much as opening an eye, and Asura was even more vigilant. Not even a small animal would get within 100 meters without him noticing.
Morning had come and Avrin woke up to see Asura was also gazing around “Master, you’re awake?” Avrin nodded and stretched, feeling more refreshed. But his heart was giving a weird sort of feeling, most likely due to last night.
“Indeed. Asura, let’s be off. If I remember correctly, teacher told me that further north near the coastline, there should be a port city that the humans have set up. Before we go there though.“
Avrin raised his hand and the nebula mist he emitted began to form a large black cloak much bigger than his own, he then threw the finished result to Asura.
“Can’t have you looking like that in the open. Last thing I need is the city guard after us.” Asura stood proudly “If anyone comes after us I will show them we are not easy kills!” Asura roared pridefully, which made Avrin chuckle quietly.
The two began to make their way further north. On their way, they spotted several farm’s with farmers using a sort of bull like creature to plow their fields. It seemed these were farmers who couldn't afford to use magic to achieve the same result, as Avrin was aware there were magic tools for such things.
The farmers themselves seemed to look hard working, dressed for their work, and had others helping them. As if like a large family community. There were also several children playing around with makeshift toys.
Avrin then spotted one child who sat on a rock frowning as he gazed at the others playing with there own toys. He seemed to look more impoverished than the others.
Avrin passed by the child without a care then stopped for a moment, gazing blankly in front of him. “Nothing….Not a single shred of care for a sad child..” It was something obviously placed in front of Avrin. How could he not feel worried about this. In his former life he would indeed show some care.
Avrin then turned and walked back towards the child, while Asura stood still. Watching curiously. As Avrin stopped, he gazed down at the child. Avrin’s own face hidden from view as well as his body. He spoke “Why are you sad?” He spoke flat out, wanting the answer.
The child looked at him nervously and then sighed quietly “My friends all have toys...But my parents don’t buy me my own...They say their crop wasn’t looking too good last season… So we had barely enough money…”
The child’s story still hadn’t affected Avrin, which caused Avrin to feel more anger than sorrow at his lack of emotion. He felt things such as revenge and greed, but why is it the emotions that were most important to a human, sorrow/sympathy/regret, were not felt by him. His eyes then widened as he thought quietly.
“-That’s right…. I’m not human anymore-” A hint of sadness in his mind. But he gazed at the child before Avrin opened his hand.
He then began to form a toy using nebula mist. This was a toy he saw on an ad once when he took leave for a holiday resort on a planet. It was the latest model. A sort of mecha robot knight that was several feet tall.
It’s chest was also able to be opened to reveal room inside for a pilot. It was more like a suit then mecha considering the pilot was only a few inches smaller.
But Avrin gave a little surprise for the boy. As the boy gazed with awe, his friends looked over and pointed with shock and surprise. Avrin then gave the boy the toy and then began to walk off without feeling much at all.
The boy laughed as he stood up and began to thank Avrin several times over while his friends ran over with jealousy and surprise as they wanted to hold it and touch it. Asura blinked as he gazed at Avrin “Master, you are generous with your abilities..” Asura spoke as if trying to compliment him.
But Avrin was silent. His face still not giving a hint of satisfaction. Avrin, being several meters away from the boy, pressed the button on the mecha knights chest to which it opened spewing out rare jewels and diamonds that would cost hundreds of gold.
The children all screamed with excitement as they all then began to thank Avrin, yelling at the top of their lungs jumping up and down. “-That’s it..-” Avrin gave a satisfied smile, his body couldn’t seem to resist his efforts to try and make himself feel happiness and sympathy, as it gave into the forced urge and allowed the emotions to emit. Avrin was feeling something he secretly craved for a while.
The two continued on while the children's screams attracted the first boys child, who in turn screamed with excitement. Asura turned to Avrin and spoke.
“Master, will we be stopping?” Avrin nodded and pointed north towards a seemingly large village that seemed to have merchants go to and from it. “We will see if that village has anything to offer before continuing.”
