chapters.title: V3: Chapter 60 Divine Intervention
chapters.content:
Full Pr credits to spectrals second voluntary pr SuperDoeDoe. for this ch thank you for making this release possible tonight hopefully some kind readers will give you some rep ^^
so i took into consideration that a lot of you have been yearning for a bit more to happen and i have decided that i will try to add a bit of action into spectrals current pace to make things a bit more exciting im happy with the result hopefully you guys are to :)
regarding blacksmithing i have found that i really enjoy the way i am doing things and i want to work on that craft a bit more for a story like this nothing is more exciting then having the mc prove people wrong when they underestimate him and pull out surprises that are not to overwhelming but are done well :D
p.s the pictures are almost done there looking great im hoping they will be done before the next releae of sr. as for you es fans the next release may be out next thursday-friday i may not show it but i am also constantly thinking of how to make that story go well to be honest i put a bit more care into es because of all the suprises and action that has been comming in for it.
Please Rate/Follow/Favourite/Share with your friends ^^ enjoy ch 60 ----------------
After reattaching his metal mask, Avrin could see that the hallways were somewhat quiet with the occasional guard or two heading through. The ship's interior seemed to be made from a steel like metal that was obviously enchanted by magic, to the point where it was slightly visible even to the naked eye.
Having learnt the basics of blacksmithing, Avrin had thought he should open up a minds eye towards things crafted from metal; this was also a recommendation by Klin. This would help him get ideas as well as understand how things could be used and made.
Avrin headed up several floors of the large ship until the ocean air filled his nostrils, it was refreshing and somewhat dry but it was still something he would love to look at. Having arrived on the top deck his eyes widened with fascination.
The sea itself wasn't as desolate as one would think, although land was out sight there were many ships in the distance, mostly scout ships and trade vessel looking ships as well as fishing vessels taking advantage of the clear weather.
The water of this ocean was pristine and unpolluted although it kept its strong blue color. The top deck itself was active with workers attending mechanisms that needed to be cared for, although they didn't look like soldiers and more like dockworkers hired to help, Avrin felt these men had some form of training just in case pirates or something would show up.
Avrin was snapped out of his curious daze by a familiar voice. “Ah Sir Avrin its good to see you.” Turning his head Avrin gazed at the man and instantly recognized him the mage that explained the mana tornados.
Although the mage blinked as he spoke “uh you are Sir Avrin correct?” motioning towards the mask he wore Avrin nodded. “I am. “ Avrin turned back around as he gazed at the expansive ship it was incredibly huge and he had a question.
“I didn't quite get your name, but I have a question. How difficult is it to craft a ship such as this?”The mage gave a soft chuckle and replied. “I apologize I am Magi Tyrin, one of 10 who help serve humanity under the Archmages orders.
As for this ship sir Avrin, a vessel such as this takes 5 years to build, but it is not that the manpower is lacking.
There are several things needed to be taken into account such as builders who understand what they are doing as well as preparing the required materials, I’m sure you have noticed the enchanted metal and wood used the process creating it is the biggest time consumer in crafting a vessel such as this.”
Avrin showed great interest in boats as well as any weapon that could be used for war, a trait of being a general. It also didn't hurt to learn at every chance he got. “With all this advancement in enchanted materials wouldn't it be easier to build vessels capable of flight?”
Tyrin let out a hearty almost sarcastic chuckle “haha sir Avrin I wish we understood flight better. Our attempts at flight are quite good but we have been met with negative support.
Most consider flying to be reserved for single use such as the races born from it, the avian tribes demons and even angels alone. They also suggest we not create vessels capable of flight as it impedes on them”.
Tyrin frowns “although I am one of few supporters who would enjoy seeing equality, there logic without the political talk is they do not want us humans to fly because they would not seem so unique”.
Avrin nodded he could understand this and agreed. “Sir Avrin will you not reconsider joining us for dinner? I had heard that your companion Asura had agreed immediately after being offered. Lord Gregson had hoped for you to meet lady Karina and possibly build a relation”.
Avrin seemed to laugh softly “Tyrin it sounds like Gregson is trying to set up a marriage for me by the effort he is attempting to get me to go” Tyrin was silent and gave a soft snicker. “Well I can't deny this, he has boasted your skills and power only seeing it once lord Gregson is a great judge of character after all”.
As Avrin was about to reply the currents of the ocean became rougher and the waves heavier with the clouds forming into a blue static appearance with thunder shooting diagonally at a point.
Tyrins eyes bulged as they widened “n..no how could this be….the weather was supposed to be calm….how could the archmages predictions be off!!”
Tyrin immediately called out “Under authority of The Magi Council Turn this vessel around!!” under certain circumstances of events of magic the magi council members who had an understanding of magic better than any other human were allowed to overrule orders of even the generals.
Avrin turned to look at the clouds as he began to feel a heavy flow of air shoot toward the point of lightning and that wasn't the half of it. The lightning that shoot towards the point didn't disappear it seemed to spiral continuously as more lightning gathered in a horizontal spiral it began to shape into a tornado not of wind but of electricity.
The ocean began to pulse with this mana like electricity, the bodies of fish large and small would surface and the static passed through the ship but did not affect it. Tyrin smiled. “Sir Avrin...now you know why we enchant the materials not only to support the size of the vessel but to resist and nullify the effects of natural events like this”.
Although tyrin showed a hint of pride he was still showing nervousness, at this point Gregson accompanied by a young lady in her 20’s who had long scarlet hair and wore detailed armor that fit well but still showed her curves as well as some cleavage and her legs with only armored boots to cover.
This girl also wore glasses and showed a mature expressionless look on her face. Her focus was fixed on the mana tornado even as her and Gregson approached tyrin and Avrin.
Gregson looking at the mana tornado sighed and clenched his fist “magi Tyrin...w..What is this?! I thought the Archmages predictions were that we would make it out of this a day before it forms again….”
Little did they know that the Archmages intentions were more fixed than they thought? Tyrin was confused as he rubbed his head. “I...I don't know...I need to contact him and call for assistance…. I doubt we can outrun the tornado…”Avrin looked carefully at the mana tornado…
Meanwhile inside an underground chamber hidden in the central continent a man wearing red and yellow robes with the insignia of humanity on his back knelt down in front of a fire that burned like a rainbow.
The man who was kneeling looked to be in his 80’s and had a long beard, in his hand he held a large staff with several crystals of all sorts of sizes and colors seemingly growing out of the wood. He spoke softly.
“Oh mighty creator of humanity the being of knowledge the goddess of wisdom and our mother. Goddess Ishana, your humble servant Archmage Gillian has come to report news”.
The flame that burns like the rainbow began to take form as it settled down before forming a figure out of its beautiful flame it was only the shape and showed no other features other than a fit beautiful body and curves.
This figure then spoke softly as the image of Ishana. “Gillian my child I see you have done as asked. “ Gillian nodded with a frown. “m...My goddess when you came to me in my sleep you asked me to lie about the mana tornado to one of my disciples seeking advice...and I did indeed tell him that the conditions were well and there was not going to be a second event but what could be so dire a goddess needs to be involved in?”
The flaming avatar walked delicately to a throne of blue material and sat down crossing her legs. “Gillian when I created humanity I had not known your curiosity would grow to become so strong. But as your creator I will take responsibility. On that ship lurks a being I cannot see anywhere near. On the elven continent an event happened, Lenaya had felt her gift to her people activate.
She also could not see within a kilometer of that area it was as if it didn’t exist. At the center of that void that kept moving from place to place I also couldn't see.”
Gillian widened his eyes. “m..My lady a gift to the elves from the goddess Lenaya?...I..Is that allowed? “ He questioned almost jealously. Ishana gave a soft chuckle. “Do not worry. Other than me no other god knows of this Lenaya asked me to use my power to see what had caused this but I had the same result of her.
Although I’m sure Septim already knows as me and Lenaya discovered the angel lord leave he must know something but I dare not interrogate him. A power capable of blocking a god's sight is something unheard of assuming it is an enigma ability user to force the activation of activation of a goddess's gift is something truly remarkable but also worrying.”
Gillian tilted his head. “Goddess Ishana would it not be simple to ask goddess Lenaya to question her elven kin?...” Ishana let out a pained sigh. “Although we are gods we also follow rules. I am here because my knowledge and wisdom allows me to avoid the other gods’ detection but this is all I’m able to do.
Lenaya is not capable of doing this and can only send simple gestures unless all gods agree for her to go down. I would do so on her behalf but the elves do not have a temple for me to manifest in and I’m sure you know how difficult it is to construct one.”
Gillian nodded “many many dozens of painstaking years my goddess.. But for a being like that are we sure whoever it is will perish?” Ishana was quiet for a moment. “I foresee this being shall perish in the ocean the sacrifice made by my children is small to pay for its death for if this being lives on I see in the future where that sightless void goes ash and darkness shall run rampant I cannot allow this”.
Gillian nodded. “My goddess t..then isn't it better to tell the other gods of this?....” Ishana smiled softly her near featureless lips showing it slightly “by doing so they would find out Lenya’s gift I do not want anything to happen to my dear friend so this is a favour from me to her”
Gillian nodded. Little did either of the two know was that the real reason they had not been able to see Avrin was because of a small favor the true god had done for him. As he becomes stronger this sightless void would shrink until he has reached a peak of power capable of rivalling the gods. But until then he has hidden them from their sight.
The large vessel was cutting through the waves as it tried to return towards the closest landmass to the east. Water covered with static crashing against the edge of the vessel made it nearly impossible for the crewmen to do anything else one touch would paralyze or kill a lesser man.
The narrative has been taken without permission. Report any sightings.
Gregson held his hand in his head “damn our luck….” lady Karina the scarlet beauty folded her arms as she showed slight signs of worry she spoke her voice carrying the maturity and elegance of her appearance “Sir Tyrin is there truly nothing we can do?”
Tyrin who had returned looking as if he had lost hope was gazing blankly at the mana tornado. “T...the lord Archmage Gillian isn't….answering from the magi sphere I have…. what is going on….what is this…” he sighed.
Avrin gazing at the tornado for several minutes now was sizing it up taking into account how large it is. “-Its not as big as I thought if I don't try now I’m going to regret it later…-” walking towards the end of the vessel and jumping up above the ship's stern he looked at it.
This caused Karinas attention to sift to Avrin. Tyrin spoke out “Sir Avrin...please do not waste your breathe only a sigil wielder would be capable of saving us now….” Avrin whispered a soft name “Astaroth..”
In his hands a large demonic looking scythe formed out of a black energy. The presence of this weapon was so demoralizing and ominous despite being in complete hopelessness everyone within a dozen meters of Avrin immediately retreated with fear. Tyrin, Karina, even Gregson quickly retreated back as they looked in fear there hearts beating.
Avrin took a deep breath this would be the first time he would use this weapon he had no idea how to properly use it. “-Fuck off...no way I’m going to die out here after taking a step forward….you want to kill me?!!-”
Anger in his face as he remembered how he had died and how painful it was and how god had brought him back to use him as a piece for his amusement how he was almost killed then captured and how he had spent years to train his body coming up against annoying obstacles and having to go around them or fall without being able to properly defeat them.
The scythe responded to Avrins anger and frustration as dark matter surged within it the blades edge began to give a low humming sonic like sound. Avrin tried to imitate the slash the doppelganger had used to cleave the ground hoping to achieve the same result.
“The swing of the scythe was horizontal to maximize the area it would hit”. By doing so a large wave of dark energy was released screeching as it tore through the air, a bluish light seemed to form and split apart.
This blue energy was mana being devoured as the wave of black energy expanded and shot towards the mana tornado. This black wave of energy seemed to grow larger bit by bit as it devoured mana seemingly not losing one bit of strength.
The force of the slash had caused the back portion of the large vessel to lift off the water nearly toppling over before crashing back down into the water causing it to shake violently as screams and shouts of the screw roared out in this event.
The black energy wave reached the tornado before it passed through it, the entire tornado seemingly dispersing in an instant but also caused the energy wave to shoot upwards and grow larger due to the energy it absorbed.
Reaching the clouds that it would then blow apart the color of the energy wave went from black to a bluish black that kept growing larger. An attack that had a limitless appetite. The surge of energy that kept going leaving the planet's atmosphere after a minute had grown incredibly long in length.
***
In a golden palace of light with heavenly flame delicately blowing on braziers with attendants of pure white tending to a being who wore an open robe showing a perfect body shape long glowing white hair as well as a strong figure. This being gazed down into a pool of green transparent water but the water reflected the world of Seleria, this being's eyes were twitching nervously as he focused on a single object.
This object was the dark matter wave that kept growing in size a truly devastating weapon in a universe of mana. “What monstrous power…” this beings ghostly voice softly echoed.
The dark matter wave had reached a point where it suddenly stopped growing and then softly disintegrated after traversing a fair distance from Seleria. This being clad in gold and white robe sighed in slight relief before a soft voice called out to him.
“My lord Septim...what could this mean…?” the man revealed as the god Septim turned back and spoke “I do not know Nefria I cannot see into it my vision is blocked”.
Nefria, Septim's wife and goddess of light wore a dress that covered her completely revealing only soft features such as her curves but her face showed appearance was not at all average but a little above so, of course this wasn't to say that one couldn't feel that her charm was indeed magnificent
“Could it be an enigma?...” her voice like a gentle breeze that would touch someone’s ears as if silk ran through their skin. Septim took a deep breath and shook his head “there is that possibility I will have to summon the other gods I’m sure they also felt it”.
Back on Seleria the clouds had parted and the ocean was clear, Avrin was kneeling a trail of blue blood seeping from the mouth slot of the mask as well as the eye sockets his right arm had been torn off and he looked near death.
“T...to much...I used to much….” he coughed out before summoning Astaroth. “Asura!!!” he called out like thunder to which a black blur appeared on deck lazily before gazing in the distance at Avrin.
Like a berserk bolt of lightning, seeing his master in a state of pain he appeared near him in only a few seconds. “m..my room...take me to my room...I need...to heal…” Avrin then lost consciousness not only was the pain insanely intense but the particles making his body were shaking causing more pain every time it would try to heal they would split and shake.
“Master hold on!!” Asura roared out like a ravenous creature before holding Avrin in his arms and disappearing below deck. Gregson was silent his mouth opened as he looked at the clear skies, Karina and Tyrin as well they had only seen Avrin go to the top of the stern before a powerful fear overcame them.
in a few seconds the mana tornado was torn apart but that ominous energy continue on splitting the clouds and passing on before it vanished from sight.
“w...what horrifying power….” Tyrin fell to his knees gripping his staff. Karina's lips quivered as she fell to her knees as she placed her hands onto the ground “incredible….simply incredibly my god what a world we live in”.
Gregson swallowed his words after the sight of Avrin's near death state caught his attention he then understood Avrin’s value skyrocketed to be able to match the power of a sigil wielder but if Avrin were to die here then it would be a huge loss, he called out “medics to lord Avrins room!!!” he called out adding the title of lord to Avrin after realising his true value.
Avrins blue blood had caused a slight trail to form, Tyrin looked at a small pool of it carefully before an idea formed in his mind. He quickly used a containment magic as he took a sample of his blood. Down the deck Asura stormed through the hall, his steps causing the enchanted wood to break slightly yelling at everyone to step aside. Asura reached the room gently placing him on the bed and looked at Avrin.
“Master….if you perish I’ll be left with these weird humans!!” Asura wasn't sure how to express his fondness for Avrin. He knew due to Avrin in the past he suffered greatly but in return he obtained power that had potential and also got to experience food and the true trials of life as well as gain intelligence his people could only dream of.
Avrin laid there unconscious the blue blood on the mask slowly drying up. Deep in Avrins consciousness, he laid on a patch of grass that was only several meters in diameter he felt his soul quiver slightly and it made him feel sick.
A voice then spoke after signing, “wow you really something Avrin…” Avrin despite being in such a weak state knew who that voice belonged to and couldn't help but give a faint smile. “o….overestimated…” he whispered out before a click sounded out from the being and Avrin felt his soul instantly recover like a miracle.
Avrin leaned up and looked at the being he had come to know as the true god. This being was looking behind himself at the planet of Seleria despite this it was not a room of space but rather a miniature version of it.
god then spoke “but I tell you that was exciting… This feeling of being surprised all the time is something I enjoy a lot so this time for making me happy I’ll help you out a bit and also give you some advice.”
Avrin stood up and kneeled respectfully to god as he offered thanks “thank you.... and since you're in such a giving mood please give me some advice on the events that had occurred to me so far…”
God thought for a moment before speaking “very well I’ll do it like this. Every time you manage to impress me greatly I’ll do you a favor that is reasonable. I will start from the beginning.”
Avrin sat down cross-legged as he expected this would take awhile. “Sky metal is indeed 2 gods that had collided and formed into one, you have seen it and understand it as well as me. Showing you during the start would take too long, I won't go on about it. But I’ll also tell you that  during that brief moment when those gods collided the power is intense enough to distort the laws of this universe and cause a tiny rip into another universe.
This allows a small, very small portion the energy of that universe to imbue with those gods and the closest universe to this Avrin is your own considering I had gotten the idea from it. So the result is always dark matter imbuing with them except in rare cases.
That being said the dark matter in that metal reacts to you Avrin it is empowered by your presence like a parasite wanting to be fed. At first it tried to absorb you into itself, to feed but you beat it back.
When your body took it in, the metal gained abilities as it was absorbed into your core. This allowed it to manifest and create a spectral dimension of this world to combat you in it. I expect you will face this every time so let that be a free tip but keep in mind these battles are important.
It is a battle of dominance where the loser is absorbed and the winner controls the main body. In this case you won and gained a boost in power as well as the sky metal scythe, Astaroth.
Although you were careless and used 5% of its power from the get go you have only just attuned yourself to that weapon”.
Avrin looked confused. “Attuned?...” God nodded before he waved his hand they were transported back in time inside the exact room Avrin had been trying to do the pulsing dragon inside and his body was right there in the meditative state but it was like this version of him didn't notice them at all.
God then spoke. “The pulsing dragon did not work because Astaroth was blocking it, wanting your attention entirely. It was only when you formed it and held it out in the real world that your powers linked together forming that contract although the weapon is you and you are that weapon this contract solidifies that”.
Avrin nodded every word God spoke was like a treasure to him he had hopped many times that he would have a chance to ask and here it was in the open for him. “How do I control it?.” God chuckled at Avrins question.

chapters.title: V3: Chapter 61 Arrival.
chapters.content:
Full Pr credits to spectrals second voluntary pr SuperDoeDoe. hey guys here is an early release of spectral courtesy of your 2nd pr super pls give him some rep for his troubles ^^
now i know i said i was planning to release the pictures but since this is an early release and i have another raw in hand i can afford to let this out :)
Please Rate/Follow/Favourite/Spread this story :D ---------------
“Don’t be dumb, everyone knows you have to walk before you run. Just because Astaroths full potential can split celestial bodies in half with ease it doesn’t mean you can’t limit it to be as strong as a dull scythe. Slowly release the limit, as you progressed your emotions during that attack, it helped fuel the weapon without a limiter and caused it to attack in such a way. But you're lucky I stepped in and stopped it from getting bigger.”
God notioned towards the attack, if he had not used his power the wave of dark matter would have kept on growing, devouring the mana of the universe towards the end of time. “That attack is dangerous for you right now, don’t use it again and when you gain experience in using that weapon you will be able to remove the devouring ability of it and only leave the attack itself.”
Silent and looking at the miniature Seleria Avrin felt it was still the only way to stop the tornado and this was confirmed by god. “But you did well, in one timeline you miss your mark and the energy wave splits Seleria in two ha-ha.”
Avrins face went green at the thought of that, it felt like a joke but a warning as well towards Avrin. “Don’t worry in all the other timelines that’s the worst case scenario. Oh yeah it seems you caused quite a stir towards the other gods.”
Avrin was confused at first before he realised what he had done “they found me because of that?” he spoke nervously. He knew he wasn’t ready to deal with them. “That’s right in fact the one called Ishana set you up before this, she is indeed a crafty one and intended to kill you right away without taking risks. I guess it’s my fault though.”
Avrin was confused about what had happened so God to blame himself “um?” Avrin spoke wanting to know, God of course satisfied his curiosity, “I made it so no god would be able to see you within a certain distance, of course I guess this made them curious as to why they can’t and felt it was some evil or something like that hehehehe.”
God seemed to make light of the situation but Avrin was fuming inside “y..you almost got me killed because of that….” Avrin whispered carefully not to raise his temper at God.
“Don’t worry” after second of being quiet, God spoke “and it’s done, all the gods have completely forgotten about you Lenaya still thinks that little gift of hers hasn’t been activated. If any of their servants ask them they will only be confused and think they are being messed with and they won’t be able to detect any disturbance or energy imbalance you cause he-he”
Avrin thought “wouldn’t it be easier for you to make everyone I know forgot about me other then the people I’m with now?” Avrin spoke as if trying to suggest a hidden favor. God only snickered.
“I know your intentions boy, although I am limiting myself you're still as transparent as water in a glass cup. Besides you would one day regret it if I did so. So for now just continue to become stronger”
Avrin nodded as he thought “my body isn’t doing so well….how long will it take to recover?” God smiled “then I’ll take that as your favor all healed cya!” Avrin immediately understood he had just been cheated “no wait that’s not fai-..” in a near instant his eyes opened as he stood up and looked around his body seemingly healed completely as if nothing had happened although the blood on his clothes still present. “D..Dammit he cheated me “
Avrin spoke while laughing to himself. “Master your healed already!!” Asura came through the side behind him several people dressed in medical attire. “Ah what a waste and here I thought these humans could help.. Master you’re too strong…”
Avrin stood up and fixed the tightness of his mask a bit “you lazy creature where were you when things were looking dim….” Asura was quiet as his stomach rumbled he mumbled. “Damn I just ate 5 minut… I mean I wa” Avrin glared through his mask. “Forget it you sinful cat” he spoke in a joking manner.
“It's all done I doubt anyone other than me could of done anything anyway…” he remembered Gods advice carefully he would have to be careful he doubted God would make them forget again. A sudden knock on the open door caused them both to turn around and gaze to see Gregson make his way past the medical team that seemed shocked and frozen at Avrins recovery ability.
“Magnificent Avrin your ability is much, much more than I expected. Without a doubt you are one of the most powerful warriors I have ever seen. To dissipate a mana tornado…that attack of yours is truly frightening, your weapon as well that scythe is menacing...all the sigil weapons are accounted for I can only assume it is something crafted so finely by the dwarfs using dragon flame?...”
Avrin was silent before nodding “you could say that it was a gift” lying through his teeth. Gregson chuckled his mind at ease he didn’t have to worry about another tornado forming to him Avrin would step in again.
“We have already turned back to reach the central continent, we will reach it in 3 days so until then feel free to do as you please. Will you not at least reconsider dinner tonight?...” Gregson spoke trying to through in one last pitch for luck.
Avrin was silent and sighed giving in “very well I will attend tonight so for now I would like to clean up.” Gregson nodded, noticing the blue blood stains of course he didn’t dare question or provoke a being he underestimated who could easily tear this ship in two. “Very well if you need me I will be with the magi Tyrin and lady Karina. “
Avrin nodded and Gregson left. Looking at the ground Avrin saw what Gregson’s curious last intentions were, he spoke “Asura I’m sure I left a trail of blood I want it all gone….” Avrin was on high alert after Gods warning although he wasn’t sure if anyone was capable of using it for ill intentions he didn’t want it to be used for anything other than his own purpose.
This was blue blood from him and the blood itself leaked a bit of dark matter. “Leave it to me master, not one drop will escape my scent.” Asura left to go handle it while Avrin quickly stripped after shutting the door until he was naked from head to toe.
Using the nebula mist he engulfed the entire room as well as the mask and his clothing before re-condensing it into a ball leaving the room spotless as if a bloodied body hadn’t even came by.
The condensed ball of mist reformed and shaped into a new set of clothes that was neatly folded with the mask on top. With Avrins boost in strength reforming things of high quality had become much easier a task.
As he placed the clothes on the bed to separate them he heard the door handle turn to open as well as a female voice “lord Avri-....” the door was opened and holding onto the door handle gazing at Avrins naked body was the scarlet beauty lady Karina.
Avrin blinked dumbfounded and intensely annoyed but still frozen “-knock….why don’t they knock!” Karinas face turned a crimson red as she eyed Avrins crotch before she quickly closed the door slamming it shut before the sound of her metal clad boots sounded out down the hall before it vanished.
“Hmph….I'll deal with her later…” with his eye twitching in irritation. Avrin quickly put on his newly formed set of clothes as well as the white mask. Of course he left the cloak off and began to exercise from push-ups to sit ups as well as methods developed over the centuries of Earths advancement.
Several hours later he had entered a pulsing dragon state to feel for his body to see if anything had changed. Other than the worrying joyful aura Astaroth gave off, nothing had changed. Leaving his room Avrin headed down to continue his sightseeing of the vessel.
Tyrin quickly met up with Avrin and smiled “l..lord Avrin remarkable, your power is incredibly remarkable!! “ Avrin sighed at the endless praise he was receiving. Later he would rather keep it low key as if this spread he would not hear the end of it.
“Tyrin I would appreciate it for now if things were kept to a hush, I do not want to reveal myself and abilities yet.” Tyrin was quiet before nodding in agreement “I also agree lord Avrin if the demons or beast tribe knew we had a second power matching a sigil wielder no doubt they would act. Also lord Avrin…”
Tyrin pulled out a vial an inch long and half a inch wide that had a thick blue liquid inside of it. Avrin knew quickly what it was. Tyrin spoke “your blood, I was examining it and I can't detect mana in it...I can't feel anything other than the weird other worldly aura it emits, its almost scary. I hope you will allow me to continue to research this?”
Although Avrin was annoyed that he took a sample of his blood he was grateful that he at least went to seek permission. In a swift movement Avrins right hand vanished with great speed snatching the vial from Tyrin hand that made him blink and step back in shock and surprise as well as fear.
Avrin spoke softly “Tyrin as good of a person as I have seen you are. Some things are better left unnoticed, please do not attempt to research anything to do with me without my permission.” Avrin spoke in a tone that was more then enough to warn.
Tyrin sweated and quickly bowed knowing he was no match for the monster he had seen before “p..please forgive my actions lord Avrin.” Avrin nodded “no need to act in fear I am only covering my trail I will be attending tonight's dinner I will have some questions then. Until then would you happen to know if there’s an armory or a black smith on this ship?..”
Tyrin was surprised at Avrins change of heart but even more so at his question, he nodded. “o..of course for repairs and such please follow me” after some time passed, Avrin was gazing around the large open room that was layered with metal the furnace of the blacksmith was surprisingly large and the room was kept tidy with several people working and repairing armor and weaponry.
Avrins eyes lit up like a child in a candy store as he looked at the raw ore as well as ingots and many hammers and tools used. One would think a blacksmith used a couple of tools, a hammer, tongs, etc. But if you paid attention you would see there was much more. Several types of hammers, light hitter, heavy hitter and a hammer with a curved shaft to get that perfect side hit that won't ruin the metal.
Many things that would help detail and make the best armor possible with those tools. There was no such thing as a blacksmith who half assed things because of the difficulty of the job, one had to have a passion to take on the task.
Avrin was quiet as Tyrin looked on. “Lord Avrin it seems you are fond of this craft I will leave you to it. I will make sure you are allowed anything here.” Avrin wasted no time walking over to an empty corner bench as he began to start to improve his own skill.
Many hours passed and the blacksmith had gotten quiet, only a single hammer constantly pounding sometimes hard, sometimes soft thuds, sometimes the sound of hot metal touching water sounded out.
Around Avrins bench all the smiths were watching with tranced eyes, impressed and somewhat jealous at Avrins ability. 14 ingots of iron with a 90% perfected ingot form. Grand masters would be able to reach that 100% but it isn’t to say that this % isn’t impressive in itself. There were only a handful of grand master blacksmiths, all of them dwarfs and only 1 in the central continent.
One of the blacksmiths spoke “damn….who would of thought lord Avrin is a highly skilled blacksmith and here I thought the higher-ups only sipped on tea and ate cake ha-ha.” Avrin smiled at this stereotype, it was quite funny and he hadn’t seen many nobles so he wasn’t at all sure if it even was a stereotype.
Taken from , this narrative should be reported if found on Amazon.
Beside the 4 iron ingots were a pile of 8 steel ingots with a 91% perfected formation rate. With every ingot Avrin improved it usually took hundreds upon hundreds of piles of ore before one would improve but Avrin had many things going for him.
Several more hours passed before he was complete. 21 iron ingots between 90-96% perfection form. 17 steel ingots 90-92% perfection form as well as 19 copper ingots with an astonishing 98-100% perfection form.
The higher quality didn’t necessarily mean the harder it was to form. Every metal needed to be mastered perfectly. Forming a hard steel ingot needed strength and focus. Forming a copper ingot required a delicate control of strength as well as precision since it was a weaker metal.
As a blacksmith improves his muscle strength he has to readjust his strength to form the ores he once attended to, that being said one could say as long as one improved they could never master a single ore perfectly, mainly because there improvement required them to readjust themselves to it.
Before long 2 attendants came to see Avrin for dinner. Without his cloak on Avrin sat polishing the ingots he had made, not only him but also the other blacksmiths joined in to help. He had after all saved them a lot of trouble and even gave them quality ingots they had been training for years upon years but never capable to achieve results like this.
Clearing his throat the first attendant spoke “lord Avrin dinner will be served in 5 minutes would you like to bathe first before attending?..”
Avrin stopped and looked around seemingly broken from his enjoyment. His motivation was one day forging sky-metal instead of experiencing the pain of absorbing it and even making a pen name for him and selling his wares to see how well he could do with his abilities.
“It’s fine I’ll be there soon“ he spoke, the attendants nodded and gave him directions. As Avrin was about to leave the blacksmiths all looked and nodded in appreciation and respect and some even asking him to come back and help them out sometime.
Emitting a soft thin layer of nebula mist over his body the mist itself disintegrated and ate away at all the dirty that had covered his skin lately the fire and effort in smithing wasn’t enough to make someone of his stamina sweat so he was good in that department but he made sure this thin coat of nebula mist emitted over his clothing to eat away at the dust and soot that gathered.
Some people that saw this were a little worried as they saw him glowing faintly and immediately stepped aside thinking he was angry.
Before long Asura found Avrin by scent and was walking beside him “master I heard the nobles eat food that’s incredibly tasty, I cant wait!!” pursing his lips Avrin then replied “Asura when we reach the central continent I’m going to have you train enough to make you lose weight so enjoy your fill while it lasts he-he.“
Avrin spoke in a way that was both joke-full and threatening at the same time that made Asura realise maybe he did eat a lot, “he-he sorry master have mercy.” Before entering Avrin knew it would be weird to attend in the same clothes he was wearing all day so when he and Asura were alone he engulfed them both in nebula mist and changed the design on their clothes.
Now showing white and gold instead of black the hood also was thicker so one would think the mask was apart of the outfit. His outfit looked more elegant and noble like. Asura on the other hand barely looked different in the fact that he looked scary and towering.
The two attendants saw Asura and Avrin recognizing them both and were somewhat impressed by their clothing fit for a noble and even a king. they opened the large door in the hallway that was decorated as if it weren’t even on a vessel.
Inside the interior of the room was surprisingly good with a chandelier as well as a long dining table with tyrin and Gregson already seated. “Ah lord Avrin lord Asura I’m thankful you have joined us tonight. Lady Karina will arrive shortly with her lieutenants.”
Avrin took a seat that was moved for him by an attendant while Asura sat beside him. The table itself was covered in a white cloth that seemed to be finely sewn. The table and chairs seemed crafted of high quality wood and lacquered gracefully.
“How could I not attend after being asked so many times “ Avrin spoke in a tone that one wouldn’t know if he was joking or annoyed but Tyrin replied softly “ha-ha I apologize Avrin but Gregson truly wanted you to attend how could I not assist a friend.”
Gregson nodded “indeed it’s as Tyrin says.” Avrin I wanted to discuss some things while Karina isn’t here. “They all began to speak on friendly terms without the lord honorific, thinking right now it was wasting effort.
“What would that be?” Avrin curiously asked. “Will you not reconsider my proper offer with your power you will surely be a high figure in humanities army no less then king Leo Zircus” Tyrin didn’t intervene in such words, as the truth was already a fact.
“No thank you the offer I proposed is one I like, I am not familiar with the current army humanity has and would find it more enjoying to start from the bottom and make my way up.”
Gregson grinned as he placed his elbows on the table and chuckled “Avrin surely someone such as yourself is a one man army what could anyone other than a dragon or sigil wielder hope to accomplish facing you.”
Avrin felt he wasn’t off the mark “for me its not about combat situations but more so understanding the armies structure. A general is only as good as his subordinates. Where I am from a philosopher called sun Tzu reaffirmed this.”He began to explain the story of Sun Tzu and the art of warfare. ((A.N I have to book of the art of warfare mainly for spectral regalia so I can understand things if you are interested to what story he is explaining http://journeyeast.tripod.com/suntzu.html))
Both Tyrin and Gregson’s faces turned pale and then the green Gregson spoke “t...truly this Sun Tzu man is someone of great intelligence….humanity could learn much from him….” he spoke in complete respect.
Avrin had to learn a lot ever since he was a general just because the space age had come it didn’t mean lessons of the past couldn’t be assimilated. At that moment the doors opened and an attendant spoke “Lady Karina with her lieutenants have arrived. “ Karina in an elegant blue crystal dress accompanied by a female also in a dress and a male in a noble outfit made their way bowing in respect with prideful looks on their faces.
“I apologize if we are late..” she spoke softly before making her way to her seat she snuck a glance at Avrin before going a deep red and shutting her eyes for a moment as if trying to suppress the hot steamy figure that she had seen.
Avrin only frowned a bit but was at least glad she didn’t tell anyone he had to have some point of respect for this soldier. “All is well lady Karina. Now that we are all here let the feast begin” with a clap of his hand the food began to flow out, of course the one excited the most was Asura who barely kept himself from salivating.
With talk about the state of the world as well as events of the elven continent and what each group had discovered from Gregson’s battalion, to the rose blades the conversation turned to Avrin.
Karina spoke first “Avrin it is finally good to have a chance to talk to you. Gregson has boasted highly of your skills and I was not disappointed you are surely a force to be reckoned with I do hope an offer has been set for you?”
Gregson chuckled “Karina don’t bother Avrin is like an immovable object not budging, as for our deal unfortunately he made me promise to not reveal it.” Karina frowned a bit and added jokingly “oh but is royalty not permitted?” she grinned and Gregson laughed knowing she was joking.
Asura gouging himself on food was quiet and they continued to speak surprisingly Avrin didn’t speak much even when asked questions he remained silent and mysterious other than yes’s and no’s.
The night went on without a hitch, God didn’t just make the gods forget but Gillian as well as Tyrin had forgotten about some things as well Gillian about the lies and the event and meeting with Ishana and Tyrin about Gillian contact during it all.
As the night went on 3 days seemingly passed, well in those 3 days Avrin had reserved a sparring room and sealed it off while he practiced with the extremely limited Astaroth. He had figured out by willing it he could place a limiter on the weapon that wouldn’t break unless he purposely forced it off and the weapon would not resist this limiter.
Avrin had learned that Astaroth was an incredibly agile weapon despite its size. The blade seemed to cut through the air as well as the mana that made up that air a truly terrifying weapon. While spending these few days training
A voice echoed across the ship using a magical enchantment as if being spoken through a speaker. “Prepare to land we have reached the central continent the port city of Lumiria!!”
Stopping his training Avrin was sweating a bit, he had made sure not to waste any time doing nothing such as sleeping or resting. He had been training 3 days straight without any breaks not even when he wanted to do some blacksmithing.
He made sure to tell Asura to stop and inform the 3 higher ups not to bother him, that way he could maximize his time. Wearing nothing but pants Avrins nebula mist as if sentient immediately removed the sweat, dirt and grime from his body “I still think it would be nice to have a bath “ he spoke to himself with a soft smile.
“Master come out already I’m bored lets go lets go!!” Asura seemed excited, Avrin had even developed a unique sense during his training session. By sending a faint static of dark matter out he could use the mana particles as conduits and allow him to feel the presence of everyone around him.
For this advancement 300 meters was his limit although he was able to augment his eye, this sense was a double safety measure. Making his way up seeing the commotion of the crew prepare Avrin finally made his way up to greet the ocean air, as it touched his skin it was a somewhat refreshing feeling.
But what caught his attention was the large city ahead in front of the vessel with several ships beside it going back and forth trade, military, fishing, and civilian. All sorts. “Welcome to the central continent Avrin.”
Gregson spoke as he walked beside him “training hard I can already see you have gotten stronger by your presence.” Avrin felt Gregson was using instinct or just trying to get points with Avrin.
“When we arrive is there anything I need to take care of?” Gregson nodded “I would prefer if you came to the capital with me that way we can handle what you like better. I have also been informed that you are fond of blacksmithing and apart from the dwarves the human capital boasts the second best blacksmith shop.”
Avrin nodded “very well “ a smile adorning him under his mask there was much he wanted to do and see what humanity was like what had they accomplished he would find out soon.

---------------
The docks of Lumiria were a hub of activity ever since the large vessel carrying Gregson's forces arrived, as well as the objects and exotic things they had acquired from the elven continent. Of course their destination was obviously to the capital city.
Gregson explain to Avrin as both him and Asura followed behind, being guarded by a small group of soldiers. Gregson explained that the goods were something the king enjoyed showing off, being able to acquire unique things was all the rage at the moment between kingdoms and their royalty.
Although Gregson was a soldier of a different kingdom he was currently tasked with serving the capital as if he were born there, it was something all soldiers of high rank and promise would do as a show of good faith towards the empire.
“You would think such a large empire would have its own forces to handle a menial task. I can’t help think the more you tell me the more it seems that you were sent just to go pick up some goods this king sounds irritating.”
Avrin expressed a little dissatisfaction. Gregson although a soldier of the empire showed a little discomfort at his words as did the soldiers. Who would dare talk back to Avrin, someone who showed to be on par with the king in strength.
“Master I think this human king must be strong to order servants of others to get things for him”, Asura spoke somewhat complementing Leo in a positive yet negative manner.
Gregson whispered softly “my lords, although I dare not talk back to you, because we are in the human continent people see the king as a god like figure. It would be best to not talk as such about him, those people do not know of your strength like those of us on the vessel have witnessed.”
“I suppose you're right.” Avrin agreed he wouldn’t talk so much about the king's negative ways in his own eyes he ruled the way he saw it and it matter not to Avrin.
The 3 of them made their way further down the docks ramps watching as the many people were unloading crates with the emblem of the empire on them. Avrin was feeling his body was quite eager for activity, he truly wanted to train and get used to Astaroth. His 3-day training was but a blink of an eye to him.
“Lord Gregson when will we be departing to the capital?” Gregson smiled “Right now actually, the carriage should be here soon, do not worry lord Avrin you are not missing much these port cities are usually very similar.”
Gazing around there was quite a heavy presence of soldiers and guards, not just on the docks but also on the streets. Avrin couldn’t help but ask why to which Gregson replied “humanity has many hidden enemies and we can never spare enough to protect ourselves, the beast tribes despise us for what we have done and the demons are crafty.”
The beast tribe Avrin could understand but from what he knew regarding demons, this seemed rather pointless considering their magical capabilities. The carriages had been prepared for several minutes and were already awaiting them.
3 carriages in total 1 for Tyrin and Gregson, 1 with several designs portraying roses and blades for Karina and her lieutenants and 1 for Avrin and Asura that didn’t look too bad.
Asura frowned as he looked at it, “master I’m starting to hate traveling, it’s boring and I want to fight…” Asura was starting to get frustrated. Fighting and combat was in the creature's soul and with this intelligence and power he was craving to show it off.
“I agree Asura, when things are settled we can head to a battlefield and improve ourselves for as long as we please.” Gregson chuckled lightly as he spoke “lord Avrin with you and lord Asura on the battlefield I’m afraid there won’t be many people left when you are done with them.”
Avrin had a bit to do, he knew he had to visit the blacksmith in the central continent but that was only a hobby, his main focus was establishing himself first. As they separated, Tyrin was already inside the carriage. Gregson parted from Avrin who was making his way to his own carriage.
A soft voice called out to him. “Lord Avrin would you be so kind as to allow this lady to accompany you?” both him and Asura turned to look seeing lady Karina with her attractive armor set up with several of her members who looked a little stunned at their captains words.
Avrin felt no reason to decline her, maybe he could also learn a thing or two from her. Then again she may have intentions, at this point Avrin wanted to see what she want. “I would be honored if lady Karina would accompany me on this journey.”
Showing a pleasant look Karina nodded gazing back at her group before making her way inside the carriage of Avrin. Asura though snorted quietly and hopped on top of the carriage and lay down casually. The guards who were escorting them were used to this .
As Avrin entered the carriage ,the small convoy began to stir and move. Avrin leaning on his leather covered gauntlet looked out the small glass pane window. Karina also stared outside and the quiet awkwardness continued until they left the port city’s gates with the many carriages containing exotic goods as well as the soldiers on a horse like creature and marching to their sides accompanying them.
Avrin was the first to break the ice. “Karina we haven’t talked much have we and yet I find it interesting that you're assertive enough as to want to accompany me?”
Karina turning and gazed innocently at Avrin and removed her glasses that had a golden frame and fairly thin wide lenses. She began to clean them with a cloth that seemed to be sewn well. Her voice spoke in a tone as if she tried to make Avrin fall for her.
“Lord Avrin you are quite powerful to the point where your attack seems to be on par with sigil wielders although that was only on one occasion...and you were at near death… I can only assume such power comes to a large burden that being said I can presume that you can only match a sigil wielder for a short duration of time.”
Widening his eyes under his mask only for a moment Avrin showed a hidden smile behind his mask “-this girl is indeed intelligent but what is her intentions? I can't let down my guard around her so for now I’ll give her the benefit of the doubt.” – “indeed I’m only able to match a sigil wielder for a very short duration of time but why are you asking such sudden questions?”
He spoke softly he wanted her to think that was his limit if she knew he could only get stronger it may cause some issues. “My lord Avrin, my uncle, King Leo Zircus, would find your services extremely important won’t you consider accompanying me to see him?”
Avrin raised a brow despite all his facial emotions hidden behind the mask. “Sorry I serve no one, everything I do is for myself” making sure his tone was clear and to the point. Karina seemingly experienced, didn’t want to give up and went on.
“Avrin I’m sure Gregson offered you quite a deal was it to join his kingdom so that they may receive a higher position in Humanities Empire? I can tell you that you are wasting your time, Gregson is a man who has limited sight and is stubborn. If not for his family’s past deeds as well as his daughters abilities he would be only a common officer.”
Karina showed a devil like face as she crossed her legs. Avrin began to see a second side of her, he was a little surprised at how quick humans here changed. One night eating and laughing with each other, the next killing each other. Avrin hadn’t seen anything on this level even as a general, it was all kept down because only those with skills would be given an opportunity.
“Gregson seems like a fair man and his deal is nothing of the such, I merely want to obtain things myself. And I am not fond of serving a king I haven’t even met.”
Karina gave a light laugh as she stood up and walked over sitting next to Avrin. She placed a hand on his lap and lightly traced it up his outer thigh near his inner thigh while speaking in a seductive manner.
“Avrin the truth is I was mesmerized by your power, a man capable of achieving something that needed the gods themselves to make. I have also seen your appearance something only the gods themselves can match oh how handsome you are. Wont you consider joining me then and assisting me? Humanity has many enemies and with each other we can achieve greatness.”
Avrin felt like puking at this woman’s words as well as her touch, not only was she seducing him but such a speech could only be reserved for a hero, a champion of good and Avrin had no intention of choosing sides he was his own man and those that choose to stand by him are the people that he will treat well.
He would love nothing more then to provoke her but he was in no position to do so. “Lady Karina..” he spoke as he used her title despite her calling him Avrin hoping the message would get clear “humanity is something I have no interest for. If the world were to go to war tomorrow with everyone picking the sides of their races I would choose to seclude myself while I wait for their petty rivalry to end.”
Karina backed up as she looked at Avrin with a bit of fear not only was he showing no interest in one of the few beauties of the empires advances but his tone and message was clear. This was something he was doing for himself and he couldn’t careless about what happens to the humans.
She inhaled and frowned. “I understand lord Avrin… despite this I must still make a report to the king. Should you ever change your mind then find me using this” she took a small metallic card from a slot in her boots and handed it to him. It was giving a faint glow and had an arrow on it with a red dot at the point presumably a tracking device.
“Very well” he smiled despite it not showing. She then moved up to the front and opened the door of the moving carriage. With steps of grave and showing her skills she jumped from it and used her footwork to gracefully reach the carriage of her comrades.
Asura's head popped down from the roof as the door was left open. “Master that whore has a big mouth….who would want to serve a human king ha-ha”
Avrin also laughed lightly “Asura shut the door you’re letting in the cold” he sarcastically spoke. The convoy continued for several hours entering a mountainous path that seemed eerily quiet.
If you come across this story on Amazon, be aware that it has been stolen from . Please report it.
Standing atop the mountain a group of large individuals wearing full brown cloaks watched the convoy. A masculine voice spoke out in a aggressive tone. “Is the trap set?” Another voice spoke out “yeah...this is the large one that left the port and they’re carrying some nice goods for the king, if we get them here we can make quite a bit of coin” the owner of the voice snickered.
Asura whispered as he was lying on the carriage. “Master…this smell....there are a lot of damn pests on the mountains, these are bandits right?...” Avrin nodded also feeling their presence with his newly acquired ability to detect.
“That is fine Asura they can do no harm to us, but use them to our advantage. Do not attack until I give the signal” Asura somewhat groaned quietly before agreeing. It had only been 2 more minutes before an incredibly large boulder was pushed onto the large ridge to block the path of the convoy, immediately Gregson came out with Tyrin as they began to issue orders.
From the top of the ridge hundreds of men wearing cloaks began to jump down as well as bombard the convoy with arrows and to top it off there were even some who knew magic.
Taken by surprise the convoy began to experience losses quickly and Tyrin who had tried to cast a barrier spell was shot in the shoulder by an arrow. “Gah!!” he cried out clutching it and falling down before he was dragged back into the carriage by several of his guards.
The rose blades acted quickly as they began to attack with grace and vengeance Karina roaring out “these leeches!!! Show them no mercy make them all suffer for all our comrades who have fallen!!”
Gregson had been surrounded by dozens of bandits who were hungering for his blood. “Filthy worms…” he uttered before a draw of his blade and swift movements allowed him to kill 5 of them in but moments.
But for as many as they killed many more replaced the numbers. The leader of the bandits standing proudly on the ridge with his arms crossed. “These dumb military types….they think we wouldn’t attack a convoy that has skilled people without being sure of our own numbers….we managed to gather nearly all the bandits in the region after we got the tip off that something good was on the way ha-ha”
Asura was clenching his teeth growling softly as his claws dug into the carriage to the point where Avrin started to see them from the inside “master….now????” Avrin smiled. “Not yet.”
Several rose blades had died or had gotten injured to the point where Karina who was killing several bandits with each swing was forced to retreat “tsk...to think that such weaklings have taken us by surprise FALL BACK!” she roared out.”
With each moment several lives were lost, the bandits were replaced but there were only a hundred or so soldiers who were guarding the convoy. The bandits started to attack the goods carriages to stop them, and Gregson immediately called out.
“Don’t let them take those!!! They are for the king!!” several soldiers charged and began to combat the bandits buying a bit more time but it was no good. With only 28 remaining asura was starting to salivate from eagerness..
“m..Master….nowwww?” Avrin grinned and formed a book in his hand as he began to read it while resting his head on his hand. “Make sure to kill them all…”
Standing up Asura's muscles began to ripple as his body grew 20% in mass, his teeth showing as he emitted a powerful monstrous killing intent that froze the nearby combatants bandits and soldiers alike.
He released a terrifying roar that caused the walls of the rock formations around the path and the hill itself to shake slightly. This froze the higher ranked bandits. With all gazes on asura he vanished like a static shadowy blur and in moments he had cleaved 17 of the nearby bandits in half before vanishing again as their blood and innards sprayed out.
Asura who was reveling in the joy of combat had begun to test some techniques that required live test subjects. Sending out sharp waves of dark air from his claws while his tail which had grown in length and thickness tore apart at the bandits.
The leader on the hill began to shake from anger and fear as he began to sweat “w..Who..no what the hell is that!!!”
Gregson and Karina who were also frozen as Asura tore apart the bandits who were starting to see the side of Avrin's so called companion, a monstrous beastly figure that had begun to paint the mountainous path red with the blood and innards of his enemies.
“HAHAHAHA” Asura laughed out and roared as the bandits filled with fear despite their numbers they begged to the bandit leader to flee, he clenched his teeth “you bastards kill it!!!”
Asura focused his attention towards the voice despite the screams and sounds of battle, he heard the voice that seemed to be targeted to him “kill me?...” using his speed Asura made his way up the mountain wall, tearing apart rocks and stone as he climbed up until he appeared in front of the small group of bandit leaders.
“go ahead….kill me” he spoke as if provoking them and it seemed to have worked in moments the group of 5 charged towards him with large battle axes and their own huge frames.
“You monster!!” One of the larger bandits called out while swinging his battle-axe down towards Asuras head. Reaching up Asura grabbed the head of the large battle-axe and clenched his hand shattering the steel that made it as if it were glass.
In a second he had punched a hole through one of the leaders with such force that it caused the air behind him to ripple and his innards to fly out before he dropped dead with a dumb look on his face.
3 of the leaders showing signs of fear, recomposed themselves before charging again but at that instant a shadowy blurs swiped across there legs and moments later there legs were torn apart before their bodies fell to the ground as they screamed in agony.
The shadowy blur shrunk showing its true form as did Asura's tail, who spoke, “ooo nice, I can use my energy to grow it to.. I wonder what else…” clearly the thought of mercy hadn’t popped in his head at all. He proceeded to kill the 3 using raw strength as if tearing a helpless animal apart.
His cloak and body soaked in blood he looked at the leader of the bandits with a monstrous grin. “Ah damn...I forgot one...don’t worry I’ll let you join those weaklings soon enough” as he began to walk towards the bandit who then looked behind to see his troops were already in the distance fleeing he knew he couldn’t get away.
As asura raised his right hand to destroy the human a voice entered his head. “--not that one, bring him to Gregson--” (A.N - is personal thought while two -- is telepathy)
Asura blinked as he looked around and spoke “master?..” Avrin who was in his carriage smiled and replied using a newly acquired technique. “-- This is telepathy Asura I’m using dark matter to transmit my thoughts to you using mana as link conduit I can also hear your voice as it transmits through the mana its quite an interesting ability--.”
Asura widened his expression revealing his teeth and smiling “master that is incredible I want to learn it too!” showing signs of interest. While Asura was occupied, the bandit leader took the chance to slash with a long sword towards Asura's head thinking the creature was crazy talking to itself.
As the blade hit Asura it shattered into pieces unable to pierce his defensive fur but it made Asura growl and in a half second he had tore the man's sword arm off “sneaky bastard…” he spoke but Avrin's voice called out again “--remember alive bring him to Gregson….--”
Annoyed and frustrated Asura gave in his masters’ request as he began to drag the screaming bandit leader down the small mountainous hill. The soldiers were busy cleaning up and carrying their dead away while Gregson was looking at a report of the casualties and damages with Karina by his side.
A sudden flash before a thump was heard. Asura had arrived behind them and dropped the bandit leader who was clutching his wound in pain while calling out “s...spare me my lord!!” he called out to Gregson who looked at Asura then the man figuring what the situation was.
Gregson called out “have someone heal this man's wounds….then chain him up...he will have his justice in the capital “ Gregson showed a deep hatred for this bandit. Karina’s gaze was fixed on Asura she looked at him with awe as well as fear, he had instantly changed the tide of the battle and an ambush at that. She began to think even more highly of Avrin “-two monsters….what are their purpose….-”
Asura then returned to his own carriage and Gregson dared not ask him to wait. “Master sorry I dirtied the clothes you made me…” Avrin looking out the glass pane seeing the mess “its fine I doubt its something that we can fix for it to not happen again.”
Avrin's intention was to get a good look at how well Asura had improved and what he was like in a combat situation which was why he suppressed his own desire to fight to get a better understanding. He wasn’t let down Asura indeed improved despite the creature doing hardly any training it was a little scary.
But this was somewhat expected, Avrin would also improve over time without training but he does so to further increase the improvement rate. A flow of nebula mist flooded from under the carriages door frame and engulfed Asura who didn’t move as he knew what was happening.
In seconds the blood and stains on his clothing were removed as if nothing had happened. Tyrin who had a bandage over his shoulder and was walking to Avrin's carriage stopped, his eyes widened as he gazed with awe, “-i..incredible…thank the gods I was more careful with my actions…-”
A sudden flashback of Tyrin as he showed Avrin the vial of his blood and Avrin snatching it from his hands and destroying it. Tyrin was smarter and wanted Avrin's trust he had given it to him on purpose knowing it would be taken away but also know that Avrin wouldn’t suspect anything else from him.
Which is why Tyrin had taken a second vial and hid it well, he was the most eager of the lot to return to the capital so he could study the vial and see what secrets Avrin's blood held, his intentions of course would be kept secret.
With Asura's outfit now cleaned he jumped back onto the top of the carriage and laid back down “master, I’m hungry…” he groaned in a pitiful manner that Avrin ignored as Gregson now approached the carriage with Tyrin beside him.
“l..Lord Avrin your companion Asura is surely a force to be reckoned with…Thanks to his actions a lot of our dead comrades have received revenge and the culprit who orchestrated this all will be put to justice. I fear what would have happened had you not agreed to come with me.”
Avrin tried to down play it all as some thing on this scale after what he had been through was nothing. “I apologize I had not acted sooner, I expected your soldiers to be capable of handling it but I had no expected there to be so many bandits.”
He spoke although it was a lie and he knew that there were at least 500+ of them using his dark sense. “It's fine lord Avrin for now we will be departing quickly just in case another attack occurs.”
With the rose blades mourning their dead comrades and Karina busy with it all, the convoy quickly went on after collecting there dead. Over the course of the trip they had been able to properly bury them and hold the proper ritual as they entered a town only a few hours travel from the mountainous path.
With the convoy fixed and mercenaries hired for protection their travel hadn’t met any more resistance with a force of a few dozen soldiers and 100 mercenary’s, who would attack them in the open.
Continuing on Avrin admired the sights of the farmlands, they were incredibly well cared for with villages littering the horizon. It seemed humanity took advantage of the land. As time passed by they had finally reached the capital city of the human empire.
