“Erebus, you understand that because of this, you have caused a system where others will be looked down upon. But that being said, this system is somewhat useful. From your information, people can be reconverted if they achieve results.
Forget that. I want you to gather the Archbishops when we are done here and have them reconvert every individual leaving. Only tell the cardinals to not do so. Erebus blinked a little “But My Lord, although it is fair, what if things get out of hand? People with that strength may want to leave…”
Avrin took a deep breath and nodded. “This is why I leave that decision making to you. Have them know that their so called Lord has arrived. I want them to know I do not look down upon them and want to help them. To do that though, I need you all to listen to me.”
Carefully making mental notes, Erebus replied “Lord Avrin, do you not intend to stay with us?” Avrin shook his head. “I can't. I have 2 other purebloods like you with me. I also need to train as well as develop connections in the human kingdom. Know this race is known as Spectral, the one who created me named it as such and so shall it be”
Avrin couldn't help but speak in such a tone. It was too interesting. He felt he played his role much better now. Erebus, although eager to ask about the one who created him, dared not interrupt. “Remain here for a month more. I will allow you that time to convert those who need a new life most.
After that, I will send another pureblood. He is a blacksmith with incredible potential. He is no less than you, so consider him a real brother. With his help, take our people to the Northern Continent and slowly strengthen yourselves while concealing yourselves at the same time.
The last thing we need is people looking to take advantage of us as well as the servants of the gods taking notice.”
Listening to Avrin’s advice was a big relief to Erebus, who until now had been making the decisions. Of course, for Avrin, this was good too. By sending settlers ahead, they would prepare everything ahead of time for him, while he would gather information and improve himself.
To help speed things ahead, Avrin decided it was time to share some knowledge with Erebus. This method is something he wasn't fond of immediately, but it would help Erebus and his now new people a lot.
“Just as I had done for Asura, I will give you some of what I know to assist you. This is something you will have to moderate yourself to teach others. “
Erebus nodded, staying quiet as he had been mostly doing during Avrin’s entire speech. Making his way to him, Avrin emitted a ball of nebula mist.
Avrin’s idea was simple and less of a hassle. He would store information inside this mist and then solidify it, allowing Erebus, during his own time, to absorb it bit by bit. Of course, Avrin had to be selective in this regard.
“Leave me for now….” Avrin spoke, knowing this would take some time. Erebus froze a little before quickly leaving, not daring to speak. Avrin focused solely on the mass in his hands “Knowledge of some fighting techniques, the Pulsing Dragon… yes that will help, Void Blade, Void Sphere, the danger of Sky metal.
I dare not think what would happen if it absorbs one of them. Who Asura and Eitri are, how to form Infernium, how to be a blacksmith...” After having spent more time selecting and adding the information, Avrin felt there was no strain at all; it was much simpler than forcing it into one’s head, until he finally decided on instructions to share.
These instructions were what to teach everyone, and not to share the information of Infernium due to how dangerous it could be if it circulated outside of their race. He couldn't stress enough that he wanted everyone to learn the Pulsing Dragon, as well as how to fight and blacksmithing information.
By adding certain positive things, down the line, it would be advantageous for them. Although it was easier than forcing it into someone's head, the amount of time needed to put it all together in a way that works as well as make it absorbable with no backlash, was annoying. Finally Avrin stopped a half day later when the sun was starting to rise.
A large soccer ball like sphere that was crystalline and held several different colored mists inside of it floating that were about was formed. “-Erebus… Come-” He used the telepathic link before Erebus rushed in a few seconds later with a look of joy that turned to an even greater look of joy after seeing the sphere in Avrin’s hand, having an idea of what it was.
“Inside this sphere is knowledge I have selected as well as instructions on what to teach. Make sure you take the time to recreate the right parts, but also do not stress yourself over it. Everyone who learns this is to train and share a bit of information to the next person until they all know it.
Remember the time frame I have given you. When I send Eitri whom you will know about soon, then you will leave. I'm sure you already know how to form gold coins. When the time comes before you leave, I'll give instructions to you and Eitri”
Erebus nodded “My Lord, I thank you for this gift and for not abandoning us. I'm curious, what will you do now?” Avrin stretched slightly, causing some bones to crack a little from having sat for a half day.
“I'm off to go train myself and make good use of my time as well as ponder these events.” Avrin spoke softly as he made his way to a back exit. “My Lord, I wish you luck in your training. I will lead our people to greatness!”
Saying nothing more, Avrin left. “-This changes everything… Although the positives outweigh the negatives, it doesn't remove them. With this, there will be more of a chance of people finding out about us. I need to focus on training myself. Unfortunately, I need to postpone the main event with Gregson a bit further and come up with a new agreement. It no longer benefits me, as I have the fates of others resting on my shoulders now-”
Avrin’s goals had shifted significantly. At first he wanted to join the army from the lowest rank and work himself up to gain an understanding of their methods, but he wasn't so sure it was the most useful course of action that made use of time anymore.
Frowning to himself, Avrin wondered if the course of action he took was the right one for the long term result. No one ever said that by following your heart you would always succeed. Some sacrifices must be made.
But the thought of being a part of something again and having a people who wanted to start anew, become a part of the Spectral race, was something that caused him to smile. Making his way through the tunnel, he had just realized something.
“Why is this city built upon ruins?” Confused about this, he ventured on, using his divine sense to guide him, almost like sonar. Having spent a couple of minutes, he found a passage connected to a sort of sewer system.
Somewhat fazed by the stench, he dared not remain more than he should, and used the nebula mist to eat away at the ceiling under a location hidden beside an open area. Jumping out of the freshly made hole, he looked around before sealing it with the same nebula mist used to devour the ground.
The city had become a hub for activity, as he casually glanced around the corner seeing drunkards with women under their arms as well as adventurers looking for a place to rest. Avrin gazed up at the night sky and let a sigh escape his lips.
He began to ponder if maybe he was becoming a bit too soft. With hundreds of individuals singing tales of adventurers past, as well as songs most women would find appalling, he took a step out into the open before his heart froze.
The entire streetscape, as well as the air and life itself, seemed to stop in time, as if someone had paused it with a remote. Not even a sound was heard as Avrin looked around in shock, he was freely able to move so he wasted no time bringing Astaroth out from its dimension.
Emitting his divine sense, he felt nothing at all. The sound of footsteps could be heard before a voice that was familiar eased the feeling of his heart tensing up. “To be honest, I never expected you would let them go like that and even welcome them with open arms, so to speak”
An individual clad in a cosmic white skin casually strolled by the frozen individuals as time had frozen. “This is a little different than what I'm used to…” Avrin replied softly. The being that had frozen time was none other than God himself, who had paid Avrin a visit. “Let's talk a little, and summarize what you have done so far.”
The entire landscape seemed to shift over, as if a page was turned, transporting both God and Avrin to a park like area. God made his way over to a bench and sat down as he looked up at Avrin, who placed Astaroth away as he felt no threat.
“Yet again you have exceeded my expectations. When I first created you as a Spectral, I thought your personality would change for the worse until you became a tyrant more or less. But with my omniscience limited, circumstances keep changing you.
In this case it's for the better. You changed a beggar into a leader of a faith. And that man then began to spread it to those he saw fit. Quite choosey.”
Avrin showed signs of nervousness. “I apologize… I didn't think I would be worshipped as a god.” A soft ghostly chuckled left the lips of God “No need to apologize, I care not for that. Free will is my greatest gift to life. If you choose me I am happy, if not, then it doesn't bother me at all as I am left with those who love me.”
A sigh of relief left Avrin as he remembered something, but as he about to speak, God, seemingly knew all, replied. “Do not worry, I didn't forget our deal. Remember though, I won't grant you anything that changes anything too quickly and unfairly. Well, other than that, what is it you want. I'll give you 2 wishes. First for changing yourself and exceeding my expectations, second for accepting those people as your own kind.”
Avrin was delighted and he let out a wide smile that was quite rare for him as he began to ponder things. “-Ok ok… Ok let's see…. Something... Should I ask for Sky Metal? No, that would be cheating… What about the location of some? Hmmm, what about information? Something I can use… Details of technology?... I'll consider it…. Ahh yes, that's it. I was so worried about it but this is perfect-”
God, who seemed to freeze like a mannequin with limitless patience, spoke. “A decision I see. Let's see“Reading Avrin’s mind in an instant, God replied. “Ah yes, you do have that teleportation ability. Well, it's more or less a work in progress, but I can see why you haven't used it. It's quite risky.”
Avrin nodded “I would like to make a breakthrough with it so I can freely control it without worry of destroying myself…” God replied “You are quite smart. You originally got the idea from the way you were executed. You break yourself into controllable particles and reform yourself. Very well, I'll make it easier for you and give you a breakthrough with nothing more when we are done. Now then, your second wish?”
Avrin nodded. He already knew what he needed. “In my current state, I'm not confident I can defend my people as well as myself. I need a way to improve greatly. Will you tell me a method of training in which I can greatly improve in a short amount of time?”
God was quiet for a moment. “The Pulsing Dragon is pretty sloppy, I'll tell you that. In all the countless universes, there are a number of good ones. Let me give you an example. If the Pulsing Dragon trains you at 1x speed, there are some that can train you at 5x 10x 15 to 100x the speed. But that in itself is cheating, so let's see. I'm not a big fan of borrowing things, so let's start from scratch.
When I leave, you will receive a breakthrough in your teleportation as well as achieve the first step to a new meditation technique that is perfect for you. Depending on what you discover will be the fact that changes its speed.
Don't bother with the Pulsing Dragon anymore, you will improve slowly considering you're rate of improvement is far beyond what it has to tell.
Although the techniques it has are still useful, but try to be original and make your own. It's more fun.” With a soft laugh, God vanished, not giving Avrin time to reply. And as time resumed, a spark was felt in his mind.
If you discover this tale on Amazon, be aware that it has been stolen. Please report the violation.
“Ah... That's it! Damnit how could I have not seen it in the first place…”  The breakthrough Avrin received was regarding teleportation. The answer was quite simple. His Divine Sense’s range was significant, and he could also empower it.
It hadn't occurred to him that teleporting within his Divine Sense would be easier. Extending it outward using a bit of energy, he found Eitri’s now abandoned blacksmith shack before he began to teleport himself.
His body seemingly converting to dark matter before a warp like feeling and a near second later he reformed at a position he sensed. He turned red, embarrassed by such a thing. It had completely slipped his mind.
“I need to pay better attention…” Sighing slightly, he emitted his Divine Sense again, before using the completed ability he named Divine Step, mainly on the fact that he needed to establish his Divine Sense and it allowed him to freely teleport within it.
He reformed outside the city walls as the range of his Divine Sense was still limited but improved not only every time he used it but as he improved as well. He made his way towards the mine that he and Eitri had been to since it was a familiar place to him.
Taking no longer than a few minutes with his current speed, he looked around before entering it and going inside the depths. Having encountered several of the previous life forms, they only added to his experience.
Avrin choose to dispatch them with a simple Void Blade before the same scene as before regarding cannibalism occurred, making it easier for him to dispatch the rest.
Relying on his Divine Sense again to map as much of the cave as possible, he found a room with a few stalactites and a couple of creatures sleeping. Unfortunately for them, he did not want blood to interrupt his training and decided to absorb them as they were. It was something he had also been interested in trying.
2 orcs that were seemingly sparring with each other while 3 goblins slept beside one another as they scratched their bellies and snored. The orcs had spotted Avrin first before charging toward him with that bloodlust.
Avrin had already released 5 Void Spheres towards every creature, and moments later, they were engulfed inside that sphere, unable to break out. The formerly sleeping goblins were screeching and panicking as they smacked against the spherical prison.
Closing his hand, the Void Spheres followed, shrinking down as they converted the living creatures inside to dark matter as they were crushed. The spheres returned to Avrin and seemingly fused with his body.
Only 20% of their energy pool was added to Avrin’s, not even enough to empower him despite their weapons somehow baring the flaming enchantment. He hoped Eitri would somehow figure something out. Avrin then found a comfortable position as he entered this new meditation.
He felt for his heart and all the dark matter that made him. The technique was straight forward enough for now and a bit of a hive mind was involved. The particles that made him had basic instincts such as feed, repair, slowly improve, defend, this technique’s first step was to empower every particle and give them instructions.
Of course, there were so many to do that it would take millions of years. But that was part of the short explanation given by God’s instruction in Avrin’s mind. Empower some particles, give them the order to then empower other particles, then give those particles the order to empower more. And so on.
Only when all his particles were empowered and fed with mana converted to Dark Matter would he be able to achieve step two. His body was like a light bulb purposely set on a dim light setting. Avrin knew this would still take time. He worried, mainly to know if the mana around him could cope, but for now it wasn't an issue.
A month had passed since Avrin had begun this technique. The cave room around him was distorted to an almost alien like area. With the entire place changing to the point where the few bugs in the room had their mana already absorbed and replaced at the same time with dark matter.
But Avrin, who was somewhat aware of this, developed a recycling method. Every week he would reabsorb the dark matter waste that corrupted the room and that would be like a second source of energy.
The dark matter waste itself was more useful than the mana the room held as it didn't require that little bit of energy to convert. It was all changed into matter and used to empower his cells. Avrin, who was sitting having not budged an inch for an entire month, his body shone a radiant blue with purple tints.
Having removed his mask and cloak for the training method, his face was revealed to have a glossy glow. Over this training he felt himself increase in power yet again. The exhilarating feeling of one's pores opening up to breath had reappeared as if each particle that made Avrin had been well fed.
If Avrin was to compare one particle now to one of his prior self, it would be equal to 5 of his weakened ones. In theory, this technique was to increase one's abilities to prepare him for the next step of the meditation, but the real fact was that one would store an incredible amount of energy within their very being.
Only someone who had control over such things would be able to efficiently use this technique, which made it perfect for one of the Spectral race. When the final particle had been empowered, as if a trigger had been formed, Avrin searched his mind again for the next step.
Avrin had discovered 2 things during his training. One was the knowledge of this technique God had given him being in the shape of a training manual with clear instructions. Avrin figured this may be for the ease of passing it on to other Spectrals or individuals.
He would not dare share his own experiences with them as he believed in hard work. The second was, as curious as he was; he was never able to turn the page in his consciousness to peak at the second step or any other. It was only until this moment that the page bent to his will and turned, revealing the next stage.
The second step again seemed to focus on the particles of one's being. Avrin felt that the matter/particles that made him would be the basis of this training, so he didn't feel disappointed. He was to slowly merge particles together until they became larger. Only when enough particles had formed that they formed a blue sphere and only when he had a million of those blue spheres would he be able to progress to the 3rd step.
With no one to argue with, and not currently in the mood to talk to himself, he tried it out first, willing one particle to slowly devour another. It resulted with the one devouring to only gain 10% of the energy.
Avrin wondered if this was truly the method. It was so wasteful, he knew he would have to devour more mana/energy around him to replace those lost particles and then re-empower them. Regardless, Avrin was extremely excited. As if playing a videogame with the building blocks of his body he continued this method.
Another month had nearly passed; Avrin had had no luck in finding a more effective way of combining them. Although he felt better than ever and significantly more powerful than he previously was, he was still a little disappointed.
Making his way out of the first tunnel after absorbing the dark matter waste, he had learned to permanently instruct his other particles to empower the new ones, saving him the time of doing it himself.
By now, the creatures had already seen Avrin and knew he was bad news and also felt a bit of the new power he had as he hadn't been able to contain all of it inside himself yet.
He wanted to vent his frustration out a bit. A large orc seemingly appeared from the side as it rushed towards Avrin, swinging its club around, thinking it had caught him by surprise. But at this stage, the only thing that surprised Avrin was how much of a dumb joke this creature was.
“Disgusting...” Waving his hand, he had toyed with a technique he had discovered by accident using his Divine Sense. When he was meditating, a stalactite fell towards him, and this made him act on impulse. Willing the energy of his Divine Sense to act, it formed an invisible force almost like telekinesis, smashing the stalactite away.
The method for this was similar, but unfortunately for this orc he was merciless, using the creature to vent his frustration its body exploded in the right direction, not one drop of blood as well as flesh going any other way other than right.
The stench, to Avrin, was bearable, but to the other creatures it's a feeding frenzy. Rushing towards the innards and remains of the orc, they began to chew and devour it. Avrin, having nothing better to do, was curious and just looked at the creatures as he mocked them.
“Eating their kind… Cannibalism at its finest…” Waiting 5 minutes he spotted one goblin which had been eating at the leg of the orc that had been blown to bits. The goblin, seemingly full, threw the leg away and wandered off.
Avrin widened his eyes and clenched his fist. “That's it!! How could I have not seen this…?” Another breakthrough had occurred. He rushed back to the area of meditation and wasted no time starting.
In a few moments, he was at the sight of all his particles. “When a particle devours another one, there's only so much more energy it can contain. What if...I adjust it a bit? The answer may not be devouring each other but a union…”
Bringing two particles together, he slowly began to will them to share their energy and bring them together. It had taken a minute before he achieved the result he was looking for. The two particles had bonded and fused together combining both their energies, creating a super particle with a 10x value of an empowered one.
“Perfect! Now, with the little time I have left, how can I properly cut the time down?”----------------------(Authors Afterword on this ch this May be a spoiler you have been warned)-------------------

Gazing at a lone particle that had a red color he found out that it was linked to another; it carefully seemed to emit a faint red light into that particle that would then slowly shift into that deep crimson color before heading off to another and fusing with it to form a stronger particle.
“-Perfect, although this process reminds me a little like programming. Other than this, it seems more willed. The particles themselves can't contain much information due to the energy storage being priority, but with this I can give a basic order. The order I need to give truly is simple-” Avrin was praising his ability to learn quickly.
Then again, for someone with a mind more advanced than a human’s, as well as his experience in analyzing things, it was made much easier. “-Let’s see. I'll be heading to see Gregson soon. I'll do it like this then. Each control particle takes a minute to form. I can't tamper with its structure but I hope maybe one day I'll be able to do so and create a particle with a larger information capacity to maintain my body’s needs even more so-”
Avrin was planning carefully, and had even named the crimson particle. One might see his intentions as weird and disgusting tampering with the body, but to Avrin, such a method could not lead negatively as long as he took his time and didn't rush things. Experience was also crucial, so for now he would have to use himself as an experiment.
His intentions were to take one of the Spectrals that were made and tamper with them, but he had long forgotten that. The very thought, with his current mindset and emotional state, irked him somewhat although if the person was someone who truly angered him, he would have no worry doing so.
But he would never try it on an individual who didn't deserve it. It may haunt him later, and for a being that lived for god knows how long, such a thing would be eternal torment. Having spent 4 more minutes, he had a total of 5 control particles prepared. Their structure was simple; red spheres that emanated a dark red light as they pulsed.
These control particles were issued with a simple task. Create a total of a few billion control particles then alert Avrin. With this, Avrin would then do the next step. He knew that these control particles needed at least 2 minutes, which is 1 minute longer than Avrin himself needed to create more of those C.Particles (Control Particle)
While he would do his own tasks, the C.Particles would also do their own tasks. For now, he had received a significant boost but wouldn't proceed further yet. When he had a billion C.Particles he would task half with fusing particles while the other half would recreate new ones.
Avrin felt if the balance was overly lost, it would be incredibly dangerous for him. He also didn't know what would happen if he had amassed too many type 2 particles. (Particles that are fused with another) Right now, in Avrin’s body, he had 3 types of particles. Type 1 particles being the normal that made his body. Type 2 particles which were 2 type 1 particles combined.
And the final Control particle which didn't have a type and could be considered the worker ant of the body that was maintaining things. Avrin knew creating type 2 particles at this point had a 30% chance of success, and they would need to be recreated using energy from his body.
Of course, at this moment, it had no real effect on him, but he knew that later on it may prove different. Standing up after breaking his meditation, he felt for his body without entering the meditative state.
He had been tampering with the particles for so long over the months that he could faintly feel the presence of the control particles. He also felt the birth of a type 2 particle. As faint as it was, it made Avrin smile.
“One day this will become a method I will have to think carefully if I am to share it with my people” Speaking as if he had already considered them his own. Slowly making his way out of the tunnel, he gazed back and looked around.
Avrin had felt a small attachment to this entire cave. It led to the discovery of a legendary ore it also made him lose an arm. It allowed him to meditate freely and the creatures also allowed him to create a breakthrough.
“Such a thing isn't needed, but alive or not, I thank you for being so hospitable” He gave a soft chuckle before heading off. Heading out of the tunnel, all the creatures of this cave had learned that Avrin was not to be trifled with as many had witnessed his power and his ruthlessness to attackers.
This made it eerily quiet. As if they didn't want to perish like the orc they had devoured. Having walked out towards the end of the tunnel, he saw the bright sun light and it made him squint a little, since he was in the cave for so long. His eyes needed only a moment to adjust.
Avrin hoped that someday, with control over his particles, he would be able to shift and change his body. Standing out wouldn't do him any good. Exiting the cave he took a deep breath of the air that entered his nostrils and stretched, before gazing up into the blue sky.
“--Asura how is Eitri?--” Avrin wasted no time using telepathy, “--Ahh, Master! The Dwarf looks good, good! Like us now, hahahaha--” Asura spoke, overjoyed. Avrin slowly began to walk towards the city of Altea's’ military quarters, taking his time while conversing with Asura.
“--Not his appearance, Is he awake?--” And Asura followed with his reply “--Yes, he woke up 2 weeks ago. Uhh, sorry Master, I forgot to contact you. Right now he is practicing his abilities--” 
Avrin let a rare true smile adorn his lips.
Avrin was quiet, as he extended his divine sense as far as he could to see how far it would reach. Having picked up the familiar energy of the Spectrals as well as Erebus’, Eitri’s, and Asura’s in their respective locations. Avrin’s divine sense had a range of 50 kilometers, enough to get a good scan of the outer city as well as the area around. “--Eitri, good morning--” Avrin grinned to himself before several dozens of seconds passed by before Eitri spoke “--Is that you boy? Can you hear me? How does this telepathy shit work!?--”
Avrin laughed quietly “--I can hear you. You sound angry. Is everything ok?--” Avrin had a feeling that if he saw Eitri right now, he would see him glaring. “--You bastard... Do you know how much that hurt! I swear, next time I see you, I'll return the favor--” Avrin continued to smile while heading down the path as several military trade convoys passed him. But those were occasional.
The convoys themselves had supplies as well as equipment and also new recruits. “--I'll look forward to it. How does your body feel? Worth it?--” Eitri, who stayed quiet for a moment, replied “-Yeah yeah, it's good, but it still hurt. So this is what it's like anyway, huh? The big bastard Asura told me what we were. A Spectral huh….. I thought you were some enigmatic user but it turns out I was wrong.
Just what are you?--” Avrin kept silent as he watched a small battalion of soldiers march past him dressed in simple plate mail with the emblem of the empire. “--One day I'll tell you, for now, I need you to listen carefully and please pass this to Asura. Both of you are to head to...--”
From there, Avrin began to explain where Eitri and Asura were to head to, as well as a quick explanation on the church as well as who Erebus was and for him and Asura to get Erebus to share some knowledge of the sphere that Avrin gave him.
“--Huh... What about you? Are you not coming?--” Avrin shook his head even though Eitri wasn't in front of him. It was a habit of his, as telepathy was still somewhat new “--For now, it's best if I gain as much knowledge and experience as I can here.
I may even get useful connections. Besides, now that you are a Spectral, you can possibly make all the Infernium you need. I don't need to say how important it is, though I'll trust your judgment--”
Eitri, who was currently folding his arms while sitting down on a log, laughed out, which made Asura, who was training himself, turn to him, confused. “--Does that mean I'm your race’s personal blacksmith?--” Avrin quickly replied “--Not at all.
You are your race’s personal blacksmith now--” Mentioning the fact that no matter what, the same sort of blood and energy now ran through his veins. He was only dwarf by height, and even then, one day when Eitri would learn to control his form that may be a memory.
“--Well, putting it like that, you make me sound like a traitor. But fine, I guess it doesn't sound bad being able to work with legendary ores. I feel this will also help me become a greater blacksmith. One day I'll rub it in that damn council’s face--”
Avrin stopped for a moment as he was ending the conversation “-- Asura, Eitri, Erebus, I'm speaking to you three now. Make sure everything is in order. Eitri, I'll be relying on you to learn as much as you can and practice and teach the willing in blacksmithing.
Asura, other than me, you are the strongest warrior. Make sure to protect them and teach those who want to fight. And Erebus, for the converts, you are known and most trusted. You will act as leader--”
“--Of course Master, Fine, Yes My Lord--” the three spoke in unison. Avrin added on, still communicating “--Erebus, Asura and Eitri will explain things to you when they arrive. But when they do, I want you to prepare to leave the city in a safe way.
Do not bring attention to yourselves, and head north. If you need to rest as you travel that's fine. But remember, I'm only able to communicate within my divine sense’s reach. Once you cross it, you will all be on your own until it reaches you again--”
Erebus replied. “Of course Master, about the issue regarding reconverting. It seems it isn't possible…--” Avrin blinked and frowned as he sighed physically. “--I see. It's a shame. Regardless, I suppose a proper way is to be put in order. I took the time to think it over carefully. The system you have in place isn't appealing, so I’ve come up with a base for you to work on.
Because my intention is to establish an empire, then we will go using that system, but make it more open and available to those who receive it. Consider yourself ranked as King, currently the highest pinnacle of power for our race other than myself.
Under king it goes in order. Grand Prince, Prince, Archduke, Duke, Marquis, Earl, Baron or Baroness, Arch Knight, Knight, Squire, these titles should be based on several requirements. Mainly on how strong the individual is. If their potential is to become a Prince when they are a Squire, it does not mean you are to make them a Prince based on their potential.
Strength alone isn't what will help this empire grow. We also need smart thinkers and craftsmen. Those crafters who are capable may also be allowed into this system. But to hold confusion a simple solution is needed. Add the title Craft, such as Craft King or Craft Duke. Eitri, what I said before, consider you a Craft King. But that isn't to say you won't be able to train and improve your strength--”
Eitri’s voice resounded in the telepathy. “--Fine, it seems simple enough. Craft King it is. But what if there is someone who is a Craft King with the strength of a Knight or something--”
Avrin took a breath and nodded, by habit himself.
“Good question. People who are ranked can share a different rank. For instance, a Craft King may also be a King. Consider my title as Emperor, but I am not as good as you, Eitri. In smithing, my rank would be Craft Duke, for example. Emperor and Craft Duke, This way people who want to improve themselves will not find it such a waste. Eitri that being said if you would like I can change your title to Craft Emperor. There is no doubt that with your talent and methods, no one will surpass you--”
Eitri replied after a second of thinking. “--My title is fine. As long as I am able to improve myself, I have no issue. One day, there may be a better talent out there that it can be reserved for. Hahahaha, don't expect me to call you Emperor though--” Erebus made a “”Uuu wuu” grumbling sound before speaking “--Y...You dare speak to His Highness that way?!!” He already accepted the rankings.
Eitri replied back “--This man... Hey Avrin, don't tell me the rest of our so called race is like this loon?--” Avrin laughed to himself which made a passing group of knights look at him strangely as they wondered and whispered weird things about him.
“No. Erebus is loyal and his intentions are good. Erebus, don't worry about Eitri, its fine. He is a good friend and has helped me a lot--” Replying with acceptance, Erebus was quick to forget it. “--If you say so my Emperor--” Having already replaced the Lord title was quick for such a man.
“--Asura, your training should be going good. In the northern continent, although it's lawless and no one will judge our people as much, I feel it may be dangerous. Do not start fights and only protect our people--” Grumbling to himself Asura finally agreed “--Master. If no one picks on me and annoys me, it will be fine--”
Avrin spoke again to the three so that they both knew as a reminder. “--For the matter of blood purity, it is strictly forbidden for you three to convert. If you are to do so get someone who is on the level of a Squire. As for how you will measure this, I have felt how strong the priests are and feel that their level will be equal to that of a Squire’s.
The narrative has been taken without permission. Report any sightings.I do not want our race to be filled with ranked individuals who are not capable and strong, only those who deserve it. I will try to figure out a method to deal with the issue of purity. That being said, those who want to live their lives happily are free to do so.
But for now, I don't want anyone breaking away from us. They are to know that the world may persecute us as this is the truth--”
“--Truly wise, Your Highness. And with such a way for us to work things out, I thank you for your advice. We 3 will make sure to prepare things well for you. And I'll do my best to judge individuals based on their strength. This also means we 3 will need to do our best to keep ahead of the others--”
Avrin was glad someone capable was in charge. This would let him ease up and focus on his own improvement. He truly thought it was too early to start increasing the numbers of his race. He lacked the experience and information he would need to try his best to fix things, which is why he couldn't focus completely on his training as he had been worrying about such an issue.
To him, it wasn't a matter of leaving them to their own devices. If someone got their hands on that power and figured out how to twist it, with Avrin’s current power it would be difficult to stop anyone in a high position of power who may have the backings of a Sigil Wielder or a higher force. “--Asura, Eitri, make your way to Erebus.
You should all know how telepathy works, so use that to communicate once you are within the reach of each other's divine sense. Otherwise, Eitri knows the directions--”
With the two confirming Avrin’s words, the telepathic link for them went silent, leaving Erebus who spoke. “--My Lord, such people, why is it you allowed such weird individuals your pure blessing?--”
Avrin was quiet for a moment as he also pondered it. Asura’s circumstances were unique, and Eitri was based on a friendly encounter Avrin had a hunch would lead to great things. So he replied. “--This is the way destiny planned it out. And such a thing isn't bad. They are both as reliable as you--”
Erebus remained quiet than spoke again. “--I will use that to better myself. Be well, my Emperor--” And with that, Erebus dropped the link and Avrin looked up at the sky as he was alone. “I wonder if you predicted something like this would happen”
He spoke, motioning to God, who was obviously watching all his moves. But he got no reply, which didn't disappoint him. After all, to God, this was a form of entertainment. With his divine sense in place, Avrin had already learned the different and familiar feelings of an individual's mana.
Although it was the same source of power, it was like a fingerprint. All different but similar and having been with Gregson before, he was able to identify his presence among them in the military outpost connected to the city walls.
As Avrin advanced and grew stronger, all his abilities would strengthen, and with all the knowledge he gained by using them, the way he could do things also changed and improved.
Teleporting based on sight changed to teleporting based on the range of one's divine sense. This branched into being able to appear near someone with a mana source. The world itself was filled with mana, so Avrin was easily able to focus it out to the point where it was like it wasn't there at all for him.
His body seemingly disintegrated into black and purple particles that vanished in the wind before as seemingly fast as he had vanished from sight he just as quickly reappeared seeing Gregson sitting down at this desk gazing up at Avrin before nearly falling back in shock.
“M...My god...Teleportation, That's impossible!!” Avrin blinked several times as he looked around, seeing the door open as two guards raised their weapons at Avrin, also somewhat surprised that he was inside. “Lord Gregson an intruder!!” Everyone was quiet for several seconds before Gregson broke the ice.
“N...No, its fine, you can leave…” The guards looked at each other then Avrin, and slowly left and shut the door. “Next time I'll use the door...” Avrin spoke and Gregson laughed. “Good idea. But teleportation, Have you always had that? Why use it now?”
Avrin replied. “It's a new trick. Also, you seem to be looking well. Something good happen?” Gregson put a document away as well as the quill and ink he used for it. “Indeed. The empire gave the appropriate sums and more to the families who lost their loved ones in that ambush. And the perpetrator of it all is being tortured gruesomely. Also, the higher ups are taking care of the rest. The king enjoyed the goods. An almost perfect trip”
Avrin walked over and sat down on the chair in front of Gregson's desk. “That's good to hear. And as much as I’d like to hear things, it's time we discuss things about me.” Gregson raised a brow “What's the rush? Surely you're not having second thoughts?”
Shaking his head, Avrin replied. “Some things came up and made things a bit more random, so the future will continue to be uncertain. My commitment will never be solid, so this is a warning in advance. “
Gregson frowned and moved his elbows onto the table, cupping his hands as he eyed Avrin. “You're trying to say you don't want a permanent position, but something that can be changed at will?” Avrin nodded. “You are indeed smart, Lord Gregson. I want to know what openings are available for me that won't tie me down for years.”
Gregson was quiet for several moments and then stood up, walking to the windows and closing the curtains. He then went over to his desk and took out a folded document, handing it to Avrin.
Avrin, who was used to technical documents, wasted no time opening it and reading it. His brows under his mask furrowed.
“You can't be serious?” Gregson laughed quietly. “Avrin, surely being a bodyguard isn't so difficult? “ Avrin shook his head. “Not at all... The issue is the boy is 14 years of age and is in the military? When did this massive empire start hiring soldiers at such a young age?”
Gregson only laughed, as it seemed Avrin showed a bit of worry. “Let me give you more information on a few things, Lord Avrin. Firstly, I'm not sure of your connections, but please keep this confidential. This boy is the grandson of the Prince of Misfortune.
Avrin, the bloodline he holds is rough and picky. His family wants to reclaim their position in nobility as well as the throne. But no one takes them seriously. They know King Leo will never lose his position, for not only does he wield the Sigil Weapon of humanity, but that strength has shifted into his bloodline.
I'm sure you have heard the news of his son?” Avrin nodded. “So he thinks joining the army will make him stronger? Sounds like he is trying to please someone” Gregson frowned and leaned back on his seat. “As I have said, his family is picky.
And he, out of his siblings, isn't a so impressive talent. He is looked down upon. His older sister and brother are seen as great talents, he lives in their shadow. I know his father personally; he is a good friend of mine”
Avrin narrowed his eyes. “It sounds more like you're worried about this boy. You seem to even know the circumstances.” Gregson laughed nervously “Avrin. A child without the love of their parents will suffer.
I fear if this boy isn't looked after, he may do something not only to put himself in danger, but shame his family because of his dream of impressing his father. He is fragile and weak willed, but he is willing to try. This is why his father proposed this idea of sending him to the military”
Avrin folded his arms. “Some father. It sounds to me that he wanted to be rid of the black sheep.” Gregson chuckled. “Precisely, I often talk to this boy.
He is kind and hasn't done anything wrong. And you are someone of immeasurable talent, which is why maybe you can teach this boy a thing or two, keep him out of trouble. The fact that you want something temporary makes it better. What do you say Avrin? This boy will be in charge of a group of 40 knights. “
Avrin was tempted to rub his head. “Even in charge of the lives of so many individuals...” Gregson shook his head. “Don't worry. It is only because of his base nobility. Every noble, based on their rank, is given an amount of knights to command. He would only be tasked with scouting around. But if you accept this, I'm sure you may make use of these men and women. “
Avrin thought carefully. He was a general in his former life. He would be babysitting a noble who commanded a fairly large group of knights. His task was to look after him and teach him a thing or two. “What If this boy refuses to listen to me?” Gregson spoke. “I'll change the hierarchy. It should be simple. You would be in charge of the boy, but second in command of the knights. I'll even give you tasks that won't seem boring. I only request you look after him for 2 years until he enters the branch academy, and if you take a liking to him, you can go with him. Hahahaha”
Gregson laughed sarcastically, as if trying to get a reaction out of Avrin but the opposite was given. “I see. Well this may prove good for me. It doesn't sound so hard, Even allowing me entry into a branch academy. My only request is you allow me to pick my own missions. And free roam of the 5 continents and their islands.
Gregson froze up a little. “W...What, But...such a thing... Why?” Avrin replied softly. “I will be bored out of my mind, and I also want to improve myself. This boy’s intention is to get stronger. He won't get stronger if you assign us missions to kill the run of the mill naked goblin with a pot on its head. He has to see the world and the creatures that are fierce.”
“Avrin, teach him a bit, not show him the dangers of the world… The best I can do, based on your strength, is allowing you free roam of the islands around the Central Continent, as well as free roam of the continent itself.”
Avrin kept silent, giving a seated position that said he wasn't convinced. “Ahh, Avrin, do not feel wronged. The islands hold dangerous Natural Beasts…. There's a legend that there may be a few dragons sleeping on those islands. “
Pursing his lips, Avrin felt it was good. “Very well, my last condition is I won't be ordered by anyone. And I may leave any time as long as I get the boy to safety first.”
Gregson smiled and nodded. “Agreed, Now then, payment, How shall we settle this. “ Avrin stood up “I don't need any money.” Gregson laughed, not doubting that with Avrin’s strength he was rich, and being able to not pay him would benefit the army as well.
“If you wish, with this settled please rest here tonight. Tomorrow I'll have Kael sent here as well as the unit prepared.After that, you can pick a mission and be on your way after receiving a Link Stone”(---------Authors Note---------)

The link stone given to Avrin was something that could be bound by infusing mana in two crystal likes stones. These stones would serve as a sort of walkie-talkie using the same frequency, in this case the mana that is uniquely shared between the two. Of course, that alone isn't all that's done. The stones must be created together from the same material at the same time.
Each stone is worth a staggering 200 Gold, and are often only given to high ranking officers or officials, and even then they may be needed to be given back after a task. After Gregson left to go take care of things, Avrin did indeed go to take the time to rest.
Although his stamina was incredibly high, this human like instinct of worry for one's self kicked in. Something that would take years to be rid of and even then such a thing is written within one's mind. Avrin rested on a bed, his hands behind his head. He wore nothing but his top, and his gauntlets were removed as well as his mask.
Of course, he had made sure to layer the walls with a unique ability of the Divine Sense. This ability would coat everything and would last for several hours. When something with enough force touches anything coated within Avrin’s range, it would send a signal back to him and awake him.
Avrin couldn't stress how careful he had to be from now on. He felt that now, the fate of many lives depended on him. His mind drifted easily into a willed sleep, nothing but darkness rushing his mind, a feeling he was now very much used to. To him, the darkness was neither an enemy nor a friend.
To him, the darkness was a servant that he would learn how to control as he himself grows stronger. Having trained and figured out several methods and always constantly trying to improve himself.
A full night had passed, and Avrin woke up to his Divine Sense triggering. Looking around quickly after waking up from a disappointing dreamless night but somewhat refreshed, he heard a voice. It seems the voice originated from the link stone that was glowing blue.
He had figured that not only did movement trigger his Divine Sense, but this mana device also did. He would have to think on it later. He grabbed the stone and looked curiously as a voice spoke.
“Avrin, are you there?” The voice was a little clouded, but it was none other than Gregson. Avrin replied, not sure if this would go through. “I'm here, Gregson. What's wrong?” He waited a few moments before Gregson replied, telling Avrin to meet him at a military camp 5 miles west from this outpost.
Gregson knew Avrin had teleportation ability, so he hadn't prepared transport for him, thinking he would be able to repeat it. And he would be correct. It was easily within Avrin’s sense’s reach. Of course, 50 kilometers was Avrin’s best range for Divine Sense when he was still and focused. On the move, his best sense could be a maximum of 25-30 kilometers. Keeping his mind focused he scanned around, as if a bird’s eye view of the landscape formed in his head, looking for Gregson's mana source.
After searching in the direction he was told, he found Gregson. His body turned to that same particle like ash. And as if a page had been turned, it reformed hidden in a storage alley, away from prying eyes.
“-This is so much easier. I don't think I'll ever want to walk again, heh-” He joked in his mind with a grin on his face. Having already equipped his cloak and gauntlets, he moved the mask onto his face and positioned it before walking out into the open.
Looking around, he saw many young teenagers training, as well many boot camp like homes. But the layout and structures were quite neat and seemed to be built well. Avrin drew some attention from a few guards who noticed this cloaked stranger appear from the alley. They quickly tried to go to him but stopped as soon as a voice called out in their direction.
“Ah, Lord Avrin, welcome!” He chuckled as he looked at Avrin. Gregson knew right away when Avrin arrived. The Link Stone also doubled as a sort of tracking device between the two. He jumped at first when he felt the other appearing nearly instantly, and gazing towards the alley, he knew it was Avrin. Utilizing this strange teleportation ability that everyone on this planet would kill for.
“Lord Gregson.” Avrin spoke to give the man face around all these soldiers. Walking beside Gregson, Avrin looked around. “This place, It's a training camp, correct?” Gregson chuckled softly “Indeed it is. Take a look over there.” Pointing to a young boy with light brown hair wearing a perfectly fitted leather tunic and brandishing a wooden sword with the look of a cat trying to act as fierce as a tiger
“Hya” The boy roared as he charged towards an older individual before barraging him with what Avrin seemed to think were careless sword slashes. He had trained in martial arts, although not for long, a genius like him was able to grasp many things and learn a lot. He could tell this boy was just rushing in with all his strength.
The adult, seemingly a soldier, easily blocked and countered, side stepping and turning to hit the boy on the back, causing him to stagger in pain before falling down. “Young Kael, you're doing it again. Please use what I taught you…”
The man spoke, causing Avrin to look at Gregson. “Isn't this a little unfair to me?” Laughing softly, Avrin joked, as if to say that Kael seemed too untrained. “Please Lord Avrin, the boy isn't that bad. He is willing to learn and get stronger. Motivation always gets the best of someone”
Avrin couldn't argue. “Indeed it does.” The two walked over to the group of knights who were laughing softly as Kael tried again and again. These soldiers seemed a little too relaxed in Avrin’s eyes.
During his position as a general, he rarely commanded a group of soldiers that had time to relax freely, as they were always in territory belonging to pirates or rebels, never having time to even blink unless the person wanted to be slow while doing their task.
“These men are part of young Kael’s personal unit. Men, women, each of them has nearly a decade of experience. Despite his father’s intentions of putting him here, he cared enough to make sure his son was tended to by experienced individuals.”
Thinking carefully, Avrin watched the boy, who was covered in dirt, giving that fierce willed look the adult training him seemed to be frowning, as Kael got back up again and again, no matter how much he tried, “Argh, boy ,you and that stamina!” The man roared slightly, and barraged Kael with several attacks but was sure to hold back.
“Lord Gregson, the boy’s siblings, what is their position to his again?” Avrin wanted to confirm where they were as opposed to their brother. Gregson replied. “From what I know, his brother and sister are doing quite well as 2nd years in Gaia Academy. They are truly the pride of their family. One might say young Kael here is the leftovers”
Avrin grinned to himself. He loved nothing more than to prove people wrong. From his teachers in the military academy to the soldiers in his old regiments that said he would amount to nothing. Constantly pushing himself to get somewhere to prove them wrong.
Their respect meant little to him. What he wanted most was to rub it in their faces and prove that they were the ones who were dirt. That was Avrin’s motivation. And as the years went on, he slowly learned to fit it in his duty.
“Kael, you're still not using the technique. You need to learn to block then counter. On the battlefield with a monster, they will show no mercy. You need to hold your own. We all needed at least 15 years before we could become strong enough!”
Avrin laughed out, which made Gregson blink and even the onlookers and Kael as well as the man acting as his teacher looked at Avrin. “15 years? That is way too long. 1 year is all a capable teacher would need for him”
Avrin tilted his head a little. Gregson blinked and laughed slightly. “Lord Yin, please do not mind Lord Avrin. He jests quite often.” Gregson then mumbled to Avrin in a hushed voice “Please ease up on this man. He is a Lord, 1 step down from me, and quite prideful at that... He is a lead instructor…”
Yin laughed and eyed Avrin up and down cautiously. “Indeed a capable teacher might. But I do not believe men who hide their faces behind simple masks. Or are you too pretty to wield a sword?” Not only Yin, but the other knights themselves laughed. Even Kael laughed, as if he was trying to fit in.
Avrin laughed softly “Not at all Lord Yin. You could say that after looking at people like you for so long, I have become too horrified, hahaha“He laughed along with them before they all stopped and Lord Yin gave a furious look.
“Kael, give this man your sword…. Let’s see if this man is actually worthy of berating me…” Kael blinked and slowly walked over to Avrin. Gregson stepped between Kael and Yin. “L...Lord Yin, please reconsider…. This man...”
Yin quickly replied “Please Lord Gregson. For speaking in such a way to my fellow knights, I won't forgive this man… Lord or not, after I make him eat dirt, we shall see who may talk…”
Avrin looked at Kael up close before taking the sword and stepping over to the small arena. He gazed at the wooden sword, seeing that it was chipped and slightly bent. Yin replied as he took an offensive stance.
“Look my comrades, hahahaha. This so called ‘Lord’ acts as if he has never held a sword in his life!” The laughing continued as Gregson rubbed his forehead and walked over to Avrin and mumbled. “Please Lord Avrin… Have mercy on this prideful man.”
Of course, Avrin didn't reply, and this made Gregson take several steps back. As a few silent seconds passed, Yin grinned. “Prepare yourself!” He rushed Avrin, dashing with all his might. One could see this man was a peak expert leveled warrior.
Whispers went out quickly “Lord Yin is truly something. He should enter the level of a master soon” One of the knights responded, but as the other knight replied back, they were left with their mouths open, dumbfounded at what happened.
In a near instant, Yin proudly struck the wooden blade towards Avrin, Avrin sidestepped effortlessly and tapped the man’s back with the wooden sword, causing him to stumble, losing balance and hitting face first into the ground.
Everyone was silent, even Gregson, who was starting to see Avrin’s level of expertise yet again. “Lord Yin, what are you doing down there? Does dirt really taste good?” Yin, who was shocked, blinking and looking around, clenched his teeth as a vein appeared on his forehead. He quickly back flipped up and began to barrage Avrin with quick sword slashes that even caused the air to ripple slightly, causing the onlookers to stand back in worry.
Of course, Avrin effortlessly dodged each one as if he were dancing elegantly around the tip of the wooden blade. As much as Yin tried, he couldn't get his sword to touch Avrin. It was as if he was a desert illusion. Once you neared it, the mirage would get further or change directions. You would never get there.
“Damn you!!” Yin howled as he raised the sword, gripping it with both hands. The wooden sword cracked and emitted a fiery mana as he roared, “Flame Tempest!!” Gregson then yelled out in reply “Yin, NO!”
The knights quickly scampered off. Even the other knights and youngsters training looked cautiously as the air around the wooden sword created a sort of vacuum in the shape of a mini tornado that emitted great heat like a fiery inferno.
“Isn't this too much?” Avrin responded, as if still not impressed. Of course, for Yin, who had been called out by this stranger, infuriated him even more so that he couldn't land a hit on him after berating back. He was like a child being led on.
He had no choice but to activate an expert level skill reserved for high officials of the army. One of few great techniques worth thousands of gold, Yin jumped and slashed the inferno like vacuum down towards Avrin, who showed no expression due to the mask.
“Idiot…” Avrin replied before slashing upwards with the wooden blade with great force, causing it to crack and shatter into millions of shards, but not before a wind blade cleanly cut the inferno vacuum in half, even though Avrin held back. And the inferno vacuum, although destroyed, weakened the attack. The blade of wind blew Yin away and then cleaved along the ground for nearly a few dozen meters.
This novel is published on a different platform. Support the original author by finding the official source.
The dust that kicked off and the heated air settled down as Avrin stood there as if not impressed, gripping the hilt of the broken wooden sword. “Intending for a death match? You're years too early to try that with me” Avrin spoke.
Yin, who crashed into a nearby haystack used to feed the horses, was quickly tended to by other soldiers and medics. Whispers of the individuals and students who were shocked and surprised yet curious at Avrin moved around.
“What technique was that? A wind blade, Is that the knight level gust blade?” Another shook his head and responded. “No way, It looked like he casually just swung his blade and it just destroyed Lord Yin’s attack!… He must be a master or higher…”
Hushed whispers and onlookers gazing between Yin and Avrin, Gregson gave a nervous laugh and approached Avrin. “I apologize…. Deep inside, I resisted stopping this, because I was also curious of Lord Avrin’s abilities.”
Gazing at the broken wooden sword, Avrin dropped it and replied as he dusted himself off. “It's fine. If it was not me who taught this man a lesson, he may have lived his entire life thinking he would never find another stronger than him” Avrin knew this all too well. Such a thing would be a life threatening mistake. Yin may not see it this way, but Avrin’s intentions may have helped him preserve his life for a longer time.
No one dared look wrongly at Avrin. In their lives, one would see maybe one or 2 expert level individuals face to face, and a master level individual would always be running a dojo or academy. Gregson walked over and patted Kael’s shoulder.
“Young Kael, I hope you liked the show. This Lord Avrin is the man I spoke to you about earlier today. He will be leading you and training you personally.” Kael, who was shocked and not able to utter a word, looked at Yin, then Avrin.
He had thought Avrin was some shameless Lord who built his reputation based on wealth, like many others have, and not strength. But he was proven gravely wrong. Gregson led Kael to Avrin and Avrin looked at him. But it was Kael who spoke first.
“F...Forgive me Lord Avrin for laughing at you earlier!” Looking at the young boy, Avrin couldn't help but remember Amias as well as his own master, Shimaru, who was with him for a short period but enough to build respect.
“Here is my first lesson. Never underestimate anyone unless you want to end up like Lord Yin over there” Avrin gestured to the wounded and unconscious Yin, who was being carried away on a stretcher.
Gregson smiled. “Kael, this Avrin is a great fighter. I hope you won't give him trouble and listen well. I guarantee you won't regret it. Lord Avrin, I will leave you here now. Please take this. “Gregson handed Avrin a gold badge with the symbol of a winged sword with gold edges and platinum in the middle.
Avrin was easily able to tell the materials in the badge due to his experience in being a smith. He took it with his right hand and gazed at it. “This is?” Gregson, as if expecting Avrin’s question, smiled, “The Altea Military Badge. It will allow you great treatment in all of humanity's cities and military bases. Just show this and it will be as if you are a king to them. Of course, I hope you won't abuse such authority” Gregson whispered to Avrin.
Nodding casually, Avrin spoke. “Good. In this case, I want to head off today.” Not only Kael, but Gregson replied. “L...Lord Avrin, so soon? Will you not become accustomed to things first?” Avrin shook his head.
“Nonsense, who knows when I will need to leave, you tasked me with teaching Kael, and I will not take this lightly. We will be heading to the Western islands of this continent” Gregson frowned but then nodded and sighed. “Very well Lord Avrin. I'm sure what you do is for the best.”
The day went by quickly, with everyone preparing supplies and horses on quick notice. Avrin also didn't want to be around when Yin woke up. He knew he would only cause a headache or seek revenge. Such a man’s mindset would not easily change.
And as several hours passed, Kael, as well as 40 of Kael’s knights, all got on horseback. Kael wore plate mail that a simple knight would never be able to afford. It seemed as if it's main use was to look good than to protect.
Avrin ignored it for now and got on the horse prepared for him, a large black stallion. Avrin hadn't thought horses existed on this planet, and although these creatures had nearly identical resemblances to horses, they were slightly more muscular and colored deeper as well as had simple manes.
The names of these creatures were actually Krins, but Avrin didn't like it as it felt weird. Especially because of their similarities, so he decided to just call them horses, not caring if anyone understood him or not.
Gregson stood up straight and looked up at Avrin. “Lord Avrin, please remember young Kael’s safety. The knights are all here and willing to give their lives for him and-” Before Gregson continued, Avrin lazily spoke. “An individual who relies on solely his subordinates for protection is no warrior but a coward. I'll make sure this Kael will be able to freely travel by himself without worry”
Gregson looked at Avrin then smiled and nodded “Very well Lord Avrin, I can't wait to hear good news. “ With things said and done, Avrin and the Feather unit, as it came to be known as due to it being light and barely noticeable since their actions were simply scouting, continued on down the path. Their destination was the western island’s largest island, The Twisting Lands.
The island itself is off limits due to it being significantly filled with natural monsters that put orcs and goblins to shame. With only a few military outposts on the island, Avrin’s intention was to train Kael there.
He came to learn of the island with some basic knowledge of a book he had absorbed prior to things. Filled with carnivorous plants and creatures that are all known to twist a grown man into mash it is where its name originated from.
The Feather unit silently followed Avrin and Kael, who was riding behind him nervously, and sped up to ride beside Avrin. “Lord Avrin. When do we start my training session?” Avrin, who was tampering with his Divine Sense constantly to try and efficiently use it, replied.
“When I please” Kael blinked and frowned as he spoke. “Lord Avrin, Lord Yin would train me for several hours a day, surely-” Avrin interrupted the young boy. “The Twisting Islands, when we arrive, your full training will begin there.”
The Twisting Islands being their location caused Kael to quiver with fear as well as the knights behind him. Some of them had been there before and had seen many horrors, not wanting to go back. But in this case, they had no choice but to follow.
One knight rode up. This was one of the officers under Kael, Henreth. “Lord Avrin, I heard we are heading to The Twisting Islands. Won't you reconsider to one of the lesser ones?” Avrin continued his pace and replied. “Why?”Not caring for the man’s words.
Henreth bit his lip a little and spoke “I'm not sure if Lord Avrin knows this, but those islands are filled to the brim with monsters that will make short work out of our unit… I have never heard of a 40 man unit casually training there, 100 maybe but 40? It's suicide.”
Avrin chuckled to himself, which made Kael and Henreth look at him. “You worry too much. If I knew it was too dangerous, then why would I lead a small unit there?” His words made sense, and because of Avrin’s show of power, a majority had figured his strength was at a Master’s level, so they felt a little safe.
The Central Continent of Sajuran was a large one, and after spending the rest of the day traveling, they had only gotten 30% of the way. Which could be considered significant for such a land? They hadn't encountered any monsters, something the humans of Sajuran pride themselves on.
Fanatically hunting them all to near extinction to protect each other, the dumb monsters, like goblins, knew to never expose themselves or make an estimated location known in fear of a small army destroying them.
Camp had been set up with several tents and fires prepared. Avrin was sitting 30 meters from the main camp in his meditative position, enjoying the wind blowing against him despite not moving an inch, as if he were a rock.
Gazing at the progress of the control particles, he was happy his effort paid off. A total of 5000 control particles and rising by 2 every second and higher was climbing. Of course, converting a matter particle to a control particle he needed to spend a bit more energy to create new ones.
His only issue was what would happen if his body contained too many particles. Would it be able to sustain them? Surely it would be covered in the information God had sealed in his mind. For now though, it wasn't an issue for him.
A young voice called out. Kael approached Avrin with two bowls of a meat stew made from a rabbit like creature the knights had caught earlier. Kael himself could be considered handsome or cute to many female individuals, but compared to other trained nobles and his siblings, his powerlessness made him unappealing. Especially to many of the females that come from noble families as well as train to become strong, to them he was a cute face and nothing more than a weak one at that.
Avrin broke his meditation and turned to look at Kael, who offered him the bowl. He took it and thanked him quietly. He raised his mask slightly and began to eat using the wooden spoon. Kael watched Avrin nervously to see if he enjoyed it.
“Boy, what are you looking at” Avrin spoke, a little uncomfortable from his staring. “I...I'm sorry, Lord Avrin. I wasn't sure if you liked the stew, since I made it myself.” Avrin knew this boy was trying to get on his good side, which would be pointless since he would train him either way.
“It's good” Avrin replied. He hadn't eaten a meal that wasn't synthetic for a while. Even then, those were usually rations. As the two were silently eating, Kael spoke “Lord Avrin, what was that gust blade you used on Lord Yin?”
Avrin responded simply with a “No” and Kael responded. “That technique was incredible. The flame tempest is something King Leo himself created. To see it effortlessly destroyed... What technique did you use?”
Avrin felt it would be good to get this boy eager to train, so he played his game. “No technique. It was raw strength.” Kael pursed his lips, frowning a little. Yin had scolded him every time he used raw strength, and to see it being used to defeat him was ironic in a way. “Lord Yin lied to me then… Raw strength is superior!” He pouted.
Avrin shook his head. “Only when your opponent is weaker, Technique is indeed valuable in combat. Compared to me, Lord Yin was just weaker, and myself more trained. In real combat, don't underestimate your opponent. I only acted as such to Yin because I am a good judge of character and read him well”
Avrin spoke, as if trying to make Yin’s reputation more easier on himself and not belittle him too much. Kael nodded. “Lord Avrin, can you teach me how to become strong like yourself one day?” Kael’s words were a sort of cliché, but in truth, in such a situation no one could blame him.
But it also made Avrin laugh softly. “Who knows? Maybe one day. As long as you are willing to learn, I'll teach you as much as I can. “Kael smiled and began to eat his stew before it got cold.
Avrin’s intentions were simple.
Based off of Erebus’ converting many times, Avrin discovered that he would be able to inject a small amount of dark matter and will it to not convert the person but instead focus it solely on improving the person.
Of course, the person whose body it is in would never be able to control it. Secondly, Erebus, who discovered this by accident, found he couldn't control it well. Avrin felt he would have a better time controlling it.
With understanding in dark matter particles, his order would be simple for every single particle inside that stream of dark matter he had yet to allow in Kael’s body. And that would be to strengthen his body.
Of course, Avrin was still unsure of this method and wanted to see how Kael would act in battle. If Kael was truly hopeless, it would be a last measure. He had no intention of converting this boy into his race. The last thing he needed was to have all of humanity after him.
