Giving a quick glance at Biyas before he left, Avrin slowly turned around to see several people glancing towards him. Of course, compared to everyone here, he seemed to not fit in. He cleared his throat and walked over towards a corner that no one was in.
“-Gathering so called geniuses into such a place. What could the Empire be trying to achieve?-” Avrin thought to himself.
Avrin quietly sat on a mahogany-looking bench, folding his arms as he glanced around, he saw that several of these people knew each other and were in groups. Of course, there were those interesting looking people such as the girl with the great sword or boy with the eagle-like eyes, who were keeping to themselves.
Avrin didn't doubt that everyone here had some sort of rich background or backing. Entering the palace must be difficult without a reputation. Of course, after keeping to himself, a group of people stopped talking and looked towards the boy with the eagle eyes before making their way towards him. The boy in the lead wore a haubergeon of sorts, while the ones to his side each wore different attire.
“Jinta, you dared to show your face here. Your clan has no shame. You new nobles think you deserve to be here, truly disgusting!” The boy with the haubergeon and short black hair spoke towards the eagle eye looking boy, who was known as Jinta.
Jinta glanced at him before speaking, “You talk big for a piece of trash that I beat into the ground only three days ago.” Jinta snickered menacingly, emitting a green affinity mana that seemed heavy and dense. This caused the boy who was talking to him flinch. “You….”
The commotion brought the attention of quite a few people, who looked over with interest, including Avrin, who seemed to enjoy watching people argue with each other. Especially people who considered themselves geniuses.
Avrin didn't think of himself as anything special in that sense. He wouldn't even consider these people as geniuses. At most, the majority were early stage Master level, while the few interesting people like Jinta and the greatsword wielding girl were seemingly mid level Masters.
“Jinta, you speak a lot of shit. You think you're strong. Maybe me and my friends should teach you a lesson.” After the boy in the haubergeon spoke, he and his friends emitted their own auras, each one a different affinity. None were as dense and heavy as Jinta’s, though.
The group eyed Jinta and Jinta eyed them. He was about to draw his swords, until a loud voice spoke out, “Enough!” A heavy aura crashed down on everyone in the entire room, causing them to shudder and press down onto their knees slightly.
No one was excluded, and they all paled and felt their bodies shudder. Of course, Avrin was the only one who didn't budge. It was as if that aura wasn't even there for him. A figure clad in azure colored armor with an intricate design of a lion came walking inside the room from a hall at the front, different from the entrance.
Of course, the figure glanced at everyone with a hint of disdain and mockery before his eyes came across Avrin, who didn't seem to budge at all. This made the man’s eye twitch a little. “-A hidden dragon?-” The man quietly thought to himself before speaking out loudly.
“Fighting is forbidden until you given permission. You will have your chance to go at it with each other. Until then, respect the rules of this palace that his highness has set, or I will personally kick you out!”
Avrin looked at the man. Surprisingly, he was a peak stage Grandmaster. Despite that, he seemed quite old and withered. Everyone glanced over at the old man clad in the lion armor with reverence and respect as well as fear. Unlike Avrin, they couldn't fathom the man’s level.
“Now then. I'm sure you are all aware of why you are here, but we have some new people who have risen to fame and nobility, so I will explain the details.”
At this point, a few of the people gathered here looked over towards the man and listened intently. The man continued. “In this Empire, we recruit only the best of the best. When we seek geniuses, we want those who are capable of leading us to greatness! We will spare no effort and resources in helping them grow.
That being said, we only have two positions available for this year's generation hall. Those two winners will receive the full support of the Empire and become the personal disciples of his majesty King Leo Zircus!”
At the mention of this, many people widened their eyes as they looked with amazement. Whispers could be heard as people began to get their hopes up. Of course, Avrin was feeling a little indifferent.
“Do not get your hopes up! Such an honor is not so easily obtained. For those that win and decide not to become His Majesty's disciples, we will grant one wish within His Majesty’s power! Any questions before we begin the elimination process?”
People were quiet, but at this point, Avrin spoke out, “Is it true King Leo has a piece of Skymetal?” Avrin held no fear towards the king, nor cared much towards speaking his name, but at this sign of so called disrespect, many of the geniuses looked at Avrin with their mouths open in shock.
The old man’s expression flickered. He looked at Avrin. He would have called him out for this disrespect, but he felt that Avrin was someone he couldn't underestimate, so he cleared his throat and thought about his question. “Yes. The rumors you might have heard are correct. His Majesty does have a piece of Skymetal. Why do you happen to be interested in it?”
Avrin replied, “If I win, wouldn't it be possible to obtain that piece as part of that one wish that can be granted?” Avrin clearly showed confidence in his victory, having no intention to be a disciple of the king.
“Well….” The man in lion armor cleared his throat before speaking. “The piece of Skymetal is only a decoration, despite its unusual aura. I cannot speak for His Majesty, so you will just have to wait and find out. That is, if you win. Do not be arrogant. There are many people here who I'm sure are more capable than you.”
Hearing his words the people around gazed with disdain towards Avrin, scoffing as they made note of him. Of course, no one dared to speak their thoughts, as the lion armored man was still present.
“Well then, no more questions? Good. In a short while, you will all engage in three tests. The first test is to gauge a certain aspect of you, the second test is to measure your adaptability, and the third test measures your talent.
I will tell you, it is quite rare for someone to complete two of the three tests, and unheard of for one to obtain victory in all three, so much to say it is impossible! That being said, your results will be measured, so put in your best effort. For those who fail and do not become the disciples of the king, we will surely find positions for you if you accept.”
With that being said, a runic formation suddenly appeared under the old man before it flickered and he vanished. After a few seconds, more formations appeared under everyone. Some gazed with curiosity before they too flickered and turned into white lights that vanished.
When they reappeared, they were in a large, underground space. This space was well fortified and completely open with many magic torches lighting the way. Everyone was teleported in a way that they were lined up. The space in front of them stretched on for one-hundred meters, while the ceiling reached fifty meters in height.
The ground seemed to emit a strange, transparent mana. The tiles looked like metallic marble adn seemed quite sturdy. Everyone looked around in curiosity while they spoke to each other. Of course, a few continued to gaze at Avrin with disdain, but they were snapped back to reality as a voice was heard around the entire space.
“Welcome to the pressure path. This first test is simple, reach the end of the space. Of course, if you cannot reach it, you will be measured by distance.“ A light flashed in front of everyone as a round badge appeared in their hands. No one knew what to expect. Every test was different and they couldn’t receive information on it.
“This badge will come in handy. If you cannot handle proceeding further, infuse mana into it and it will activate and allow your safety, but do so and you will be teleported to the beginning and unable to try again.”
Everyone gazed at the badge as if it were a life saving treasure. Surely if it was meant to help them, so they wouldn't treat it unfairly. Of course, to Avrin, it was of no use. He couldn't replicate mana, only devour and absorb it. But he was carefully analyzing the name of the test. “-Pressure path.. It can't be simple-”
“You may begin when you are ready. But, I warn you. Do not underestimate this test. For each step you take the harder it becomes.” The voice faded and the ground began to glow a fluorescent red.
“Ha, a simple stroll? Piece of cake.” One boy spoke out with excitement as he entered into the path. He immediately felt his body shake a little, as if he was weighed down. He clenched his teeth and began to continue forward, but with each step, it became harder and harder. Everyone was watching with interest to see what was going on.
“A magic that increases the weight around someone!” A girl with a blue robe and pointy wizard hat spoke with awe. “Simple!” She uttered before smiling. Of course, the boy had stopped only after taking nineteen steps. He felt unable to proceed further, as his muscles and bones were cracking and distorting. He quickly infused mana into the badge, to which a white barrier appeared around him, negating the effects of the increased weight.
The female who spoke earlier started chanting, “Mighty God of Creation, God King Septim, please imbue your protection towards your follower.” She than began to chant unrecognizable words, though Avrin looked with interest. He hadn't seen many magic users in his life here, so he gazed with awe as a transparent magic bubble appeared around the female, who casually walked onto the path as if it wasn't there.
Nobody wanted to be outdone so people began to use their own methods, though this test seemed a bit biased towards those who focus on physical strength, it seemed it tested one's capability to find a way around this. This was what Avrin thought, until he saw the girl’s magic bubble ripple the moment she reached forty steps, and she was out of breath. The shield seemed to drain mana from her, and just as the shield was about to shatter, she quickly infused mana into the badge.
You might be reading a pirated copy. Look for the official release to support the author.
Avrin only partially watched them. It was only until everyone had found their own limit that he looked more carefully. Jinta had managed to reach one-hundred-eighty-three steps. His face was pale and he was seated with the badge bubble around him. The boy who called out Jinta could only reach one-hundred-thirteen steps and looked at Jinta with anger in his eyes.
Avrin began to walk, relying solely on his physical strength. The increase in weight felt somewhat refreshing to him, but it was incomparably weaker than his Phantom Pulse. As he continued to walk without issue, many of the youths glanced at him with looks of shock and envy.
Jinta glanced at Avrin as he passed into the one-hundred step mark and noticed Avrin’s speed hadn't diminished. He thought suddenly, “-This person is going to be difficult to beat-”
Of course, he wasn't the only one who was shocked. The people who felt Avrin was trash due to his disrespect were eating their own words when he passed them. Soon, Avrin passed the three-hundred step mark and still barely felt a tingle. He glanced over at the girl with the greatsword in amazement. She had reached three-hundred-five steps and had been forced to enter the protection bubble from the badge. She looked at Avrin with curiosity and shock before turning away.
Avrin continued until he reached the end of the path, but the people here weren't the only ones shocked at this result. “Amazing! This has to be a new record!” Several figures were watching from a hidden chamber. The one who spoke was an old man with a large beard and bald head, similar to how those shaolin masters would look.
“Hmm, indeed. This boy’s physical strength must be incredible. If I remember correctly, he is the one with the Enigma ability that has to do with increasing weight.” He spoke, clearly not having a proper term for gravity.
Soon the fluorescent red floor dimmed and runic formations appeared under everyone again before they were transported out and back into the waiting room. Everyone heaved a sigh of relief. Of course, Avrin simply walked over and sat in the corner again.
“-Disappointing. It's almost embarrassing for me to do this-” He joked to himself. Everyone seemed to try their best to recover their energy by drinking potions and eating. Many people were glancing at Avrin with careful gazes. Especially the girl with the greatsword and Jinta. Each eyed Avrin as if he was their goal to beat.
The boy in the haubergeon carefully walked over to Avrin with his friends behind him. He had a look of arrogance and faked a smile as he spoke to Avrin, “Hello friend. You were incredible in the first test. I am Teil Juheyel, successor to the first rate nobility of the Juheyel family.” He spoke with a like of pride. He looked at Avrin, as if expecting him to prostrate himself.
Everything was silent for a moment, until Avrin looked at Teil as if he were some dumb chimpanzee. “Yes?...And?” hH was confused as to what this boy wanted. Of course, at Avrin’s reply, Teil’s face twitched a little, but he continued to fake a smile. “I was going to suggest we team up for the second and third tests. As you can see, me and my friends are clearly the strongest out of everyone here. When we work together, if you wou-”
Avrin cut him off before he could continue. “Strongest out of everyone here? Hahaha..” Avrin began to laugh. Everyone hearing Avrin laugh felt that Teil may react with anger, and their suspicions were right.
“W..What's so damn funny! You think we are crap?!! You're no better!!” Teil roared at Avrin. Avrin soon stopped laughing, “-My luck is shit. How come I have to deal with these donkeys-” Looking at Teil with a thoughtful expression, Avrin spoke, “Get lost. You’re taking up my air.”
Hearing these words, several of the youths couldn't help but laugh slightly. Even Jinta and the girl wielding a greatsword smirked a little.
“You….damn….bastard!” Teil clenched his teeth and looked around, as if looking for the old man in azure armor. He then unsheathed a dagger from behind his back and stabbed it towards Avrin’s arm with intent to harm. He felt he could get away with it using his family's reputation.
Though this action was a big mistake on his behalf. Avrin raised his right hand and pressed the tip of his finger against the dagger. The moment the dagger collided with it, it shattered like glass. This caused everyone present to look with amazement.
“What...happened?..” One youth spoke, while another replied, “That was a rare quality dagger! It was given to him by his father, but it was shattered so easily!! What incredible strength…”
Avrin looked over at the stunned Teil, who began to sweat bullets. “Well, I see you are indeed a little crazy. That's fine. When threatened, I can be crazy too…” Avrin gave a menacing grin before he stood up and raised his right hand to the side, “W..Wait! Do you know who I am!? If you lay a single fin-”
Before Teil could finish Avrin’s right hand blurred before the back of his hand slapped against Teil’s cheek, sending the boy twisting in the air, doing several flips before landing onto the ground a few meters away. Avrin considered this youth unbehaved and most likely he had never been disciplined.
“There we go. Your father and mother can thank me for punishing you later. Be sure to remember that if you threaten me again, I'll be taking your arm.” Avrin spoke before sitting back down.
Though the moment he did, the runic formation appeared again and the man in azure armor appeared. He looked over at Teil with shock and rushed over, kneeling beside him. “What happened here! Who dares fight within His Majesty’s palace!”
Teil’s friends snickered before they all spoke, “This person suddenly attacked our friend!” While another youth continued on. “That's right! We were just talking to him and he suddenly lashed out!”
That being said, the others considered these words and actions vile and bad. They all felt that if Avrin was punished and removed, then maybe, they had a chance to win, so no one spoke up in defence.
“You.. Is this true!?” The old man spoke as he looked at Avrin. Avrin sighed before replying. “If defending myself is a crime, I am guilty.” The old man considered what he said. It was five against one. It didn't matter who was wrong or right. Whoever started it first would be punished. “Well… If that is the case, I have to disqualify you from this event.”
Avrin glared a little before standing up, though a sweet yet strong voice called out. “Wait. It is not his fault. That vile worm Teil tried to attack this boy with a hidden dagger. His comrades are lying and despicable!” The girl with the greatsword responded, defending Avrin.
“That's right. That bastard tried to stab him with a dagger because he felt offended. This is injustice!” Added Jinta
The old man in azure armor frowned a little as he thought. On one hand was the son of a high ranked noble family, on the other was a boy with an Enigma ability that was very powerful. Though he had to disregard this and make things even. “Very well. You are not disqualified from this event, but you and Teil must be punished. You will both be unable to attend the second event, and will have to wait for the third event to continue.”
Avrin sighed and nodded. He quietly sat back down and glanced over at Jinta and the young girl with the greatsword giving a thankful look. He hadn't had many people defend him before, so it was a nice change of pace.
Meanwhile, Teil, who’s right cheek was swollen, was on the verge of tears of anger. He looked at Avrin with fury while his so called wound was tended to. The second event had already started and it was just him and Avrin. Other than several guards there to make sure they don’t attack one another again.
Avrin, who was quite bored, paid no mind to him and was scanning around with his Divine Sense. He was focused on scanning the palace. “-Incredible. It's just as big underground as it is above ground, fascinating… Quite a few hidden powerhouses, though-” Avrin focused on one large room that held two powerful energies. It filled Avrin with excitement. He felt a very powerful energy, as well as an energy not as powerful, but still strong. That weaker energy was Sage level at the very least. The other one is no doubt King Leo Zircus, a Mythical level being. With the help of his Sigil weapon, of course-” Avrin nearly drooled. He would love to devour a Sigil weapon.
He felt the power would be no less than converting a dragon. Avrin could feel the real power came from not the figure, but what was on the figure, which was no doubt the Sigil weapon.
“Hmmm?” A voice resonated within a the room, “Your Majesty, what is wrong?” Another voice sounded out from a middle aged woman who was opposite of the figure. A board game of sorts was in between the two. It looked similar to chess.
“Strange. I felt as if I was being watched. This is a feeling I have never felt before. Very weird.” The owner of this voice was none other than Leo Zircus, the human king. He was wearing a long golden robe with his blonde hair spiked up somewhat. He gave a very mature and courageous air, one only fit for a person meant to rule.
“Strange indeed. Maybe it is a sign of things to come? After all, Azrael has escaped, no doubt he will cause trouble.” The woman spoke regarding the events of a couple days ago. Leo nodded and thought to himself as he began to maneuver a piece on the board in front of them.
“That Azrael clearly won't ever let go of his hate. If he is not put down, it will cause my empire to suffer. I can only plead with Lord Abbadon regarding this matter, but he had told me it was forbidden by God King Septim, as Azrael’s death would incur Zephiron’s wrath.”
While the two conversed with each other, Avrin suddenly opened his eyes, as he felt the appearance of many figures. These were the people who went to attempt the second test. Of course, all of them were exhausted.
Each one seemed haggard and some were even bloodied as well as unconscious. No doubt it was quite intense for them. Even Jinta and the girl with the greatsword looked pale and were seemingly sore. Avrin could only sigh with regret, as he had missed out on this event.
Suddenly, another teleportation rune lit up. The armor clad old man had appeared again with a look of honor and pride. He glanced over everyone with a hint of disappointment. “Well done towards the youths who completed the second test.“
He glanced over towards the girl with the greatsword before nodding in approval. He then spoke out with a straight tone, “This third test is considered impossible to succeed at. We will only measure your attempt at it. It will be held tomorrow, so rest up, for you will be engaging in combat against the Empire’s greatest fighters.”------------------

chapters.title: V4: Chapter 110 Destroying Grand Masters.
chapters.content:

I hope you all enjoy this sponsored release, chapter 111 isn't written yet but i will get right to it, and like before i will release it as soon as it is available for you all. --------------------
Currently, everyone was being led away by servants to rooms that were assigned to them. Of course, none were unphased and weren’t worried about tomorrow, when they would be fighting the Empire’s fiercest warriors. They would not only lose but be destroyed. They needed to plan and think of a strategy to at least make a good appearance.
Avrin quietly followed one of the servants. As he was led away, he looked around casually. “-This third test should be interesting. I have to complete this one. It's ok if I come in second place. Regardless, I will get that one wish-”
Soon, the large group of geniuses was split and everyone entered their rooms. Avrin was sitting in his, gazing out the window quietly. He was thinking about his situation. “-If I can retrieve this piece of Skymetal, as well as the one promised by Azrael, it will be two wins for me. Though, forging them...I wonder if it is possible to control the forging process. Some armor would be invaluable for me-”
Pondering quietly to himself, Avrin raised his head and gazed at the door. Within moments of looking at it, a knock was heard. “Come in.” He spoke while looking to the window again. Of course, because of his Divine Sense, he knew who it was.
The door opened and the female with the greatsword entered the room before shutting the door.  The girl glanced at Avrin with a look of reverence and respect before she courteously bowed and introduced herself. “Greetings. My name Ophelia Lexus. I never expected to encounter someone capable of keeping me on edge.”
Avrin looked carefully at her and raised a brow. “Miss Ophelia, I’m quite thankful for your actions in my defence. Though I'm sure you're not here to discuss me rivaling you.” Avrin was not one to beat around the bush with people. Ophelia revealed a smirk and nodded.
“ofcourse!. Your name is Herth, correct? You are the rumored Enigma ability user whom the Empire and Gaia Academy are going to great lengths to recruit. I do not doubt that even if you failed this test, you would still be a winner.”
Listening to the girl, she seemed quite unfazed, though this only made Avrin even more cautious. “I cannot wrong your words. I can see both value you me, enough so that it may cause issues when i pick a side. Though despite this, I'm sure you have a point to this conversation?”
Ophelia nodded and reached over to a hidden pocket within her armor and pulled out a small metal plate with a purple wing engraved on it. “I know this may be a bit of a hindrance to you, but my uncle begged me to offer you a spot within our family with benefits and all if I was to meet you here. I apologize.” She spoke, feeling a little awkward.
Avrin glanced at the plate and revealed a strange expression. “-Dark matter? This is made from dark matter?-” Avrin interest was piqued as he looked at Ophelia. “This is an interesting plate. I have never seen the material before, it must be quite unique.”
Ophelia suddenly smiled and spoke. “Indeed! My uncle is a great mage who is planning on rising to power. He has some mysterious new methods and will surely make a change in the Empire.” Avrin glanced at her and revealed a faint smile. “Your uncle sounds amazing. After this event is over, I would like to meet him.”
Avrin spoke courteously, much different to how he was before. He was thinking the situation had turned serious. If there was a spectral loose in the world, he could cause trouble that would bring everyone towards him. Avrin’s choice was simple. Send him to the north or terminate him.
With that said and done, Ophelia heaved a sigh of relief and bowed again before leaving. Avrin had a good feeling about her. She didn't seem arrogant and was quite respectable. Although maybe it was because he was considered an Enigma user. But for now, he left the matter alone.
He decided to sleep despite not needing it. The joy of sleeping could become a relaxing habit, and as soon as he laid down and closed his eyes, time went by in a flash and the evening of that day turned into the morning of the next.
Avrin opened his eyes and stood up. His body began to stretch and turn as if it were living on it's own. His bones stretched and fit back into a preferable place and Nebula Mist surged around him slightly to clean and refresh him.
Afterwards, he left the room. The servant had instructed him that he was allowed to go to certain areas, such as the open library or the dining hall, as well as the garden. Everywhere else was considered out of bounds, and those who disobeyed this rule would be disqualified. Avrin decided to visit the open library. He had arrived quite quickly and noticed that no one was around.
Avrin spent quite a bit of time here, and soon the other so called geniuses began to wake up or exit their midnight training after relaxing and eating, and soon the servants were sent out again at 11:00am to gather everyone.
Avrin couldn't relax. He held the plate Ophelia have him in his hand and examined it carefully. It was made from dark matter. The feeling of dark matter was all but natural to him. Especially when not an ounce of mana emitted from it.
Following the servants, who began to lead everybody, they were soon back in the Generation Hall. Standing there was the azure armored old man who had a prideful smile on his face.
As soon as everyone entered and the large doors shut, he spoke, “Today the third and final test will be conducted. From there, you will be evaluated and the two winners will be picked. This test is one of talent. You may be at a certain level of strength, but if your talent is great, you may be able to defeat someone at a higher level than you. Each of you will be transported to a separate arena where you will face opponent after opponent until you fall.
I will let you know that no one has ever gotten past defeating a second opponent and only one person in history has succeeded in beating the first opponent, and that is great the Sage level master Retria Zircus, His Majesty’s sister and Successor to the Archmage.”
With eyes filled with respect and awe, everyone listened intently. They had heard rumors and legends of Sage level people. These were people who received power with their own hard work and not with the help of a Sigil. True geniuses.
“Well then. I'm sure you are all eager to start, and we are also eager to select two winners. Let’s begin.” Just like before, the runic circles appeared under everyone and flashes of light shone before everybody vanished.
The space he was in stretched for fifty meters in all directions. Avrin figured the underground space of the palace was specifically made for the Generation Hall, as a space above ground would attract too much attention. They wanted to keep things hidden and under control.
Looking around the room, it seemed similar to the room of the first test, and Avrin quietly glanced around. Though a few seconds after being transported, another white light appeared opposite of him.
A large, muscular, bearded man wearing leather fighting gear as well as the insignia of the Empire appeared. He scratched his face and looked bored. “Ah.. His Majesty picked me for this test again.. I was about to go out to drink… Oh well. I'll get it over with...Hey kid..try your best, hah..”
The bearded man didn't seem to wait for Avrin to reply as mana surged around him. He released killing intent. He seemed to take the fight seriously. One could tell this man was one who never underestimated his opponent.
“Early stage Grandmaster?” The bearded man charged towards Avrin like a bullet. He punched, not holding back at all. As if he wanted to teach him a lesson. Avrin, of course, casually sidestepped while maintaining a defensive stance. He turned his left palm and plowed it against the man’s side.
The counter was quite quick, and the man’s eyes widened. He felt his the left side of his rib cage crack and a few break as he was blown away like a ragdoll before smashing into the wall, causing a deep indentation.
The bearded man was unconscious and foaming at the mouth. “Oh?.. Guess I should have held back.” Avrin’s face turned a little pale. He had gotten a little excited. He hadn’t faced such killing intent in a while, and decided to counter with his hands instead of using Phantom Pulse.
Of course, he would have no idea that those old Grandmasters who were watching were showing looks of shock. “He just….” One spoke with disbelief. “Incredible… Such a perfect counter...one move. He only needed one move to defeat Lupen, who excels at physical combat and defence!!”  another said.
These people were stunned. Defeating someone within the third test of the Generation Hall was only ever seen once, and now it was done a second time. Many of these people thought it signalled the coming of a second sage, and even during the first time it was not an easy win.
“What now? What do we do?” An old woman who seemed to be in her seventies asked. Another woman, this time middle aged in terms of appearance, replied, “We continue. This Herth is remarkable. I would have liked to view his Enigma ability. This time, you go, Leora. You're a middle stage Grandmaster, correct? You must of had a breakthrough.”
Leora, who was the old woman, had a pale face. “M..Me?... Hmph. Clearly that Herth is hiding his power. I do not dare make a fool of myself.” The six people, all of whom were Grandmasters, began to argue with each other until the azure armor clad individual narrowed his eyes narrow and spoke.
“Fools!” His voice resounded like thunder, causing them to quiet down. “Are you that scared of a child? This was nothing but luck. I'm sure of it. I will go myself.” With that being said, the azure armor clad old man vanished with the help of teleportation and appeared in the arena with Avrin.
The hole in the wall was left, while Lupen had long since been transported out to recover. Avrin looked over at the azure armored old man with a gaze of indifference. “Senior, are you here to fight me?”
Avrin asked curiously. The azure armored old man nodded and took a fighting stance. “Indeed. You cannot be underestimated, thus, we have decided to take you seriously. You are a powerful Enigma ability user after all.”
Stolen story; please report.
Avrin tilted his head. “Very well, Senior. I want to apologize in advance for breaking the kept tradition of the Empire. This second match will not be your win.” Avrin was not afraid in the least of this man.
“Let’s see if your words can be backed up! The old man suddenly began to chant and two spheres of blue light appeared in his hands before shooting towards the ceiling. The spheres exploded into icicles that shot towards Avrin.
“-Magic!-” Avrin excitedly thought. He hadn't encountered a battle with mage before, though this magic was not strong enough to phase him at all, so a flash of disappointment appeared in his eyes. Avrin casually used his speed to dodge the crashing icicles, each one managing to pierce into the ground like daggers.
While Avrin was dodging, the old man had already used this time to chant another spell. “Mighty azure God of Water and Sea, Tialoc, allow this wizard to borrow your strength!” Suddenly, ice began to gather around the walls and frost began to build up on the ground. Avrin’s eyes narrowed a little. “Field magic, Senior?”
The old man smirked and raised his hand in an upward motion. The ice on the floor under Avrin suddenly trembled before forming into a pillar that shot upwards. Avrin felt he should hold back a little. He didn't want to show that his strength was almighty, as it may raise many suspicions. But, showing too little would not allow him to receive the reaction he wanted.
As the pillar shot up, it smashed against his stomach and pushed him upward until he hit the high ceiling. The pillar of ice glistened like a white diamond, but soon it trembled and cracked. Avrin fell and landed on his feet while clutching his stomach. The attack itself did only a bit of damage, but he acted as if he were wounded.
“A..Amazing. Senior, you are indeed stro-” Avrin was not able to complete his sentence, as the wizard held a ball of transparent light blue mana in his hands. He smashed it into the ground. “Ice Wave!” He shouted. The ice on the walls combined with the ice and the floor, causing a small ripple that grew into a tsunami.
“-He really isn't holding back. The Empire’s Grandmasters are truly something else!-” Avrin looked nervous intentionally and ran towards the wall behind him. “Running away? You can't evade it!” The old man called out, before a look of shock appeared in his eyes.
Avrin was indeed running, not because of fear, but to gain an advantage. As he and the ice wave neared the wall, Avrin leapt towards it, using his feet to kick off which caused him to gain incredible height, avoiding the ten meter tall ice wave. The wave crashed against the wall, making the arena tremble.
“He is matching Lord Delion quite well!” One of the old men observing the match spoke. By now, a majority of the matches had concluded and the Grandmasters who were sent to fight against the others had gathered to watch this fight, hoping to see the Enigma ability in action.
“yes, but he doesn't seem to be able to do much. He is on the defensive.” A woman who looked to be in her late twenties said. “Let’s see how long the boy can keep it up. In the end, this match is already enough to place that boy in the top two. Yuten is still fighting that Ophelia girl, and they are neck and neck. As for who comes first between Ophelia and Herth, we shall see.”
Avrin glanced at Delion. He was emitting a light blue aura with ice surging around his feet. “Enough games! I have yet to see your Enigma ability. If you do not want to use it, I will force it out of you!” Suddenly, Delion raised his hands and mana swarmed around him.
The entire ice field trembled, as all the ice seemed to be drawn to the center of Delion’s hands, forming a large sphere of ice. “The stage above Grandmaster is Sage. Sages are capable of utilizing their ice field to form a powerful attack. Although I am unable to form that attack, I can utilize the ice itself to improvise!”
Avrin looked closely. He had purposely dragged this fight on, mainly to see what a mage is capable of. But he didn't seem all that impressed. “Frozen Planet!” Delion roared out, and blue mana gathered around the large ice sphere that began to condense incredibly quick until it was no longer ten meters in a circular diameter, but the size of a soccer ball.
A look of caution appeared on Avrin’s face. The soccer ball sized condensed ice shot towards him like a comet. Avrin extended his arms, as if to grab it. He snickered. He wanted to test himself. This was an improvised attack that tried to mimic a Sage’s ability. He wanted to see how strong it was against him.
The ice sphere left a trail of frozen ground while shooting at Avrin. Avrin quickly wrapped his arms around it, but was still being pushed back several meters every second.
Delion gazed at Avrin. “You fool! You are truly seeking to die. Let it go and give up!” Not only Delion, but many of the other Grandmasters watching were thinking Avrin was crazy. Avrin felt a little winded and gave a serious look. He traveled seven meters before he finally stopped.
The ice sphere continued to slowly rotate in his grasp, causing frost to form on his body. “If this is all you have, Senior…” Avrin’s muscles flexed and the ice sphere cracked and shattered into pieces, causing a wave of mana to surge outward before dissipating, “ You can't win…”
Delion’s mouth was hanging low as he looked in amazement and horror at Avrin. He took this fight seriously, but never expected that this child had such monstrous strength. He felt a tinge of fear in his heart.
He knew he wasn't capable of beating Avrin, since that attack used up quite a bit of mana and was his strongest move. “I….f..forfeit…” Delion said half heartedly, before a rune under him appeared and teleported him out.
Avrin dropped the remaining shards of ice and tilted his head from side to side to crack his neck. “-Grandmasters really aren't anything for me anymore. I want to fight someone above and beyond-” Deep inside, Avrin he felt a battle lust slowly build up. This was something that he had never had as a human, but slowly grew within this body, as if he wanted to constantly seek a challenge to help himself grow.
“Lord Delion lost!! How can this be? What's going on!?” The observers were in shock as they all turned rowdy and began to argue. Delion appeared with a pale look on his face. Everyone remained quiet as they looked over to him. “Lord Delion, this-” Before the man could continue, Delion spoke.
“This Herth’s Enigma ability is truly strange. He also has hidden strength. He can defeat me, and didn't even seem to be to serious. But we can't let him be so arrogant. We have no choice. I will go notify His Majesty and see how he wants to handle the situation. In the meantime, keep him there. I'm sure His Majesty will think of something.”
It didn't seem like they wanted to let Avrin break tradition and obtain a victory in the third unbeatable test. Of course, Avrin was leaning against the wall and began to cautiously think to himself, “-They don't seem to be letting me out. Maybe they are ringing their heads together to find someone for me.
Though if I show my power a bit too much, I'm sure Abbadon will find out somehow. If he sees what I am capable of, no doubt his suspicions of me will rise. If I can obtain the Skymetal from this place, I will no longer have business within the central continent-”
Avrin had at first considered to make a reputation for himself and gain a political advantage to allow his people some piece of mind, but due to unforeseen circumstances, he thought that he had to take risks and not always think everything will go according to plan. The Skymetal has taken top priority. He didn't doubt that Abbadon would find out. Avrin would obtain the Skymetal and vanish like a breeze.
Currently, thirteen Grandmasters were gathered within the observation room, each one debating and asking about Avrin and his Enigma ability. By now, the battle with Ophelia had concluded with her losing to her opponent, so all the Grandmasters were gathered and discussing Avrin’s two victories and what would happen next.
“This Herth is truly remarkable. The Empire will surely be strengthened if he accepts His Majesty’s offer.” One woman spoke, while one of the men replied. “I agree. To have such shocking talent at that boy’s age, it is scary if you think carefully.
Just how limitless is his potential?” While people discussed this, another man replied. “You're right. I'm sure Gaia Academy will get wind of the events here. We can't let them get their hands on a monstrous talent like this young buy. Only the Empire can raise him properly. He will be humanity's new warrior!”
They continued to argue, until suddenly, an immense feeling of pressure came over them. Everyone went quiet as they watched three figures casually make their way in. One was Delion, the other was the great Sage Retria, and the final one, King Leo Zircus!
“What's this I hear about a boy who defeated Delion and Lupen?” Leo frowned as he looked  around. “Y..Your Majesty..” Everyone knelt down in reverence towards him.
“Your Majesty, the Enigma wielding boy from Laymist. Lord Abbadon had also asked us to be careful of him.”
Leo listened to his sister as he gazed at the magic screen to see Avrin casually leaning against the wall. He began to think, “I see. This boy has impressive strength. He is also under suspicion of freeing Azrael.
That being said, if he thought he was guilty, he wouldn't even be here and would have gone off into hiding. We can't be too sure. Regardless, I am not Abbadon and have my own Empire to tend to. If this boy can be roped in, so be it. If not, a friendship may be built.”
Delion, who was quite nervous around both Retria and Leo, suddenly spoke. “Your Majesty….what should we do?” Leo was carefully thinking, before his sister spoke out, “Simple. Let me handle the situation.” She spoke before raising her hand. A long, red and blue staff appeared, forming out of mana.
But as she stepped forward, Leo raised his hand and moved it in front of her to stop her. “No need. This Enigma boy will surely grow to be someone incredibly powerful. I will handle this personally.“ He gave a soft smile.
The room filled with buzz and amazement. No one had seen the king fight in many years, and now he would be fighting against a young boy who possessed an Enigma level ability. “Brother,” Retria spoke without referring to him as royalty, “Are you sure you want to do this?”
Leo nodded before cracking his knuckles. “I feel I can learn quite a bit from him. It will also allow me to test just how strong he is and see if Lord Abbadon’s suspicions were right or wrong.” After he had spoken, he vanished in the white light of teleportation.
Inside the arena, Avrin strangely  felt his heart skip a beat as he raised his head to look at the figure being teleported in.

With a flash of light, Leo appeared in the arena. Avrin had an aching feeling in his heart, and his Divine Sense instantly surrounded the man. “-Are you kidding me?-” He thought to himself. He never expected that he would come face to face with the emperor and only Sigil wielder within the central continent.
Avrin walked back to the center of the arena before smiling softly. “Greetings, Your Majesty. I am truly honored to be in your presence.” He bowed with fake respect. Avrin wanted to keep up appearances. He did not respect this man at all, but he was interested as to why he was here.
“Oh, you know me? It's quite rare for someone to know what I look like, as I don't make many public appearances. Though at least you're respectful, so I will give you that.”
Avrin listened to Leo and nodded. “Your Majesty, it would be hard to not recognize someone with such a powerful aura. I don't think there are any Grandmasters within the central continent capable of making me feel nervous, and you are not the female Sage. The only other option is that you are the king.”
Leo gave a hearty chuckle before nodding. “Yes, I suppose that’s true. Well, I won't beat around the bush. Herth, was it? I'm here to be your next opponent. I set up this test myself, and it would be a bit weird for the impossible to become possible.”
Avrin’s eyes narrowed slightly. Leo’s words meant that he was confident in beating Avrin and didn't intend to let him win. “Very well Your Majesty. Though I have a question and a request before we fight.”
Leo gave a look of awe. Not many people would want a request and ask a question when they would be facing the king and seem as relaxed as Avrin. Leo clearly felt this boy was not normal and most likely had a trick up his sleeve.
He didn't plan to underestimate him at all. A boy at his age capable of defeating Grandmasters was quite monstrous. He could only sigh in regret, wishing his son had half of Herth’s talent.
“You're quite gutsy Herth, I like that. Tell me what you want to say, I will humor you.” Avrin’s heart loosened a little and began to beat quickly. “Is it true you possess a piece of Skymetal?” Asked Avrin. Leo replied casually, as if it wasn't a big deal. “Oh, that? Indeed I do.”
Leo raised his right hand and a ring on his index finger began to glow. A large, near perfect sphere wrapped in strange paper-like bindings and metal chains appeared. The weight of it was enough to cause Leo’s arm to lower slightly.
Avrin looked at it with awe. He could feel the strange energy within those bindings. It made his heart flutter. He was even more convinced that it was Skymetal, as Astaroth began to twitch a little, as if feeling aggressive.
“This ore is quite dangerous. It almost attacked me several times, which is why I have it heavily sealed.” Leo smiled and the chunk of Skymetal turned white before vanishing back into the space within Leo’s ring.
Avrin’s mind was racing. “-No wonder I couldn't detect it, it was hidden within that ring. I never knew spacial pockets came in the shape of rings. They must be quite valuable-”
Avrin had a slight look of greed as he thought this. Leo felt Avrin truly wanted the Skymetal. It was not hard for him to see. “I'm guessing you want it. Unfortunately for you, it’s too dangerous. Though if you defeat me, I will give it to you freely.”
Avrin frowned a little. Leo wasn't making this easy for him. By telling him that, he obviously meant that Avrin would never have a chance to obtain it. He thought Avrin could never defeat him, thus he gave a false hope. “If I defeat you, I can obtain it? That is fine with me. My request is that if you have a larger arena, I would like to fight you there without anyone watching.”
Leo’s eyes widened with astonishment. The words spoken by this boy clearly showed he wasn't as simple as he thought. His own heart quickened. “Hmm, you're quite strange, Herth. Though I won't doubt your reasons. Indeed, there is my personal training grounds that is located several miles underground.”
With a click of his fingers, both Avrin and Leo were engulfed in a blue light before they vanished. The spectators showed worrisome looks. “Huh?! Where did His Majesty and Herth go?” One of the Grandmasters, an eighty year old looking man, asked
Retria, of course, knew the blue teleportation light signified being transported to Leo’s personal training grounds. “His Majesty has decided to fight the boy in a larger space hidden from our eyes. That Herth is truly remarkable to convince His Majesty to do this.”
They continued to whisper and debate the current situation, wondering what Avrin’s origins were and just how powerful he could be. Meanwhile, appearing within an almost boundless space underground, one could see it was more like a dome. The floor was even sturdier than the arena’s above, and the walls and the ceiling were unable to be seen, showing how large it was be.
Glancing around, Avrin was able to get an estimate about the size of this arena. It was the size of about two football fields, which showed making it would require a lot of work and mages who specialize in earth affinity spells.
“The only time I have ever fought someone here was when I had a sparring match with Lord Abbadon. Of course, it nearly tore this place apart. Reconstructing it was truly bothersome, though I'm sure our match won't last long, let alone be as powerful.”
Avrin glanced at Leo and the ring on his finger. “-That Skymetal will be mine, even if I have to cut his entire hand off to get it!-” A slightly crazy glint showed in Avrin’s eyes. He knew how valuable Skymetal was and how much it could help him progress. Leo was treating treasure like trash.
“That's fine Your Majesty. I am ready when you are.” Avrin smiled before taking a defensive stance. He would put all his effort into defense just to get an idea of how the king fought. This was a Sigil wielder he didn't want to underestimate.
“Good, hahahahaha!” Leo suddenly unleashed his mana, showing that his affinity was attuned to fire. His mana pool was like a small ocean that was similar to Abbadon’s yet still significantly smaller.
“First test, your agility!” Leo pulled his hand back and punched the air. The attack caused the air to split apart and push towards Avrin as a ranged attack. This attack was clearly at the very least as strong as a peak Grandmaster, as it was completely casual.
Avrin felt the attack itself looked scary, but it was definitely avoidable. Avrin dashed to the side, avoiding the large attack that plowed into the wall of the dome coliseum behind him, causing it to tremble as a large indentation and crack formed, showing that the wall was sturdy.
“Good, good! How about this?” Leo called out. One could clearly see he was playing around with Avrin. His fists turned into blurs as he punched towards Avrin, sending around thirty of the previous attack towards him.
He increased his speed somewhat as he began to dodge each and every one of these attacks with room to spare. They were not fast enough to cause him worry in the least. “Your Majesty, if this is all you have, this match will be mine.” Avrin taunted him. He wanted to test Leo.
Leo’s face twisted a little. “You little.. Hmph, very well.” He snickered before he took a deep breath, his muscles expanding a little. He turned into a quick blur and appeared before Avrin.
Avrin was astonished, but he didn't have time to think, as Leo had already punched towards him. The punch itself was at least five times stronger than the previous ones.
Without a second thought, Avrin’s speed heightened and he turned into a dark blur that avoided the attack with a little room to spare, showing his speed, at this moment, wasn't any less than Leo’s.
The punch that Leo had thrown smashed into the ground, causing it to tremble as the floor tiles cracked, a small crater forming. One had to understand the materials used to construct this dome were all of rare quality. The durability was quite high. Had this been normal ground, no doubt it would cause it to split and a small earthquake to occur.
“-What level is his base strength?-” Avrin wracked his brain trying to figure it out. Leo didn't give him time, as he continuously chased and appeared before Avrin, punching towards him and causing Avrin to constantly have to dodge. Of course, the one who was shocked the most was leo. He knew his own strength better than anyone else.
“-This boy is crazy. How is he avoiding my attacks? I'm showing the physical prowess of a peak Sage expert and, despite holding myself back, he is still dodging it all-” The pace continued on for several more attacks before Leo returned to one side of the dome coliseum.
Neither he or Avrin seemed tired at all. “I must say Herth, you're hiding your real strength, aren't you? Lord Abbadon was correct in being suspicious of you. I wonder what event occurred for you to be spawned. Are you even human?!” Leo shouted.
Avrin gazed casually at Leo. “Your Majesty, I am simply an Enigma ability user.” Hearing Avrin’s response, Leo raised a brow. He couldn't deny it, yet he still had a bad feeling. “That may very well be the case, but,” Leo snickered and his body seemingly vanished into thin air. The speed of his movement caused Avrin to feel his heart skip a beat. He saw Leo appear to his side before a punch was headed his way.
“-Shit-” With a thought, Avrin emitted Phantom Pulse around the area, causing Leo’s speed to lessen enough for Avrin to kick his feet off the ground and narrowly avoid being hit. The punch blew the air apart and caused a screeching sound, as if it was shot by laser artillery, which Avrin had used a lot in his previous life.
The punch plowed against the wall of the dome colosseum, causing a large, fifteen meter, circular hole to appear, with a depth of ten meters. Leo remained where he stood with his fist in the air as he showed astonishment.
“That was incredible. That must have been your Enigma ability to do with gravity, correct? To even handle my full base strength at the early Legendary stage to falter and avoid it... Other than us Sigil wielders, it would be a miracle to find someone capable of competing with you. Though again, let’s see how quick you react.”
The story has been illicitly taken; should you find it on Amazon, report the infringement.
As Leo spoke, just like before, he vanished, showing that his strength was above the Sage level, at the early Legendary stage. He continuously chased Avrin and bombard him with monstrous attacks, causing Avrin to keep his guard up as well as use Phantom Pulse to slow him down. Leo still seemed as if he were playing around though.
Avrin was trying to think of a way to defeat him. Although his identity was somewhat at risk, he was still contemplating whether to use his full strength to take on the king, who continued to chase Avrin. Leo suddenly snickered before jumping into the air. His mana surged again, as if an ocean was crashing down on Avrin. “-This feeling!-” Avrin had felt it before several times. It was the feeling of one being on the level of a dragon. It was a sign that King Leo had finally gotten serious.
A light engulfed Leo’s body and two objects suddenly appeared within his hands, a sword and shield. The shield was pure gold and emit a soft light. The sword in his other hand looked transparent, but still seemed sharp enough to split the sky and land apart. Avrin knew it wouldn't be good if he got hit by it.
“Well done forcing me to use my Sigil weapons. Let me tell you something, Herth. I was never good at attacking, but when it comes to defence and countering, I pride myself, knowing that on Seleria, there isn't a being that comes close to me with Aegis and Caliburn in hand. Even if a dragon were to attack, I am confident in being able to repel it. This match will not be yours. At best, you will run out of stamina long before me.”
Leo chuckled a little. Never in his life did he think he would use his Sigil weapons against a child. It made him furious inside.Then again, it also meant that this child was truly strange. Avrin snickered a little.
He didn't want to stay on the defence for too long, so as Leo raised the shield up to take his a defencive stance, Avrin wanted to test it. Turning into a blur, Avrin appeared in front of Leo before shooting his fist towards the shield.
The blow contained his full muscle strength. It caused a ripple and the air shuddered, but the shield seemed to glow a strange light before the force of Avrin’s attack was easily dissipated. Avrin got a clue about the Sigil weapon’s ability. “-It negates physical attacks?-”
Avrin smiled before he jumped back. He raised his hands and two large void spheres appeared in them. “Your physical strength is not bad at all boy! Oh?” Leo noticed the black spheres in Avrin’s hands and narrowed his eyes. “-Demonic magic?!!-” He thought.
The void spheres shot towards Aegis and collided with it. Aegis emitted a light like the shield, before the attacks were easily dissipated yet again. “That’s strange magic you have Herth. Is this your Enigma ability too?”
Avrin grinned. He could only be thankful that this king was the defensive type, but it also meant that he didn't have many options. “Your Majesty, I have quite a few tricks. For instance, this!” Avrin roared before he used Phantom Pulse on Leo. But white shield of light appeared around him, causing it to distort a little as the ground cracked, but Leo didn't seem phased at all.
“You're quite a scary child Herth. If I did not have my Sigil weapons I would not be your match at all. You're a strange existence. Then again, this is why those of Seleria refer to people like you as Enigmas. Powers that are useless, or ones that even rival the gods! You truly can’t be underestimated. How about we call this match a draw? I am willing to bite my tongue on this, given what you will achieve in the future.”
Avrin frowned. He wanted that Skymetal. “Your Majesty, that Skymetal...is there no way to acquire it?” Leo looked at Avrin strangely as the Phantom Pulse continued to circle around him. “Why exactly do you want it so badly?“
Avrin sighed. “I have my reasons, Your Majesty. I will not forfeit this fight or call it a draw. I'm confident I can win.” This Leo frown a little.
“You overestimate yourself.” Suddenly, Aegis began to glow a radiant white, before the circular shield around it expanded incredibly quick, dispelling Avrin’s Phantom Pulse and pushing against him.
Avrin was astonished. He thought Leo would be just a immobile fortress. He could never have known he was capable of this. He was unable to move and didn’t feel capable of using a Void Step to go through the shield. H felt the moment he touched it that he was weakened, as if it were draining his stamina.
The expanding shield smashed Avrin against the wall, leaving a large hole, before retracting back into Aegis. “Aegis was a weapon I chose because I needed to not only protect myself, but my Empire. I am capable of emitting a divine shield of light large enough to cover the entire city. Even a dragon would not be able to destroy this shield. But the downside is I am unable to move while I channel it.”
Avrin appeared from the crack covered in wounds, blood dripping from his mouth. Of course, the blood was red. He felt his insides quiver a little. He was caught between a rock and a hard place.
“-I could always use Astaroth and see if that does the trick, but I'm not willing just yet-” Avrin’s biggest worry was that he would miss this chance. He didn't mind being hunted down, but his actions would have consequences.
“Boy, you're quite durable, but just surrender. If I want to win, it will be quite simple. I'm just trying to boost your reputation.” Leo spoke, as if he was sure that Avrin would join him. But this was a sort of gamble.
“Your Majesty, I will not surrender…” Avrin was enjoying this fight. It gave him an idea of just how powerful a Sigil wielder truly is. He created a void greatsword in his right hand, and the appearance of this blade made Leo narrow his eyes.
“-That weapon.. No mana at all. Abbadon said that the traps guarding Azrael were unable to pick up anything. This means he is right in suspecting this strange child. But why would he free Azrael?-”
Slashing the greatsword at Leo, Avrin felt he didn't have anything to fear, as Leo still seemed to be holding back and not keen on injuring him. His best bet was to try to attack many times and figure out a weakness.
“Fool!” Leo roared, before raising Caliburn and giving a casual slash. It sent a ripple and the air was cut. Avrin’s void greatsword was easily split in half and the speed of the sword slash was incredibly quick. Enough so that it cut against Avrin’s cheek before he was able to dodge.
“-That weapon… Such an annoying situation... There are pros and cons to using my full strength, what should I do?-” Avrin thought, but from the cut that Caliburn had given him, blue blood slowly trickled down his cheek.
Leo’s eyes narrowed when he noticed this. “Herth, it seems that you have forced my hand. I wanted to recruit you, but it seems you are after my Skymetal no matter what. I also have been asked by someone that if your strength is large I am to alert him.”
Avrin looked around. He had just noticed the blue blood on his cheek, but his attention was caught when he heard Leo’s shout. “Angel! We’ll play it your way now…” Within a room located in the palace, a figure with their eyes shut suddenly opened them. This was the angel Abbadon had assigned to keep an eye on Avrin.
She had already gotten information on him and had made the trip to the Empire before hand to discuss things with Leo. Thus, several rules were made. Abbadon knew Leo would always try to strengthen his Empire and had to be cautious. Abbadon also knew leo was friendly to him, but a human was still a human, biting off more than they could chew. In this case, Leo had measured the outcome.
Not only did Avrin show enough capability to deal with the strength of a Legendary level individual, but he even forced that individual to use his Sigil weapons and enter the level of a Mythical being.
It was only then that Avrin could be countered, but this also meant that Leo had given up on recruiting him. He knew from the moment he matched up to the strength of someone at the Legendary stage that Avrin was suspicious.
He was at Laymist academy, and even the Dark Abyss Chasm when Azrael was released. His location was strange, and one couldn't feel mana from him. Leo and Abbadon were not fools. Avrin was the only one able to free Azrael.
The angel raised her hands, showing that she held a white ball of light. She had spent the entire day channeling this to prepare for the moment Leo agreed, as Abbadon didn't want an issue with him and the king.
A white flash of light appeared as the circular sphere of magic expanded. The result was that an elegant and strong looking figure was present. This person was Angel Lord Abbadon, who had been waiting for this moment.
“-Little bastard. See if I don't rip the truth from your soul!-” Avrin clenched his teeth as he swayed his hands, before being surrounded by a blue light. The teleportation runes were formed by angels in the Empire, thus it was easy for Abbadon to access them.
Avrin was on full alert, but as another figure appeared within the arena not too far from Leo, he felt his heart sink. “-Abbadon!-” At the appearance of Abbadon, Leo frowned a little. “It seems you were right. What a shame. In any case, is this boy really an Enigma ability user? He could be some sort of spell made by Driada.” He spoke, referring to to the demon queen.
Abbadon looked at Leo, who had his Sigil weapons out, and then at Avrin, who glanced back with a near expressionless look. “Herth, you're quite strong, though a lot of things are very strange. I feel I will get all the answers I need from you.
Whether you are right or wrong will be found out soon enough. I watched your fight with Leo and I am quite impressed. Catching you will be troublesome, and I would very much like to keep this matter secret, so do not cause trouble for me and surrender.”
Avrin frowned. He didn't want to conceal himself any longer. “Angel Lord, you're quite perceptive. Like a parasite that never gives up. You almost killed me in the elven continent, and even now stick around. I am simply here to collect that piece of Skymetal and nothing more.”
Abbadon’s expression changed as he snickered. He had finally found the culprit, but he soon thought. “-Elven continent?-” Thinking back, he remembered the issue with Myra and Syrana, as well as what they fought about. “I see. So you were there, correct? No doubt you were probably almost caught in that explosion. I will have to question you about that as well. In the meantime.”
Abbadon raised his hand before chanting. A white ring of light formed above him and extended for several meters in the air. “Divine Seal… The very seal I used to capture a weakened Azrael. I'm sure it is enough for you.” The ring of light shot towards Avrin, leaving a trail of transparent light in its wake.--------
