As usual remember my Temp prs are still new so don't blame them, and i am not a professional author if you guys find any errors please post them below so i can fix them asap we are also human and not able to find all errors.. --------------------
During Ursa’s mid trajectory flight Avrin swung out Astaroth to counter while rushing towards Giron, both weapons collided with one another causing the ground to tremble and split. From there Giron began to barrage Avrin with carefully located swings and slashes.
Wielding Ursa to him seemed as easy as wielding a short sword, the weapon in his hands seemed as light as ever but powerful enough to potentially kill a dragon if given the chance.
Avrin was not an idiot when it came to this battle, before he had acted he had made sure his divine sense had scanned around several hundred miles to see if any of Abaddon's lackeys were around, and thankfully it seemed he was free to do as he pleased.
He knew Giron was eyeing the skymetal and figured it was quite important if Avrin preferred it over a spatial ring.
Someone on his level of power, once they would eye something it would be difficult to urge them away. Avrin learnt this in his former life, high ranked politicians would often hire assassins to kill each other over a simple treasured artifact or precious jewel, of course such internal strife was kept secret to not show the citizens of how the clock ticked.
Astaroth and Ursa continued to clash against each other, though Avrin was holding back, the reason for this is he had learnt his lesson with Aegis, he didn’t want to damage the sigil weapon.
That was the other half of the reason he wanted to fight Giron, a full sigil weapon would no doubt allow him to greatly benefit, in the end he had to temporarily put up with Giron while he thought of a plan.
Giron narrowed his bestial eyes before he pointed the head of Ursa towards Avrin, “Berserk Wolf!” The weapon seemed to glow a heavy red before the color engulfed Giron causing his body to bulk up with his muscles and veins expanding greatly.
Avrin was careful not to lower his guard, immediately he emitted a powerful phantom pulse to engulf Giron who roared with fury as he dashed towards Avrin with an incredible speed, the ground he was stepping on turned into a small crater that broke apart.
Giron raised Ursa before bringing the axe head down, Avrin knew it would be bad if he was even close to the area the axe hit so he quickly used his void step to reappear 20 meters away.
At that moment Ursa smashed into the ground where Avrin had been standing and a rumble spread out before a wide cleave shot through the ground seemingly hitting an underground spring of water that soon ruptured with geysers blowing up from several directions.
Giron was astounded. “-Who is this person.... how is he capable of equaling me and even be faster than me? -” Giron was confused as he contemplated things, though Avrin had no longer decided to mess about with him.
Nebula mist surged around Avrin’s body as the fibers of his muscles changed. His skin had purple pulsing lines across his body as they surged down to his legs that began to reform, short spikes protruded from them as they seemed to thin out a little and form a small carapace like shell forming around his calf, of course this meant he had augmented his legs for a purpose.
Avrin knelt down before shooting towards Giron like a thunderbolt, his speed significantly faster than before.
Giron’s reddened eyes quickly knew trouble was at hand, he slashed about with Ursa to try and hit Avrin, but with a single void step Avrin appeared with ease behind Giron, the sharpened blade of Astaroth’s scythe head curving around and pressing against his neck.
This was a complete victory for Avrin, though he was a little disappointed. “-Sigil wielders, how dumb are these individuals to solely rely on the strength of their weapon and not properly learn combat techniques...-”
Avrin was somewhat thankful, he had also nearly fallen to temptation and solely focused on using Astaroth, but this meant that if he one day encountered someone who wasn’t that much weaker than him but relied on techniques and strategy then Avrin surely knew it would be his undoing, thus it was wise for him to practice his fighting skills and always do his best to use his abilities in combat, such as the void step or phantom pulse, in this case.
Such an easy win was a bit disappointing, it meant that Avrin wouldn’t have the chance to practice any other skills, but with skymetal on the line and wanting to keep himself hidden it was a fairly minor matter.
“Ha...haha you win friend, I admit defeat, I have never lost in my life, but you stranger have managed to defeat me, a sigil wielder, who at my peak is at the Mythical Level! May I know your name?”
Avrin’s brows twitched a little, this crazy animal was a bit humble when he knew his life was on the line. “Giron correct? If you want to keep your head I recommend you hand Ursa to me...” Giron’s expression flickered as he laughed without a fear of death.
“You want me to hand over to you the weapon that protects my people? And you call me crazy? You have no idea what would happen if Ursa leaves my hands and disappears. If you take Ursa, you are condemning millions of lives on this continent to die!”
Avrin wasn’t all that phased though he wasn’t at all heartless, “You tried to steal something I consider more valuable than a sigil weapon without second thought, and now you are trying to play the good guy and say millions of lives will be at risk if I take that weapon? Who do you think you're fooling. Though let’s say you are correct, what is it to me if millions die or not?”
Avrin’s words clearly carried a careful tone, of course this wasn’t like before, the lives of the people here could be avoided, he assumed Giron was speaking about humanity potentially invading.
He also knew Abbadon and the other sigil wielders would most likely help the beastmen. Trying to play to Avrin’s humanity was an interesting choice on Giron’s behalf.
“You....are you truly willing to condemn those lives because of my own greed? I admit...I was wrong for trying to seek your treasure...though...if you let me go I am willing to compensate you. Truly you seem like a hidden expert, I can’t imagine how someone so powerful managed to exist unless they are an enigma level ability user. But I’m sure you have your secrets...”
Avrin at this moment was on a thin line between making another enemy, if it could be avoided and he could benefit from avoiding it then why wouldn’t he see what Giron had to offer. “I don’t want ore...I don’t want riches.... I don’t want women....and I don’t want land.... what I do want to know is if you have knowledge of the location of any dragons on this continent?”
With Avrin saying what he didn’t want, Giron nervous face had sunk even lower, though he didn’t dare act rashly as Astaroth was carefully pressed against his neck, every time he looked at the weapon and its pulsing vein like features, it made his soul quiver and legs shake, he had a feeling that such a weapon was definitely something he couldn’t comprehend, but he suddenly widened his eyes at Avrin interest to find a dragon.
“Of course! Yes, I know of a dragon’s location. I can personally lead you there if you le-” before Giron could finish speaking Avrin raised his finger and stabbed it carefully into his back, he emitted nebula mist that soon formed into several streams of nebula mist that circulated around his body, this was not done to convert Giron but rather act as something else.
Avrin quickly let Giron go and moved back, Giron howled in a slight pain as he sensed the anomaly within his body. “What...d..did you do to me?!!” Avrin simply glanced at him.
“Just a bit of a measure for myself, if you betray me, the ability placed inside of you will devour your innards before you can expel it with mana, and if you try to expel it with mana as we travel it will still devour you from the inside out, and even if you could expel it quickly it will do more than enough damage for me to finish you off without trouble.
If I somehow find out you contact someone, for instance Abbadon, then I will just kill you. If you lie to me, well I will still kill you, all these situations will lead me to taking your sigil weapon. I’m quite certain both it and a dragon have the same amount of power, so consider yourself lucky I am giving a bit of value to the lives of your people and going for this dragon.
Avrin was not a former general for nothing, this body and his dark matter heart had made it often annoying to control his emotions and mindset, but strategy wise he was still competent, by allowing nebula mist to surge inside Giron, it allowed him the possibility of obtaining the sigil weapon if anything goes wrong, but if he doesn’t kill him and Giron takes him to the location of this dragon then he would still benefit.
Avrin would not give the dragon a chance to fight back, he knew how dangerous they were. He had given Giron a chance mainly because Avrin believed that if humanity saw the beast tribe in a weakened state they would make a move on them, otherwise why would he care. By the time Abbadon and the others intruded many individuals would have already died.
Deep inside though Avrin was hoping for Giron to betray him somehow after taking him to the dragon’s lair, this way he would be able to obtain two large boosts in power. Giron eyed Avrin with a newfound fear.
“Of...course... then I’m sure you don’t want to waste time...all I need to do is escort you to the dragon’s lair correct? And you will let me go?”
Avrin didn’t respond the way Giron had wanted him to and simply replied. “Be quiet and show me already, I am quite impatient in this regard....” Hearing Avrin’s response Giron frowned, his somewhat fur ridden face seemed to have stood on end, as well as his wolf ears twitching somewhat, “Very well.... follow me.”
Giron’s body flickered as he began to travel at a quick speed towards the south, Avrin easily managed to keep up even after de-augmenting his legs and body to revert back. He kept a 10-meter distance as he followed from behind Giron, and always made sure to keep his divine sense out, he didn’t trust this beastman in the least but felt the pros outweighed the cons.
“-How am I going to get out of this one.... I could use the alarm crystal Abbadon gave me, but by then I would have already died and he will have taken my sigil weapon...I can’t even remove that strange mist from inside my body, what is that stuff exactly, is that his enigma ability? What a scary thing...to be able to do this and wield such power...scarier is the feeling that he held back on me...why exactly is he after a dragon anyway? -”
Giron was thinking to himself with conflicted thoughts, in the end he could do nothing but abide to Avrin’s wishes and lead him to the dragon’s lair, Avrin had been following Giron for a half day, at the speed they were both travelling on foot alone they covered a good distance that would have usually taken several days.
Avrin could have gotten the location from Giron and used his divine step to eventually reach it, but this was a matter of trust that he did not have for Giron.
Eventually the two of them had reached a strange canyon within the small southern desert area of the eastern continent. Giron had an annoyed expression as he was here, of course he was not at all dumb, he had a plan, and that was to keep Ursa out the entire time, the reason for this was simple.
Deep within the canyon that seemed to extend on for a good while, a large mound of sand was covering a seemingly immense boulder that brushed up against the canyon's walls, the sand fell off this mound, but soon trembled as a part of the mound flickered before opening to reveal a large slit of an eye.
“Hmmmmm......” A deep ancient voice seemingly echoed causing the canyon to shudder and shake, “Sigil wielder...? Why are you here...?” 
A case of literary theft: this tale is not rightfully on Amazon; if you see it, report the violation.
The voice continued on and spoke managing to reach both Giron and Avrin who were nearly two miles away showing just how powerful it seemingly was, Giron snickered inwardly, the reason for keeping Ursa out was to hope that the dragon would detect it and awaken first, he would hope that it would have a better chance at attacking Avrin and possibly killing him.
Avrin felt his body shudder as the voice echoed, Giron looked at him strangely as if unsure on how to reply to the dragon, Avrin frowned as he looked at Ursa in Giron’s hand. “Idiot....put it away....” Avrin’s expression remained somewhat calm before he identified the location of the dragon using his divine sense.
Giron, who by fear of Avrin words quickly put Ursa away, felt something wasn’t right, though the draconic voice resounded again. “Answer me!”
This time the entire canyon seemed to shake, the difference between sigil wielders and dragons was the dragon’s entire body contained as much energy as a full sigil weapon. Dragons also definitely knew how to control it better than a sigil wielder without practice making them deadlier.
Giron watched as Avrin’s body turned to ash and seemingly moment later Avrin appeared in front of the dragon whose eye glanced at Avrin, it then watched as Avrin retrieved Astaroth that he had stored away during the travel, it looked at the weapon seeing how menacing it was and also how Avrin so easily appeared and covered a great distance, one thing came to its mind, and that was trouble!
A fierce, powerful red aura pulsed out which even managed to push Avrin back several meters, it bought the dragon enough time to raise its large body from the sand mound. The dragon itself seemed to look different to Wruen, its skin was more slick and held a reddish hue, its neck had a large lion like mane while its head resembled that of a snake with 4 large horns protruding from its forehead.
It also had many large spikes across its spine, and its length equaled that of the deceased Wruen. The dragon was very careful unlike its deceased brethren, a large amount of mana gathered within its mouth before it quickly fired towards Avrin a red bolt of fire and lightning. Avrin was trembling a little, he remembered when Wruen had nearly bit him to death and his advantage on it before, though this time he had the physical body of a sigil wielder and the strength to exceed one.
Avrin was confident that if he were to go all out now he would be able to handle Abbadon and another full sigil wielder, though he was still cautious and didn’t dare openly put himself out as plans seemingly never always go according to plan.
Avrin didn’t dare underestimate this dragon, his legs had augmented again to allow him great speed. He quickly slashed Astaroth towards the red fire bolt and, with a bit of effort, split it in half. As the two halves crashed into the canyon walls exploding out with enough heat to make the sand form into glass that then cracked.
The dragon raised its body as it gazed at Avrin with caution. “Who are you....” It spoke but Avrin didn’t reply as he dashed towards it using his speed capable of catching even Mythical Level opponents off guard, the dragon roared out sending a shockwave pulsing out before it turned its body, its tail seemingly as slippery as a snake cut across the canyon wall like a hot knife through butter before smashing towards Avrin.
“Stygian Slash!!” Avrin roared out as he slashed Astaroth towards the oncoming tail, a wave of dark matter energy surged out from Astaroth before colliding with the tail that was soon effortlessly cleaved off, the dragon roared out in agony as it charged up another fire bolt and shot it towards the wave of dark matter.
Two forces collided with each other before exploding out and causing the canyon to tremble again, Avrin had taken the chance to dash up the crumbling canyon wall and reach a higher vantage point above the dragon who looked around for Avrin, it was unable to detect him due to him having no mana, so it was left somewhat in the dark.
Avrin gathered a large amount of nebula mist above the dragon forming it into a large cloud, that was until the dragon gazed up and began to gather a large amount of mana, this time the horns on its forehead began to light up, Avrin knew this attack would be dangerous.
“Heaven Bolt!” The dragon’s ancient voice resounded, the sky above seemed to form into a vortex as clouds gathered, suddenly a powerful crack hidden behind the clouds echoed as a red bolt of lightning shot down towards Avrin,
“-Not a Terror Burst? -” Avrin clearly was a bit surprised he had felt this dragon would be like Wruen, but he had to be careful that dragons are the most capable casters on seleria next to the gods, even Abbadon was a step behind.
“Void Screen.” The cloud of dark matter and nebula mist that Avrin had intended for an attack suddenly shifted forming into a large screen like shield above, the red bolt smashed into it causing it to crack and shatter after a while, but it bought Avrin enough time to escape the vicinity of the weakened bolt of lightning that crashed against the canyon wall splitting it in half and causing rubble to explode out.
“You insolent worm, you dare attack me, the great Silis!” The dragon roared out again as it began to gather mana in its body, Avrin though had learnt his lesson, “Stygian Reap!”
Astaroth pulsed with energy as the closed eye on its head twitched a little, Avrin slashed in a full 360-degree circle as his hands flickered, the entirety around him a circular wave of energy shot outwards like a rocket, the attack itself unlike the Stygian Slash was not focused on absorbing energy and growing stronger and larger, this circular reap motion was meant for cutting!
Though with each use Avrin felt Astaroth was seemingly draining quite a bit of dark matter from his body, he didn’t want to prolong the battle, so as the circular attack neared Silis who quickly used the mana he had gathered to activate another spell. “Demon spawn, you emit such a disgusting feeling, see if you can break a defense only surpassed by the gods! Red Space field!”
The area in front of Silis extending out for 5 meters suddenly trembled as the mana he gathered surged out and caused the space to distort before forming into a wide screen shield of red static mana, it seemed strange as the shield reflected a seemingly desolate space.
The moment the Stygian Reap crashed against it, the field trembled as it began to form cracks. Silis looked on with horror. “Impossible!” Quickly he began to gather mana again, but Avrin had already calculated something like this, after all how could a spell by a mere dragon match the strength of a skymetal weapon.
Avrin was capable of using quite a bit more of Astaroth’s strength and only held back enough so it wouldn’t use too much of his dark matter. While the reap was attacking the shield from the front and quickly making progress in destroying it, Avrin snickered before he used a void step to appear on top of Silis’ head where his horns were gathering mana.
“Don’t mind me....” Avrin snickered before Astaroth turned into a flicker, and within moments the horns on Silis’ head were cleanly cut off, the dragon roared out in agony as it quickly twisted around, but the red space field also collapsed.
The Stygian Reap, although weakened, still contained 60% of its full strength, it crashed against the limbs and belly of Silis cleanly cutting off its two front feet and also greatly wounding its stomach.
Avrin who was gripping onto one of the remaining two horns as Silis moved around in a rampage before the Stygian Reap cut its front feet off. “Stygian Slash!” With a final attack he managed to release the attack at point blank range cleanly beheading the roaring Silis.
The large dragon’s body trembled a little before falling limp onto the ground with blood and mana gushing out of the wound, the dragon’s face maintained an agonized shocked expression, Avrin though was ecstatic, the fight against a dragon was much easier than it had been before.
He quickly expanded out nebula mist to act as a shell and net around all of Silis’ limbs including its tail, from there Avrin sat down and began to focus as he started to convert it all. He didn’t want to waste time, even as he felt Giron flee from the range of his divine sense he didn’t bother chasing him.
Giron, who was indeed fleeing in a heavy fear, was sweating bullets. “-H... He so easily defeated a dragon? Impossible...! -” He truly was afraid as he fled not even daring to attempt to remove the nebula mist that Avrin had placed inside of him until he was sure he would be safe.
Avrin remained seated and focused on converting Silis for an entire hour before in front of him was a one meter congealed mass of dark matter that rippled, it then began to shrink, from a meter to 2 feet, to a foot, and then several inches until it reached the form of a small sphere around 2 centimeters in diameter. Avrin carefully glanced at it before smirking, he retrieved the dark matter core from the air and looked at it carefully.
While Avrin placed the core into his mouth he had no idea that currently a very powerful individual was watching him, within the sky hidden behind several layers of magic to hide its presence, a large palace of gold and white was formed, inside this palace Septim was glancing down curiously, he had been careful when Wruen had died and placed magic seals around the locations of all the dragons he had created, when Avrin and Silis engaged in battle he was immediately alerted.
Septim watched as Avrin converted Silis into a lump of dark matter and then into the form of a sort of pill before swallowing it.
Septim had a look of shock and surprise as he wasn’t sure what to think of the situation. He was a little confused, he silently rubbed his beard as he began to think carefully, “- This creature is interesting, he isn’t a sigil wielder, and he so easily killed Silis.
An enigma ability?...No...the weapon he used...-” gazing at Astaroth’s image as Septim replayed the magical recording over and over again, his body began to shiver with fear. He knew the aura Astaroth emitted was something much more powerful than his own.
“-That weapon. No it can’t be, -” Septim then turned his head around to look at a large 1-meter rectangle chunk of ore that was hidden behind a shield of white light, inside that shield was truly a white piece of skymetal with white lines of energy pulsing through it like a stream of water.
“-God Essence can’t be forged anymore...the method to do so has long since been lost within this universe...how has he managed to obtain a weapon forged from god essence? -” Septim was indeed very cautious in how he thought about the situation, though not one ounce of greed appeared in his look, the reason for this is he feared that there were details even he didn’t know of.
“-In any case I should keep an eye on this one, and be sure he doesn’t cause too much trouble...-” Septim uttered before he opened his left palm, a green and white light forming in the shape of a seal, he then dropped the seal into the clear water pond that acted as a mirror for him to watch Avrin.
As the seal entered the pond Avrin who was carefully feeling for his dark space suddenly opened his eyes, he glanced around as he felt everything had gone silent. He looked up and saw the sky tremble as the clouds suddenly split apart, a white light shot down towards him with speed even he was unable to escape from. The seal flew towards him before smashing against his forehead.
“What’s...going on?” Avrin clenched his teeth as the seal caused his body to shudder. It brought no pain and slowly began to form on his forehead as if it were a tattoo branding itself, within moments just as quick as it appeared, everything seemed to regain its calmness, the clouds reverted back to their normal state and Avrin was left on his knees with a pained look, on his forehead was a white assortment of lines in the shape of a mirror.
-----------------This chapter may seem a bit rushed to some of you, but i think the pace and progress is quite realistic, especially given how quick Avrin is progressing now that he has this level of strength, though in the end its on you the readers to decide.when i start to feel like i haven't properly planned i draft up the plot in a text document which greatly improves srs quality from what i have seen, i'v planned the next 2-3 chapters so expect some progress :D

chapters.title: V4: Chapter 116 Zephiron's Intentions.
chapters.content:

i'm also considering a Q/A thread this post will include a poll so i can see if my readers would like one or not.
other then those not much else for me to say but to hopefully enjoy the chapter ^^ ----------------
Avrin felt his body twitch as the brand fully formed, a white marking with lines that formed the sketching of a mirror upon Avrin’s forehead. Immediately nebula mist surged to the location as it began to devour and absorb it, but it seemed that the brand itself was reforming quicker than the nebula mist could devour it. It also seemed that every time he attempted to remove the brand, it would absorb mana from the surroundings.
With a frown Avrin clenched his teeth as he glanced up into the sky, he had a suspicion of who exactly may have branded him with this but he wasn’t sure. Avrin’s body was tense as the dark matter core formed from Silis was currently flowing around his dark space, like an ocean current in a violent storm the dark matter was unstable and would need a bit of time before it would calm down.
Avrin’s divine sense was already expanded, and immediately a grim look appeared on his face, “Giron, and Abbadon?!!” Clenching his fists Avrin was irritated, he would definitely have taken advantage but he realized that every time he absorbed a core on a high level it would leave him in an unstable state for a while.
“-Abbadon will have no reason to hold back, once I absorb this core what will I have to fear from him or any of the other sigil wielders anymore?  Taking the time to wait and hide until now definitely saved me many irritating battles-” While thinking this, Avrin’s body turned to purple ash before he vanished, with no intention of facing Abbadon or Giron until he was stabilized.
With no need to hold his speed back he needed 3 divine steps in his current unstable state before reaching the cave the Kirin was in, a look of confusion appeared on its eyes as it glanced up at Avrin. “Muaster?”
Avrin reached down, placing his hand over the Kirin’s mane before he use his divine step to turn them both to ash and flee far north west. This time it had taken him 30 uses of this ability to reach a satisfying location.
With the Kirin also being transported with him, his teleportation required more focus and caution, he didn’t dare rush it, but in the current case he had managed to avoid Abbadon and Giron.
Avrin and the Kirin were currently in a cave system that had no real entrance, Avrin had teleported straight through and made his way down. Currently they were a mile underground which was considerably deep, the air was nearly nonexistent and it was quite cold for anyone but them.
Avrin walked over before taking a meditative position, he glanced over at the Kirin. “We have just under two years to train. In this time, unless it is significantly important, do not bother me. Do not wander off too far either.”
The Kirin glanced at Avrin with awe, its look seemed to be wondering why it at first felt an attachment to such a seemingly rude individual. “Owk...” the Kirin muttered before it gave a slight huff and walked off to a corner to begin its own training.
With time passing on quite smoothly, Avrin’s dark space had settled down very quickly when he focused on meditation. On the second day his divine sense had doubled in size, and was capable of a monstrous range spanning just over 40% of the planet.
Within his inner workings one could see shining dots of light that made up every inch of his body, these glowing dots were shining a heavy glow of purple, these dots were type 5 particles. Avrin had completely converted it all to type 5 particles, and had already begun to baptize them all.
He was 70% done with this new stage and he had decided to name these several stages, from 1 to 5 would be the infant stage, from 6 to 10 would be the beginner stage. Of course the beginner stage would obviously take longer, as for what was after that, with Avrin’s improvement, the book within his inner workings allowed him access to that information.
He gave it a simple name, the Dark Stage, and then paid no more attention to it for the moment. Within the 2 years that have passed, on Avrin’s second year when he had achieved 100% type 5 particles, he didn’t hesitate to remove the seals from the skymetal. The moment he did it lashed out towards him, though he was much stronger now and easily overpowered it.
He then tried his best to will his dark matter heart to react towards the Skymetal, and a vortex like torrent appeared on his chest before the skymetal was absorbed with a shrieking resistance. Currently Avrin was unable to see the depths of his dark space, he could only feel that it was like a river that grew slowly, and deep in the section was a pitch black darkness with only a faint light.
The skymetal chunk that had attacked him before it was absorbed had purple streams of energy running across it and pulsing as if it were alive. Within this pitch black darkness Avrin could faintly see a familiar purple glow that was slowly being tampered with by a strange energy he couldn’t currently comprehend, so he left it all to his dark space hoping it would form something useful.
During the course of occasionally expanding his divine sense Avrin also, within the first year, discovered the presence of many angels scouting around the continent of the east, even Abbadon as well as Giron seemed to scout around, this made Avrin’s expression irritated.
When he had killed the dragon he had been branded, his thought was maybe it was something to keep an eye on him. Avrin decided for now, until he was sure, he wouldn’t cause trouble and be greedy for sigils, he would bide his time.
The brand itself was strange, it would occasionally give him the feeling as if he were being watched, as if someone was watching through the seal itself. A very eerie feeling, he truly wanted to find this individual and beat them to a pulp for this stalker act.
Other than this Avrin spent most of his time assisting the baptizing of his type 5 particles to the first stage beginner particles. It was quite simple, particles would be thrown into his dark space and under the control of him, or the firstly baptized c particles, they would absorb the currently thick dark matter sludge into themselves before being placed back and given time to absorb it all.
There was no real difference in size but the glow of the particles was heavier and purer than a type 5 particle as if the particle itself was developing a sort of aura. Avrin also occasionally checked his dark space to check on the skymetal.
Disappointment always followed as he never felt any increase in strength, he felt maybe when it was done it would give the increase but he didn’t know when this would be the case, it looked the same as ever, as if it were missing something.
In his current state Avrin gave a sigh of relief as he stood up, this was because with his current state of power Abbadon had now lost the chance to put up a fight with him. No doubt if Avrin explained it to Abbadon, the latter would be furious and annoyed at his inability to locate Avrin. Avrin felt other than the gods and probably Orochi, he felt no one on the planet would be able to threaten him.
The feeling was very strange for him, he had considered sigil wielders powerful existences that made him nervous at first, but within a handful of years his progress was like him leaping over a mountain in one go.
It made him shiver slightly, he remembered god saying he has great potential to become a god as well, although he believed him at first, the belief in this fact was now set in stone now that he had seen his own progress. By playing his cards right he had advanced incredibly well, though he didn’t plan to stop yet, he felt he still had limitless things to accomplish before he could achieve his full potential.
Glancing at the Kirin who quickly jumped in surprise after it saw Avrin, it quickly spoke out. “Master you are finished?!” Avrin blinked as he could see the Kirin had also matured within two years. It used to stand 2 feet tall and was half a meter long but after 2 years it now stood 4 feet tall and is over a meter and a half long.
Its mane was thicker and also had several tufts of thick white hair around its hooves, its tail was a large mess of jagged hair, and it now had a pulsing black horn that stretched 3 inches from its forehead. The two streaks of purple from its shoulders down to its backside were now thicker and also seemed to faintly pulse dark matter.
Seeing this Avrin nodded in approval, this creature surely had good strength. Just by feeling its progress he was satisfied, he could detect that in its chest a small vortex pulsed slightly, this feeling was obviously a dark space. He was shocked as it was much weaker than his own, but it was to be as expected.
“You have progressed well, though...” Avrin listened to the creature, its voice was soft and childish. The issue was he was unable to determine something. “Are you male or female?” He awkwardly spoke, the Kirin glanced at him a little confused at his words.
“Male or female? what does master mean?” Avrin’s right eyebrow twitched as he didn’t want to pursue the matter, it didn’t matter what it was as long as it served him and wasn’t useless. “Nothing, I will be heading away for a while, I want you to continue training here. If I do not return within a year, then you know where to go to find your brethren.”
The Kirin gave a sort of shriek like neigh as it seemed saddened. “Master...! Don’t go...take me with you! I will be bored here!” Anyone would truly want to hug this adorable creature and never leave its side, but Avrin was not one who cared about hugging or adorable creatures, logic was of far more use.
“It will be incredibly dangerous. Continue to train and become stronger, and I will consider taking you with me on dangerous tasks such as this more often. Remember, do not leave this cave unless I do not return within a year!”
With that said his divine sense had already expanded out to its maximum capacity, if one could see it with the naked eye and was in space, they would see a transparent tidal wave of purple energy engulf nearly half of seleria before stopping.
With a thought Avrin divine stepped away before the Kirin could reply, reappearing above the western ocean far past the central continent. He divine stepped again before reaching the western demon continent Zephiron, named after the demon god. Avrin just felt the god himself seemed arrogant to have a whole continent named after him but he soon ignored it.
He focused his divine sense around the western continent allowing him to better focus the faint particles of dark matter to gain more minute details of things. It was like an abundance of activity, as if Avrin was watching millions of ants from a human’s point of view, he could see what he wanted to see, and identify nearly everything, the stronger the individual the more Avrin could notice them.
Within the center of the demon continent Avrin could sense a large barrier that stretched in a dome shape the size of a palace. Avrin’s divine sense could penetrate inside of the barrier but it was still quite strong so he couldn’t feel everything inside.
This tale has been unlawfully lifted from . If you spot it on Amazon, please report it.
Avrin then felt a powerful energy at the early legendary level, he felt this would be his best chance at finding Azrael so he divine stepped again and effortlessly traversed a fair distance.
His location was under a city that was abundant with activity and trade, of course everyone within this city were demons! Deep underground, at least 30 meters in depth, a large system of tunnels was filled with armor clad individuals or people wearing robes while reading some strange tome.
These were all demons and none of which was weaker than an early stage expert showing that the demon’s strength was clearly abundant.
“Father...2 years have passed do you think Avrin will come?” A soft yet strong tone sounded out, this was Lilia who gave a happy yet curious look towards a large individual clad in red and black armor who was currently gazing over a map of the western continent.
This man was Azrael who had been freed by Avrin, he looked much healthier and had seemed to bring together as many followers as he could to prepare for something. “We can only hope. He is an integral person to help me.”
Within moments a voice sounded out behind him. “Integral am I?” This was Avrin who had divine stepped behind Azrael several feet away, this caused Azrael to jump in surprise as he dashed away, his heart was beating heavily as he looked at Avrin. “-I... I couldn’t detect him? -” he thought to himself.
“Avrin!” Lilia shouted out, by now Azrael had revealed to her that Herth wasn’t his real name and most likely a disguise and that his name was Avrin. Lilia rushed over and bowed in respect towards Avrin, any more and it would look like a kowtow.
“Lilia? Get up…” He spoke, he truly didn’t like being bowed to, it was quite weird for him. Lilia nodded and looked up at him. “Truly, thank you Avrin, for bringing about a miracle of justice and freeing my father!”
Avrin wasn’t sure how to respond so he simply nodded, at this point Azrael walked over with a look of surprise and smiled as he spoke. “You managed to find your way easily I see. Amazing I didn’t even feel you enter. Truly strange methods you have, though you are an enigma ability user so I’m sure it is normal for you.”
Hearing this Avrin spoke. “My methods allow me to travel quite well and keep myself safe from enemies. Though in this case finding you wasn’t that hard, though you don’t seem to have recovered? Your strength is at the early stage of the legendary level?”
Azrael blinked again in surprise. “You can feel that? Amazing...indeed right now I am at the early stage of the legendary level and I am purposely holding myself back. I am 90% recovered from the situation before, being trapped for hundreds of years does that to you, at my peak I am an early stage mythical being!” He said proudly with a sort of prideful look.
Avrin also seemed surprised, if he had a sigil weapon then no doubt he would be incredibly powerful, enough to match Abbadon. “Avrin it is good you are here, I have been making plans for your arrival but firstly, this is yours.”
Azrael walked over closer to Avrin, but at this point the brand on his forehead lit up, this made Azrael quickly widen his eyes as he dashed back and unsheathed a long sword, with his actions Avrin also kicked back and looked over at Azrael in surprise, Lilia who was confused also jumped back in reflex.
“A… Avrin what is the meaning of this!” Azrael roared out as he looked at the brand on Avrin’s forehead. Avrin blinked in confusion before noticing the brand was active. “This mark on my forehead? Why what’s wrong? A beam of light shot from the sky branded it into me....and I can’t remove it...what is it?” Seeing that Azrael seemed to know of it, Avrin wouldn’t miss this opportunity to also know what it is.
Azrael seemed conflicted as he looked at Avrin, he was currently sweating bullets as he could feel the brand activate. He spoke with nervousness as he looked at Avrin’s expression. “T... that is a mirror mark.... placed by a god.... I am not sure which god it is...but when it activates it means one of the gods are watching you....”
Avrin’s face paled a little as he clenched his fists, he could only sigh. “They can hear me to correct?” Azrael nodded as he glanced over at Avrin, “Since it looks like you didn’t know...I can’t blame you for this.... you must have done something to rouse one of their interests, what exactly did you do before you were branded?”
Avrin gave a soft smile as he looked at Azrael, a slight intent of power and pressure rose up in his expression, despite him being in his human form with the cloak's hood over his head his face was still somewhat revealed, one could see the expression he gave was quite powerful. 
This look made Azrael quiver with nervousness, Avrin who was much more powerful than a sigil wielder was a nearly unmatched existence on seleria after many cards being played right.
“I... will pass.... but I must say you have gotten incredibly stronger than before...or maybe you were always this strong?” Azrael couldn’t help but ask, the last time he had seen Avrin, although he couldn’t feel his presence, it wasn’t at the point where he didn’t know he was there, but the Avrin currently was more so unfathomable then before, his presence even made Azrael nervous.
“I’ve spent the two years training and honing my abilities, though I’ll consider your words a compliment, in the meantime” Avrin suddenly cleared his throat as a look of longing appeared on his face, even Azrael noticed this.
“Oh yes! I believe this is now yours.” Azrael raised his right hand to reveal that he had a spatial ring of his own located on his index finger, he pulled out a small glowing sphere about a foot long and within was a fist sized chunk of ore with black veins of streaming energy across it.
Avrin’s expression was strange, he glanced over at it with a frown. “That skymetal...it’s quite small...but it looks familiar. Azrael, to be honest with you, I fought Leo Zircus and defeated him as well as stole his spatial ring tha-...”
Avrin was about to continue before Azrael quickly spoke out, he expressed shock not at fighting Leo but rather the spatial ring. “THE RING! Avrin!! Please tell me you have it...!! Where is it?” Avrin was taken aback as he looked at Azrael in shock.
“The ring… It got destroyed in a conflict between me and the sigil wielder Giron.” Again Azrael showed no shock in Avrin’s battle rather his legs seem to tremble as he sighed, he looked at Avrin carefully seeing he didn’t seem to be lying. “You fought Leo Zircus, that bastard, and even Giron and still live… Incredible....”
He glanced at Avrin and gave a slight chuckle. “The truth is Avrin, the ring Leo Zircus has was not for him but rather mine... The ring I have now is a spare one that I keep on hand.
The skymetal within that ring he had was also mine, when I found the skymetal it was fragmented and somehow repairing itself, before it could though I absorbed the main chunk with my main ring and the second smaller chunk which is this with my second ring to keep on hand just in case.”
Avrin had to commend Azrael, he sure was cautious and in the end it was a good thing he had two spatial rings, but to obtain two of them he truly was powerful. “Ahh what a shame. That ring contained valuable items...though what’s done is done.”
Azrael could only sigh in regret before the chunk of skymetal hidden behind the spherical barrier floated towards Avrin who happily took it in before placing it within the enchanted sack he held. He then glanced at Azrael and spoke. “Is there any way to remove this brand?” His question was quite straightforward and also something Azrael was thinking about.
“Regarding this Avrin, there are two possible methods. One is to have a god remove it...which is unlikely. The other is I’m quite sure that the sigil weapon Void which contains the only few god ranked spells given to us mortals, may contain a dispel powerful enough to remove it. Though I am not certain as I have never held the weapon.”
Avrin could tell Azrael contained fairly good knowledge of Void, if he didn’t know better he may believe that Azrael once possessed it at one point. “I can see why the god branded you Avrin, you engaged in combat with two sigil wielders, truly an interesting turn of events especially since you yourself are not a sigil wielder. Though for this, “Azrael saw that the marking on Avrin’s forehead dimmed and deactivated. When this happened he quickly spoke.
“Avrin, I won’t be able to allow you to help me regarding Orochi… If the god that branded you is Septim and he finds out I plan to free Orochi, then things will be bad for me...the risk in freeing him is something I am willing to take. “
Azrael seemed serious regarding this but Avrin though for a moment before replying, “Does it make a difference, once Orochi is released Septim will discover you either way, and stop him?” Avrin curiously asked.
Azrael snickered before shaking his head. “The gods have an ancient law in place after Orochi was sealed, that is they are no longer allowed to interfere with the worldly matters, regardless of anything that happens. If Orochi is to be freed, I can only hope Septim curses his luck and leaves it as it is.”
Avrin frowned a little as he rubbed his forehead. “Worldly matters, nonsense.... this brand then of mine truly is unwarranted.” Avrin sighed before looking suspiciously at Azrael. “Though I’m curious, you were locked away for so long, how do you know all this?”
Azrael snickered a little before replying. “Branding an individual is considered viewing, though… Zephiron is a bit of a risk taker....” Azrael raised his right arm and lowered the sleeve after removing the plating to reveal that under his arm a black brand that was previously invisible began to form. Being the first of my kind the god Zephiron branded me as well.
This is called a Vocal Brand. Although it doesn’t allow Zephiron to see what is going on. Every 100 years it will have secretly gathered enough mana under the noses of the gods to let him give me some advice. The risk I take and my actions are all on the advice he gave me when I was sealed...I do not doubt that his words are not truth.”
Avrin glanced curiously before the brand quickly vanished just as quick as it appeared, no doubt Azrael took a very very huge risk to show it to Avrin who was branded by a god even if Azrael explained it for a few seconds, it showed just how thankful and trusting he was now to Avrin.
“Very well, that is fine, judging by your explanation then Septim can still interfere as long as you are within Orochi prison?” Avrin assumed this was the case, and Azrael who kept his eye on Avrin’s brand whenever he spoke nodded.
“Indeed. Once Orochi is freed and leaves the area not even Septim due to the laws in place will be allowed to interfere. Zephiron had also given me a chant to a god rank spell that is enough to free Orochi, of course in the process the mana usage will render Void useless for the next 10 minutes.
Entering the prison shouldn’t be too hard since Void also has a god ranked concealment spell that Zephiron notified me about. Unfortunately, if I knew of your issue beforehand I would have inquired about a god ranked dispel...”
Avrin was a little lost in thought. He was thinking not of freeing Orochi or helping Azrael, but why Zephiron is putting in plan so many things, Avrin had a gut feeling that this wasn’t something good. He had obtained his skymetal and only had to help Azrael retrieve Void, after that it would have nothing to do with him anymore and he would go to the north to train with his people.

Avrin put the thought aside for now. Right now he was thinking of the skymetal that he had stored in his enchanted bag, it was part of the main piece he obtained from Leo’s spatial ring. After waiting for so long the skymetal within his dark matter heart had not been forged yet, Avrin had a strange feeling it had something to do with this small chunk.
If this was the case then Avrin didn't want to absorb it now. If it suddenly activates and attacks him while he was occupied, it would spell trouble for him, so he thought it would be best to wait until he was alone.
Azrael glancing at Avrin suddenly spoke with a curious expression. “Avrin, you're capable of fighting on par with sigil wielders, and even managed to defeat Leo Zircus, just who are you truly?.”
Avrin simply glanced at Azrael and gave a soft smile. “In time not only you, but this whole world will come to know of who I am. Currently there is no need to reveal myself, in the meantime Azrael how did you want me to handle the situation with your daughter?”
Avrin didn't want to linger on the topic of who he was and thus brought up the final matter he had to attend to. Azrael who frowned a little as he couldn't find out Avrin’s true identity though he suddenly gave a serious look, “Judging by your strength Avrin, I have to tell you, do not underestimate Void.
I am not sure if my daughter has managed to master it or not, but this sigil weapon contains spells used by gods. It contains the most destructive force on this planet under the gods and above the dragons. I wish I could say I don't want to make things an issue for you, but my daughter....well she is still my flesh and blood, I only ask you do not kill or injure her greatly! She is still a child..”
Avrin was a little stumped judging by how things are, wasn't Driada born before Azrael was sealed long ago? He was wondering how Azrael could still consider her a child. “I’m not promising anything but it will depend on the situation, since I am also in a good mood I’ll try a bit harder.”
Avrin smirked a little before speaking again. “The place she is currently located at, I’m assuming it is covered by a large barrier of sorts?” With this spoken Azrael was a little astounded. “Oh Avrin, you researched before hand? Indeed this barrier is set up by Void as well and is a Mythical tier spell, Mage King’s Shield. I dare say that even us sigil wielders would spend a little time trying to break it, though I have a plan in how to deactivate it. Lilia please go over and retrieve the scroll over on that table.”
Azrael spoke to his second daughter who had remained silent the entire time. She simply smiled with excitement, she felt things were making progress, she hadn't been able to assist her father many years ago, but now she was able to. She was about to rush off before Avrin spoke, “No need!” Avrin glanced expressionlessly before his divine sense, which had already remained on the large dome like barrier, flickered somewhat before Avrin strengthened it. Avrin’s body turned to a purplish ash before he divine stepped an incredible distance. Such a feat could only truly be accomplished by the gods, and even they may not be able to do so easily.
Avrin could only see Azrael's astounded look before he had left and soon appeared within the barrier with no need to even break it. Avrin was a spectral being created by god himself and even given potential to become something incredibly great, how could he be stopped in his current state by a simple barrier.
Glancing around after he had reformed, Avrin could feel the atmosphere was a little desolate and cold, he could clearly feel everything within the palace now as the divine sense had re-expanded out. Within a large hall not to far from him, a being at peak of the Sage level and a power much greater, presumably the sigil weapon, were currently located within.
“-Simple, saves me a lot of time, but I will take Azrael's words to heart,-” Avrin knew sigil wielders couldn't detect him other than this Demon Queen, so the moment he had entered Driada who was currently sitting on her throne with a glass of wine in her hand suddenly felt Void quiver slightly.
“What's this?..” She waved her hand and Void rose up from its pedestal beside her throne before opening up in front of her and revealing a large layout of the interior of the palace, within was a small black dot that was currently glowing back and forth.
Driada’s eyes widened for a moment as she threw the glass of wine away before it shattered on the ground, the guards who had been within the hall all revealed curious expressions but none there wanted to ask what was wrong. Driada grabbed Void and carefully analysed it.
“-This dot, it symbolises that individual I have been searching for, I could only ever find him once after a few months then after a few years, and now Void you’re telling me he is within my palace!-” Driada clenched her teeth and looked as if she wanted to throw a tantrum.
Though the black dot which symbolised Avrin casually made its way across the map, several screams and shouts echoed out, this continued for several moments before everything grew deathly silent. The guards within the throne room were immediately alerted and roared out “Protect the queen!” While another would also shout out “Who dares attack the Demon Queen's royal palace!”
Driada tried to feel for what was going outside, but gazing she couldn't feel any ounce of mana, not even the black dot, it was as if it were there but not there. The large black obsidian doors in the royal throne room trembled slightly before silence was all that was left. Soon a faint purple mist began to seep in through under the door before the door seemed to wither and explode out.
A large tidal wave of nebula mist surged in catching some of the demon guards in surprise, they shrieked out, because as soon as the nebula mist touched them their armor began to disintegrate and their skin seemingly burn as it was eaten slowly by nebula mist. It hadn't taken long before they were grasped within the mist and thrown against the walls and pillars of the throne room, knocked unconscious.
Driada remained vigilant and had already cast a barrier over herself that expanded out a meter, this barrier was the Mage King’s Barrier, she was currently wondering how this individual entered without even breaking her previous barrier. “Impossible! How did you enter!”
With all the 10 guards at the Master level easily taken care of, the nebula mist surged to the ceiling and the ground before footsteps could be heard, an individual with a black cloak and hood that covered his face made his way casually within after seeing everyone was handled. “I truly have a bone to pick with you, Driada was it? Although I'm here on your father's request I also know for quite awhile you have been tracking me down, and it was only after I handled your goons did you stop.”
Driada was already standing up with Void prepared in her right hand, her eyes narrowed slightly, she revealed a slight look of fear. When she gazed at Avrin she felt as if she was unable to discern just how powerful he was, this worried her.
“Yes, you can see why I have tried to track you, though it was quite hard, eventually I gave up as I was unable to, but here you are, which saves me time, and then you say you are here on my father's behalf?” Driada grinned a little before Void began to tremble a little. “You definitely have something to do with freeing him, both you and my little brat of a sister, you're after my sigil weapon? “
Suddenly several glowing star shaped objects began to surge out of Void, each one representing an affinity of mana, from darkness to light, fire to water. Avrin was carefully examining the situation, though he was already acting, the nebula mist had already engulfed the entire floor of the throne room only unable to enter through Driada’s barrier, several shadow pillars began to form around her while Avrin spoke.
“If you know why I'm here, then save yourself the defeat and me the trouble. Hand over Void and I will be on my way.” Avrin didn't want to remain and trouble himself longer than he needed. But as expected Driada didnt accept and infact roared out. “ARROGANT!!” Driada then began to chant several phrases each one causing the star shaped objects to flicker before they all shot towards Avrin.
The flame one was the first to near him before it pulsed out and exploded into a flame pillar with a width of 10 meters. It effortlessly pierced through the nebula mist surrounding the ceiling and shot through as it exploded into the sky for a few moments before vanishing. Avrin had already used his speed to dash back and avoid it, a look of surprise and awe was planted on his face.
“Now this is magic!” He spoke with a look of excitement. The magic he had seen so far seemed quite lame in his eyes until now, but then again what could he expect from people of that level, Void was truly incredible.
Nebula mist surged around Avrin as the light star neared and exploded out, of course Avrin had already formed a shield of dark matter that was incomparably stronger than before. When the light star exploded out, it formed into a glowing white sword that struck down with a powerful might.
The sword slashed down across the dome like shield as it cleaved the ground somewhat before causing the shield to tremble slightly and crack a little. The power of the sword continued beyond the shield and split the portion of the palace in its direction in two with a large cleave that spanned for a 100 meters.
Avrin knew his own body's durability was powerful but these spells were still on the level of a Mythical being and would be able to injure him somewhat. Even worse was that she could use all the elemental affinities and together they posed a threat to him.
“This is what happens when you offend and go against the great Demon Queen! Not even the Angel Lord would dare easily fight against me! In this world I only stand below the gods!” Driada yelled with maddened laughter. Avrin frowned before he willed the 5 shadow pillars, that were currently congealed into spheres of pure dark matter that soon gathered enough energy before they surged and shot up like spears from within the mist.
The sudden sight cause Driada to panic but it had caught her off guard, the shadow pillars smashed against her barrier with strength no less than the Mythical level showing Avrin’s current ability. They easily penetrated through the barrier and seemed to hold the barrier with Driada inside of it in place, with Driada’s concentration lost the mana stars seemed to stop in motion.
It was then that Avrin’s hands flickered before several powerful condensed void spheres shot out and precisely hit all the mana stars before turning them into ash although Avrin regretted it a little since these would make decent dark cores. He waved his hands once more the moment Driada began to chant again, and before she could continue the shadow pillars exploded into nebula mist causing the barrier to shudder and crack even more.
The tips of the shadow pillars that were already a couple of feet in had turned into nebula mist that remained in the barrier, it began to twist around Driada before forming into void spheres, Driada panicked in her mind but her incantation was finished. 
Love this story? Find the genuine version on the author's preferred platform and support their work!
Void surged before a pulse of dark light exploded out from it. “Zephiron’s Pulse!” A surge of dark mana caused not only the nebula mist inside the barrier, but the barrier itself as well as the nebula mist gathered around her to explode away, the spell was incredibly powerful as it even destroyed the walls and supporting pillars of the throne room and not even stopping.
The entire palace began to tremble showing that it was clearly unable to hold all this. The remaining individuals who had not been knocked unconscious by Avrin had already fled, Avrin could simply sigh a little before using the dark matter that still remained to form a barrier over the guards that he had defeated within throne room as the palace began to crumble slightly, the ceiling collapsed greatly as a large hall was opened up the moonlight shot through illuminating the dimly lit throne room.
“You’re truly crazy..” Avrin shook his head in disappointment slightly. Driada whose hair was now messy and gave an annoyed twisted look no longer looked like an attractive seductress but more so a corrupted devil. “You...HOW DARE YOU!!” Mana of all sorts of affinity began to surge around her from Void before she began to float up and shot past the hall formed by her spell.
She was now 50 meters above the palace, she glanced down at Avrin with annoyance and began to chant again. “E’rtil Nuiya Opthinio Luesuis Neyuinik” while continue her chant Avrin had a strange feeling, but excitement continued to well up in his body as he grinned. His body exploded out with dark matter that continued to seep out not only from the mana in the air but also from his enormous dark space.
After 10 seconds of chanting, Void seemed to tremble slightly as well as Driada’s face going pale, one could tell the spell was something she could barely handle. A slight tear in space appeared above a nearby mountain before the mountain was seemingly ripped apart, all the debris and rubble was sucked into this rip in space, of course all this happened several miles away.
Another rip in space appeared above Driada, the debris that was sucked in was shot down and began to form into an object. Eventually one could see the object formed was an enormous spear, all the debris was crushed extremely tightly together, the 700 meter high mountain was now condensed in a 100 meter spear.
The spear began to radiate mana from all affinities as the tip of it began to form a spiral of energy that seemed to distort space slightly. Driada laughed as she spoke with her voice echoing out, although the only one around to hear it was Avrin as the city had already been evacuated very quickly, and all the spectators were quite far with fear of getting closer.
“You insolent worm! I had tried to recruit you before, but now you are going against me! This is a God Tier spell of Malakus, Continental Spear! Rumored to have the strength to pierce a continent!!”
Driada clearly was experiencing a surge of excitement but Avrin only snickered before a vortex formed within his hand, a mass of dark matter seemingly formed into a spear of his own with a length no greater than 2 meters long, with a width of 5 centimeters. The spear itself was black and purple but emitted a heavy tyrannical aura one could say this was the most powerful weapon Avrin had personally formed using his current maximum strength without the help of a sigil weapon.
Of course this was done out of experience but without holding back. Driada glanced at the spear in Avrin’s hand and felt her heart shudder slightly, she could see the dark matter still surging around it. She roared out in her temper before pointed her hand towards Avrin.
The large Continental Spear shot towards Avrin like a comet descending from the heavens, a small air vortex seemed to form around it with the spiral of all mana affinities at its tip shining about like a being ready to exert justice.
Avrin raised the spear in his hand aiming it carefully towards the continental spear, with his body experience and divine sense it was nearly impossible for him to miss it, “Let’s see which is stronger then, your god level spear or mine!”
Avrin’s right hand shot outwards before the spear released, it seemed to screech and shriek in anger before space distorted, it seemed like an evil unleashed upon the world after experiencing torture and now wanting revenge.
The spear suddenly exploded forward before it distorted, it began to zigzag in many angles as if it were sentient. It then shot towards the tip of the continental spear, both of them colliding before an explosion of force pulsed out causing the palace to crush down, even the buildings near it weren't spared as they were crushed to dust. Avrin as well as Driada needed to create barriers whether of mana or dark matter to protect themselves from the aftershock.
It was only for a couple of seconds before Avrin’s spear easily gained the upperhand, it shot through the continental spear after destroying the mana affinity tipped point. The continental spear shattered into a rain of rubble and dust, but Avrin’s spear zigzagged again as it shot towards Driada who gave a look of horror.
Avrin’s eyes widened before he quickly willed the spear to not hit her, but its speed was beyond his expectation, it had already pierced and destroyed her barrier before shooting towards her chest. It barely drew blood before it quickly zigzagged around with precision and shot back down towards Avrin before it was grabbed.
Avrin could feel the spear was quite tyrannical, he has used dark matter on the level of two sigil weapons, he wouldn't want it to go to waste, and would be sure to reabsorb it when he was done. He divine stepped in front of the shocked Driada who didn't have time to recover, the spear was pointed towards her head as he glanced at her.
Driada glanced back with shock and horror, “You....” She uttered out, of course Avrin didn't let her continue. His hand flickered before he personally snatched Void from her at near point blank range. Even more shock appeared on her face as her eyes welled up. “You… You bully!!!” Tears began to well up in her eyes as she burst into tears cursing Avrin and began throwing a childish tantrum with childish curses. Avrin’s expression flickered as his face paled a little, he absorbed the spear he had created not even bothering to name it at this moment, but he knew it was something that would truly help him later on if he didn't want to use skymetal weapons.
Avrin frowned and gazed at her “-Azrael wasn't joking she truly is a child-” after thinking to himself he reached over and grabbed Driada by her left hand. “Be quiet, and stand still....” Driada who continued to cry and curse at Avrin was about to take her hand back before she felt her body become heavy and then like him turned to ash.
Divine stepping with an individual of dark matter wasn't hard for Avrin, he had no need to touch them unless he was in a dire state, but when it came to objects and beings made of mana he needed to either have a grip of them or have them within a cloud of nebula mist that scaled to them.
Avrin had been gone for 15 minutes, Azrael had already heard from his connections of a battle taking place within the royal capital. He gave a nervous look although he could do nothing but wait, he was no match for his daughter if she used Void. “Father, please relax, Avrin will surely come out victorious!” Lilia spoke with pride as she glanced at Azrael who was seated.
Of course all his subordinates were tending to their own matters, trying to not look nervous themselves as they understood what was on the line. Though space seemed to ripple slightly before small ash like particles formed into two individuals. One was an annoyed Avrin while the other was Driada who was crying and cursing at him.
Driada suddenly stopped and looked around, Azrael also looked up and the two of their eyes met. “Father!...” Driada clenched her teeth as she felt her heart skip a beat, Azrael glanced at her then at Avrin as well as Void in his hand, a smile formed on his face and color soon returned. “Avrin...it seems I underestimated you again. I hope my daughter wasn't to much trouble.“
Azrael frowned a little and his right hand emitted a black light that shot towards Driada who was exhausted and afraid, the light engulfed her hands and seemingly covered her in runic seals, she fell to her knees and growled angrily. “Let me go father!!” She roared out.
Azrael clenched his teeth and shouted. “SILENCE!. You dumb child....have you learnt nothing in all these years, your mother and I have truly spoiled you and in the end it wasn't you who had bothered to lift a finger to save me but your poor younger step sister who has suffered more than you!!”
Driada’s eyes narrowed as she laughed and spoke out. “You're despicable father, how can you refer to her as even half my sister...she is the spawn of a human, you betrayed mother when she died and fell in love with some human?...Only for her to die as well during the war, hahaha” Driada seemed to laugh madly again.
Lilia only frowned with a saddened look, Azrael’s expression flickered before he walked over and raised his hand about to slap his daughter, but when his hand came down, Avrin raised his hand and grabbed it and glanced over at Azrael.
“Avrin...you?.” Azrael was stunned that the one who stopped him was Avrin, Driada was also shocked at this. Avrin simply glanced over and spoke. “Although she has angered you greatly, she is still your daughter, and you her father...these relations are something I'm sure need to be remade, that being said you told me yourself she is still a child and also spoiled, handle the matter in a different way, and if you still insist on hitting her, do it when I'm not around...”
Avrin’s glance weighed heavily on Azrael who quivered a little before nodding and gazing at Driada before sighing. “You're right...my temper has gotten the better of me… I apologize Avrin. Lilia and you two, come put Driada within the earthen cell..” Lilia glanced at Driada and soon two individuals of the peak master rank came over and the three of them began to lead a silent and shocked Driada away.
Azrael then glanced at Avrin, he was truly interested in furthering relations with him, but the brand Septim placed on him made things annoying. “Well things have been handled. You're quite quick with your methods. I'm jealous of that teleportation which seems to be unique to you, of course if it is learnable I wouldn't mind coming to an agreement with you, I also know the location of a dragon within this western continent, how about it Avrin?”
Avrin glanced curiously at Azrael, though he was no longer currently interested in dragons if this brand wasn't removed, as well as the fact that he was branded the moment he killed a second one. “I will pass on that, for the moment though, see if you can remove this brand.” Avrin passed Void over to Azrael somewhat reluctantly as he had to force a bit of the greed away.
Azrael nodded and could only sigh in regret not daring to push the matter further, he had taken Void and began to read across it as he began to give looks of awe, confusion, and even laughter at times. “This is amazing...so many spells and possibilities...some even I have tried studying but have never been able to comprehend, Avrin this-”
Avrin’s arms were already folded as he gave a somewhat annoyed look, Azrael paled again and soon laughed. “Of course the dispel, let's see here, oh here it is!” After turning a few pages he had found what Avrin was after.
“This spell is known as Holy Surge. a high level Mythical spell capable of removing any curse, poison, and ailment, under the power of the gods. I won't keep you waiting longer, the chant for this is in ancient tongue instead of the common language formed today,”
Avrin simply remained quiet as he waited for Azrael, of course inside he was eager and hoping it would work.----------
