“Yeos, Myisdio Ty’uirin Hyisha’Gik, Nyurenin Sento!” When Azrael’s chant finished a white light surged from Void before shooting towards Avrin’s forehead. It engulfed the brand that began to shake slightly and tremble for a moment, the entire light on Avrin’s forehead lasted for 10 seconds before the spell grew fainter and fainter. It then vanished leaving Azrael stunned and nervous.
“Avrin....the spell cast on you is God ranked, I’m afraid a Mythical level ability like this won’t do...though, you’re an enigma ability user, I’m truly stunned you yourself are unable to find a method to remove it.”
Avrin sighed a little. “-If it was that simple I would have already done so! Even when I divine step the brand is quick enough to track and follow me and reform with me, such a cheat of an ability I will truly murder the god that branded me...-” as the thought crossed his mind Avrin gazed at Azrael and spoke. “If that’s the case I thank you for trying, I should be going.”
Azrael quickly replied to Avrin, “Though I couldn’t remove the spell, I have to warn you of several things, the one who cast it, is no doubt the king of gods Septim. I have long since been around with my creator Zephiron, and the energy within that brand is definitely of Septim’s. This is a real shame, I wanted you to assist me in my plans...but since it is Septim it's truly impossible to allow you to join me. Though only a god can remove that brand on you.”
Avrin listened but in truth he didn’t feel like he was at a loss, he would return to where the Kirin was and see if he could fix the issue with the skymetal, if all goes according to plan he would be able to improve his strength by another leap.
He knew where the gods most likely were but with his divine step even if he managed to go up there, there would be no way he could enter through that shield and even if it was possible many issues still arise. He could only wait till he became strong enough to remove it on his own or hope for his luck to get better.
Though Avrin also knew something big was going to sweep across seleria, this was Azrael’s plans on freeing Orochi. If this happened most likely only the northern continent with little matter on seleria would be spared, then again if the worst happened, Avrin would just have to step in and decimate Orochi with all his might. Of course this would only happen if Orochi threatened the livelihood of his people.
“Azrael just why do you want to free Orochi to use?” Avrin couldn’t help his curiosity though the question posed caused Azrael’s face to give a cold angry look. “The reason for this war...Abbadon was cautious and jealous at how my demon race had grown immensely strong, and needed to start a war to unify the races...thus he killed my wife.
Even when he tried to deny it with the god Zephiron on my side how could his lies work...eventually I sent a large force to invade and hunt down Abbadon but he used this as an excuse to unify the races against me and even eventually had to get Fafnir to defeat me!”
Avrin showed not much of a change even though this war was started hundreds of years ago and he now knew the reason, it was simply a matter that was none of his concern. “Well that is fine, though let me give you a warning Azrael, if Orochi attacks the northern continent, I’ll slaughter it myself.”
Avrin’s words contained no heavy aura or killing intent. Azrael wasn’t an enemy thus he had no need to threaten or scare him, Azrael simply laughed it off and spoke. “Do not worry, Orochi is one against the gods, you and him have no matter against each other.
In this case Avrin I will have to bid you farewell, no doubt the disturbance at the royal capital will be brought to Abbadon’s attention, and I’m sure he is searching for both you and me. I need to prepare myself and get used to this sigil weapon. I will bid you farewell here.”
Avrin also agreed with this, he nodded and soon the two exchanged few words before Lilia also entered and gazed at Avrin. “You're leaving so soon?” A saddened look appeared over her face, one could see she had begun to look up to Avrin.
“I have my own things I need to tend to, you will also be busy in the future and need to help your father, “Avrin gave a simple reply to her, though Lilia sighed, she wanted to learn more about Avrin as to her he was truly a strange being that appeared out of nowhere. The top individuals of seleria had been set in stone but here he was some unknown that had appeared and trampled on several of these individuals.
Lilia wasn’t sure how to reply she could only bow again and thank him, “For all that you have done from freeing my father to assisting in retrieving Void as well as not harming my sister, thank you Avrin!”
In his eyes Lilia truly was the most innocent of the demon race he had seen and even then she was a half breed, it made him falter somewhat when he wondered if Azrael’s chase in revenge would endanger her, but in the end it was still none of his concern. His body turned to a purple ash as he divine stepped away, his monstrous divine sense had already expanded out and after 2 divine steps he had reached the underground system in the eastern continent where he had left the Kirin in.
The moment he appeared the Kirin had woken up from its training and like a puppy it ran over to Avrin and began to jump up and down around him. “Master is back. Master is baaaaaack haha!” It truly was excited, this made Avrin feel a little awkward, he didn’t expect it to make much progress. He had finished the task given to him in such a short amount of time it was laughable that he told the Kirin if he didn’t return within a year it was to go find its brethren.
“Quiet down.” Avrin spoke and sighed before the Kirin seemingly ignored him for a moment and then stood still before speaking. “Master! Next time take me with you, this place is so dark and boring, don’t do this to me!” It gave a miserable look as if it wanted to cry out in misery.
Though Avrin simply smirked at the pitiful creature, he walked over and sat cross legged before reaching into his enchanted sack and then pulled out the sealed small fist sized chunk of skymetal that Azrael had given him. “Whoaaa master what is that, it looks nasty!!!......Can I eat it?”
Avrin wasn’t sure whether this Kirin was playing dumb or just plainly dumb, he even questioned whether the sphere he had given it had worked to its full efficiency. “No you fur coat...you cannot eat this...it’s not only important it’s also mine!” With that said Avrin willed his dark matter heart to activate and within moments a vortex appeared out which caused the Kirin to feel frightened and jump back, the skymetal within the barrier Azrael had set screeched, not only was the barrier devoured but the skymetal followed, and soon it was absorbed within it.
Deep within Avrin’s dark matter heart, a large patch of land with black grass seemed familiar, this was the patch of land that opened up when Astaroth was devoured, though instead of switching from black to green it was now black to red blood colored grass.
In the distance a dark matter core of energy with a red smaller yet also bright star like energy was forming around it. Also circulating around this pitch black star was a smaller black mass of energy smaller than the red star and showing signs of instability though it had a sort of barrier of transparent purple energy around it seemingly keeping it intact.
Suddenly a space opened up before the skymetal that was devoured came screeching in. It was thrown over towards the center largest black star before it shrieked with anger and misery. It began to melt and congeal all within an instant before forming into a small mass of black energy similar to the unstable mass within the barrier that orbited with the red star.
The newly formed energy from the skymetal shot over towards the unstable black mass before it entered the barrier and soon combined with it, at this moment the whole space trembled as the black unstable mass grew to the size of the red star and gave a much more stable look as if it had been cured and was healthier. It pulsed out with energy before the entire mass shot into the center large black star that was indeed the core of Avrin’s dark matter heart, where skymetal would be forged.
The mass began to congeal and take shape it began to shift and form, it took the form of a humanoid figure who moved both his hands in front of him, his left hand near his stomach with its palm faced up and his right hand over his chest palm faced down, the humanoid figure was formed from a small trace amount of energy by the center dark matter heart's core.
While this figure maintained this position the skymetal seemed to form into, shrink down and congeal in between the individual’s palms that were kept in this position in front of him.
The skymetal shrunk and reshaped until it took the shape of an object, this shape and position was quite strange but familiar to the earth of Avrin’s past universe.
This was a weapon mentioned within the Rig Veda, a collection of ancient Indian Vedic Sanskrit and hymns. This weapon was in the form of the Vajra. This Vajra was simply a double Vajra, the top and bottom parts of a the Vajra seemed contain a deep dark emptiness possibly matched only by the hunger and depth of a black hole, the center contained a black living crystal that was transparent and seemed to pulse with hunger and eagerness to eat.
The Vajra pulsed with energy as it seemed to give a baby like scream having just been born, it trembled before the humanoid figure holding it also trembled, the crystal within the center of the Vajra was held onto the top and bottom half by a collection of vein like bindings that acted as chains.
The crystal emitted a heavy dark glow before the doppelganger like figure similar to Avrin in appearance was transformed into a stream of energy and instantly devoured within the center of the Vajra, of course the amount of energy was so miniscule that it wasn’t even noticeable within it, showing just how much of an appetite it had.
The Vajra again felt the mass of the dark matter core and emitted another pulse as if trying to devour it, but the moment it happened the dark matter core emitted a heavy menacing pressure which caused the Vajra to shriek in fear and shoot out from within it. It then hovered about before eyeing the red star that was Astaroth.
The red star seemed to form a single closed eye before opening and gazing at the Vajra, the Vajra was still a small black eye formed from the center of the crystal gazing back at Astaroth. They both emitted heavy amounts of energy as if trying to compete, though the dark matter core again pulsed out which caused both Astaroth and the Vajra to shriek and close their eyes, the Vajra immediately trembled and tried to free itself.
If you discover this narrative on Amazon, be aware that it has been stolen. Please report the violation.
In the distance back within the grasslands that were changing from black to red, Avrin was already inside, the moment the Vajra had formed he had been sucked within to this world after examining his inner workings, this was the light in the distance of his inner workings that he was unable to see until now. He watched the Vajra cause trouble for the dark matter core and even go as far as to challenge Astaroth. Avrin could only smirk before gazing carefully at the Vajra, the Vajra seemed to gaze back towards him as its eye opened again.
Avrin felt himself quiver as if the force of a whole galaxy was weighing down on him, it was intense but the feeling it gave was nothing compared to the feeling within god’s presence. In this case he only broke out in a small cold sweat.
The Vajra shrieked again as it shot towards Avrin who of course was already prepared for this. This was his body and there was no way he was going to ignore the Vajra and give it time to prepare itself and attack him like Astaroth did.
The Vajra smashed against the invisible wall that seemingly held it in place, it shrieked again in anger before its core pulsed, the invisible wall trembled before it appeared in the same view as the white brick limitless wall that split this dimension in half.
The moment the white wall appeared it no longer seemed to notice the Vajra as if it were unaffected by it in the least. But the door on the other hand, the plain wooden door trembled before it was shattered and the material absorbed within the Vajra that soon charged towards Avrin with an attempt to devour him to.
“You're trying to best me within my own body!!” Avrin willed Astaroth to appear, the large red star that was orbiting his dark matter heart vanished before reappearing as Astaroth in his hand.
Avrin struck down with Astaroth towards the Vajra, a large surge of energy surged out which caused the entire mass of land to tremble. Avrin felt that if this was in the real physical world then he would probably already be dead, but due to this being the core of his inner workings then it was possible for him to survive.
The newly made Vajra seemed to shriek in anger again as it felt it was unable to overpower Astaroth but even then Astaroth radiated a heavy energy as if it were also angry that it couldn’t overpower the Vajra, had it not been for Avrin already possessing ownership the two weapons would most likely clash in a terrifying battle.
At this point Arvin's dark matter core shot a point of black light that penetrated Vajra’s center which made it scream in pain, it struggled for only a moment before it dimmed down, it then reformed into a mass of black energy that was thrown back to where the dark matter core was and began to orbit it silently like an obedient child.
Avrin carefully relinquished control of Astaroth and it reverted back to the red mass of sun, and the two skymetal weapons began to orbit his dark matter heart, it was then that Vajra pulsed out silently this pulse engulfed not only Avrin's core dimension but his inner workings as well and his dark space.
He felt his body shudder before feeling as if he was energized greatly, it was as if a hit of adrenaline entered him, he clenched his teeth as static purple and black lightning engulfed around the figure of his consciousness, the strengthening was so intense that not only did it put his particles on hyper drive it even caused them to finish.
No longer were they type 6 Beginner particles but now type 8. It had been enough to power up his dark space and particles to convert all his c particles into type 8 beginner c.particles to a full 100%, and even his type 8 beginner particle progress had neared 96% completion.
Avrin knew his body was very different when compared to his people, he was innately stronger but this also meant that his particles contained a need for more energy. He would even go as far as to say one of his type 1 particles would be equivalent to a 1000 type 1 particles of Asura or the other pure blooded spectrals.
The strengthening had been vastly different to when Astaroth had powered him up, Avrin who was trying to keep his body calm after skipping nearly 2 levels felt that his strength had improved greatly. If he was to combat against Driada’s continental spear he was certain that he could stop it with a shadow wall with only a few scratches.
In the physical world Avrin’s body was surging with dark matter that seemed to become darker and more focused causing it to give a more condensed pure look. The Kirin was currently hiding behind a rock as it looked in fear. Avrin’s aura was much more monstrous than before as if he had undergone a huge change. “Master is really strong!!...” It thought to itself.
Within Avrin’s core dimension he was cross legged, he tried to feel for his inner workings but they were seemingly in overdrive as they began to baptize themselves in the dark matter sludge that became a bit thinner and more liquid like. “-At this rate I will reach the peak of the beginner stage within a month and break through it within 6 months if I put all my focus into it!-”
Avrin was truly proud of his progress, he could not help but remember the time where he came to seleria and almost got killed by Syrana with only her half sigil weapon, and now he felt that even if there were a 1000 of her, he could still win.
Avrin opened his eyes and gave a heavy sigh of relief, at that moment the grass that was turning black to red suddenly had a new color added, this color was a deeper darker black than the usual black that seemed to be purplish, Avrin carefully glanced at the white brick wall that vanished before reforming off in the distance another step closer to his dark matter core, this was the effect of absorbing skymetal.
With the grass going from a purplish black to a crimson blood red to a deep dark endless jet black, Avrin had assumed these were representations of his power, his dark matter heart, Astaroth, and the Vajra.
Avrin soon willed his consciousness back to his mind as his physical body opened its eyes, his monstrous aura died down before he calmly raised his hands in front of him. He willed an object to appear, and a slight glint in his left eye as if his soul and core had received the signal a double sided Vajra appeared obediently hovering in the air.
The aura it emitted was unfathomably mysterious, it would be alien in feeling to no matter who gazed at it. Avrin had read up on some historical texts as well as mythos and even religion, the meeting with god made him think about it all, but the Vajra had seemingly formed and he felt its ability was to devour.
“In Hinduism, Indra is the deva of rain and storms, he wields a Vajra or thunderbolt, but you also have a never ending hunger, a weapon symbolized and suited for a god, your name will be one to do with Greek mythology, you will be named Limos!!”((Authors Note: Limos is the Greek goddess of Hunger/Starvation))
The Kirin who had been watching this entire time was watching with awe, it watched as the mysterious Vajra appeared in Avrin’s hands causing its fur to stand on end like a frightened cat, it then felt that the Vajra posed no threat and Avrin even named it, but that was the final straw, the Kirin dashed out in complaint and began to nag.
“Master!! That’s not fair, no fair!! That stupid thing has a name but I don’t have a name! I want a name master I want one!” Avrin snapped to attention and gazed at the pitiful Kirin in front of him. “True, you need a name to, Kirins are ancient east Asian creatures of mythology, and you remind me of a thunderbolt, though I think Indra is too strong of a name for you, I will just call you Shandian because you remind me of lightning.”
Avrin looked at the Kirin that gazed back silently at him for a moment. “Shandian? I’m Shandian? YES!! I'M SHANDIAN!!” The creature began to hop around crazily as it began to call its newly given name again and again. Avrin gazed at the sight he felt that it was a child so it possibly couldn’t help it, in any case he simply smiled then gazed back at Limos.
“What can you do Limos?” Avrin gazed carefully at it, it was floating silently, of course he felt it was a strange weapon and he truly wasn’t sure in how to use it. Avrin then grabbed it from the air and held it near his face to gaze within the crystal inside.
The moment he did this, Septim just so happened to activate the brand to see what Avrin was up to, as he did, he gazed over towards Limos as he was able to see what Avrin could physically, but at this moment Limos seemed to stir as the brand activated, a closed eye formed within the transparent crystal being held by black veins, it opened and seemed to gaze at the brand, as if it could see Septim that saw it.
Septim who was glancing down casually from a pool as reflective as a mirror saw this, he suddenly felt his soul shudder and quiver. Limos began to emit a heavy hungry aura as if it were enticed by Septim’s mana, suddenly a pulse of energy erupted from Limos before it shot towards Avrin’s brand.
It caused Avrin who had seen the eye gaze out to suddenly jump in shock, but within the heavenly palace of the gods of seleria the area Septim was in began to twist and distort, Septim watched with widened eyes as a an eye formed within the air, the eye was more crystalline with a pitch black celestial looking pupil, the eye began to distort before closed black lips formed from midair curving into a wide smile, the lips then opened to reveal a deep endless darkness with no teeth, Septim was truly afraid but also astonished.
If Avrin knew more about the levels of gods he would understand just how powerful Limos was and the conditions needed to form skymetal, in truth having two chunks on seleria would cause not just a universal outcry but also an outcry spanning several universes. This was the power skymetal contained, Avrin’s body was only able to absorb a simple insignificant amount from Astaroth because he would have exploded if he absorbed any more.
For Limos he benefited more and absorbed more because he was stronger but even then it was still nothing in benefits. The moment Limos opened its mouth was for a fraction of a second, but it was also the moment a large amount of mana, spanning 1% in total of Septim’s mana, had surged towards it all happening very quickly. Septim howled in fear as he had felt an enormous weakness causing him to go off-guard, he couldn’t even defend himself nor could he against a skymetal weapon of this level.
As the stream of heavy mana energy that seemed incredibly pure to what Avrin had seen before neared Limos’ lips Avrin had already unsummoned Limos in fear and fright at how it suddenly reacted to the brand opening,
The image of Limos within the heavenly palace vanished as it was unable to absorb any of the mana from Septim, who then crumbled down onto his knees breathing heavily with a heavy cold sweat. His next reaction was to quickly wave his hand once as the mana surged back towards him, and with a second wave another interesting thing happened.
Avrin who had been stunned at Limos’ actions frowned a little as he sat quietly, but suddenly he felt his forehead itch before the brand that had formed on it disintegrated and was removed, he was stunned as to what had happened.
If he had known what Limos had tried to do he would have laughed at Septim’s misfortune. If he had known he had stopped Limos from absorbing the mana of Septim which he could have used to skyrocket himself to the level of a god, then he would want to cry at his own misfortune.

because seleria is a world  different from those out there no one on the planet other then the gods of seleria know the truth of what lies beyond their world, that is why the planet has its own ranking system, the reason why avrin also ordered erebus to implement his own ranking system for their race was also to get a bit of order and seperate the stronger from the bunch, there is one main ranking system that goes over everything and this will be revealed in time.

chapters.title: V4: Chapter 119 Heading To Ailera.
chapters.content:
!!!!! Pr Credits To Draconis Von BloodTrap &  Dragonofsomesort  Who Constantly Help With SR chapters, Please take the time to rep themfor their work :)
Hello, its good to be posting chapters again, i wanted to thank you all for being patient with me more or less i have recovered and have been in the mood to continue writing, thanks again for those who have supported me, this is last weeks regular release, and tomorrows regular release should be following as soon as it is done early or on time as soon as it is done i will post it. ---------------
Septim remained in a cold sweat with a look of shock on his face. In half the time it takes for a heart to beat, 1% of his total mana pool had nearly been absorbed. The sinister aura of Limos which had used his brand as a conduit to reach him had frightened Septim greatly.
“What a terrible feeling, but no doubt it is the same feeling formed by God Essence. How is this possible, God Essence on this planet?! And it was even forged? Or maybe it was imbued into that thing…? This is incredible.” A look of excitement flashed in Septim’s eyes as he stood up slowly and carefully, trying to calm himself down.
He had felt branding Avrin would lead to some form of entertainment, but never would he have expected that it was the cause of a dangerous situation. “In any case, it was a good idea not to kill him. Somehow, the impossible has become possible, and he possesses something even cosmic entities would tear up galaxies for. Having my planet within a spatial barrier was a good plan. I can only hope none of those high leveled gods pass by and sense it.”
As if Septim thought of something, a twisted look of fear and worry appeared on his face. The images of shadowy silhouettes larger than planets and as big as a normal person but each carrying a feeling and memory of terror that could frighten him greatly.
“What am I to be afraid of! If I can find the method that boy used to craft or imbue that power into a weapon, even I can hope to match those powerhouses. Me and the others are hiding in fear of being caught up in battle, but if I can obtain and use the power of God Essence, I can end this experiment early and forge my own empire!“
Septim’s body quivered in excitement, his mana surging around with anticipation, causing the white hall he was in to shake and crack slightly.
“No! I can’t rush things. If I aggravate him and brand him there is a possibility I may even lose my life. Making an enemy out of him at this moment is out of the question, I need to find a different solution to how I handle things. My biggest question is how God Essence was found here! I need to carefully examine this with the others. If I missed out on anything, maybe I can use it as a bargaining chip with that creature.”
“I will watch the world a bit more. I’ll let him have his fun with this experimental planet and tinker. If I can discover his purpose, maybe I can bring him to my side. Of course, branding him is also out of the question. I shouldn’t even think of doing so for those close to him either. In any case, I need to search for any remaining God Essence. To think this solar system had not just one, but two chunks...if any of those ancient ones discover this, this galaxy would be shredded apart in search of it.”
Shaking in fear, Septim was even more determined to keep things under wraps.  Avrin’s Limos had left him with many questions and even set him in a secret frenzy for a search. While things concluded, Avrin was still shaken up by what had happened, his body quivering slightly from Limos’s actions, but he was also extremely excited. He felt the brand was removed and with the actions of Limos no doubt it was thanks to that.
He silently snickered, seeing that if he was branded again he may have found a permanent way to remove it. Nebula Mist surged out of Avrin before forming into a circular disc. The disc itself was slowly forming until it formed completely.
Ever since the Kirin ate the shield he had purchased in the Twisting Lands, Avrin felt wronged. He was planning to give it to Eitri in hopes of him getting some inspiration, but the Kirin had eaten everything. Avrin was only impressed by the fact that it managed to devour the shield as if it were nothing.
He looked at the imperfect copy of the shield he had seen before, clenching his teeth slightly. “You devoured a potential treasure, I will make sure you train hard and become useful to me..” Avrin had a bitter feeling in his heart but pushed it away. He was certain the Kirin was rare, after all it had managed to react to his Divine Sense.
“Shandian, we are heading to the northern continent.” Avrin spoke in a soft tone. He knew that his Beginner Type 8 particles were nearing the peak of that level. The book within his consciousness stated that once he entered Type 9, which is the second stage, he would be in a weakened state while his particles underwent a sort of metamorphosis. He prefered to be where his kind was to undergo this process.
“Master, I can finally see the others!” Shandian was clearly excited and it hopped about like a human child that was going to the amusement park. Avrin, of course, was also in a good mood due to the brand finally being removed.
Though, if the god had wanted to brand him again, he felt it would be easy for them. But, judging by how they didn’t, it could only be that Limos had done something to keep them away. In any case, staying here was not a good idea.
Avrin’s Divine Sense engulfed both him and Shandian and then expanded out across Seleria before reaching the northern continent. Although the minute details were not so clear, Avrin could still clearly feel the humanoid figures no longer made from mana but of dark matter. The stronger the dark matter was, the easier it was for Avrin to pick up.
“-It seems Kael made it safely-” Avrin thought with slight relief when he detected Kael. He was currently at the peak stage of the Master level. He also detected Eitri and Erebus who were both also at the peak Master levels. Of course, as he felt around he noticed that the strongest signature within that area was Asura, who was at the early Grandmaster level, though he was not within the the area the other Spectrals were, but at least a couple days travel away.
“-Why is he around humans?-” Avrin curiously thought before he focused even more. He noticed that his Divine Sense that had expanded out also reached the city of Altea. He detected another dark matter signature, this one at the mid Grandmaster level.
“-That must be the one I was looking for, though at this moment it wouldn’t be good for me to go there until I make my breakthrough. I will let you enjoy yourself for the moment-” Avrin quietly thought before he gazed at the eager Shandian who had remained quiet.
He quickly used his Divine Step, turning him and Shandian into dark ash that soon warped and vanished. It only took a few seconds before they both appeared within the northern continent. Of course, Avrin had not decided to go to where his people currently were, but to where Asura was.
“Sir Asura, it has been a couple of years since the day you saved my humble town. Ever since that incident, the damn capital still won't send reinforcements!” A small, round individual with short hair in brown and blue noble attire frowned a little as he held a small cup of wine before laughing softly. One could see despite his appearance he gave off a friendly, fatherly feel.
The individual who he was speaking to was a tall, burly, robed individual with a human looking face and a large beard. His appearance was a bit ragged, but this was, of course, Asura, who had learned how to change his appearance from Kael when he arrived.
“Who needs reinforcements when you have me! These stinky trolls won’t even dare step foot near the area anymore, which means your hunters can go around as they please.“ Asura, who was holding a large drumstick, was eating with a look of satisfaction.
The round man, who was the mayor of the town, laughed and nodded. “Of course! You know, I can’t thank you enough for that. The capital sends many groups here to see if they can gain a foothold, but that damn king of ours never assists us. It’s a miracle we have survived this long. If it’s not trolls, it’s bandits or raiders.”
The man frowned as he remembered countless outposts and towns that had been made previously over the years which were wiped out because of these. In fact, his own town would have joined the numbers had it not been for Asura.
“How could I let a town that makes such good food perish! Hahahaha!” Asura began to laugh. In front of him was a table filled to the brim with an assortment of cuisine. Of course, not one was missing meat.
“Of course, Sir Asura, eat as much as you please. Thanks to you, there is plenty more supplies. Actually, I wanted to discuss something with you regarding a small expedition if-” Before the man could finish, a knock on the door sounded out.
“Hmm? Come in.” The mayor spoke out, to which a guard adorned in leather and chainmail armor appeared and then spoke with a nervous look. “Lord Mayor, the representative from the capital has arrived and is waiting for you in your office.”
The mayor frowned before sighing and rubbing his forehead then standing up. “Forgive me for parting early, Sir Asura. You know how these representatives are ever since we managed to establish ourselves.”
Asura simply laughed and spoke in reply. “It can’t be helped. They want to take as much advantage as they can from you now, hahahaha!” Asura laughed again. The mayor simply gave a bitter smile in agreement before bowing. “Stay for awhile longer, I will be back in a half hour.” With that said, the mayor left.
As he and the guard walked out, the guard couldn’t help but speak. “Lord Mayor, out of curiosity, just who is that Sir Asura? It has been two years yet we know little of him and he only comes here to eat.”
The Mayor gave another bitter smile before replying. “Your guess is as good as mine. Every attempt at friendship has been met with awkwardness. It’s as if he treats this place as a restaurant and nothing more. Regardless, he still saved us and is a hero. With him around, we can easily feed everyone here, so this is the least we can do!”
Asura was continuing to gouge himself but with his hearing he still picked up on the words said. It was then that Asura stopped eating for a moment and frowned. “That damn Kael.... Ever since he came, everyone is giving him all the attention and saying he is a young hero!”
Asura’s lips quivered a little and some crumbs stuck in his beard loosened and fell. Of course, Asura didn’t like attention to begin with, but inwardly it filled his ego. When Kael arrived nearly two years ago, he was greeted with caution at first, until he revealed Avrin had sent him, and with him doing his best to help out their race, everyone was looking up to him. Some people even went as far as to want to become his disciples and some families had tried to offer their daughters’ hand in marriage.
Asura had lost a lot of attention and Erebus didn’t bother him anymore since Kael was willing to help. Asura had nothing to do but come here where he was still appreciate and bask in the limelight.
“Hmph!... At least here I am appreciated, and the food is much better than that dark matter made crap!” Asura picked up another drumstick and was about to chomp down on it before a soft, familiar voice sounded out behind him.
The tale has been taken without authorization; if you see it on Amazon, report the incident.
“Dark matter crap? You endlessly eat, and are still a gluttonous pit...” Asura, hearing this, at first wondered who it was. He then felt that maybe a Spectral followed him. “Who the hell do-”
Turning around, Asura glanced over to see a black cloaked figure with a white, horse-looking creature with a small horn gazing dumbly and quietly at Asura. Asura, of course, looked at the individual first. His Divine Sense expanded over him the moment he had spoken, but Asura wasn’t able to tell what level this individual was. It was as if he wasn’t even there.
“Y...You....” Asura was not as dumb as before and had matured and gained quite a bit of intelligence. He broke out in a cold sweat, quickly got up and knelt on the ground. Although he couldn’t feel this individual’s aura and presence, it was a cold, dark, scary feeling.
“M...Master!” Asura quickly knew that only one Spectral would have this weird, alien-like feeling, and that was the one who converted him. Avrin, who was leaning near the window with his arms folded, grinned a little “Well, you’re not as dimwitted anymore, you quickly recognized me. It’s good you have gotten smarter.” Avrin spoke in a harsh compliment.
Avrin had Divine Stepped in a hidden area before the mayor had vanished and he secretly Divine Stepped again inside to see Asura. “Why are you here, Asura?” Avrin hadn’t overheard the conversation. Asura simply glanced at him and cleared his throat.
“Well..Master, I...” He then glanced over and saw Shandian had rushed over to the table and was starting to eat as much food as it could. “HEY, THAT’S MINE!!” Asura felt like tearing up. Avrin blinked, as he was now dealing with two constantly hungry buffoons. His Divine Sense engulfed them both before the three of them turned into dark ash and vanished from the room.
They reappeared several miles away, on top of a small, rocky hill. Asura, though, felt his heart jump. “-Master has gotten much stronger...I wish I could do that-” He quietly thought. Shandian, of course, had a bone from a piece of meat in its mouth as it glanced dumbly at Avrin and then Asura while it chewed on the bone.
“Explain, Asura...” Avrin’s intention was that his people were to seclude themselves and not have anything to do with the outside world until he arrived. Of course, Asura could see the cold, curious look Avrin had and began to explain things from the beginning.
Several minutes later he was concluding it all. “So, Master...I felt maybe we could use this town as a sort of cover and I was trying to make use of it!” Asura was nervous, not sure if Avrin would believe him or not.
Avrin showed an expressionless gaze. He knew Asura’s intention in staying after these two years was not really to use the village but to eat its food and bask in the limelight, though he hadn’t revealed anything and had stayed anonymous, which was a good sign that he had gotten more intelligent.
“Very well, I’ll forgive you for this. I am not a cruel person. As long as you keep your true identity hidden and not cause our people to become discovered, you can continue to visit.” Avrin didn’t want to become heartless. He knew a good subordinate would be one that was spoiled a bit. Asura, hearing Avrin’s acceptance, felt relief and quickly bowed. “Thank you, Master, thank you!” Glancing at Shandian, who had approached and started sniffing him, Asura felt a bit irksome. “Master, what the hell is this thing? Can I eat it?” Asura asked.
Shandian, who had heard this, frowned and growled like a dog before biting Asura’s leg. “Ah!!“ Asura jumped away as he felt the pain. He then glared at Shandian with a face of fury.
“You....little bastard...” Asura mumbled with his fists clenched. Dark matter surged around him, causing the ground to crack a little. Shandian, who wasn’t as strong as him, clearly felt fear and rushed over to hide behind Avrin. “Master! That bearded dumbo wants to eat me… Please smack him!” Shandian urged Avrin in a teary tone. Of course, Shandian had long since been able to communicate with the proper vocals, as its body had adapted somewhat.
“Asura, this is Shandian, a special creature I have invested in. It isn’t something to eat nor to hit. That is until it becomes stronger, you are not to lay a finger on it.” As Avrin spoke, Asura glared at shandian. Avrin turned to look at Shandian as well. “You are not to be a wimp. Once you become stronger, I think both of you sparring will be beneficial experience as long as neither of you kills the other.”
Shandian quivered a little as it gazed at Avrin with a look of astonishment, then Asura, who was now grinning and cracking his knuckles. It turned to look at Avrin with a pleading look, but he simply sighed and shook his head, definitely amazed at how much of a wimp this creature was. He felt it was still a child, so it couldn't be helped for the mean time.
“Master, you will be heading over to the mountain home now? I will bid you farewell and return to the town to cont-” Asura was interrupted by Avrin, who looked at him strangely. “To continue to eat? Is what you’re thinking. You better start training more, Asura. I could feel Kael’s strength and he is catching up to you. Fine, go back and do as you please.”
Asura quietly chuckled and scratched his dirty beard and bowed again before he turned tail and dashed away. Clearly he was uncomfortable around Avrin and enjoyed his own freedom. Of course, he was still hungry and wanted to eat. Avrin, for the moment, had no use for him and could always contact him with his Divine Sense.
“Master, that bearded bastard is nasty! Can’t you please punish him!” Shandian cried out, wanting Avrin’s favor. “Punish him? Grow stronger and punish him yourself. If you train properly it will be easy for you. Don’t seek others to protect you. I personally converted you, I have high expectations for you, but also at the same time your potential is no less than his. Probably even more so. Don’t let me down.”
Avrin’s words were, of course, meant to light a fire in Shandian to make it train hard and become useful. He couldn’t protect his people every day of the week, he wanted to explore around and needed strong individuals in his stead.
Shandian reacted. As he expected, its body tensed up and it gave a heavy look and nodded with pride. After this, Avrin used his Divine Step again and they both turned into dark ash before disappearing and then reappearing several hundred meters from the mountain entrance.
The reason Avrin didn’t go inside was because he wanted to see what Eitri had done to make it hospitable as well as the other things. From this moment on, whether his people knew if he was here or not was second place. This was his makeshift kingdom, what would he have to worry about now.
Avrin glanced over to see several large mountains and hills that covered around. A man made path that led out was present, but it was well hidden. Avrin began to think as he glanced down to see the entrance with six guards. Of course, they were Spectral and at the peak Expert level. Each one was stronger than the usual Expert and could most likely match a mid level Master. This was the latent power within a Spectral.
Avrin, though, was curious and wanted to test just how strong his people were and how they would react to an attack. The reason for this was the guards seemed to be a bit lazy and sit around and chat casually.
“Shandian, wait here and watch how I test your brethrens’ strength.” As Avrin spoke, Nebula Mist engulfed him. His outfit changed and he was now covered in a dirty grey robe with a large hood that covered his face. Shandian watched curiously, as it was excited to see what Avrin would do.
Many years ago, before Avrin had died, he once faked his identity and neared a space raider hideout. Of course, the raiders were laidback and didn’t think much of him and told him to buzz off. Avrin faked being a cripple and when the raiders neared, he pulled out two silenced laser pistols and dealt with them.
His method was similar here, as he faked a limp and looked like a ragged, homeless individual. He had already willed a very thin coat of dark matter around him to cling onto mana particles and hold them but not devour them.
This was a method he found quite easy to do. It allowed a coat of mana to go around him and make others think he was made from mana. With Avrin’s increase in strength, he would be able to discover new methods and abilities he had previously not thought about until he needed them.
“Huh?” Just then, one of the guards, who was adorned in red, plate-like armor from head to toe glanced over and pointed. Though a few of them had Divine Sense, it was not extended at the moment, as they were in a lazy mood “Who the hell is that?” The guard uttered before they all turned to look.
Each one glanced at the ragged, hidden Avrin with a strange expression before one’s Divine Sense went out and engulfed him. “Shit, it’s not one of ours. What do we do? This is the first time this has happened! Is it a homeless person? How the hell did he get here?”
The six mumbled to each other, wondering what to do. One of them laughed and spoke. “Lord Erebus stated that no one is to know of us, let’s just kill him. Besides, the mana he has can be converted into a Dark Core. Just consider it a snack.”
Hearing this, Avrin’s expression darkened. Unless one was an enemy he was sure of, he wouldn’t convert them to a Dark Core, and even then unless it was an enemy he truly hated he wouldn’t do it while they were alive.
One of the guards casually walked over to Avrin and laughed. “Hey you...damn its a shit day to be you. I’m gonna have to kill ya, blame your own luck.” The guard raised the large halberd made from dark matter, and then slashed it down towards him with no hesitation.
Avrin stopped and glanced with his face hidden. The moment the halberd smashed down onto his shoulder, it broke into fragments as if it were glass smashing against a boulder. The stunned look of the guard was like a deer in headlights.
The other guards were stunned as well, but in a heartbeat, Avrin extended his left hand and grabbed him by the neck before raising him up from the ground. “You have a lot to learn. You’re still so weak....”
The guard was gasping and trying to move Avrin’s hands but they wouldn’t budge. It was then that four of his comrades rushed over to try and help him while another rushed inside to get other Spectrals.
Avrin threw the guard he held like a ragdoll towards the oncoming guards. One was hit and sent flying while the other three charged towards him each with their own weapon of choice. “Die!” They roared out with intent to kill.
“Weak or not, not hesitating to kill a strange intruder is a gamble. though one who attacks is a different story. Let me see how strong you have all become!”
---------Avrin's Inner Workings Status

Just a side note, i was looking at the top 5 yesterday and was a bit saddened because they haven't updated in awhile and are most likely busy with RL matters. SR is progressing at the pace i want it to and from what i can see is improving, just goes to show that drafting out in word pad or any simple txt document, really affects the process, you get your thoughts down and when you start writing the next you can review it, and its as if you have 2 minds comparing ideas, my yesterdays self and my today's self, if that makes any sense.
i hope you all enjoy the chapter, if you have any questions feel free to msg them below, i am still going over 119's questions. also! some news. i am having 3 pieces of art done, 2 pieces of skymetal's raw chunk form, of Astaroth and Limos, also a picture of Shandian.
Also im thinking the third one is a picture of Astaroths Scythe form, in any case this is all thanks to those who continue to help support SR the money given is not pocketed by me, it all goes back into the story to help improve the quality, this is what my readers deserve, it also means you all play a part in helping SR improve whether it be in supporting from donations, or commenting  on potholes/errors/simple advice, i appreciate all the people who are legitimately trying to help

------------
One of the guards jumped several meters into the air and swung his void greatsword at Avrin. The power was enough to cause the air to split slightly. Avrin simply grinned before raising his left hand and flicking the head of the blade that looked to be in slow motion to him. A sound resembling a mini sonic boom sounded out as the blade head shattered and the guard tumbled down to the side several meters away, stunned.
Two of his comrades decided to flank Avrin from both sides. One held a large spear while another held two long swords. They charged towards Avrin. One could see they had trained with each other, as they seemed to work well with each other.
“Good, looks like you’re all not so lazy!” As they neared Avrin the spear thrusted towards his right side while the two long swords stabbed towards his left side. Avrin bent his back down with ease and the blades stabbed the air.
He reached up and grabbed the spear head as well as one of the long swords before pulling forward. The two guards who had looks of anticipation to defeat an enemy were now shocked as their balance was easily broken and they tumbled forward.
Avrin was not slow. He kicked his right foot forward, letting him shoot back a little and then he regained his balance all in a split second while the guards were still tumbling forward. He reached over with both his hands and grabbed them both by the shoulder plates before raising them both up as if they were ragdolls and then throwing them off to the side.
The fourth guard was left there stunned. He was behind Avrin, about to attack, but he was watching as his comrades were so easily dealt with. Avrin turned to glance at him with an indifferent expression. “Hmm? Don’t tell me you’re not going to attack. If you won’t, I will...”
Avrin made his way towards the guard who was now quivering with fear. The guard quickly threw his weapon down and raised his hands. “I...I admit defeat!” Avrin was astounded. This was so sudden he wanted to laugh. “It’s not that simple. Your friends took my blows, you need to as well.“
Avrin approached him and simply raised his right hand. Avrin then flicked, but this flick was weaker than the one he used to break the void weapon. The guard was sent flying several meters away, landed, and then tumbled another meter.
Avrin was sure to not injure them harshly, as they were all just stunned and shocked. Avrin looked around and spoke. “You’re all too weak...you need to train harder.” One of the guards who was knocked away by Avrin had a red face of anger as he roared out. “Who the hell do you think you are to tell us to train harder!”
Avrin was about to speak, before his eyes widened slightly and he stepped to the side. A red blur smashed down in the spot he was just standing in. The ground split open in a thirty meter line with a width of half a meter. The red blur was, in fact, a greatsword, which, after examining, Avrin was sure was crafted by the Legendary ore he had given to Eitri.
After looking at the owner, Avrin couldn’t help but smirk inwardly. It was someone he was familiar with. “Ah..you’re quite good, Mister. Though, you hurt my people. I won’t let you go so easily unless you surrender. I don’t like killing those who aren’t evil.“
This was Kael, who had an air of maturity around him. He had grown quite a bit, but still wore the black attire he had formed before leaving Avrin. Avrin could tell he had even managed to fool Kael, who had gotten stronger.
“Is that so?... What do you know about killing, boy? You still look as if your nappies are being changed.” Avrin’s intention was to provoke Kael a bit to see how strong he had gotten.
Kael’s expression flickered before he simply laughed and then dashed towards Avrin, slashing in a frenzy. Avrin could tell there was some technique, but it was still enough at his current level to easily dodge. Though with each slash and thrust, the air split and stretched, slash marks appeared on the ground and the boulders nearby were crushed to dust.
“How is Lord Kael’s attack being so easily dodged!?” One of the stunned guards spoke out with shock and another replied. “Nonsense. This stranger is not simple, but he can’t attack Lord Kael at all!”
For every second they talked, more and more Spectrals who wanted to assist and help would pour out and guard the entrance. There was now over thirty who were in red plate armor, which was obviously made by ore Avrin had given to Eitri.
Soon, cheers for Kael could be heard. “Lord Kael, you got this!!” One spoke out, while another continued further. “Show this intruder not to mess with the Spectral race!” 
Avrin was a little stunned. Kael had gotten stronger. He could see each attack was aimed towards vital parts. “-This boy has gotten more powerful, though it’s not enough!-” Avrin thought.
Avrin dashed away several meters before Kael glanced at Avrin and smiled. “You’re quite strong, Mister… Though I’m not holding back anymore.” A surge of dark matter occurred around Avrin and Kael’s expression changed to one of an animal with battle lust. He dashed towards Avrin, his speed and strength much higher than before.
With one hand holding the greatsword, another formed a sphere of dark matter with a purple flame within. Avrin observed this carefully. The greatsword he side stepped and dodged, but the purple flame was shot towards him.
Avrin was intending to dodge it, but the sphere exploded, the flame within turning into embers that shot like a rain of sparks. They pierced into the ground and even pierced into Avrin’s attire. Of course, with Avrin’s current durability, this attack barely scratched his skin.
As Kael watched with a look of caution, he gazed at Avrin, who didn’t budge. Kael’s eyes narrowed. “Who...are you...” He carefully said. Avrin raised his head and then tilted it, his face still very well hidden. “Is this all you have?” Hearing this, a look of anger appeared on Kael’s face.
This anger caused dark matter and a black aura to surge around him. Draconic scales began to form over his skin. The onlookers were stunned. “This is Lord Kael’s draconic form. It is my first time seeing this...but the rumors are true...the aura he releases is terrifying...” Another also spoke out with fascination.
“This stranger is done for. I once heard from a senior that Lord Kael killed a peak Grandmaster beast with this form as if it were cattle for the slaughter.”Avrin knew Kael could do better. He knew his strategies were quite careful. The draconic form Kael had was different to what he had seen before, though.
His skin was now covered in black scales and his appearance was more draconic, with two large horns curved back from the top of his head. This form was more controlled and not complete, but Kael stabbed the great sword into the ground and cracks appeared from where it had been placed.
Kael then raised his hands and Nebula Mist surged around them before Void Sphere after Void Sphere was formed. They shot towards Avrin like a machine gun shooting bullets. Avrin, though, simply raised his right hand and whenever a Void Sphere neared him he would smack it away. But the amazing thing was that the Void Sphere that shattered after being smashed away would reform around Avrin.
Avrin humored Kael, and before long, Void Spheres had gathered around Avrin and surrounded him. There were nearly a few hundred. “Surrounding me? Though I don’t think it will be enough.”
Kael snickered before the dark matter that formed the Void Spheres all squashed together above Avrin into one big Void Sphere. It happened in a second, and above Avrin was an enormous Void Sphere ten meters in diameter that shot towards him like a meteor.
Avrin was about to jump out of the way, but Kael, who had willed the sphere, already acted. He had formed a ring of Nebula Mist that closed off Avrin’s retreat. The Void Sphere contained something that felt familiar to Avrin. “-Phantom Pulse?... This little brat actually managed to learn about gravity?-” Avrin was stunned. The attack itself had several steps.
Kael would distract the opponent and make them think the attack was a simple barrage, they would then form above the opponent and once it caught their attention it would shoot down like a meteor while emitting a miniature version of Phantom Pulse to keep them in place. Kael also acted and cut off their escape with a ring of dense Nebula Mist.
“Very good...but.” Avrin spoke and Kael glanced over. This attack contained his current understanding of dark matter. In his draconic form, his control over dark matter increased, along with his base strength, but this form was the most he could currently control without going berserk.
The Nebula Mist surged towards Avrin, engulfing him. The large Void Sphere emitting a Phantom Pulse also crashed towards him. “Lord Kael has done it!” The onlookers felt this stranger who attacked was surely done for. “This is the price for attacking us! This stranger is definitely a Grandmaster, but so what! Under Lord Kael’s attacks and tactics, it’s nothing!”
“Too arrogant.” A voice sounded out from within the Nebula Mist and the Void Sphere that was crushing down on Avrin and had formed a mini crater under him suddenly distorted and exploded. Soon after, the entire area engulfing Kael, as well as the others, surged and distorted a little.
“This is the control over gravity that you need to work towards.” Avrin spoke before he emitted Phantom Pulse and effortlessly destroyed the Void Sphere and Nebula Mist. The onlookers were all flat down on their faces or backs, being crushed into the ground.
Kael was on his knees. Even his sweat didn’t have time to run down his face, and it was also smashed down into the earth. Cracks began to form in the area, and the coating of mana around Avrin had vanished.
Those who tried to use Divine Sense to feel around him would feel as if a hole in reality in the shape of a human was present. They would not know that Divine Sense would not pick up a Spectral stronger than themselves. Avrin’s particles were able to avoid detection from their weaker Divine Sense.
Kael was stunned, but he knew there would only be one person who had a true Phantom Pulse, let alone one as strong as this. “M..Master Avrin!!” Avrin, hearing that his identity was revealed by Kael, simply smiled and the Phantom Pulse he emitted vanished. 
If you encounter this story on Amazon, note that it's taken without permission from the author. Report it.
He couldn’t blame Kael for this. After all, Avrin had increased in strength by leaps and bounds. His training outpaced theirs by many times. Considering he was also the progenitor, it was common place.
When the Phantom Pulse vanished, the stunned guards slowly and weakly got up. The entire area was filled with cracks and slash marks from battle. Avrin glanced over at Kael and Nebula Mist surged around him before it reverted his dirty outfit back to his previous attire. Avrin raised his head to reveal the humanoid appearance that he used to travel with Kael.
“Master, it is you!!” Kael looked up at Avrin. He even felt somewhat teary eyed, as Avrin had given him so much and even sent him here where people like him were situated. Here, he felt wanted, and those who needed his help asked. It was truly like a family.
“Kael, you have improved, but there is still so much more you need to learn.” The onlookers were stunned at this sight. “Master?.. Did Lord Kael call him master?” A confused guard spoke out. A smarter one put two and two together.
“W..wait… If he is Lord Kael’s master...then....!! That means he is our Savior Lord Avrin!!! He is the savior who converted Lord Erebus!! He is our ruler!!” The guards were astounded. They all clearly felt and saw how easily they were overwhelmed and how even Kael in his draconic form was easily defeated. No one but Avrin could accomplish this so easily.
As if wanting to curry favor with Avrin, they all rushed over in droves and knelt on the ground in front of him. “Uh?...” Avrin glanced over at the dozens of kneeling figures. It was a little awkward for him, and a new feeling. “Stand up....” He spoke, and as if they were puppets, they all quickly stood up.
Kael made his way over through the crowed and looked at Avrin with shining eyes. Despite being one who had killed and matured, he still felt like a child in front of Avrin. “Welcome back, Master. You have gotten stronger!“
From there, those who had felt the Phantom Pulse and the sound of battle earlier had started to come out from the entrance. A lot were adults with no combat experience and worried children being led by their mothers.
“What should we call our savior?” One guard spoke, while another replied. “He is our ruler. It is fair we call him our monarch. He isn’t married, so can’t be called king.” They all started to debate a little before they agreed to call Avrin the monarch. “Lord Monarch, welcome back!!” One spoke before they all replied in unison, welcoming Avrin.
Many of the civilians who were watching with caution overheard everything and even asked some of the guards at the back what was going on. Eventually, nearly the entire population of Spectrals had come out to see Avrin, who was surrounded and being bombarded by questions.
Questions like “Lord Monarch, where have you been?” and “Lord Monarch, can you teach me that ability?” could be heard. Some even asked if he brought anything for them and even if he had defeated any dragons or Sigil wielders. Avrin was quiet and overwhelmed by it all. Kael simply laughed as he watched and let it all happen.
Avrin was looking around with a bit of a stunned look. The entire crowd was made of Spectrals, each one formed from dark matter. He gazed at the old men who decided to keep their looks, he gazed at the adults who had children on their shoulders, the children were waving at Avrin and trying to ask him questions. He then looked at the women who gave him looks of worship, as if he was their idol, as well as some who held newborn children.
For someone like him, who had emotions that had been tampered with, it left him stunned, but at that moment his dark matter heart began to surge slightly. Within his inner space, inside his dark matter core, a strand of jet black dark matter changed and shifted.
Its color was no longer pitch black and purple, but was now a pure, natural green that floated around before forming into a pebble sized sphere that hovered by the top of the dark matter star before being absorbed within and was now only a faint green light.
Meanwhile, in a white space, there was a figure sitting on a white chair. This figure had skin that seemed to be transparent and reflect nebulas and galaxies, as if the entirety of existence was within his body. The figure had no discerning features, but suddenly the figures eyes opened, revealing inside was a mirror image of Avrin’s inner workings and the green light that formed.
This was none other than God, who was observing Avrin. His voice sounded out, echoing across this plain of existence that, despite him being the only one here, continued on forever. “Emotions are very powerful, for the fragment used to give you life by your father, you may one day consider yourself blessed or cursed. That heart of yours has a will of its own. It uses the emotions as fuel for evolution, emotion created by the people around you, the emotion of hope.
Hope is a strong emotion, enough to be used by a fragment like you to empower yourself in the future. Green matter...I look forward to seeing how the third Spectral progenitor uses it. Your predecessors were disgustingly powerful in the eyes of others, but it’s much too early for you to learn about everything....too early...“ God’s eyes shut, and it was as if the gates of existence were also being closed.
On Seleria, within the northern continent of Ailera, Avrin was still surrounded by his people asking question after question. He wasn’t sure how to answer, so he remained quiet, but suddenly a loud, hoarse voice sounded out.
“Where is he!!! That bastard brat better have gotten me some high quality ore!” A short, stubby, pale looking individual wearing a soot covered blacksmith apron with metal gauntlets on his hand walked out from the mountain entrance. This individual's face was also covered by soot and his beard seemed to be a little charred. It was Eitri.
Everyone glanced over in surprise at how Eitri spoke about Avrin. Eitri walked over to the crowd and roared out. “Out of my way!!” From fear of Lord Eitri they all made a path and dared not speak another word. Soon, Eitri approached and stood a few feet in front of Avrin and looked up.
Though he couldn’t recognize his appearance, he knew that it was a disguise. “Hmmm...” Eitri remained quiet. He also couldn’t help but inwardly feel thankful to Avrin for all that he has given him. Eitri cleared his throat and spoke. He wanted to thank Avrin, but he had his pride. He simply extended his hand out and spoke. “What did you bring me?” He spoke like a child expecting a gift.
The onlookers were also curious as to what Avrin may have brought. Avrin looked at Eitri, his eyebrows twitching a little. “-This little....heh..-” Avrin smirked a little before reaching over to his enchanted sack and placing it on Eitri’s hand.
Avrin then spoke out. “I brought quite a few Dark Matter Cores of good quality, and Lord Eitri has volunteered to hand them out. I hope you all enjoy.” After Avrin spoke they all looked at Eitri, who was shocked. “Avrin, yo-” Before he could continue, he was swarmed by people who were asking him for Dark Matter Cores.
Avrin had a way out now, but people still followed him. Avrin called out with a soft voice. “Shandian, come out now.” Those that heard Avrin looked around confused, wondering who he was talking to, but in the distance a four legged creature came rushing down with its tongue hanging out before looking around nervously. People stepped aside, confused at the creature.
Shandian walked right up and stood at Avrin’s side. One could see it was nervous and afraid of all the Spectrals present who were staring at it with fascination. “Master, what is that?..” Kael, who was excited about Avrin’s return, pointed as he walked beside him. “Shandian? Just something I picked up on my travels.”
Shandian was deathly quiet and looked as if it wanted to cry, but was too nervous to do so. Many whispers from the people following Avrin towards the entrance that led inside the mountain were curious as to what Shandian was. “Is this the Lord Monarch’s pet?” One man spoke while a female in her mid twenties replied. “I’m sure it is. What else could it be?”
Shandian frowned a little as it gave Avrin a pitiful look, but it suddenly felt the white fur on its back being tugged on softly. It quickly turned to see a six year old looking girl looking at it warmly. The girl had the appearance of a Spectral, with her pupils a soft purple. She smiled at Shandian. “Horsey?” By now, the information sphere Avrin had given them had gone around to them all. Much had been hidden but basic knowledge of the animals he had seen though.
Shandian knew what a horse was too, and its mouth trembled a little. “I’m a Kirin!” It replied as it also knew thanks to Avrin what a Kirin was. The girl smiled and gently tugged on Shandian’s fur again. “No, a horsey!“ The girl replied again, clearly showing she was still quite young.
From there, many children surrounded Shandian and began to tug and lead it away from Avrin. Some even tried to ride on its back. Shandian gazed at Avrin, who glanced back and simply gave a soft chuckle.
Leaving Shandian with the children and adults who supervised, Avrin was still followed by around twenty to thirty individuals who weren’t interested in the Dark Cores nor Shandian and wanted to know more about him and want to learn from him.
Avrin stopped suddenly and the rest, including Kael, stopped as well. In front of him, fifteen meters away, at the entrance, was a man in black robes with a large, red, metal staff engraved with interesting designs. The staff head was surrounded by rotating Void Spheres. There were four people to his side, each one at the peak Expert level.
Suddenly, the all five knelt down and said “We greet the Lord Monarch.” They had overheard what name everyone had given him and decided it was for the best. The four individuals were the top experts under the pure Spectrals Avrin had personally converted. The one in the center with the staff was, of course, Erebus, who could be considered as the most loyal to Avrin.
“Lord Monarch, welcome back!” Erebus spoke with a tone of excitement. He knew that Avrin coming back meant that much would happen. “Oh, Erebus? Hmm, lets all go inside.” Avrin said.
The interior of the mountain had been nearly hollowed out enough to fit a small city, though with Eitri present, it was quite easy to create pillars of powerful enough quality to keep everything looking beautifully decorated and stable. The mountain city design was influenced by dwarven and human design gained from information held by Eitri and Avrin.
The houses were more so made together in the form of apartments, though the quality did not diminish at all, as they were beautifully crafted by individuals trained by Eitri, himself included.
The ground was paved and not rocky at all. Near the entrance, a large, square area spanning fifty meters in length was paved with metal tiles.
Avrin could see many weapon racks and a large building. A big sign was hanging near the entrance that read “”Training Field, Military Office.”” Avrin continued to glance around and everyone could see he was examining the area. No one dared to interrupt him.
“”Medical office, Blacksmith, Housing Section and of course the main building in the center that seemed out of place within this world that was carved into the inner mountain face. “”Headquarters”” Avrin then stopped at the center of the small city, which was a small, ten meter in diameter green area with a couple of trees, flowers and grass growing.
“Well, it’s liveable, and that’s what matters. I can’t help but feel that you are holding back on a lot of things, Erebus?” Avrin finally spoke. By now, the four individuals had shooed away the curious people following Avrin that now watched from a distance.
“Lord Monarch, I did not want to set anything in stone that would be hard to change. Many things here are temporary, as I have waited for you to come back so everything can be discussed.”
Erebus’s words were pleasing to Avrin, as it was nice for him to speak to someone who planned well. “Very good. Before all that, delineate what has happened since we parted way several years ago.”
