chapters.title: V4: Chapter 121 Bypassing Obstacles.
chapters.content:
!!!!! Pr Credits To Draconis Von BloodTrap &  Dragonofsomesort  Who Constantly Help With SR chapters, Please take the time to rep them for their work :)
i decided to do this weeks regular release early since i will be busy this Wednesday, its not one of my best chapters but i'm sure you guys will understand the pacing once you read it till the end. i noticed that what i consider myself bad at, is writing from the perspective of non spectral characters, that being said its something i will have to improve. i noticed a few individuals pming me regarding loopholes and continuity issues in my past chapters, i'm thankful to you all for managing to pick these out, it lets me fix and reword these before it becomes a large issue ----------
Currently seated at a table with Avrin were Erebus and Kael. Erebus had even gone as far as to personally brew tea, which he had come to love, his personal favourite was ginger with some lemon, he felt it was refreshing.
Avrin was seated with his right hand against his cheek as he listened to Erebus explain everything in a not too long or short summary. Having listened for a half hour, it was nearing the end of things until today.
“Lord Monarch, as I have explained up until now, I have done my best to keep our race hidden. Of course, I’m sure you know how hard Asura is to handle at times, but he hasn’t given away any secrets, which is good.” Erebus finished his story. Kael was silently listening while drinking the brewed tea with both his hands over the simple cup.
“Well then.” Avrin started before quietly thinking, then taking a deep breath. He didn’t want to be a general in this life as well, he wanted to be free to do as he pleased. Erebus, in his eyes, was doing a fine job but he wasn’t strong enough to properly lead in this world, which meant Avrin still needed to hold the reigns. Regardless of the outcome, the Spectrals would most likely always treat him as the rightful ruler.
“I realise our understanding of this universe is limited. As I grow stronger, I know that there are beings out there that greatly tower over us. That being said, regarding the rankings I had told you about before, it was a good move on your behalf to not put them into place as levels of ability. In this case the proper way to do things is to use these as titles of ranking in status instead of power. I refuse to believe such a vast universe lacks a ranking of its own.” Avrin explained the way he wanted things for several minutes.
Of course, he wanted order to be a focus early on instead of later when things may get out of hand. From there, he decided that Erebus would be ranked as a King, second under Avrin. This was because Avrin trusted his leadership, as he seemed to be the most thoughtful of the bunch. Asura and Kael would be ranked as Grand Princes.
Despite them being as strong as Erebus, this was just to keep them in line. Eitri, of course, was ranked as a Craft King. Avrin realised he would have two at the top in both categories hoping this would allow people to see what to work towards. It was not strength alone, but wisdom.
Shandian would be ranked as an Earl. Avrin decided this because Shandian still had a bit of progress to make. With these individuals ranked in title, it meant there was a chain of command. Though he had little time right now to properly organize this all, he trusted Erebus to organize it for him. After all, it would be incredibly dumb if Avrin did not make good use of his loyalty.
“Erebus, from here onwards, make sure titles are given deservingly. This is the first generation and I expect many to work hard for the later generations to look up to. My main goal at this moment for our people is for them to strengthen themselves. I can’t always be around to protect you all, and allowing everyone to come here was a gamble that paid off.” After Avrin finished, Erebus was eager to speak.
“Lord Monarch, does this mean your title as Emperor will change to your current status?” Erebus’s question was quite straightforward, but it was simple. “Both will be fine. It does not matter to me at this stage. Things will slowly fit into place.” Avrin replied before standing up. His body felt strange, as if his particles were shifting and changing, but he knew what this was.
“-I will be entering the second phase of the Beginner stage soon. I will be incredibly weakened, so it’s best if I focus on overcoming it as soon as possible-” Avrin quietly thought before Kael spoke out.
“Master, is everything alright? You look tired?” Hearing Kael’s words, Avrin glanced back and spoke. “I’m going to be entering into seclusion nearby. Until I’m ready, I don’t want anyone to bother me. You both know what to do. Kael, from here on out, Erebus is your superior. I will return when I complete a certain something.”
Avrin extended his Divine Sense and vanished in a mist of purple ash before reforming four miles away inside a hidden cave entrance that was narrow but lead down inside the earth. Avrin emitted Nebula Mist that caused the entrance to rumble slightly before debris fell and blocked it. From there, he made his way down the cave with a small frown of disatisfaction.
The reason for this is because Avrin had arrived but had to leave so soon he hadn’t had time to properly look at everything or offer some advice. This was because he felt his body was at its peak. The closer he neared the peak of a particle type it would go into overdrive, as if his C.Particles were eager to reach the summit.
Having reached the bottom of the cave, he felt unsteady and somewhat dizzy, but he managed to take a meditative position before feeling for his inner workings. As soon as he arrived, his particles were seemingly unsteady and excited, as if they were about to shoot out in all directions.
“-Perfect, they all have enough energy to begin the metamorphosis. All that’s needed is a little push-” Avrin willed all his particles, from C.Particles to the normal Type 8 particles, which had reached 100% completion, to condense. From there, it was simply a matter of willing the cores of the particles to condense.
The shell of the particles slowly turned a transparent purple before the cores were shown. The cores shrunk immensely, and began to beat unsteadily like a heart, but the moment they all beat at the same time the link between them all had snapped.
This feeling was not at all good for Avrin to feel. It made him nauseous, as if his body was about to crumble into ash like when he uses Divine Step, but with no destination, which made it worrying.
Avrin soon felt his own consciousness slip slightly. With his last ounce of strength, he willed Nebula Mist around his physical body and formed a simple barrier that would be enough to last for as long as there was mana around and as long as no one broke it. From there, he glanced at all the particles of his body. The sight was quite unique, if one looked into the night sky and saw all the stars, then all one would need to do is imagine them shrinking and growing, as if beating like a heart, that would be the sight Avrin saw.
“-Nothing to do but wait now. They have been without me for that long, a few weeks or months won’t hurt-” Avrin wasn’t sure how long this process would take, but he knew in this meditative position, time would pass as if he were sleeping. From there, he began to look over the book God had given him.
Several days had passed without Avrin budging an inch, though while he underwent the second stage to advance his particles from the limits of Type 9 to the end of Type 10 and the end of the Beginner stage, the world of Seleria hadn’t remained silent.
Within the great, boundless ocean of Seleria, a lone individual was casually walking over the ocean floor, his body covered by a transparent blue sphere of mana that kept the water at bay. The creatures of the ocean dared not approach this being. They were afraid of the pressure he faintly emitted. The figure, wearing a beautifully made robe made from a material similar to silk, lined with gold and gems, his face was discernable. This was Azrael.
“It should be time.” Azrael quietly spoke before lifting his right arm and raising the robes sleeve. The brand that Zephiron had given him began to light up with a red and black color before a voice sounded out.
“Azrael.... Interesting indeed. You being free was quite a topic between us, though unfortunately none of us had been observing your prison at that time. Interestingly enough, we were able to observe the battle between that strange individual and your daughter. A shame me and that bastard Malaku had tried to brand him, but it seems Septim beat us to it.” The youthful, snake-like voice sounded out with a tone similar to that of a troublemaker.
“My Lord, indeed. Avrin had been branded by Septim, I assume it is because he battled Leo Zircus, but regardless, I understand our time is limited. I am currently a mile away from the sea tribe’s underwater city. I assumed it was better to be here just incase Orochi’s prison was near.”
Azrael spoke with a deep tone of respect. This was his creator and could be considered his father. “--Oh? Very good. Who needs knowledge from those winged cretins and these sea fish when you have me! A mile east of their city you will find a large, rocky arch. Past that first arch you will find a smaller one on the surface of the seafloor covered in coral.
If you look closely, you will find some runes. Infuse your mana with them, and it will open up a portal. Enter that and you will be transported many miles under Seleria, near its core. You will be within a dome of energy keeping the heat and pressure at bay. You will then be transported to a path that leads to a circular platform that spans two-hundred meters.
On this platform is Orochi. This platform is an area Septim is allowed to do as he pleases with, whether he descends or not! You have to be close enough to explain things to Orochi as well as use the chant. Bahh!!!... I don’t have much more time. Tell that nine headed lizard he must quickly leave the platform as soon as possible! After it escapes to the path, use the pendant you must have prepared and teleport both you and Orochi away!--”
With those last words being spoken, Zephiron’s voice quietly faded and the brand flickered before dimming and soon appearing like a normal tattoo. Azrael had a hint of thankfulness and worship.
“My creator has gone through many years of effort to compile this information, I am truly in his debt...” Azrael clenched his fists before his body, with the sphere of mana, flickered and soon vanished with an incredible speed befitting a Mythical level being.
When he reappeared after several minutes, he was at the first arch. He suddenly raised his hand and began an incantation that lasted several seconds. The moment he finished, a large, one meter rune appeared on the surface of the sea floor, emitting a heavy red glow, before dimming slightly.
Azrael then glanced over at the first arch and looked in the distance before spotting the second, smaller arch hidden between the coral and sand. He made his way over before taking a deep breath. His body began to quiver with a newfound fear. He felt that although Septim didn’t think that anyone would know of this, that if he was caught by him, it would be his doom.
After reaching the smaller arch that was barely the height of a man, he focused closely on it. The arch was made from a mix of coral and rock and blended in well, though small, fingernail sized runes were engraved all across the inner sides of it.
Azrael opened both his palms and pushed dark mana into them and around the coral and rocky arch. Within moments, the runes began to glow with all sorts of colors before the mana converged into one point and formed into a sphere of white light that collapsed and pulsed out, forming into a mirror-like portal that contained magic and laws of magic that were higher than he could comprehend.
Gazing into the mirror, he spotted the obsidian path that lead to the circular platform, around this platform was a large dome of mana that protected the interior which happened to be this obsidian path and circular platform which was in the distance.
At the center of the platform a second dome of magic could be seen, though if one looked closer they would notice this was not a normal magical dome. The second dome itself was made up of bars of white affinity mana that were densely packed together, Azrael could barely see a shadowy figure inside.
Azrael snickered quietly as thoughts of revenge resurfaced in his mind. He stepped forward against the mirror, encountering a little resistance he assumed was meant to keep the water at bay, but in an instant he had appeared on the other side. The moment he did, the portal closed. There was an arch that he could use to exit if he had a change of heart, though considering his determination, it wasn’t going to be used.

“Layla.....It’s been countless years...though a chance at avenging you has occured...I’ll drown the humans in their own blood, and I’ll rip the wings off of every angel...I’ll have Fafnir’s head torn off and hung at the gates of my kingdom if I survive....”
Azrael gave a soft sigh. He remembered the time before he left.----Flashback----
Several days ago, Azrael was glancing over some things that belonged to his deceased wife and Lilia’s mother, Layla, when suddenly a soft voice sounded out. “Father, when will we be leaving?” This was the sound of Lilia, who had a resolute look on her face.
Azrael glanced at her and smiled softly. Layla was a human a being who, when compared to a demon, was quite fragile. But regardless, the two had fallen in love. “Lilia, you will remain here.” Having said this, Lilia frowned and spoke in agitation. “Father....you promised together we could avenge mother.... It’s one thing for us to hide here so as to not be discovered by Abbadon....but...with this why do I need to hide?”
“Lilia...I’ve lost your mother, this is a task that you just need to watch from the sidelines. I won’t risk losing you too.... Avrin also made me value Driada.. You’re both my daughters and are safer when hidden here!” Azrael spoke with a firm tone.
“Father!...” Lilia uttered out in displeasure at this decision, but Azrael gave a soft sigh. “Very well. In that case, take this to keep yourself safe.“ Azrael reached for Void and opened it up before beginning an incantation. A blob of green light soon formed above his hand, floating.
“Something that will save your life.“ He spoke silently while Lilia, who would never think her father would betray her or do anything to harm her, happily extended her hand to receive it, though with a thought the green blob of light shot with incredible speed, faster than Lilia could react to in time, and it hit her chest, not making a thud but rather absorbing into her body. Her eyes grew heavy as her vision distorted and blurred.
“Fa.....ther...” She spoke before she fell to the ground, making a small thump. Within moments, several of Azrael’s close guards heard this and came rushing in after hearing the sound. “My King?” The guards gazed strangely at Lilia, who was on the floor limp, and Azrael, who looked as if he wanted to cry.
“Keep my daughter safe.....until I return...” Azrael shuddered slightly before he left to where he knew the sea tribe were living. Due to him being branded by Zephiron, he had bypassed a lot of searching and the trouble of having to go to the Avian tribe and convincing them to not tell Abbadon about Azrael’s presence as well as raising suspicion of what he was after.--------Flashback end--------- Azrael casually made his way across the obsidian path. Looking around, he couldn’t help but shudder. He turned to look and saw the location he arrived at was a simple rocky protrusion from the top of the earth. Around him was a sea of molten hot iron that seemed to glow like a mini sun, which extended for as far as his eye could see. He knew that if this barrier of mana wasn’t present he would have long since been turned to ash.
Glancing over at the platform with the second, miniature prison dome, he took every step as if Septim would see, very slowly and carefully. Though, on his twentieth step, a heavy, serpent-like voice sounded out.
“A visitor?... I wonder how long it has been since I have seen a living creature...” Many dozens of glowing eyes in different colors from within the darkness of the glowing bars peered through. Despite being surrounded by so much light, it was not enough to pierce this darkness and reveal what lurked inside this prison.
“Orochi....it’s quite an honor to have the pleasure of meeting you...though you can see I’m quite nervous being here. If Septim finds out, then not only my hopes, but your hope of being free will be gone.”
“Ha.....hahaha… You want to free me?.... You have magic capable of removing a barrier of Septim’s creation?” The deep voice resounded out again. Hearing this, Azrael frowned. “I come here with advice given by Zephiron. Freeing you is simple, but if you aren’t willing to listen or help me, then I see I have wasted my time.”
Azrael was a former ruler and has lived for many hundreds of years. He was capable of manipulation, and in this case it worked. “Halt!...” Orochi’s deep yet powerful voice sounded out, though the moment he spoke, Azrael, who had turned and took steps to back away, suddenly stopped, to which Orochi spoke again. “I’m listening...” It said.
Azrael hiddenly smirked before speaking. “My request is simple, and it will benefit you too. I want you to help me kill humanity as well as all the angels and the dragon Fafnir, all those who were part of my wife dying. In return, I will guarantee you will be able to devour the Sigil weapons of both Abbadon and the wielder of humanity's Sigil weapons, Leo Zircus.”
Orochi listened carefully. The offer was indeed enticing, but how could it not fear Septim’s wrath.
“You want me to be free....then rampage around and incur Septim’s wrath again?...You must be crazier than look… You must be the demon king Azrael, correct?...Heh… No less than that worm Abbadon.”
Azrael’s face twisted a little before he soon began to explain many things in detail, even more importantly the fact that the gods could no longer interfere. He also explained that with the chant given by Zephiron he would have to use his speed to quickly leave that circular platform or risk Septim descending to punish him.
“Hmph...to risk myself...while you who are not on the platform will not suffer… Very well. If it is a chance at freedom, I want it… If you do manage to free me, you have my word as a dragon that I will litter this world with the corpses of those who were responsible for your wife’s death and you being sealed...”
Azrael’s expression eased and delight appeared. He remained quiet for a few moments, as if imagining the scene. One could say that the thought had caused him to become somewhat crazy. He could negotiate with Abbadon to form a peace treaty but instead decided to pursue revenge and war.
Before Orochi could wake him up from his thoughts, Azrael stepped over and was only a meter away from the circular platform that looked as white as polished ivory. It was also littered with strange runes Azrael couldn’t comprehend that pulsed with a white light similar to Avrin’s brand.
The platform was composed of two ring layers. The first layer, which was definitely used to detect intruders, spun in a slow circle. The second was still and where the dome of magic that formed thick bars of white light that sealed Orochi was located.
“Yies, Nyio Tysera Nyera Hyonta Cysis.” From there Azrael began a chant. While this happened, Void began to glow, causing the space around it to distort. With the chant, a heavy, dense mana surged out of Azrael and Void, forming into a dense hammer of dark magic that radiated a dark affinity aura.
“-No doubt this is a spell Zephiron personally uses, otherwise how can this brat obtain it. Heh, after I keep my word, what is stopping me from taking that book which I’m sure is a Sigil weapon. Ahh, the taste of godly power...almost enough to make me drool-”
While Orochi was having these thoughts, Azrael opened his closed eyes and grasped the hammer, which seemed to radiate a sort of profound darkness. The moment he gripped it, he felt his body involuntarily shudder.
Gripping it with two hands as Void floated beside him Azrael shouted out. “If you do not flee in time, then you can only curse your own luck!” Azrael roared out before he followed Zephiron’s instructions and threw the hammer with as much strength as he could muster towards the dome.
The moment the hammer entered the circular first dome, the runes began to glow, but the moment they started to glow the hammer had already reached the second dome, smashing against the barrier that shuddered and began to crack like glass.
But Orochi was too afraid as to what would happen if Septim came and he, from the inside of the darkened interior, rammed against it, causing it to crack into fragments. His large, shadowy figure was not discernable as he rushed with all the speed he could muster like a meteor and ran towards the obsidian path, causing the wind inside the mana dome to swish about like a torrent. Azrael was almost swept away but maintained his position.
The moment Orochi left the circular platform, a white light shot down. A man clad in a gold and white robe who had an ancient look and seemed to radiate power. The figure glanced over at the platform and the fragments of the prison used to hold Orochi before glancing towards the obsidian path.
This man was none other than Septim, who looked in Azrael’s direction. Azrael felt his heart shudder and he even forgot to breath. Septim was not glancing at him, though, but what was behind him. The large, black and green figure which had its monstrous wings spread, spanning at least sixty meters.
Its main body was much larger than Wruen, who was one of the larger dragons. The creature glanced over with one head that held a dark glow, its breath emitting a dark mist. Then, its second head, which emitted a white and bluish glow and a frosty mist, and so on until all nine of its heads appeared with a menacing, wrathful smile.
“You dare break your shackles.... You have not learned your lesson...” Septim’s voice thundered out as he narrowed his eyes before he turned to Azrael. “And you, after breaking your own shackles, dare to meddle in my affairs?.... You couldn’t have found this place out so easily, no doubt that Zephiron has something to do with this.” Septim clenched his fists and mana surged out of him, causing the area to shudder slightly.
“Hah!.... Some prison, old fart!.... I hear you gods can’t interfere in this world. I dare you to come here!” Orochi taunted, which made Azrael feel helpless and want to puke with fear. Septim’s face was red and he gave a twisted look of anger.
“Correct.... a law is a law....and I, Septim, keep my rules for a reason.... We gods can’t interfere but...this barrier is held up by my magic...under my control...” Septim snickered before he raised his right hand and clicked his fingers.
Azrael knew on instinct that he needed to flee. He quickly withdrew the pendant the moment Septim casually raised his hand and threw it on the ground. The barrier containing the heat shattered and Septim stood casually as a white barrier formed around him. Of course, at the same time, he frowned as he saw that a dark light formed by Azrael’s pendant created by Void’s magic engulfed him and Orochi before the two vanished in a surge of dark light.
Septim sighed slightly before he vanished in a burst of white light, reappearing back within the heavenly palace located far above Seleria. The moment he appeared over a large circular rune with four white pillars on all four sides, a skinny figure wearing a black robe with a pale face, the head of this individual had shaven sides with a simple ponytail at the top of his head as well as pointed ears, glanced over towards Septim.
Septim looked over at this figure and grunted slightly. “Zephiron.... If this plan of yours doesn’t work it will set us back hundreds of years!” Septim spoke towards the black figure, who happened to be Zephiron.
“Hehehe… Relax, this will work perfectly. Of course there is no such stupid rule as us gods interfering. That Azrael is a perfect catalyst for this all. When the world burns and bathes in enough blood, watch Enigma users pop out of the woodwork. Then we will have more than enough material to continue our plans.”
Septim remained quiet before thinking a little and walking off. Zephiron snickered as he thought. “-Azrael, Orochi, you mortal pawns think we gods haven’t planned ahead… Though your usefulness is nearing its end, it will have been of use for this wonderful experimental farm of ours.-”

Back on the ocean floor, the water surged and the sandy ground split apart as Orochi’s large figure appeared, followed by Azrael, who quickly formed a water barrier around the both of them. “Water.... This is water… It’s so cool here.... Perfect… This is good....” Orochi reached up with his claw and ripped the barrier Azrael had placed with ease. The water flooded in, engulfing its body, causing it to shudder slightly.
“Water.... Perfect.. So cold...hahaha..... I’m free… I’m finally FREE!!” Orochi’s mana blasted out like a monster. It caused the water to blow apart and even blew Azrael back and onto his knees from the pressure. Azrael was astonished at how powerful Orochi had become.
“-Such power.... Just how strong is this creature…?-” Azrael had no idea that Orochi had broken through to the Early stage of the New Deity level after devouring the Sigil Enhancements crafted by each god for their respective Sigil wielder.
The monstrous mana which shot out could be felt across the entirety of Seleria, showing how powerful it was. Within a white chamber, Abbadon was lecturing several young angels, teaching them about spells and mana affinities, when the pressure of Orochi’s mana hit, it was enough for everyone to feel it. Of course, the one who had the most shock was Abbadon, whose eyes widened with a look of fear. “N...No.... It can’t be...”
Giron was eating high class meat and drinking fine wine within his home, laughing as he told the story of how he supposedly killed Silis, which was a lie, and some doubted him. Though these were people who knew of its existence and were close to him and dared not call him a liar.
“So that’s how I-” Orochi’s mana hit him next and caused his family and friends to look with shock and horror. Giron, though, had a stunned expression. He quickly reached for the object he used to communicate with Abbadon.
Within the southern continent, the elven forest, Myra sighed as she walked passed Syrana’s room with a feeling of loneliness. They were like sisters and best friends, close to each other and backing each other up, yet Syrana had ditched her easily to go search for Avrin.
“That bastard Avri-” The mana surged over the forest, causing the birds to scatter and everyone to look in fear. “What a powerful affinity.... A dual affinity?... No...this isn’t just two affinities....Impossible!!! It’s all affinities?!!.... This can only mean....Orochi! Other than him, what creature could possess all affinities!” Confusion and surprise was adorned on Myra’s face as she clenched her teeth.
Several minutes before Orochi released his mana, within the central continent and in the eastern kingdom of Hajhl, in which capital city housed many exquisite buildings, with the city’s main trade being art and fresh produce, it was quite well off. A large, well-made building that seemed fit for a king was guarded by some lazy looking guards who, despite being adorned in well made armor, seemed to look casual.
Suddenly, three robed figures made their way towards the building before the one in front stopped and gazed up. The two other figures stopped and followed the eyes of the first one, looking up. The one on the left spoke with a soft, teasing, female tone. “See, see, I told you my methods of extracting information pay off time and time again.”
The figure in the middle, despite having a female voice, sounded more harsh and unforgiving. “We would have been here sooner if we had looked into them changing their name...”
The figure on the right asked in a curious tone, also being a female. “Master, I think it’s good that we made it here, though, no one would have guessed that they would change it only a week ago. Regardless, this is definitely the headquarters of the Gold Stone Mercenaries.”
The figures continued to look as the light reflected a bit to reveal their faces. These were none other than Syrana, Ayame and Izanami, who had set out to search for Avrin, having spent a little more than two years gathering information and going on misleads that led them on a wild goose chase to find this mercenary group.
“Hehe, indeed. It wasn’t that bad. I’ll have you know, although we got many bad leads, we finally made it!” Izanami said, making Syrana’s eyebrows twitch in disatisfaction. She felt that it had taken much longer than it should have. The Twisting Lands was the biggest waste of time, and even more so the mercenaries changing their names and moving headquarters. Syrana was nearing her wit’s end.
“Forget it. Let’s go in.” Speaking with annoyance, Syrana walked up the marble-like steps. After she neared the the top, the lazy guards suddenly became serious, stood in front of her and spoke. “State your business.” One spoke as if he had been practicing the lines for a week.
“I’m here to see your leader, a woman named Felia.” Syrana spoke softly, but her voice carried a sort of heavy feeling. The guard thought for a moment before replying. “Appointments need to be made days in advance and be sent by mail or carrier bird. If you don’t have an appoi-” Before the guard could finish, Syrana’s forehead tensed and a vein appeared. Green, nature affinity mana surged out of her, showing that she was at the early mythical stage.
This frightened the guards, who now knew they were dealing with an expert. And going by what they were taught, experts were always allowed in. “P..Please forgive me..... Go.....r..right in. I’ll have someone notify Lady Felia!!” The guard shuddered before the dense mana dispersed. The three soon entered the building.
The interior was gorgeous, with hand carved wooden beams, furniture, and doors and their frames. The floor was a special wood that underwent petrification when imbued with mana, causing the it to have a unique pattern.
The building, composed of four levels, was quite expensive. Of course, with Felia’s newfound wealth, it was an easy purchase. On the fourth level, Felia stood dressed in similar leather attire to the one she wore within the Twisting Lands. Though this seemed to fit her curves perfectly. One would guess she had it specially commissioned due to its beautiful design, bringing together blue, white, and gold. It even had the emblem of her mercenary group as an insignia on the back.
Felia was writing on parchment in regards to forming several smaller branches in a way to extend her power. She definitely would not miss an opportunity, and it had been in the making for two years, but she stopped as she heard a knock on the door. “Oh?... Didn’t I say not to bother me? What’s the issue?” She uttered out in a soft, civilized manner. Her long hair now hung at her lower back in a ponytail. She seemed quite at ease, as if nothing could shake the podium she was on.
“Lady Felia...supposedly some experts have arrived....” A man’s worried voice sounded out. Felia frowned for a moment as she pondered the situation. Over the past two years, several powerful individuals had come, seeking information about the dungeon. They had told her it was supposedly a dragon’s lair, although Felia didn’t believe them. She didn’t rebut it either, as to garner a bit more importance.
“Let them in.” She spoke with a soft tone, thinking the situation was just a follow up to some other things. Though she was a little surprised. She had, after all, felt many people would try to seek her group out and bully them into giving them money or information. She had tried quite hard to pay off individuals to spread fake rumors on purpose in many taverns in an attempt to mislead these individuals into a dead end in hopes of buying enough time to establish herself.
Of course, she took any situation with experts seriously, especially the first batch that had managed to find her even after all the misleading she had paid a fortune for. Several moments later, Syrana and the other two were being escorted through the large building. “Do you think she knows where he is, Master?” Ayame couldn’t help but ask. “I’m not sure.” Syrana spoke bluntly with a tone of hope. She truly wanted to teach Avrin a lesson after the situation he put her through.
“You have me around. It will be easy to discern whether she knows something or not!” Izanami also wanted to give her thoughts on the situation. The trio were led up stairs and past several guards and individuals who seemed to be busy with their own matters, until they were finally led down a hall with a single room at the end. Of course, the hall also seemed to be guarded with magical runes to act as defences. One could see the owner has spared little expense in securing protection.
When they reached the end of the hall, the man escorting them knocked, and a soft voice called out. “Come in.” Felia spoke from inside. The man glanced at the trio behind him and opened the door before speaking. “If you please.” He tried to sound dignified and respectful. After all, he was not one to take the risk of offending someone powerful. Syrana was the first to walk in, followed by Izanami, then Ayame. When the three entered, the door was softly shut. Syrana glanced at the figure behind a wooden desk, who was casually looking back at her. This was, of course, Felia.
“Three supposed experts? To what do I owe the pleasure?” Felia spoke with no stutter and a calm expression on her face. Her elbows were on the table, her hands folded, while she looked over at the three.
Syrana gazed at Felia strangely. Although she had seen a few elven people in her travels in the southern continent, if there was a chance that Avrin and her had journeyed together, then considering the situation, it annoyed her strangely.
“Finding you was not enjoyable at all...but what’s done is done. As long as I get some answers, I’m quite forgiving. In this case, I’m looking for someone who I’m certain you have traveled with.” Syrana casually spoke out before lowering her hood to reveal her appearance. Ayame and Izanami followed suit.
Felia glanced over and her expression flickered a little. Gazing carefully at Syrana, she wasn’t sure who exactly she was, considering she was not born on the southern continent but on the central continent. “Looking for someone who you’re certain I know? I have a lot of mercenaries under my wing. Some come and go, some even die. Though if you give me a name it will shorten the list.” Felia spoke back.
Syrana had nothing to hide and waited for a moment before speaking. “I’m looking for someone called Avrin.” Felia, after hearing this, felt her eyes narrow as she responded the moment Syrana replied. “Don’t know him… Sorry.”
Syrana walked over and slammed her fist onto the desk in an aggressive manner. “Bullshit! Don’t think I haven’t come here unprepared. The dungeon your little group went to was home to a dragon. You think he is going to let your little possy come in and run amok without acting? A little digging in ancient texts can easily identify that place, and I sure as hell don’t think you're capable of fighting a dragon.” Syrana spoke in a blunt, aggressive manner.
Her temper over the years had reached a frightening level, especially towards Felia, who, despite having not met her, had been the end result of a search that was frustrating.
“Hmph! I’ll tell you what I told everyone else. When we arrived at the end, we found no dragon. Other than Sigil wielders, who is capable of fighting one? And going by this Avrin person you're looking for, are you implying he is capable of fighting one? How would I find the money to hire someone like that before my current situation.”
Felia had seen Avrin’s strength. Although it was astonishing, she didn’t believe he could fight against a dragon, so her words held some truth. Though she continued to speak. “So I’m telling you, I don’t know any Avrin.” Felia finished.
If you spot this story on Amazon, know that it has been stolen. Report the violation.
Syrana remained silent and frowned a little. She then turned to Izanami, who was quietly watching from the sides, spoke to her. “Fine… Handle this before I destroy this place...” Syrana spoke before walking back. Izanami gave a sly smile before walking over towards the desk and sitting on the edge of it, glancing at Felia.
“What a shame. Though, I’m sure you will let us know if you find Avrin, correct? I’m sure you know we are quite powerful?” Izanami spoke. Felia grunted quietly as she looked at Izanami with a bit of disdain. “As long as you don’t cause issues for my group, then if I hear of anything, I’ll let you know...” She didn’t plan to at all and her words were quite hollow.
“That’s fine, it’s all good. Let me describe him for you.” Izanami gave a light laugh but Felia remained quiet, hoping these three would leave soon after. “Avrin has long silver hair, a handsome face no less than angelic, his body...enough to make any decent woman drool with lust. And he is quite good under the sheets. I could go on telling you about our encounter.”
While speaking, Izanami chose her words carefully as to see the change in Felia’s reaction. Felia, of course, felt her body tremble a little and her eyebrows twitch as she remembered Avrin’s appearance. Her cheeks lit up in a pink hue, but she tried to remain calm.
That is, until she heard from Izanami regarding him being good under the sheets. This made her clench her fists in anger, wondering why Avrin had never made a move on her. For a moment she had even forgotten about the situation. She would never have guessed that the seductive Izanami had skillfully set her up.
“Oh, Avrin also wears a blue cloak at all times...” Izanami uttered with a slight grin. It was then that Felia, who had been filled with annoyance and had for a moment forgotten the situation uttered with a bit of anger subconsciously. “You mean a black cloa-” Her eyes widened and her heart beat heavily. She glanced up and spotted Izanami, who snickered silently, then over towards Syrana, who was walking towards her with a grin.
“-Shit… This seductress got me… And I thought I was good-” A nervous smile appeared on Felia’s face as she placed her hand under the table towards a dimly glowing, circular rune.
But before she could even reach it, Izanami pulled out a short weapon similar to a kodachi and stabbed it directly into the table, perfectly over the rune, destroying it. “Oh, I don’t think so. Be a good girl and remain still.” Izanami smiled coldly towards Felia, who had a worried look.
“You think I’m going to tell you where he is? Even if I knew, I can see your intentions are surely not good.” Syrana walked over and her mana moved to Felia, who had just dashed back off the chair before falling to her knees from the astonishing pressure.
“Ah!” She helplessly uttered before glancing at Syrana with fear and anger. “That’s none of your business… I have a bone to pick with him… Tell me everything you kn-” It was at that moment the pressure from Orochi hit the city, dispersing Syrana’s surge of mana and even causing fear to well up in her heart. “-Such a powerful affinity.... Has a god descended?... No...this feels sinister… Why does it have several affinities?-” Syrana broke out into a slight cold sweat and clenched her teeth, glancing at Felia.
Ayame, who also felt the pressure felt her heart beat quicker as she clenched her fists, trying to remain calm. “Master?.... What...is this?..” She helplessly spoke towards Syrana, who remained calm. Izanami, who also widened her eyes, couldn’t help but feel her soul shudder from the pressure. She had never felt this afraid in her life. The surge of mana felt distant, but not one trace of it felt weak. If it were in this city, no doubt the people within would already be dead from the pressure.
Felia clenched her teeth as well, but took this chance, as they were distracted, and reached into a small tool belt to her side before pulling out a single blue sphere that she threw towards them. Syrana glanced over, but it was too late. The sphere exploded in a radiant blue light that activated all the hidden runes within the room. Immediately the building, which was full of people who had also felt the mana, were woken up to reality by the sounds of an attack upstairs. All the guards made their way upstairs to assist Felia.
The surge of mana Orochi had showed soon vanished, which helped keep the focus towards the alert. Syrana gripped Felia by the collar of her leather attire and raised her in the air with ease. “Big mistake… I’m not done with you...” Syrana frowned as Felia resisted, though soon the door was kicked in and dozens of armored individuals charged through. “Leader!!” Several shouted as they saw Felia’s situation.
These were guards who had little to nothing, and it was thanks to Felia that they were able to become successful in life. They owed her a lot, including their lives. She had saved many and even given them a chance to support their families. They would not hesitate to give their lives for her. Several charged towards Syrana, who looked at them with disdain.
As five neared, Ayame’s figure flashed towards them as she charged towards the guards. Her body flickered with agile movement before her palms smashed against the exposed points of the armor they wore, from the back of their knees to the shoulder joints. Using her fingers and palms she managed to stun five guards who were at the early stage Expert level, showing that her time during the two years was spent not just on searching but in increasing her strength.
Ayame then stood in the center around the stunned guards. She glanced over towards the group at the door and spoke. “Anyone who doesn’t want to taste the floor stay where you are.” Although Ayame was at the peak Expert level she knew her main advantage and focus was on speed and technique rather than raw strength.
“Where is Avrin...” Syrana spoke as she pinned Felia against the wall. Felia looked angrily towards Syrana before lifting her knee and smashing it towards her gut but Syrana was skilled and not easily beaten. She moved her free hand over and effortlessly blocked her knee. “Go to....hell...” Felia muttered out.
Syrana grew impatient, frowned and was about to speak before she felt a surge of mana above her. The ceiling cracked and a figure smashed down. Syrana quickly let Felia go and dashed to the side, avoiding the blow. A sweet, childish voice sounded out soon after.
“Damn, I missed! This bitch is pretty fast, hahaha!“ This was none other than Wyni, who brandished the Unique level Legion Hammer obtained from the dungeon. Syrana frowned. She was contemplating simply leveling this entire building, but it would cause a commotion if an elven Sigil wielder did so within a human city.
“Nice timing, Wyni, but you ruined my ceiling!” Felia spoke with a nervous laugh as she rubbed her neck and gasped for breath. Wyni had, of course, gotten stronger and with the Legion Hammer in hand, was at the level of a peak Master. She had trained immensely with the hammer in order to get used to it and improve.
“Pssh… What’s it matter? Just buy a new one. Now, let me handle this. Clovis should be here soon. I was closest when my rune shard broke.” She was referring to an expensive magic that used a shard of crystal inscribed with a rune. When Felia activated the blue sphere which triggers all nearby runes, one of the runes inscribed to break both her and Clovis’ shard activated which alerted her.
“That’s fine, they’re after Avrin. I’m not sure why, but it can’t be good. We just need to buy enough time for the city lord’s troops to get here. I’m sure that old geezer will have felt mana. He owes me quite a bit too.” Felia stood up and unsheathed a short sword at her side. She was at the early Master level and although she wasn’t as strong as Wyni anymore she still prided herself on her swordsmanship.
“Avrin? Gahh, I miss my little Kael.” She frowned a little before glancing at Syrana and dashing towards her with the hammer in hand, though before she passed a meter, Izanami flickered with her two blades and slashed at Wyni, who quickly used the Legion Hammer to block. This caused sparks to fly up and as Izanami’s blades slashed downwards as they were deflected to the ground, causing a large gash to appear. Izanami focused on Wyni and gave a sly smile.
“Sorry, but you’re gonna have to play with me for a bit.” Izanami spoke before her own aura surged out. She was considered not only a genius when it comes to gathering intel and manipulation, but also when it came to strength. She was already a mid level Master when fighting Avrin, and now she was at the peak of the Master level, where she could breakthrough to the Grandmaster level at any time.
Izanami jumped back and removed her robe to show her stunning appearance that even left some of the weaker willed guards shock and awed by it, Wyni looked over at Izanami with a face of dissatisfaction before grinning. “A shame a body like that is only useful in seduction!” Hearing Wyni’s words Izanami simply snickered and replied. “Sounds like you’re jealous, and if you think it is wise to underestimate me you’re sorely mistaken.”
Izanami finished before her body vanished. She blurred with speed as she slashed towards Wyni who, of course, didn’t sit still and take it. Wyni’s physical strength was indeed stronger than Izanami’s, but her speed was lacking, so she could only focus on defending, and even then some attacks went through, causing cuts and scratches to appear over the spots she wasn’t quick enough to cover.
Izanami appeared behind Wyni and slashed towards her right hand in an attempt to disarm her, but Felia, who was close by, used all her speed to shoot towards Izanami and thrust with her short sword towards her. Izanami frowned before kicking off the ground and dashing back. Felia pointed the blade towards her.
“Wyni, just buy a bit more time for Clovis and the city lord.” Felia mumbled. While this happened, several guards who were quite loyal charged towards Ayame with weapons of all types. Ayame had to be careful. Several individuals were early stage Masters. Although not as quick as her, their raw power is equal to her form without relying on the White Dragon’s bloodline.
She nimbly avoided many of the attacks surely meant to kill. She found it troublesome, when traveling, she had been made to kill every enemy she had to fight, but when entering cities and villages Syrana had forbidden it completely. It was quite a handicap to her, considering all her techniques are meant to not only stun the opponent but to finish them the moment they were unable to move.
“Master....this is annoying, please make a move!” Ayame called out. Syrana, who had been watching until now, sighed and her own body flickered towards Ayame, who was surrounded by four individuals who glanced at her with ill intentions. Two of them were early stage Masters who had just charged towards her.
In an instant, Syrana appeared behind them and they both fell to the ground with their mouths frothing and their bodies limp. “I’m going to give you one last chance to tell me where Avrin is, or I’m going to bury your mercenary group!” Syrana called out, but the moment she did, deep laughter sounded out from behind the guards waiting in the hallway.
“Hahaha! Bury our group? You need to deal with me first!” A surge of fire affinity mana shot out, causing the guards to quickly step to the side and make way for the red robed individual.
“Clovis!” Felia called out with a sigh of relief.

Suddenly, from the hall the guards were packed in, a surging blur of fire burst out toward Syrana, clearly with intention to harm. Syrana frowned before her own mana rose. She then punched outward with her right hand to meet the flaming blur. Both collided, causing the room’s walls to crack and the unstable flooring to crumble. Some of the slower guards fell through into the room below, but not before uttering helpless shouts.
As the flaming mana eased up, Clovis was revealed, who gave a stunned expression. He could feel his hand was numb, as if he hit a very solid wall that didn’t budge. His face paled as he gazed at Syrana before jumping back to regain his footing. “Impressive, to stop my attack with seemingly little effort.”
Syrana casually moved her fist back to her side before replying. “I have better things to do than staying here to fight. I simply want to know where Avrin is.” Felia, who revealed a grave expression, clearly felt Syrana couldn’t be underestimated.
“She has to be at least a peak Grandmaster. Was there an expert among the sylph race other than the Sigil wielders?” She contemplated quietly, clearly having no clue that Syrana was infact one of those Sigil wielders.
Wyni, who was glaring at Izanami while keeping her guard up, called out to Clovis “Damnit, it’s about time you got here. What took you so long!” She had a nervous expression, knowing Izanami would take any chance she got to attack.
Clovis simply laughed before speaking while his mana surged again. “Sorry about that, Miss Wyni, but don’t worry, I’ll handle this now. As for you intruders, I’m just getting warmed up! Flame Fist, First Strike!!”
Clovis’s speed increased before he shot like a bullet towards Syrana, feeling that this time the result for him would be better. Syrana’s eyes narrowed and she casually sidestepped. Of course, with her speed and strength, it was almost too fast fast for Clovis to even register.
His fist punched through the spot Syrana had just been, but Syrana was glancing at him from the side, watching as he gave a stunned expression, his head slowly turning to look at her. It seemed to all happen in slow motion. Syrana’s right hand formed into a fist and she punched Clovis. The punch itself seemed to cause a mini sonic boom like a whip. The punch collided with Clovis’s side and he was blown through the walls of the building and even smashed through two others near the mercenary’s HQ.
Syrana raised her fist, which emitted a small trace of smoke, though she frowned a little as she looked at the large hole Clovis had been smashed through, she then turned to gaze over at everyone. What met her were fearful but amazed expressions. The guards were trembling and even Wyni’s mouth was agape.
Ayame quietly muttered to herself. “As expected of Master. How could some nobody be a match for her.” Izanami had a more preserving thought as she quietly laughed, “-I have to never get on her bad side....-” A drop of sweat ran down her cheek and she found it hard to comprehend Syrana’s speed. She could tell she was holding back greatly to not kill anyone.
Syrana walked over to Felia, but this time, no one stood in her way. Syrana’s mana surged slightly, Felia’s face was twitching with a newfound fear. It’s as if she wanted to realise something.. “J..just who the hell are you....” She spoke out. Syrana, of course, ignored those words, with no intention to reveal herself and cause trouble.
“Where is Avri-” Her words were cut short as flaming blur shot through the hole Clovis had flew through. “Flame Fist, Inferno Flurry!!” Clovis appeared beside Syrana with a grave look. Blood was trickling through the sides of his lips and he was pale, but he didn’t give up. He began to barrage Syrana with fists imbued with flame affinity mana, each punch caused the air to heat up and tremble.
“-Resilient!-” was Syrana’s first thought when she saw Clovis appear. She had used the strength of an early stage Sage to hit him away, hoping to knock him out, but clearly this human, in her eyes, was like a cockroach that was hard to get rid of. While she was dodging and blocking Clovis’s strikes, she felt many surges of mana, and one even at the mid Grandmaster level from outside, surrounding the building. She knew the city lord had arrived.
“You...” Syrana clenched her teeth before her mana surged out and gave everyone present in the building an oppressive feeling, causing some to drop to their knees. Her left hand shot towards Clovis, hitting the side of his neck with her palm.
The strike caused the ground to tremble, Clovis opened his mouth and his eyes rolled back before he fell limp to the ground. In one strike, Clovis had been knocked out.
Syrana’s fit figure then vanished before reappearing in front of Felia. Her hand shot out, smashing against the wall behind Felia, causing it to shatter. She then spoke with a simple to understand word, considering the situation.
“Speak!” Accompanied by Syrana’s terrifying pressure, Felia had felt it was best to just tell what she knows rather than to hold back and possibly endanger the lives of her comrades further. Filled with regret, she clenched her teeth and spoke.
“Promise me...you won’t harm any of my men, and also give me your word you won’t harm Avrin!” She knew it was all wishful thinking, though she wanted to grab at what she could for a bit of reassurance. Right now, she had little choice. Syrana quickly replied. “I won’t harm any of your men. As for Avrin, that is none of your business, stop stalling further.
Or, I could always bring you with us and have our seductress get information from you.” Her words carried a somewhat comedic yet serious threat. Izanami pouted and called out “Hey!” Felia glanced at Izanami, who simply smirked. Her eyebrows twitched a little before she looked back at Syrana and quickly began to explain things.
“The port city of Rael, the city lord has a connection to Avrin… He knows more than me..” Felia’s heart felt heavy with each word spoken. She felt she was betraying Avrin, despite all the good he had done for her. She had no real choice.
Syrana looked at Felia carefully before glancing over at Ayame and Izanami, who both quickly grabbed their cloaks and dashed out of the newly made hole in the wall beside Felia. Syrana glared at Felia before speaking. “If this is a lie...you will have nowhere to run.”
Syrana dashed out following the two others, though the moment she left was the moment the sounds of rushed footsteps echoed out before a small group of heavily armored individuals and one man who was clad in blue plate armor with no helmet and an aged look with a white beard looked around. This man was the city lord. “What happened here?”
Hearing his words, Felia could only glare daggers at him. “Useless bastard, you’re late!” Speaking with an angered tone, she knew that around she was valued quite well and the city relied on her newly established mercenary group to handle many issues.
Meanwhile, to the east of the city, three figures dashed away into the forest, which covered a large amount of ground. After the three had traveled for a few minutes, Ayame finally couldn’t hold back any longer and spoke. “Master...that pressure from before, what was it?” Clearly she meant Orochi. She felt the situation with that was more noteworthy than talking about the current information on Avrin.
Syrana nervously bit her lower lip as she looked a little nervous. Only Izanami, with her keen eyes, could pick this up. She felt the situation wasn't so simple. Syrana suddenly stopped, remaining silent for a moment even as the other two waited. Syrana finally spoke. “Izanami, Ayame, both of you head to Rael and find out what you can from the city lord. I’m heading to the capital city Altea to see something.”
Izanami smiled and replied. “Very well.” Afterwards she pulled out a rolled up parchment with a map before going over it, though while she did, Ayame glanced over at Syrana with a dissatisfied expression. “Master, this is the first major lead in two years!” Syrana frowned and yelled with a bit of impatience. “I know! But this is more important. It can’t be avoided.” She sighed a little.
“Izanami, you’re in charge. I expect you to handle it all.” Syrana spoke and, with her incredible speed, vanished quickly towards the direction of Altea. “Master!” Ayame called out and was about to follow, but Izanami placed her hand on her shoulder. “Lets go, don't worry about her.” Hearing Izanami’s words Ayame’s cheeks puffed before she frowned and sighed. “Fine...”
Syrana, who was making her way towards Altea at a great speed, felt the enchanted sack at her side emit a faint pulse of light affinity mana. She then reached inside and pulled out a small, smooth surfaced stone with two white wings engraved onto it. She spoke to the pulsing object with a dissatisfied expression.
“Abbadon...what the hell was that?” Suddenly, a voice seemed to emit from the stone in reply “You’re at the central continent already? Interesting indeed, though forget that. Head to Altea. It seems Orochi has been freed. The other Sigil wielders are all gathering, including Myra. If we don’t face this threat together then we face disastrous consequences.“
Syrana felt her heart skip a beat and stopped for a moment. She had heard of Orochi and how powerful he was before devouring the Sigil enhancements and that he brazenly went against the gods. Right now he must be incredibly powerful, for them all to gather and face him. “I’m on my way.” She spoke before placing the engraved stone back into the sack and heading off again. “-How can he be released? Didn’t God King Septim imprison him where no one could find him… Wait a second...could Avrin have been responsible?-”
Reading on this site? This novel is published elsewhere. Support the author by seeking out the original.Syrana had felt that because Avrin was searching for Skymetal, if he had found Orochi, who may have possessed a piece, maybe the deal was to free him for that piece. Of course, she felt it was too far fetched and put the idea behind her.
Within the great oceans of Seleria, a large shadow was making its way through the deep blue water. This was the nine headed dragon Orochi, with Azrael following not too far behind and keeping a nervous, careful expression while around the dragon. One of Orochi’s heads turned back to look at him and simply laughed. “Why are you so afraid? A deal is a deal, after all.” The dragon laughed before Azrael frowned a bit and spoke. “That may be so, but why are we heading in this direction? You know what is ahead, it has nothing to do with our deal.”
Hearing Azrael’s disatisfaction, Orochi gave a simple reply. “It’s simple. I need a snack and some exercise. I’m sure you know what it’s like being sealed for hundreds of years, hahahaha.” The dragon laughed again, showing that it was a little crazy.
Soon, the two neared a large open area of the sea floor. Located there was a large, thin bubble of white light that seemed to give a radiant shine over the sea as well as a large city that was housed within it. Of course, the bubble didn’t stop water from going through. This was because the inhabitants of the city were the sea tribe! This was their city of Azuros.
Azrael, upon seeing the city, had a bad feeling. Orochi simply ignored him and swam over. Within the city, large spires made from coral, sea stone and seaweed were lined up across the city. The streets and many architecturally important objects were made from special materials such as blue pearl and Azure Tortoise shell, which was the main material used in creating everything here.Tthe streets were lined with humanoids that had dark blue and light blue skin with scales over their bodies. Their feet were webbed and their heads were all but human, with large, round, black eyes and gills that acted as ears. These creatures were all hairless and all wore simple clothing made from sea materials. Of course, some guards could be seen wearing a bit more armor-like clothes made from sea creatures.
This was because the couldn’t forge anything underwater, they had to make due with what they had. Parents taking their children around and eating, as well as having fun. One could say this was a city paradise. Azuros, the city that had never once experienced war, famine or hardship was a true paradise for people seeking peace. Of course, this very day, that peace would be torn asunder.
Within the centre of the city, a large palace towered over the others. It was lined with white pearl and rare materials to show that it was the hub of everything. Many of the sea folk went in and out casually. Nothing seemed to be restricted in this city, as if they were a tribal family that looked after one another.
Though as beautiful as the city was, over the hundreds of years, its beauty was suddenly interrupted as a shadow loomed over everything. Many of the sea folk gazed up to see a large shadow within the bubble, blocking out quite a bit of the radiance. Some of them were confused and stunned, but not afraid. After all, the sea tribe had never truly felt fear. They all had figured it was something else. One of the young children even called out in a damp voice.
“Mama, is that the Divine Protector?” Though the child’s question wasn’t answered, as a deep laughter resounded out. The fire affinity head of Orochi could be seen glowing a deep red. “I love fish!!! But even better, I love fried fish!!” Suddenly the head opened its mouth, to which a vortex of flame affinity mana gathered.
The water of the ocean didn’t seem to be capable of putting this strange flame out, and even more fearful was that Orochi suddenly fired a beam of flame that evaporated the water and smashed down towards the city.
Orochi was one of, if not the, most powerful dragons. After absorbing the Sigil enhancements and breaking into the new Deity level, he had gotten immensely stronger. The beam of flame mana crashed against the spires of the city and they all began to burn and collapse, causing debris to fall. The beam of flame made its way across the streets, turning the helpless sea folk to ash. Everyone began to scream in terror and try to flee in all directions, unsure what to do in such a situation.
The large city had now become Orochi’s playground as he blew apart the structures of seaweed and coral with ease. Water, which was fire’s natural enemy, was useless against such a powerful vortex of flame that didn’t seem to be hindered, showing that a new Deity’s strength was quite significant.
Even as the water began to heat up and many sea folk were burnt alive or burnt enough to turn to ash and scatter into the water, there were some that wanted to fight back from the city. A large mass of warriors clad in blue pearl armor shot upward, carrying golden tridents in their hands. They numbered at least a few thousands, each one at the Grandmaster level.
The sea tribe had never faced any real war and was able to build up its strength over the years. These warriors swam out towards Orochi and brandished their tridents, imbuing water affinity mana into the tridents and firing them off towards Orochi, each one carrying the strength of a Grandmaster.
If this had been used against an army of the land above, then most likely the armor would have been annihilated. Even a dragon may be a little annoyed at this. But Orochi simply laughed before his dark mana affinity head slid out to the front and opened its mouth, its eyes beginning to glow, and a dark sphere of mana gathered into its mouth before it exploded out, shooting strands of black light to all the tridents.
Azrael was stunned as he spoke out. “I...Impossible...” He quickly opened Void and went over it before his eyes widened. “That’s the God level magic Corrupted Shadow… How can he…?” He was unable to finish before the strands of dark light all hit a trident. The tridents turned from a shining gold to a glowing jet black and the water that had rippled through the force of them shooting outwards like comets suddenly remained still. This was because all the tridents were frozen within the water, not moving an inch.
Not one of the sea tribe warriors kept a calm expression. They all began to mutter and speak of how strange and asked what was going on. Of course, no one had an answer and stopped speaking. This was because the tridents all turned around and faced back towards the thousands of warriors before firing off back towards them with even more monstrous strength. They all gasped and began to flee, but it was as if they were being hunted by spears. The tridents impaled many in a near instant, with only a few hundred escaping with their lives, and even they were wounded.
Blood had begun to cover the clear water, and Orochi simply laughed again madly before it swam over, causing the water to split apart. Orochi began to casually devour the dead and wounded with all of its nine heads, as if it was at an all you can eat buffet. “Food!! You’re all food, whether in flesh or mana!” Orochi was greatly enjoying himself. Azrael revealed a pale expression.
“T..The sea tribe had nothing to do with me being sealed… Have...I done wrong?..” He questioned himself before his hands balled into fists. “No...this is for my revenge… Me perishing is of no big deal. Whether this world burns in the aftermath is not of my concern...it’s all....it’s all for her..” His body shook with conflicted emotions.
Orochi didn’t seem to forget the city, as the flame affinity head would often fire spheres of condensed flame towards the city which would cause explosions, though one could tell he wasn’t serious and was just enjoying himself, as if playing with an ant nest with tools specially made for handling the nest itself.
Suddenly, a surge of mana appeared within the palace. Orochi’s light afinity head had its eyes narrow before it casually spoke out. “Radiance Shield...” Suddenly, the head pulsed out before a shield of white light formed in front of Orochi. At that moment, a blue beam of light shot towards him from the palace, colliding with the barrier and causing it to tremble a little before it eased up to reveal an amazingly made trident with strange, runic symbols. The trident was jagged at the front like a thorn, but had a blue glow, while the runes were glowing white.
The trident then shot backwards and a man caught it with ease. This was a sea tribesman who was at least two times larger than the others. His eyes were not black, but red, and veins were pressing up from under his flesh. He emitted a heavy mana and was quite muscular. He wore a simple cloth around his waist, which was decorated by gems and also a crown of a strange but most likely rare material, as it seemed to shine even without light.
Behind him, dozens of other sea tribesmen began to gather until they numbered at least fifty, each one as powerful as an early stage Sage to mid level Sage. The sea tribesmen with the large, trident which radiated power roared out in anger. “You destructible serpent! The first thing you do when freed is rampage against my people!!! If I don’t cleave all your heads off then the legacy of I, King Tryil, have built up will have been for naught!!”
Finally showing himself, this was the sea tribe’s Sigil wielder and ruler, King Tryil, with the Sigil lance Leviathes. Hearing his words, all of Orochi’s heads stopped devouring the dead sea tribesmen and showed looks of disdain towards King Tryil, who raised his Sigil weapon and began to gather mana towards it.
“A dumb water bug has enough guts to talk to me like that? If it’s a fight you want, I will gladly oblige!” Orochi clearly didn’t seem to take the battle seriously. Its flame affinity head shot a vortex of fire towards Tryil, who then willed Leviathes to release its attack. “Feel the wrath of Leviathes and my people!!”
The three forks of Leviathes, which had gathered small, condensed spheres of a light blue mana, had suddenly exploded out into cracks of lightning that seem to easily traverse the water. The lightning shot towards the flame vortex, smashing against it. The two struggled for a moment before the lightning circled around it and smashed against Orochi’s flame affinity head.
“Urgh..” Orochi shuddered for a moment and stopped his attack. King Tryil, who had seen this, smirked with delight, while the Sage level sea tribe warriors behind him cheered. Orochi glared menacingly at Tryil. “That strung.....you little whelp.... You’re DEAD!” Orochi seemed to have gotten angry, as the flame affinity head had suddenly lit up with a heavier glow before it charged another vortex of flame that caused the water around the head to split and distort. Though the flame beam was shot towards Tryil, the flame this time was now blue and incredibly hot and condensed. Tryil’s eyes widened before he used his strength as someone at the peak of the Mythical level to quickly burst to the side, avoiding the flame. But a majority of the Sage experts behind him were not quick enough, as they were scorched into nothingness.
The beam of flame hit the sea floor, causing it to shake and even melting into it. The sand below was formed into glass before shattering from the strength and pressure of the beam.
Orochi glared menacingly at Tryil. “Why are you avoiding me.... Didn’t you want to fight!!?” Orochi snickered. Tryil, who watched his troops die, felt even more rage, but also fear at how strong Orochi seemed to be.
Tryil felt that Orochi had indeed gotten immensely stronger. He gazed up and saw a shadow dwarfing even Orochi move over the large serpent. Tryil showed a look of delight as he called out. “Divine Protector!”
Orochi also noticed something as he turned to look behind him, though at that moment a large beam of blue light smashed against his body, causing Orochi to shoot downwards against the sea floor as sand kicked up everywhere, blocking view of him.
As the blue beam of light faded, from above, where Orochi had been, a large creature similar in shape to a whale but with large fins that seemed to be positioned like wings, as well as a long tail that stretched on for a hundred meters and a dark azure scaled body that heaved up and down with each breath the creature took was shown, as its large, draconic mouth suddenly closed and specks of blue light that lingered vanished.
This was considered the laziest dragon in all of Seleria, but also the largest and one of the strongest, the Sea Dragon Sulemani!

also volume 4 will end when chapter 126 is released, just a heads up im also planning to release 125 soon, i just want to edit over a bit and give time for people to comment here which is something i enjoy reading, but i wont keep you guys waiting to long, il change the sponsor queue when 125 is released.
