P.S my shoulder has been killing me for nearly a week now i haven't been sleeping well and my doctor has said that i should take some time off work as well as stay off any laptop/pc, that being said im thinking of taking a small 1 week break when volume 4 ends, nothing to major just enough time for me to buy a new mattress and help my shoulder heal.
------------------
Sulemani’s deepened voice echoed out with disatisfaction towards Orochi. “How dare you harm those under my protection, vile trait-” Just as the large dragon was about to finish, Orochi’s large figure shot up from the sand that had covered the view of everything around him. He was like a comet that was directed to Sulemani who, of course, gathered his own mana before roaring: “Aqua Field!” Around the dragon, a torrent of water surged like a dense bubble that seemed impenetrable.
Orochi’s roar seemed to cause the very sea to twist and turn before it smashed against the bubble, its claws ripping it apart with ease, which caused Sulemani’s large eyes to widen. Orochi continued towards the large whale dragon’s belly with its tail, though Sulemani used its large, fin-like wings to lift itself up. Although this happened, the dragon was smashed and a large gash appeared on its belly, which usually is considered a weakness for dragons in human mythos, but for Sulemani, this was its best defensive area, yet it was gashed with just a swipe of Orochi’s tail.
“You!...” Sulemani called out, but Orochi's wind affinity head began to glow. Above the ocean, in the sky, clouds gathered and a large cyclone began to form. Of course, this cyclone was not normal. It was gathering the mana in the area into itself.
Within moments, the cyclone was glowing with the hue of many mana affinities, almost like a soft rainbow where one would meet death. The dragon made the mana cyclone smash into the sea as it began to drill down towards Sulemani, who glanced up in shock.
“How did you get so powerful!?!” The dragon opened its mouth as it began to prepare a large, blue colored Terror Burst. The cyclone’s tip neared Sulemani as the water was unable to go near it due to the wind pressure, another feat of how powerful a new deity truly was.
“Terror Burst!” Sulemani roared out before firing the blue beam of destruction towards the mana cyclone. The moment it got close, the beam was twisted and torn apart before it too was absorbed into the cyclone and used to strengthen it.
Before Sulemani could escape, his large, mountain-like body was caught up in the suction of the cyclone and it was struggling to escape. Orochi, who was watching from the side, simply laughed and began to charge a flame vortex. “You dare attack your brother!! Fine then, if you are with these creatures, you can die with them!!”
Tryil dashed towards Orochi as he had been watching from the side and had been gathering mana. As he shot towards Orochi’s abdomen from underneath, he thrust the trident outward while a blue surge of mana spiraled around him. “Azure Impaler!!” This was the Sigil wielder’s strongest attack. He knew Orochi was incredibly powerful, and if he held back, it would spell doom for him.
Of course, Orochi’s ice affinity head slithered down to gaze at him and smirked. “You little bug can die now...” Orochi casually spoke before the eyes of the head began to glow a snow white and its mouth opened out before a pulse of white light shot at him, causing the water to freeze. The ice was so cold it was not  colorless and transparent, but a deep blue instead, cold enough that enough so it could form glaciers that lasted many millenniums.
Tryil was stunned, as the attack he had released had slowed down his body soon felt incredibly cold, as if he was being stabbed by pins and needles. Moments later, a large arch of ice from Orochi’s ice affinity head flew down, covering the now frozen to death Tryil down to the sea floor which had a sheet of ice around it.
“Just like that...he killed a Sigil wielder?” Azrael was truly stunned. He could only assume that Orochi had reached an unfathomable level. How could such a dragon be defeated?
Orochi gazed at the struggling Sulemani, who roared out and tried to gather a Terror Burst as it saw Tryil die. Orochi’s gaze was filled with disdain.
“I’m done playing with you...” Orochi’s middle head, which held no affinity, opened its mouth before a deep green and black sphere of mana began to form. Sulemani suddenly shot out his Terror Burst, but Orochi was already prepared. “This, is a Terror Burst!” The nine headed serpent called out before the sphere shot, causing another surge of mana spanning hundreds of kilometers to be felt.
The Terror Burst of Sulemani was dwarfed and soon dissipated under the strength of Orochi's, which engulfed its body and soon, even as the dragon roared in agony, it was blown apart and then burnt into arcane ash. He was now truly one with the sea.
The beam of condensed mana shot through the mana cyclone that struggled to remain active and even shot out of the ocean, flying up into the sky and blowing away the clouds. The attack was intense enough to reach near the exosphere of the planet before dissipating.
Orochi’s mana cyclone soon also dissipated and now all that was left was Azrael, who glanced in horror and also happiness. The dragon’s strength was enough for him to feel revenge was truly possible. “Thank you, Avrin… Truly, thank you for this chance.” He spoke to himself.
Orochi reached down towards the arch of ice that had Tryil frozen in it, and with a swipe of its large claw, caused it to shatter into pieces along with Tryil. Of course, the Sigil weapon Leviathes was unharmed. Orochi picked it up with its claw, making the weapon look like a toothpick, and placed it into one of its mouths, devouring it and snickering. “This one should take one-hundred years to properly break down, though another boost in strength will be good.”
Orochi then glanced around in the darkened sea, stained with debris, sand and blood, before roaring out. “Tialoc, you scoundrel, so much for your sea tribe!!! HA HA HA!” Orochi clearly felt that taunting the god who couldn’t intervene was a joy only reserved for it. How could it know that Tialoc was indeed watching with a sad and angry expression. Had it not been for Septim and the others warning him, he would have rushed down to butcher the nine headed monster.
Orochi’s large wings began to beat before it shot up in a twisting motion, breaking the surface of the ocean like an awakened doomsday. It spread its wings and emitted a pulse of mana which pressed down against the water, pushing it greatly, before pressing up against the clouds, also causing them to disperse.
“Fresh air! Being locked away for so long, how can I not enjoy this! Now then.” Orochi turned to glance in several directions as a thin sheet of mana spread from its mind and engulfed the planet. This was the mana equivalent of Divine Sense. Of course, only new deities and higher beings could use such a thing.
The downside was, unlike Divine/Dark Sense, which was wielded by Avrin, only Avrin and potential Spectrals would be able to use their sense to their advantage. Azrael floated up quietly beside it, not daring to utter a word, and was ignored by Orochi. Orochi spoke out as it looked over in certain direction. “Perfect.... All the bugs are gathering in one spot, most likely thinking of how to deal with me… Good! It saves me the trouble of searching.”
Azrael, hearing Orochi’s words, was stunned. With Void, he was only capable of simple searches, yet Orochi somehow was able to tell that at such a distance. These bugs he assumed were the Sigil wielders were all located there. “-Is this new level truly such a benefit?-” Azrael contemplated.
He didn’t doubt this, as only the gods such as Zephiron were able to sense so easily. But here, Orochi was doing the same. “-Can he have achieved the realm of the gods?-” Azrael felt things were twisted, unsure if he was right or wrong. He just wanted revenge and, despite saying he wanted the world to burn as a result, he wasn’t so sure any more.
“It’s time to fulfill my part of the deal. Let’s go visit the central continent.” Orochi laughed before its body surged forward like a flying fortress. Its speed began to pick up before its wing beats caused mini tornados. Azrael, of course, had to use the full capability of his mana just to keep up with it. Orochi’s heads all gave a crazed look as the dragon flew towards the central continent. On this day, Seleria would be turned upside down.
Meanwhile, within the Northern continent, Avrin was within his innerworkings. His main focus was on assisting all the particles progress as best as he can under a perfect state. “-Incredible.. In this state, as long as I focus my attention solely on improving the Type 9 particles, the process and learning curve is cemented into my very being. This benefit truly is incredible in speeding up everything. I don’t know how long it’s been, but my C.Particles are already at 60% completion, while these normal Type 9 particles are at 20% completion-”
Avrin’s body was like a universe shaped into a humanoid, with the small specs of light being particles that made up his body holding it together and balancing it. The particles would all flicker intensely, and one could say the C.Particles were the stars that held the Type 9 particles in a steady condition, like an orbit, while connecting them all to each other.
“-The downside of this is I’m incredibly weakened. I do not doubt even an Intermediate level individual could easily kill me. Thankfully, I do not have any enemies that know where I am. Once I reach the Dark stage, I wonder if my strength will be enough to allow me to leave this planet and find one where me and my people can strengthen ourselves without issue. That would be much more beneficial than here-”
Avrin was unaware of the events transpiring in the outside world. This included that all the current living Sigil wielders other than Azrael and the deceased Tryil were currently within the underground chambers of Altea.
Orochi was in no rush. Word had already began to spread of a rampaging dragon. Orochi would find small islands and wreak havoc on any living thing it found. Of course, Azrael dared not speak in urging the dragon. He knew how powerful it was, and that if he angered it, it may turn on him.
Though the news, thanks to magic, had already reached the capital. These started off as rumors that were heavily moderated and kept at bay with the help of King Leo Zircus.
Seated around a large square table were five people. These were Abbadon, King Leo, Chieftain Giron, a humanoid covered in feathers with a large, vulture looking head, its beak extended and wearing a robe that shined with a powerful grey glow, this was the leader of the Avian race, Matriarch Skrawl, possessor of an unknown Sigil weapon that no one had information on.
Stolen from its original source, this story is not meant to be on Amazon; report any sightings.
Giron frowned as he glanced at Skrawl and then spoke with a look of disgust. “Why is it this thing is here again, aren’t you Avians neutral?” Skrawl glanced at Giron and her beak opened up. She squawked. The squawk itself caused the room to shake, as if it were imbued with mana. She then replied. “Thing? You fur covered bastard, you have guts indeed. Speak with respect, or I will have to cut you open and hang them over my city gates!”
Skrawl was violent and arrogant, even more than Giron, whose veins were pressing against his forehead, mana surging out of his body. This caused Skrawl to quickly stand up and emit her own surge of mana. The two were clearly about to go at it and battle to the death.
“Watch me cleave you in half, winged wretch..” Giron spoke, but before the two of them retrieved their Sigil weapons, Abbadon roared: “Enough!” His own mana surged, engulfing the two. With Abbadon being an angel, as well as the only one with a Sigil enhancement, he was stronger than the two. He was at the Mythical level when going all out with his Sigil weapon, stronger than even Sulemani.
“Have you both no idea the trouble we are in! Not long ago, Tryil’s insignia shattered, meaning he is already dead... and now we are all in the same boat. I have no idea if Fafnir is going to assist us, as I have recieved no reply, but for us right here and now we are the only ones present who are willing to fight Orochi!” One could see that beads of sweat were rolling down Abbadon’s foehead, his hands even shaking slightly. If even he feared Orochi, how could the others not.
“I agree with Abbadon.“ The soft, sweet voice belonged to Myra, one of the leaders of the Sylph race, who was holding a small sphere that emitted a glow of light that surged through her hands. This was a special device created by the humans and the angels that allowed one to interface with similar devices spread out across all important human outposts. It allowed one to transmit information of urgency. The cost of this device was expensive so it was used only for urgent matters, such as the rampage of Orochi.
“Judging by the direction, he is already heading here. It will take him several hours if he keeps up his current pace, but he is only being stalled by destroying anything he comes across. I suggest we evacuate the port city of Letunia immediately, otherwise this will no doubt add onto the hundreds of thousands already dead if we are to confirm that Tryil’s city has fallen.”
It was at this point that the one armed King Leo, whose face was pale with anger, already with resentment towards Avrin, spoke out. “I refuse.... If word gets out that Orochi is headed here, do you know the consequences and the cost such fear would have on my economy?”
Myra frowned and gazed at Leo before speaking in anger. “You truly are crazy. You’re willing to let that dragon come and destroy a city and kill thousands? The result will still be people fleeing in fear and they will blame you, their so called king, for not warning them beforehand. Not only are you looking at an economical downfall, but a potential rebellion!”
Hearing Myra lecture him, Leo clenched his teeth. “You....” He stood up, his remaining fist still clenched. The feeling only fueled his anger, as he was not able to have his arm reattached. The mana that lingered around was somehow eaten away, although the corruption of whatever remained on his arm didn’t spread and grew weaker. If mana was used to reattach the arm, then the strange corruption would devour the mana and strengthen again. He could only wait until it was completely gone.
“Don’t you tell me about the situation. Who would dare go against me? And it isn’t that I do not care about the lives of my people, but a plan must be made beforehand! Where will these people hide? Have you considered that? If I was to evacuate several cities, then I would have millions of refugees to deal with. Do you not think Orochi may consider this an easy target?”
Myra’s cheeks puffed up as she glared at Leo. They both had reasonable points, but none were able to get one up over the other. Abbadon finally decided to speak, as tensions on all sides were high. “All of you are unreasonable… There is no doubt. If we work together, defeating Orochi will be a simple task. Our issue is we have no trust or experience in fighting dragons.... The reason Creator Septim had given us Sigil weapons is to save ourselves from situations like this,”
Hearing Abbadon speak, Giron was about to reply, but the doors towards the darkened room suddenly opened. Standing there was a figure that made Myra smile with relief. “Syrana!” Myra’s eyes were reddened and tears welled up. Syrana glanced over at Myra and smiled warmly. She then glanced around and cleared her throat. “I came as soon as I heard. It looks like we are all nearly here? I don’t see Tryil or Driada anywhere?”
Syrana casually walked over to an empty seat beside Myra. Abbadon replied softly to her. “You haven’t heard, have you? Going by what Myra said in your search for someone, I do not blame you, as this information is being kept secret, but Driada has gone missing. No doubt she is working with Azrael.”
Syrana, taking her seat, gave a soft breath and a look of seriousness. “Well that is one down, but Tryil should be here. Wasn’t it his races duty to oversee Orochi’s location or something like that?” Clearly she was unaware of the gravity of the situation. Giron leaned back and gave a relaxed look as he spoke. “That guy is dead from what Abbadon told us.”
Hearing Giron’s words, Syrana gave a serious look of shock. Her heart beat faster and she seemed to be lost in thought. “Regardless if he is dead or not, if we can convince a few dragons to assist us, then what could Orochi possibly do?” This was Leo, who stood up and walked over towards a nearby table with an exquisite set of liquors within crystal bottles. No doubt each one of these were priceless. Of course, since he was one handed, it was somewhat time consuming for him to pour himself a drink.
Syrana glanced over at Leo and smirked a little. “Who could have cut off the arm of the great King Leo Zircus? Was it you, Giron?” She turned to look at Giron, who simply laughed and glared at Leo. “If it was me, I would go for the head, not the arm.”
Hearing this, Leo clenched his teeth and the bottle he clutched was squeezed and shattered in his hand. “Shut your mouths.... As for who did this....once I find that long silver haired bastard I’m going to rip him to pieces.... I want my Spatial Ring back.”
These words immediately caused Myra and Syrana to wince in curiosity, but it was Giron who spoke. “You think you had it tough? That bastard almost killed me with that scythe of his… He even planted some strange black energy in me… If I didn’t lead him to a dragon, no doubt I would have died.” Hearing the word black energy, it was another thought for Syrana and Myra.
Abbadon frowned a little before speaking, “We can assume that he is working with Azrael, but I’m more so interested in why he wanted your Skymetal. What use could he possibly have for an unmeltable ore?” Abbadon was inwardly jealous as he himself wanted the ore to study a little, though Syrana quickly spoke out. “Long silver hair, black energy and Skymetal?... This person you are speaking about, did he also have strange blue eyes and a black robe?”
Abbadon and Leo quickly glanced at Syrana. “You know who that is?!” Abbadon called out in surprise, but before she could reply, a large surge of mana pulsed out across the entire central continent from the eastern side.
All of the Sigil wielders present quickly forgot about Avrin, as they were shocked by how powerful this felt. Abbadon clenched his teeth and looked over to Myra, who was focusing on gathering the intel from every outpost spread across the direction Orochi was flying through. Abbadon knew Myra was the best out of them all at processing information, which was why she was busy waiting for incoming messages.
But as Abbadon glanced over at Myra, he saw she was shaking nervously before she uttered out a sentence. “Letu...Letunia...it’s been destroyed… Orochi is heading to Altea as we speak… He will be here within minutes!” Abbadon’s teeth clenched. “You said it was several hours before he could arr-” Abbadon’s words were cut short as a loud rumbling shook the city.
Several hundred meters above, in the sky, the air seemed to distort before mana began to clump up together and form a large white rune that spun at a 60 degree angle before expanding out. The center of the rune suddenly collapsed in on itself to reveal a blue ripple of space. From within the space an enormous figure suddenly shot out from within before it hovered above Altea, this was none other than Orochi, who was now glancing down casually at the city.
Of course, following behind Orochi was Azrael, who had a nervous look. “-A teleportation gate without the need of constructing a rune array...incredible… Just how powerful is this monster?-” Oblivious to Azrael’s thoughts, Orochi glanced down to see all the people who were pointing up at it with terror and fear, knowing what a dragon looked like in an instant. “I’m done warming up, you cowards can all come out to meet your fates!” Orochi’s words resounded with a large tremor as it pressed down upon the city.
He got no reply. His flame affinity head smirked. “Very well then, if what I have done wasn’t enough to get you out, then let me give you all another push!” The head’s mouth opened before a sphere of flame began to gather. It was about to fire off the vortex, before a thin bolt of green light smashed into it and caused it to explode in the creature's mouth, causing it to shudder slightly.
“You....” This was the first time Orochi had been hurt. Although it was a weakened sphere, it was directly in its mouth. The head was injured, but not overwhelmingly. Glancing down, Orochi spotted Syrana, who was frowning while aiming her Sigil weapon towards Orochi. “You better evacuate this place...” Syrana spoke towards Leo, who was nervously glancing up with Caliburn wielded in his remaining hand.
“There won’t be time… Everyone is already panicking..” He spoke with regret in his voice. He could see the streets were filled with people already fleeing. The guards stationed around the city were doing their best to lead everyone out, but there were some who abandoned everything and left.
“Tsh… Go help them, we will try and stall for time.” Syrana spoke before she roared: “Surging Thorns!” The warbow Eclipse began to glow with a green light before an arrow of nature affinity mana formed with glowing thorns seemingly spiraling around it. From there, Syrana began to fire off one after another towards Orochi, who simply glanced down at her and the others with disgust.
The arrows all smashed against Orochi, causing small scratches and marks to appear, though the primary effect were the thorns that sprung out and began to encircle Orochi in an attempt to bind him.
Giron then revealed himself as he lunged up and roared out with laughter. “I’ve never killed a dragon before, you will be my first!! Taste my Dragon Slayer!” With the greataxe Sigil weapon Ursa in hand, it built up an energy that was released the moment he slashed towards Orochi. The wave of sharp and violent energy shot towards it, who frowned with disdain.
Though at the same time, the others also began to attack. Leo had no choice but to rush off to assist his people. Despite being arrogant, he knew with his current state he wouldn't be of much help. He truly also didn’t want any more humans to perish. If he was to reveal himself, some order would be returned.
Abbadon and Skrawl had yet to reveal themselves, but Myra had already finished an incantation. “Surging Wrath!” The nature affinity thorns that had surrounded Orochi, who was still floating in the air, suddenly thickened and expanded rapidly. In a near instant, they had completely engulfed him in a spherical thorn prison.

Chapter 125 here, i went over it a little and checked to see if i needed to space anything or reword sentences i felt were a little cheesy/dumb. i hope you all enjoy this chapter, next release will be this wednesday, hopefully my shoulder will be fine so i wont need to take a break ~_~
thanks again to all my readers for supporting spectral regalia, right now the biggest help so far is for not only my sponsors but for people sharing this story to others, im thankful for those who put this story on wattpad and other sites because it brings new people, im not a greedy author and i enjoy seeing new people pm me saying a friend recommended it to them, so this Wednesday im going to spoil you guys a bit more, im planning a an illustration poll to ask you all what 3 charecters/objects you want drawn next. ------------
This was another reason Syrana and Myra couldn’t be underestimated. Because their Sigil weapons come from one source, their abilities complement each other’s, meaning they work perfectly together.
A section of the thorns around Orochi weakened and withered under Myra’s command. This was because the section was the direction the Dragon Slayer slash collided against. She did this so the attack would stay at full power. A deep, disgruntled voice echoed from within the sphere as the wave of energy collided against Orochi from within. “Bugs.....is this all you have?!” 
Orochi’s body began to glow a deep, poison-like green before it pulsed out. The pulse of energy not only broke the vines, but it also dispersed Giron’s attack.
The pulse smashed down against the three Sigil wielders, blowing them back somewhat and even smashing the tops of some buildings before it dispersed. Orochi was soon revealed with a few scratches and marks. His right shoulder had a small gash from Giron’s attack. It seemed he was testing himself against the attack Giron had used.
Above Seleria, within the palace the gods use as their home, not only Septim and Zephiron, but the other gods Nefria, Ishana, Lenaya, Gravuna, Tialoc and Mallauku, each with the appearance nearly identical to their respective created races, other than Gravuna, who seemed much more harpy and human-like than the ugly look of her Avian race. Of course, their appearances were not the only requisite parts about them. They wore clothing that radiated power, but this power was not at all as much as the aura of mana that seeped out from them.
They were all gazing down at a pool of water that seemed to be as reflective as a mirror. The water rippled only very faintly, but the scene that played out within was Orochi’s battle with the Sigil wielders. “Hmph… That nine headed monstrosity sure is a buffoon. A new deity could have easily defeated the Sigil wielders of the races without breaking a sweat.” The brutish voice was from Mallaku, the god who had created the beast tribe. One could see he didn’t take fancy to Orochi taking his time in combat.
“You still haven’t formed an ounce of strategy over these millenias of living. This creature is obviously enjoying himself and testing how far these pests can go.” This was none other than Zephiron, who enjoyed taunting Mallaku greatly. But Mallaku, who had long, gritty red hair and a muscular body that seemed almost rock-like, stood up and clenched his fists. “Do you never know when to shut your mouth you vile cretin!” Mallaku was not fond of Zephiron.
“Brother, stop provoking him. And Mallaku, you need to calm yourself.” A sweet voice belonging to a female who wore a simple white dress adorned over her body that did well to hide her fair curves spoke out. Appearance wise, one would see she was more so just a bit above average, but the charm she radiated made up for it. This was Septim’s wife and Zephiron’s sister, as well as creator of the Celestial race, Nefria.(A.N for those of you who forgot, the Celestial race are the angels, it's an ancient name that few still remember)
“Sister, you seem to be taking this easily. After disagreeing with your husband and me over this matter, you seem quite calm.” Zephiron spoke curiously in regards to the battle. Nefria glanced over at him and closed her eyes for a moment before speaking. “In the end, we were sent to this planet to experiment and collect specimens for King Lestyn. My husband reminded me of the task, so I no longer have any qualms with your plan.”
Hearing her talk, Septim cleared his throat and then glanced over at Ishana. “How many Enigma users have we collected so far?“ Ishana wore a red cloak made from a strange material definetly not found on Seleria. She had brown hair that was shoulder length, and her most distinguishing feature would be the two strange gems embedded on each of her cheeks, one blue and one green, Her complexion was nearly jade-like, but she was a bit more appealing than Nefria in appearance.
“Over the establishment of this planet and the seeds of life King Lestyn had given us, twenty-three, the most recent being a female we discovered with the ability to see any form of mana. Of course, information in regards to how effective it would be against deities is insufficient, as she was placed in light stasis after being acquired to preserve her.
Septim’s eyebrows furrowed a little before he frowned. “We are still short of the fifty requirement. If things go well, we should be able to complete our task within one-hundred years. If not, then we will be pushed back several hundred! Gravuna, are you sure you have found all the current Enigma users?”
Septim couldn’t help but stress the time frame in regards to finding Enigma users. Gravuna, of course, who herself was an aged woman with wrinkles and a sort of chubby figure with untied grey hair, wearing a large blue robe no less in quality to Ishana’s. “Of course! The reason I was sent with you lot was because of my race’s ability! On this planet, no Engima user can hope to escape. The only troublesome one was that alchemist several hundred years back, but he to failed to elude us.
“Very well. Lenaya, the remaining seeds of life King Lestyn has given us need to be prepared just incase we need a fallout plan. We will be relying on you to clean up the mess should we need to recycle things.”
A small girl a little bigger then Myra and wearing a green dress with flowers and vines spread around it that pulsed softly glanced over at Septim with a smile. Her long, curly brown hair seemed to not be tended to, but still seemed to shine with radiance. Her emerald eyes also gave off a playful feeling. “Don’t worry Mr. Septim, I got this!” Her young, sweet voice sounded out.
“When things are handled, I want to personally kill Orochi.” The voice that spoke seemed to carry a violent air. An individual adorned in a blue jerkin with several silver-like plates that seemed more liquid like than metal looked at Septim. His eyes were red from anger. One could see he was holding a heavy grudge. This was the creator of the sea tribe, the god Tialoc. Glancing over at him, Septim sighed slightly. “Very well. When all is done, Orochi will be yours to do as you please with. Right now, though, like we discussed, none of us is to interfere.”
Suddenly, Mallaku called out in a bored tone as he scratched his inner ear. “Remind me again why we are letting this nine headed idiot kill?” Zephiron frowned a little as Mallaku spoke. He then replied in an intelligent tone. “Because, after carefully analysing the situation and where the Enigma users were located, I have all but concluded that each one was born in an area where tensions and catastrophe was high. The other is that their parents met great hardships. I’m not absolutely sure, but this is what I have discovered.”
Ishana’s eyes narrowed as she heard Zephiron speak. “Although you carefully analysed the situation, if this were the case, then Enigma users would not be so rare. The only reason King Lestyn has taken an interest in this solar system is because of a premonition he had while meditating. No doubt there are forces at work we don’t understand yet, which is why I’m still concluding that this plan of his is foolish and a waste.”
Zephiron glared at Ishana, who glared back. Septim frowned and called out. “Enough, the both of you. In the end, none of us want to remain here longer than needed. This is the only potential lead we have. We should be thankful that we have discovered so many to begin with. Thankfully, we are under King Lestyn’s protection, and none of the other major Powers know of this.”
Septim seemed adamant in Zephiron’s plan, as if he wanted to end this situation quickly and leave. While the gods talked, Orochi, who had been taking the attacks of the three Sigil wielders, finally made a move.
“Do you realise now? All you bugs can do is scratch my itches. The level I am on is unfathomable to you. Let me show you!”
Orochi’s nature affinity head suddenly turned to face Giron before its eyes began to glow a deep green. Giron, who was on the ground panting from having used a lot of mana, suddenly felt it tremble. Within moments, large vines shot up, entangling his limbs. Giron roared out as he tried to break free, but found it was of no use.
“Free me, you cursed creature!!!” Giron roared out. Orochi simply snickered before replying. “Oh don’t worry, your fate isn’t death, but something much more useful. Become sustenance for me!” The vines entangling Giron suddenly began to glow a metallic green before Giron roared out in pain. He felt the mana within his body drain out, and within moments, his body was limp, as he had blacked out.  A green and red fruit soon sprouted from the vine before Orochi’s large figure landed on the ground, causing the nearby buildings to crumble and the ground to shake.
While Myra and Syrana, who also seemed exhausted, watched with amazement and shock, Orochi reached down with his left claw and picked the small fruit before placing it into his mouth and swallowing it whole. “Such a delicacy… It will take five years to digest this, but the more I eat the more that adds up to.” Orochi chuckled before gazing at the two Sylphs who watched with caution and fear.
“Keeping you all alive to gather mana that is used to form Arcane Fruit is truly useful.” Orochi then laughed before Myra roared in anger. “You damned dragon! You even dare use forbidden magic looked down upon by the gods!!” Myra felt anger not because of what he did to Giron, but because the magic he used was one that was quite ancient and had been destroyed.
If someone had gotten ahold of it, then it would be disastrous. Even then, the amount of mana needed to form one fruit would cause catastrophes. She also knew that if Orochi used Sigil wielders then he wouldn’t need to kill thousands for this.
Orochi chuckled before reaching over and grabbing Ursa from the grasp of the weakened Giron. As he was about to place it in his mouth, a large wind surged by him before a cut appeared over his scaled fingers. He roared in pain as he looked around before gazing up to see the winged matriarch Skrawl with a small dagger that seemed to radiate wind affinity mana. The dagger’s edge was incredibly thin, and the wind that touched it seemed to howl in pain.
“”Squawk!”” The Avian sounded out before looking pleased. Orochi turned to look down and saw that Ursa was missing. He gazed around before spotting Abbadon, who glanced a little nervously at him as he wielded the greatsword Twilight in one hand and Ursa in the other.
“You....how dare you steal a meal from me...” Orochi seemed quite irritated. Abbadon raised Twilight before slashing downwards. He was no longer holding back. The wave of light was even stronger than Ursa. Abbadon's Sigil weapon was one that was complete, after all. As the wave of black light shot and cleaved across the ground towards him, Orochi roared in anger before rushing over towards it. 
Love what you're reading? Discover and support the author on the platform they originally published on.
His right claw suddenly surged with mana before he swiped at Abbadon’s attack, dispersing it with ease. This action caused the other Sigil wielders to look stunned. Abbadon frowned before he jumped in the air, his wings expanding before he began to fly away as if to buy time for the others. He also called out: “Skrawl, go for the back of his necks! Only your Metaris can cut through him easily!” He spoke, referring to the dagger Sigil weapon Skrawl wielded.
While they were engaging in combat, near the outer edge of the city, millions of people were flooding out in every direction that wasn’t toward Orochi beside King Leo, who stood watch on the walls of the city with his sister on one side and a Grandmaster on the other.
“Your Majesty....” The Grandmaster spoke as he looked behind to see the battle taking place near the center of the city. “At this rate, I am not sure if we can evacuate everyone in time. It seems our great city will crumble...” The Grandmaster spoke with a sad yet frightened look. Leo didn’t utter a word. It was only when his sister, the only human level Sage, spoke that he turned to look. “Brother. Our people are counting on us, we need you to strategize!”
Hearing her words, Leo clenched his teeth and was about to speak, but a heavy feeling engulfed him and the other two. In moments, two swords stabbed directly towards them. Leo was quick to act, as one had slipped by him and beheaded the Grandmaster, whose headless corpse collapsed, while the other was broken apart by Caliburn with a bit of effort. “Who…?” Leo spoke, but soon felt his eyes widen as a figure casually made its way from the stairway that led up to the city walls.
“How long have I waited....and it seems you’re ready for the taking....” The figure spoke before he was finally revealed in the sunlight. This was Azrael, referring to Leo who was missing an arm. Leo felt his heart skip a beat before he glanced at his sister and spoke. “Split up our people, send some to the Northern continent and some to the Southern continent.
This way we will have a better chance at survival if one side is destroyed. The other will have time to prepare and flee.” Leo’s voice was firm and carried the tone of a ruler. His sister glanced at him before looking at Azrael. “Brother....” She spoke, but couldn’t continue, as Leo’s mana surged out and he roared: “GO!” With fear creeping up on his sister, she dashed away with the strength of a Sage. Leo then turned to look at Azrael.
“Look at the misery you caused my race… Your actions have destroyed the sea tribe, and now you’re holding onto a grudge to rule the world again?” Leo spoke with a frown. Of course. Azrael held a maddened look as he spoke out. “Rule the world? Again? Are you out of your mind....YOU MURDERED MY WIFE!!!”
Azrael’s dark affinity mana surged like a torrent, engulfing Leo, who felt his body quiver. Not only was Azrael’s base strength equal to Abbadon’s, but with his full Sigil weapon and Leo’s half one, he was truly no match. “What are you talking about!?” Leo shouted. But before he could continue, Azrael’s face twisted before he spoke.
“Chaos Scorn...” His voice seemed to light up before a black sphere of light formed above them. Hundreds of dark affinity needles shot towards Leo like a fully loaded machine gun. Leo clenched his teeth before he raised Caliburn and began to block and deflect as many as he could. “-Preposterous! With Aegis, I could have easily taken this!! But each one is enough to pierce me with ease, I can’t--” He couldn’t finish his thought before a sharp pain was felt on his knee. The distraction also caused him to slouch a bit and allowed several more pains to be felt around his body.
Leo’s body trembled as he kicked back, leaving a trail of blood, but avoiding the attack. Of course, the large sphere of black light was much smaller now that it had used the attack and wasted mana. “Done already?.. I don’t know who I have to thank for putting you in such an easy to kill state...but none of that matters now.... I have waited hundreds of years for this.....but my focus will be Abbadon… You can die now.”
Azrael began an incantation. Leo, of course, clenched his teeth, knowing it would be bad if he gave Azrael time. In the end, he was in a very bad position. He rushed over towards Azrael, roaring in anger. “DIE!!” Though before Leo could get too close, the black sphere of light shot towards him before exploding. The city walls trembled and crumbled a bit and Leo was blown back with burn marks more injuries. He glanced over towards Azrael, who looked back. The difference being Azrael was no longer in incantation. Leo glanced above Azrael as he felt a large surge of mana.
“You really think Orochi...is going to let you live...?” Leo spoke softly, knowing that without Aegis he was nothing. Azrael raised his hand, causing the large patch of distorted space to ripple before black sparks began to gather around. “I don’t know....but as long as Abbadon follows you to Hell, then I have no regrets...”
Leo smirked before glancing at Azrael. Leo then surged his mana as he pointed Caliburn towards the black, distorted patch in the sky. At the same time, from the patch, a large, jagged lightning bolt shot down, causing the air to split. This was a God level spell, and one of Void’s strongest, Spatial Lightning. It used mana to weaken a small patch of space that allowed one to direct the Spatial Lightning within that tear to shoot down. Of course, he could only do this with the weakest of Spatial Lightning, as it was all he could handle.
“Lion’s Thrust!” Leo roared with the will of a warrior before he surged all his mana to Caliburn and thrusted towards the lightning bolt with all his strength. It sent a beam of orange light towards the lightning bolt. The attacks even attracted the attention of the other Sigil wielders and Orochi, who stopped for a moment to see what was going on.
The Spatial Lightning collided with Leo’s attack, struggling only for a moment, before smashing down and dispersing it. It soon engulfed Leo, who was now seen as a black silhouette inside the blinding light of the lightning. But that silhouette slowly began to disappear.
The lightning’s attack was mainly piercing strength, so when it shot against the wall it caused it tremble a bit before it soon dissipated to reveal that not only was Leo gone, but a hole that lead down into the wall and several hundred meters into the ground had been scorched and pierced as well.
With Leo not in sight, Azrael felt his heart ease up, as if half the weight had been removed. This signalled that a second Sigil wielder, the human king Leo Zircus, had been killed. Beside the hole was a dirtied sword. This was Caliburn, all that remained of Leo.
“One down....” Azrael spoke out before glaring over in the distance towards an individual that was hovering in the air and glaring back. This was Abbadon, who had a sour look. Because his attention was taken away for a moment, Orochi inwardly snickered before he spun in a 360 degree motion, his tail swinging like a whip before smashing towards Abbadon, who quickly gasped and raised both the Sigil weapons he held to block.
Though it was barely enough, as he was hit away like a comet piercing into the remaining buildings and then back outside onto the abandoned streets like a ragdoll. Moments passed before he weakly got up, covered in bloody wounds. “Not good.... He is toying with us… He is too strong...” Abbadon could clearly tell Orochi was holding back.
The ground trembled as Orochi’s large figure began to casually walk towards Abbadon. Dozens of mana arrows from Syrana’s warbow Eclipse were barraging the creature, and Skrawl, who attacked the backs of his necks. Myra even used draining magic, but all it did was scratch Orochi, no longer even damaging him. This was because Orochi’s body was now covered in a thin coat of mana. His light affinity head was glowing as he channeled this, and it allowed him to ignore the weak attacks the Sigil wielders shot at him.
“Abbadon, several hundred years ago, I stole the Sigil enhancements your angels were delivering. To think me being trapped would give me enough time to break through to the level of a God. Soon, not even this planet will be able to hold me.”
Abbadon stood up weakly as he clenched his teeth and glanced over at Orochi. “You cursed creature.... The gods will surely smite you where you stand.” He wasn’t sure what to do. He had no doubt that even though Orochi was large, he could easily catch up to him. “Smite me? Very well. MIGHTY GODS!!! I AM WAITING FOR YOU TO SMITE ME!!”
Orochi’s heads all gazed up as he and Abbadon remained quiet, even as he was continuously attacked by the other three Sigil wielders. “Hmm? It looks like your gods have abandoned you. But it’s fine. Like I did with that beast fool, you’re not going to die. You’ll become sustenance. It truly would be a shame to kill someone who can feed me for ages to come!”
Orochi’s nature affinity head suddenly began to glow before the same thorns that engulfed Giron soon engulfed Abbadon. Though at this point, Azrael also saw Abbadon was captured and landed nearby. “Abbadon...” Azrael walked over, nearing the glaring angel while wielding Leo’s Caliburn in his left hand. “Azrael...you...look at what you have done… You have cursed the world to doom!” Abbadon struggled as his eyes held anger towards Azrael.
Azrael clenched his teeth. “You brought this upon yourselves!!! You started this war the moment you killed my wife, and now you have to deal with the consequences.” Abbadon’s eyes widened before he spoke out. “You fool!!! That’s what this is about? All these years, that was that reason!!?! Killed your wife? We didn’t-”
The vines suddenly began to glow as Abbadon roared in pain. His mana was all absorbed into the vine before a fruit somewhat larger than Giron’s formed, identical in color. Orochi frowned as he plucked it. “Too much talk.” The dragon casually spoke as he swallowed the fruit whole.
Azrael, of course, didn’t pay much attention to this. He was too filled with the desire for revenge. He raised Caliburn and thrust it towards Abbadon’s chest, but before he could a white shield of light engulfed Abbadon. “Huh?...” Azrael spoke before glancing at Orochi to see it was he who had saved Abbadon.
“What do you think you’re doing!?! We had a deal!!” Azrael angrily shouted. Though Orochi simply glanced with disdain as he retrieved Twilight and Ursa from Abbadon’s unconscious body.
“Deal?... Abbadon will be facing a fate worse than death, I can assure you that. I’m keeping my part of the deal. Speaking of which, we should be even now.”
Azrael clenched his teeth as his eyes reddened with anger. “Orochi...you.... Is this how you are planning to handle things!! The deal was that he and Leo would perish. I have already killed Leo, and now Abbadon is all that remains!! How can my wife’s spirit rest if he still breathes!!”
One could see Azrael clearly held a passion in taking revenge. Orochi was no longer being attacked by the three Sigil wielders, who watched with caution, and were contemplating how to handle things.
“Your wife’s spirit? What care do I have for that crap! Because you killed Leo and freed me, which I am thankful for i will give you a choice, leave your Sigil weapon and the human’s Sigil weapon then piss off. Otherwise, you will also end up as fertilizer.”
---------------

“Orochi!! You are trying to cheat me, how can the deal be concluded when Fafnir also lives!” Azrael spoke with no more care as he was too enraged. This began to irritate Orochi. “Oh, that scrawny fool? I have already killed Sulemani, there is no need to spill any more of my brothers’ blood.”
Azrael, hearing this, felt his heart quiver in anger. He roared out as he began an incantation. Orochi simply frowned and let him do as he pleased. “Syrana...we need to flee...” Myra spoke quietly towards Syrana, who stood nearby, watching Azrael and Orochi feud. “Probably the best chance...we need to evacuate our people.... Lets g-”
Before she could finish, Orochi roared out. “Where do you think you’re going!!” But before he could act, a nearby mountain in the distance suddenly began to crumble as a rip in space above it was absorbing the rocks and stone. A rip in space above Azrael in the sky had already formed into the shape of a spear.
“Oh?? So you can do this much.” Orochi chuckled as he waited. “You are trying to cheat me!! I freed you from that hell and now you’re going back on your word! Even you cannot go unharmed from a God level spell. Continental Spear!!”
The spear that was soon completed was different from Driadas. It was more condensed and radiated a more powerful aura. Azrael lept away before willing it to smash down towards the location of Abbadon and Orochi, hoping at least to kill Abbadon in the process.
“You think a silly thing like that is at the level of a god?.... Have you all not lived long enough to know the power of a god? VERY WELL!!!” The moment Orochi shouted, his voice echoing, his mana surged monstrously as he had finally no longer decided to play around. This was the pressure a god could show. Beings that hadn’t reached his level were unable to compete in any way.
When the pressure of his mana surged out, the large Continental Spear shattered into dust, as if it were nothing, while the pressure engulfed Matriarch Skrawl, who decided to flee, as well as Syrana and Myra. The three felt their bodies churn as they coughed up blood and fell limp onto the floor, having blacked out. Azrael felt his anger rise as he grabbed a pendant and broke it. It was just in time, as the black light engulfed him, the pressure surged out, but didn’t reach him.
Around Orochi, the buildings had all been flattened to dust. Of course, he was careful to not injure the weakened Giron and Abbadon, but as his nature affinity head began to glow and form vines over the weakened remaining Sigil wielders. Orochi’s main head smirked.
“In this world, who has the strength to compete with me.... Once I burn it enough, I will take my brothers and flee… The truth of this existence will surely surprise them! Tiamat should be slumbering nearby..”
Orochi gazed around before his light affinity head began to glow heavily. The entire city of Altea was suddenly engulfed in a white light, before a large thick barrier of mana in the shape of a dome engulfed it. This was so that no one but him or the gods would have the strength to enter.
Orochi then shot up into the sky before shooting off towards the direction of the former human capital. “That fool Azrael… I’ll let him do as he pleases and find him later for that Sigil weapon.” Meanwhile, within the heavenly palace, the gods looked down with curiosity. “He finally decided to end things. About time… Pfft, Continental Spear, that little thing? Why did you add my magic to that damned thing anyway!” Mallaku spoke out in anger. He was clearly not impressed.
Septim, glancing over, was pondering a few things. “It doesn’t matter if I added it or not.. And your spell? If I remember correctly, it belongs to the Nev’Lex Empire.” Zephiron snickered as he argued with Mallaku, who again glared towards him.
“I’ll return soon.... Keep an eye on Orochi. He is only to destroy enough to cause a near catastrophe for the world. No more, no less!” Septim didn’t wait for them to reply before he vanished with only a trickle of light in the spot he had been in. He didn’t even wait for Nefria, who was about to speak of her concern towards him.
Septim looked around before raising his hand, a faint surge of light affinity mana swept out engulfing a hidden an object. The space around this invisible object began to distort before it was revealed. It was the rectangular piece of Skymetal with white veins of energy pulsing through it. Glancing at it, Septim felt his heart beat crazily.
“No doubt at first I thought this was what King Lestyn felt… I was even planning to gift it to him to retrieve resources and surge upward from the middle stage of the High Deity level to the Elder Deity level. But to think that there may have been more pieces of Skymetal. If I can convince that creature to forge weapons or armor for me, then maybe only those tyrannical beings will be able to harm me...”
One could see a look of greed shine in Septim’s eyes as he glanced over at the piece of Skymetal. He, of course, looked behind himself to look at a small ripple in the water-like mirror he had used to find Avrin at Silis’s corpse, but the picture revealed was of the mountain area where the Spectrals were currently living in, the reason being he had use for them and would definitely not let Orochi set foot around it, as it would ruin something he considered even more important than the Enigma users. That is if he confirms it and it is to be true.
Seleria, the planet of life and potential, with creatures ranging from Sylphs to Beastmen, magic and wonder, adventurers and academies filled with the young wanting to grow in strength, several  hundred years of history, good and bad, with godly decrees and bloody wars. One would think that for as long as there is peace, then war must be given to balance the natural law of things.
But what followed was no war. What followed was a massacre of species. A year and three months had gone by and Orochi had begun to rally his brethren, starting with Tiamat, the dragon who had single handedly been the reason Sigil weapons had been created. He himself has quite a temper. Although he refused Orochi at first, he was easily beaten into submission, causing the land to scar even more so.
The already ruined former human capital was now nothing but ash and rubble. Orochi then set his sights on more of his brethren. With so much time passing on, Orochi had either gathered all his brethren that accepted, or killed the ones that hadn't. He had a total of twenty dragons, including Fafnir, who feared for his life after Orochi laid waste to his dwarven home, nearly destroying the entire race.
Of course, the dragons Orochi gathered hadn’t remained still. He ordered them to go destroy as much as they can, and with a year of destruction, the one brimming Seleria was now in ash and ruin. Chaos was reigning supreme. The Sigil wielders were being used as fertiliser for Orochi’s strengthening and were of no use, and Azrael had long since fled and hidden himself.
The Eastern continent, although had fought back at first, easily crumbled under the might of a dragon. The Western continent soon followed, as thousands of demons were killed and devoured by the dragon kin. The Southern continent, where a large chunk of the human refugees from the kingdoms of the central continent fled to, were met with a doom that followed them.
Millions perishing and displaced, even the elven forest laid in ruin. Along the swamplands, a large figure was limp and covered in bloody wounds. The carcass of this creature was already rotting for several months now. The surrounding swamp and forest had been charred around it. This was the mighty dragon Lang that Avrin had tricked. Lang had refused Orochi due to loving the nature that the god Lenaya had created and even fought back, but against several of its kin, it was picked off easily and died with nearly no combat at all.
One could find the corpses of several dragons littering the lands. No longer were these creatures hidden away, but now exposed in the open, as common to see as night and day. The only difference being when one is seen then the one who sees it will surely meet their demise.
Above the Northeastern sea, an incredibly large, mountain-like fortress was halfway sunk into the ocean while smoke and fire surged out from the enormous fortress that was built above it. The earth and land around it began to crumble and the faint runes scattered and broken across it were barely glowing.
This was the Avian’s flying fortress and home for all Avian creatures. With Matriarch Skrawl no longer around, it was simply a sitting duck. It was not easy for the dragons to cause it to collapse, but with Orochi stepping in, the struggle was met with the flying landmass collapsing into the ocean while burning in flames.
The Northern continent was not free from doom either, but it had escaped a large chunk of destruction. The dragons knew that hardly any notable humanoids live here and didn't pay much attention to it. That isn’t to say that the dragons that lurked around hadn't already gone by and destroyed many of the structures. The already desolate Northern continent of Ailera had become even more barren and desolate.
During the third month after a year had passed had Orochi finally gathered all the dragons in the central continent where the ruins of Altea city were now his home. The dragons had all gone into a slumber on Orochi’s orders. Now that he had destroyed and did as much as he could, he held only two annoying regrets. One was that he couldn’t discover Azrael, who surely used a magic to conceal himself at the God level, and the second being that he needed to wait a long time to absorb the Sigil weapons and the fruit he had gained from the Sigil wielders’ mana.

Of course, within a certain mountainous area, the Spectral kin knew that the outside world was facing a catastrophe. Enough time had passed for many of them to establish and work on their Divine Sense. Erebus had even personally gone to explore to see the state of things. When he returned, he wasn’t pleased with the recent events.
Several months ago, when the dragons started to attack the Northern continent, Asura had brought the entire population of the outpost with him back to the mountain the Spectrals resided in. Erebus, of course, had not been pleased. Asura had brought up many good points though. His intelligence had already begun to sink in.
----------Flashback Four Months Ago---------
Within Erebus’s office, Erebus was currently seated with a frown as he gazed at Asura. “You haven’t explained why you brought over two-hundred people here, Asura!” Erebus rarely got irritated, but with Asura’s actions, it was hard not to.
“You may be higher ranked than me, but I am still the strongest one here! I have never asked for anything and have helped over the years, I think this is suitable. You also know that the dragons outside are destroying Seleria. These people are under my protection, and should all be converted to our kin. It will help our manpower and strengthen us.”
Erebus’s brows furrowed as he rubbed the bridge of his nose. “With this, we have to expand underneath the mountain some more. You should have prepared for this sooner. You had months before hand to ask, and we could have at least organised some things. But there have already been issues where we are looked at as strange by those you brought in. You need to handle their mindset or this is not going to work. How can they be like us when they fear us.” Erebus let out a soft sigh before glancing at Asura, who stood up.
Asura looked carefully at Erebus. “People fear many things. If we don’t explain things to them, then they will continue to fear. I will handle it just as you said.” He spoke with a firm yet beast-like tone before vanishing using his own Divine Step.
When he reappeared, he was in a large, emptied out building that was made on rush. Inside, there were children crying and loud debates and arguments as well as normal conversations. Makeshift beds had been made and elderly people were looking around as if they would meet their end soon. Asura knew that these people had seen the destruction caused by the dragons.
He had even risked bringing them here and being seen by the dragons. He had heard about Avrin’s skirmish a year ago and got the idea of concealing their presence, but this time, instead of using mana to coat the dark matter, he used dark matter to coat over the mana. It had expended a lot of his energy, but he had saved these people again.
“Mr...Mr. Asura...” A somewhat chubby man nervously approached Asura with two guards that looked around cautiously. “Oh, it’s you, Mayor.” Asura spoke casually. The mayor cleared his throat. “Please, Mr. Asura, again, just call me Reginald… As for, uhh...the situation....” Asura glanced at the mayor again to see he was in a mess, unsure what to do or tell these people. He was clearly hoping Asura could help since he was considered their savior.
Asura then looked over at the two-hundred people who were spread out amongst the hall. He could see the fear in their eyes, as well as the loss of hope. They felt they were taken by a cult of sorts, as if they had been tricked. Asura could easily hear this with his keen ears.
Asura snarled as he suddenly spoke in an angered voice. “QUIET!!!!” It caused the entire hall to go silent, and even the young babies and children who were crying to keep their mouths shut as they all looked at Asura who soon spoke.
“You’re all saying that this place is one of a cult? One of death and that I tricked you? Let me tell you something. Outside, you have seen it. Dragons are rampaging, and to our knowledge, it isn’t just Ailera, but the entirety of Seleria. I brought you here because it is safe!”
Hearing this a nervous man suddenly called out. “Safe!!? We would be safe if you led us back to the port city South of our outpost and back to the central continent. King Leo could protect us!”
Soon after that man spoke, many people began to speak out. Asura roared out again. “QUIET!” The entire hall went silent for a second time. “This is a place of utmost secrecy. That being said, We will give you supplies and send you off.
Once you overcome the wildlife that has been hiding and starving, as well as the potential dragon that can sense your mana, and even head to the port city which I have already seen in ruins, then you can go to your capital by using the already destroyed vessels, and traverse the dangerous sea to reach the central continent which, like the rest of the world, is in flames. You people don’t understand. A Sigil wielder is meant to fight one dragon! But how can your king fight against five of them, or even ten! As I said, this place is being kept secret. The reason we will let those who want to leave go is because we are 100% certain they will not even live to see the next light of day.”
Asura’s words hit these people hard and frightened some, as they all began to whisper and some even cry. Erebus and Kael were quietly watching from a hidden area, wondering how Asura would handle things. “King Erebus, do you think things will go well? I do hope Asura can manage.” Kael worryingly said as he knew a lot about Asura’s temper. Though Erebus glancing and listening understood Asura’s tactic and simply rubbed his goatee and spoke. “Watch carefully. Asura has gotten more intelligent than you realise.”
Asura suddenly raised his hand before he began to gather Nebula Mist. This caused all the people to suddenly look in awe at Asura. The Nebula Mist surged around before forming into a bowl filled with food and meat.
This caused the onlookers to quickly yell out in surprise and shock, some asking what sort of magic is this and others even calling it crazy. Of course, Asura simply smirked. “You have all seen how I have defeated your enemies, and how I can create food from thin air. The truth is, you can all become as strong as me if not stronger.
You can make food and never go hungry again, you can train hard and one day reach the goal of destroying dragons. Even now I strive for that goal, but I do not want it to be my end. You can live for as long as you want. You can heal your wounds and never watch your loved ones die. Your children can become heroes, your elderly can live their youth. You can all strive to become gods!!”
Amazement filled the hall. Many had even forgotten the dangers of outside for a moment and already began to yell out in craze. “Please give me power!” One teenager called out while an elderly man spoke as he held his wounded hip. “Heal me oh great one!!” Many people were contemplating this, but some were not convinced and still cautious.
“H...How do we know you’re not tricking us!” One person spoke out as an elderly man soon followed. “This is evil’s work! The evil god Zephiron’s work!” Asura listened to them all as some began to reconsider.
“Very well.... Let me show you. Which one of you would like to train and have this power?” Suddenly, the old man with the injured hip pushed his way through before nearing the rocky edge that Asura was standing on. Asura glanced at him and then looked towards one of the two Spectrals clad in red and black armor. The man glanced over at Asura confused before Asura ordered him over.
“Convert him...” Asura spoke casually before the knight looked over, feeling a little excitement, as converting had been forbidden for quite some time. “Very well, Grand Prince Asura.“ The armor clad man removed his gauntlet to reveal his pale yet strong looking hand before he reached over with his remaining arm and reached for the elderly man’s right hand, after which the Spectral pointed his free index finger and stabbed it into the elderly mans palm. The elderly man screamed in pain and began to try and pull back and some people even looked with worry.
The Spectral began to channel Nebula Mist and dark matter inside the elderly man’s body just as he was taught. Asura also spoke out to ease the worries of the others. “Converting is a little painful, but it is not life threatening. It works by injecting the energy we use into your body. It will strengthen your flesh, your bones, and allow you to live for as long as you do not piss anyone off enough to get killed!” He shouted with harsh words.
The elderly man bit his lips in pain as he soon felt the pain vanish as his body felt a little weird. He also felt a little tired, and he soon collapsed against the Spectral who removed his finger and gently laid the elderly man down.
“Grandfather!” A young woman rushed over as she sat beside her grandfather with tears in her eyes. She looked up at Asura and screamed out. “What have you don-” A noise interrupted her, a heavy sort of snarl. But as she looked down she could see that her grandfather was snoring as he was resting, but his body was shifting and changing as a small mist circulated around him.
“Your grandfather is safe. After conversion, one will enter a slumber that lasts for a day. When you awaken, you will be a Spectral!” Asura didn’t need to sugarcoat much. He wanted to save as many of these people as he could. He could only hope that once the old man awakens then things would go smoothly.
And indeed, after the day had passed, the old man awakened and was looking youthful. His changed happened in front of the eyes of everyone. The old man was amazed at his body, saying he felt incredible and even stronger and that he didn’t feel any negatives. This caused many people to also undergo the process. Some were even more skeptical, but the more people that had gotten converted the more there was to convince the others to try it, and with them stuck, this was the only way out.
It had taken a week of convincing and converting before everyone, including the young children and babies who their mothers were very protective of at first, had been converted. Each one was feeling better then ever. Kael had also stepped in to help as he began to lead the new Spectrals away to help them settle in and give them the correct information.
Asura felt his heart beat quickly. He didn’t think he could manage to convert them all. Even the mayor was skeptical at first. Though Asura felt at ease. Erebus walked beside Asura as he looked in the open space while Kael and the others led them away. “You did well. Actually exceeding my expectations.” Erebus spoke while laughing quietly.
“Of course! I was the first among all of us to be converted, how could I not be anything special.” He spoke, trying to inflate his ego. Erebus chuckled again before speaking. “Though it’s good you remembered to not personally convert them and to use a Knight ranked Spectral. We can’t have a big influx of pure individuals going around. The Lord Monarch wants people to work for their power.“Asura nodded as he was lost in thought. “Hmmm...”
------------Flashback End-----------
1 year and 3 months had passed since the dragons had rampaged across seleria.Within the capital of Altea, a white robed individual was currently making his way around. Of course, the dragons that were slumbering out in the open all spotted him, some even rising up as they growled in anger. “A human dares come here?” One large dragon with several horns over its face spoke out in anger.
Another with blue scales and a single eye with a large pair of ram-like horns snickered before it began to charge a weak Terror Burst. The others all felt angered as they wanted to kill this intruder first, but the human called out. “Mighty Orochi!!! I know where you can find people not of this world who can help you increase your strength with no limits!!!”
The dragons all laughed and even the one eyed dragon dissipated its terror burst as it also laughed. They all began to think that this human truly was trying to curry favor, but before they could continue to attack a large deep voice resounded out. “... Increase my strength with no limits?” Orochi’s monstrous figure and his nine heads were uncurled as he began to raise his body up to glance down at the robed individual.
The man snickered under his hood as he raised his head. Although the man seemed human like his most notable feature was not the pale skin he had, but the purple pupils reserved only for spectrals.
