other then my rambling enjoy this chapter! Authors note in regards to several pm questions i have recieved
Also enjoy here is a current list on the levels of power minus the ones i havent introduced yet.  this is the accepted ranking in all 5 univeres, some races may have special titles they grant their own powerhouses but in the end this ranking is the core one.
beginner - trained - intermediate - expert - master- grandmaster - sage- mythical- legendary - New Diety - High Deity  - Elder Diety - Ancient Deity- Supreme Deity - Primordial Entity - Cosmic Entityi made a mistake a few chapters ago in regards to legendary and mythical, in this case i wrote that abbadon going full force was at the early legendary level and syrana aswell at the early legendary level, at this point the sigil wielders are at the mythical level, so its to deep into the lore of the stort to change, thus i simply made legendary above mythical, and will go change the fact that syrana is now syrana from being at the early legendary to the early mythical, this was brought up to my attention by a loyal reader, so im quite grateful
--------------
Avrin knew that time passed on slowly in his inner workings. He thought carefully about his recent choices and how he had to leave his people again soon to train. He remembered back as a human reading a chinese light novel that had been translated to garner more attention. In this novel, the main character would meditate for awhile and return to defeat any foes or take revenge upon those who had hurt his family.
Avrin couldn't help but give an embarrassed smile. His father was a Deity of the third universe, which was formed by Qi. Avrin had no intention of being someone who followed such a path, he was himself and no more.
Avrin was certain that five months had passed, and his particles were no longer being trained separately. He was short on time and decided to train both. His C.Particles were at 65% Type 12 completion, while his normal particles were at 40% Type 12 completion. He was certain he would be able to finish in one year and have a little time to spare. That being said, he eased up and spoke soundly within his inner workings.
“Can you tell me more about these Fragments of God?” His voice echoed across his body. He suddenly felt his soul shake for an instant before he turned to look at his side, seeing the image of God, who was floating with his hands behind his back while looking around Avrin’s inner workings casually.
Many people would often think of strange ideas that they were a reincarnation of a religious figure, but right now God was within his body. This was quite a strange feeling, but he ignored it as the figure spoke. “About these fragments? Well, I can shed some light as it is part of the trade. You have to know that other than this universe, there are four more, each one having a Fragment of God that relates to it.
The first universe is made of dark matter. The fragment you possess relates to creation and destruction. The second universe contains the Body of God, which is God’s immortality. The third universe, the most fun to watch in my opinion, contains the Soul of God. That universe is made of Qi. In fact, the first three universes were born at the same time, though the third universe grew quite powerful. Your eastern tales are influenced somewhat by Deities that had wandered through many years ago.
Moving on, the fourth universe is the most mysterious out of the five. It contains the fragment relating to the mind or Imagination of God. Describing it would take too long, so I’ll move on to this universe, the fifth universe. This uses the Voice and Breath of God to make miracles, so to speak. Using spell incantations, one is able to make things happen. The Breath of God, which contains life force, is mana.
Avrin was very focused, doing well to etch this into his mind. His reason for asking is because he understood the importance of these fragments and needed to know just who may come after him if they discovered he had one. “Why wasn’t I reborn within my own universe?” This question was quite simple, but he assumed there was a reason.
God looked at Avrin and a featureless grin curved upward on his face. “If we were to compare potential and speed, if each fragment was born in their respective universes, they would progress at exponential speeds. You will come to understand this later on. You have to know I’ve set rules in place. Everything must be perfectly balanced and perfectly started. When one Inheritor dies, another will not be reborn until they are all dead.
Avrin’s expression changed slightly, remembering the scene of the boxes that God had shown him. “There must have been many people who possessed the fragment I have. I wonder how powerful they were...” Avrin could only helplessly sigh, but his eyes widened as he heard God’s laughter echo across his inner workings, causing his particle advancement to cease for a moment. God stopped laughing and looked as if he was remembering something.
“That truly did bring me back to a good memory. What a crazy man that was… Ah, back in those days humanity wasn’t even formed, but the universes were like gasoline and the inhabitants were the sparks flying right above it. Conflict was common, but the first Inheritor of God’s Heart, he almost had it all...” God shook his head before his smiled twisted into a disappointed frown and soon even that vanished as his lips disappeared.
Avrin took it as that individual being monstrously powerful and nothing more. “When I forged that white fragment of God Essence into armor, I noticed a green and orange light within my core. The orange light was in my blood when I felt anger....does...does the reason this heart tamper with my emotions have to do with cultivating those lights to use as power? Are my emotions a source of strength!?”
Avrin wanted an answer. If his heart, which had a small will of its own, intended to tamper with his emotions, he wanted to know the reason. He wanted to be certain of how to control this for his own gain and not for his doom.
“The Heart of God is  heavier than existance, containing all sorts of unimaginable feelings and emotions. These emotions are more important than you think, Avrin. They are part of your power, but whether you are able to control them or them control you, well that’s your issue.” God’s answer was quite conflicting, but at the very least it confirmed his suspicions. The emotions he felt, as long as they were strong, would change his power relating to that emotion.
He thought silently for a moment. Orange had to do with anger, burning like the sun, and green, he wasn’t certain when he formed that, but because of the color, he attributed it to some sort of positive emotion.
“Can you offer me any valuable information?” Avrin didn’t dare consider himself a genius, nor was he arrogant enough to not use an opportunity like this to improve himself. “Oh, is that your use of a favor?”
Avrin’s expression twisted a little while he carefully thought. In the end, it would help him, so he wouldn’t hold back as he most likely had more opportunities. “That it is.” The moment he finished speaking, God raised his left hand and pointed towards Avrin’s head.
In that moment, flashes of light appeared in Avrin’s mind. Many, many images of tips, clues and more information to do with the past, present and even God Essence, though it all stopped for a moment as it showed the vast emptiness of space. Avrin gazed for a moment as he looked at this emptiness, with only the stars littered about. He suddenly felt as if space trembled for a moment. He looked to his side and saw a massive leviathan-like creature that dwarfed Seleria shoot like a planet that had been flung out of orbit. Avrin quivered slightly, because he could feel this creature was even stronger than his grandfather.
As these images appeared in his mind, he came to know that this was the Primordial Entity Orphelium, one of a handful that were at the peak of this level and unable to progress further, as if they were facing a mountain they couldn’t surpass.
Avrin didn’t know what Orphelium’s intentions were, but he could see the ravenous hunger in his moon sized eyes. Avrin turned to look in the direction the creature was headed, and he suddenly felt his body zoom at a speed faster than light before it slowed down and he gazed upon a blue and green bead.
Avrin knew this as Seleria. He knew the continent layouts by heart now, as he had used his Divine Sense a few times to feel them. Avrin’s expression was calm for a moment, before his heart shuddered and a look of intense danger crept up on him. “To here?! But why?”
Avrin quickly found himself tugged away from and back to his inner workings with God by his side. Avrin was stunned. He now knew where Orphelium was headed and it made him shiver. Just how could that creature know about Seleria, and why was it headed here? Avrin was quiet with an expression of urgency, as if he needed an answer.
“This interesting creature once obtained the fifth universe’s fragment. He didn’t invoke the Cycle of Reincarnation to rebirth himself, oh no. He was happy with his current self, but he used it to ask me to give him the easiest step to becoming a Cosmic Entity, and I gave him a faint sense that relied on himself to find Seleria and find this source of power. The restriction was, he was only allowed to use the physical speed of his body to travel.”
Avrin gazed at God with a look of shock and horror. He clenched his hands and spoke. “You.... You intended for this fragment to be his? No wonder I was born within this universe. You foresaw him obtaining it and asking for a way to advance easily. Judging by that creature’s look, he intends to eat me....”
Avrin felt his heartbeat quicken as he seemed a little rushed for time. “Don’t feel so bad. He doesn’t need to eat you to become a Cosmic Entity. You have raised quite a few resources. This is also a chance for you to befriend a powerful entity. Simply give him a couple hundred of the people you converted. Its not as if you can’t convert more.”
Avrin’s expression suddenly froze. He had a strange look as a thought crossed his mind. “Resources?...” His face paled a little, because at this moment he realised something. The people he converted were never meant to be a race that would grow alongside him, they were meant for him to convert and use as puppets and strengthen before he would pluck them and convert them into dark cores to absorb for himself. He suddenly felt that the heart he had inside of him was quite ominous and menacing.
“They aren’t resources!” Avrin’s expression flickered. It was at that moment that God seemed to look a little confused, before he realised something and laughed again. This laugh simply echoed, without causing a disturbance. “Ohhh! You never knew that your converts were simply resources? Avrin, you’re quite amazing.
After I managed to find this planet, which ticked a lot of boxes, from the safety it had to the God Essence and even the reason this planet was created, which was to raise Enigma users as cattle, I figured you would pick up on that and understand your situation was a little similar. You are an interesting fellow. It seems I owe you another favor! Well done, Avrin, well done. Though you only have around seven months before that crazy thing arrives to dine. He probably will eat the planet in one gulp.”
“He wants to eat my people? Over my dead body...” Avrin smirked, then glanced at God. “Everything is making sense now. The fragments, these universes, the hierarchy of it all, God Essence and the like. I dont have the full picture yet, but I can put many pieces together while I learn.  “Seven months, huh...” Avrin began to think over something that was a little crazy.
“I wonder if he will let me convert him....” As Avrin spoke these words, God tilted his head a little. “So you can convert him into a Dark Core? I’ll tell you now, Avrin. The peak Primordial Entities of the five universes are very old. Orphelium has knowledge of God’s Heart and a little understanding on what you are capable of. There is no possibility he will let you convert him, for better or worse.”
Avrin simply sighed. He thought some more, “How can me and my people escape unharmed?” , He felt attached to these Spectrals. They had lost hope and were left to fend for themselves until they abandoned everything to try and find new life with him. There was no way he was going to let them die.
“Avrin....you know the answer to that...” As God spoke, Avrin looked at him carefully. He indeed knew how to save them. Avrin didn’t want to resort to such measures. If he perished afterwards, then regardless of what happens, they would be dead.
“If you helped him once to find me here, then I take it if I go somewhere else, you won’t assist him?” Avrin spoke in a somewhat serious tone. He wanted to be sure in regards to several matters. “The trade with Orphelium was simply to tell him the location of something he could eat, which in turn led to him hibernating for several thousand years.”
Unauthorized tale usage: if you spot this story on Amazon, report the violation.Avrin looked at God and chuckled softly. “I can’t understand your mind at all, but I assume everything is planned and happens for a reason. In regards to the answer, if I do happen to choose that route, I have two favors left. One is in regards to saving my own life, the other is the one I just earned. May I use that new favor to help bring them back safely after the matter is handled?”
God clapped his hands together as if he were delighted. “Indeed! Now you’re using your brain a bit more, Avrin! If that path is taken, then I am able to completely return them to normal for that favor.”
Avrin smiled before glancing at a few particles that had just touched upon the strength to cause a slight tremble in space. “My people...huh… It seems I’ve grown attached to this world. I intend to bring it, as well.”
God looked at Avrin with a slightly surprised expression. He then spoke in a soft manner. “I assumed you intended to do that. After all, you still have quite a few people you are attached to that you would not like to see perish. Because no doubt if you and your people escape unharmed, Orphelium would not hesitate to remove this planet from existence. But Avrin, when you’re particle types are complete, you still won’t have the power to do this. It will expend too much.
The moment God finished talking, Avrin’s consciousness vanished. His physical body suddenly opened its eyes, and he grinned softly. “I do indeed know that, but I have a plan to escape that bastard.”
Avrin’s Divine Sense expanded out before he vanished. Within the palace above Seleria, Septim was enjoying a meal by himself. As the space distorted slightly and Avrin’s body formed from ash, Septim jumped in surprise. “It’s...you, Avrin? What are you doing here so soon?”
Avrin looked at Septim. He didn’t feel any real fear towards Septim, nor Orphelium. In fact, he was grateful to Septim. His plan couldn’t be achieved if it wasn’t for him. “The deal we made. I want ownership of Seleria. You guys are not allowed to interfere in it anymore. In return, I will give you a God Essence weapon when the agreement ends.
Septim looked at Avrin, astonished at first, before the greed in his eyes surfaced. His lips curved into a smile before he quickly spoke. “Agreed!! Hahahaha, yes, yes Avrin this planet is yours. In fact, by tomorrow, you won’t even find this palace here. We will move to the nearby moon.“
Avrin felt a sense of relief. He was now free to do as he pleased with this planet. One could say he was now the god of it. The feeling he felt when knowing he had ownership of a planet was strange. “I thank you.” Avrin gave a slight bow before he Divine Stepped away, as if he were in a rush.
Septim had an overwhelmingly happy look. He rubbed his hands together and began to eat from the laid out meal in front of him. “Hah… Perfect… Things are getting better. But I wonder why he wanted this planet?... Hmm, possibly to save those he cares about?”
Avrin was standing straight in the sky. Under his feet, space trembled slightly, as if it were a surface. He knew he had to think smarter, plan ahead carefully. He couldn’t be arrogant, nor ignorant, but at the same time he also had to be, so he would feel more curious.
He looked down at Seleria with a blank expression. Beside him, a figure appeared in an instant, again with their hands behind their back. “Ownership of Seleria. You’re quite lucky this Septim had that particular piece of God Essence. You may possibly escape out of this unharmed. But remember, the universe is a big place, and when you reach the peak of the Dark Stage I will no longer support you.”
When God spoke this, he knew exactly what Avrin planned to do. This involved Avrin even using up his final, life saving favor, so God didn’t expect to see Avrin when he reached the peak of the Dark Stage, which equalled a High Deity.
“Everything happens for a reason. Three pieces of God Essence within one system, on one planet. Even now I feel as if you were carefully preparing me for what’s out there.” Avrin spoke as he looked towards God, who remained quiet. Avrin knew this was part of the deal God made with his father. In this case, Orphelium was a little dumb and didn’t make his deal with God detailed. Obtaining a Fragment of God was not easy at all. Avrin didn’t doubt that even Cosmic Entities would greedily obtain these fragments if they knew where they were. Information was kept incredibly tight on these matters, as, if it spread, catastrophe would befall the universe.
Avrin’s body quivered for a moment before a trickle of silvery white light came down from his right eye. This liquid started off as a single, small line and began to grow at a rapid pace. Before long, Avrin’s body was engulfed in this liquid and it began to change and destroy his clothing, changing and reforming it.
This had happened in ten seconds total, and as the liquid settled, the God Essence forged armor was revealed on Avrin. The feeling he felt in this armor was that he was invincible. He now knew much more in regards to this. One fragment of God Essence had power equal to an Ancient Deity, and every fragment he obtained, this power would go up a level. Only when he obtained all the fragments would it come full circle and grant that piece of equipment raw power equalling up to two Cosmic Entities’. Though Avrin knew that finding these other fragments would be very close to impossible and would take a long time.
The bleach white skeletal wings that seemed like rods protruding from his back suddenly began to surge with white and a purplish black energy, white signalling the energy of the God Essence and the other representing dark matter. These strange glowing rods suddenly shot off Avrin’s armor before swirling around him and then shooting off in all directions like flashes of light.
Avrin was using so much of his focus that beads of sweat were flowing down his forehead and cheek. He didn’t move an inch as he did this. He willed these rods to stab deep into each far point of Seleria, and a large octagon was formed.
The moment these rods found their mark, their points began to glow and in several moments, white veins shot from these rods and took root within the earth. They spread at a quick and visible pace.
Avrin felt his body weaken. With his current strength, he is able to control 70% of the power from the equipment he had. When he learned by the time he reaches the mid Void stage, he would be able to use the full power of Astaroth in its current form, as well as Limos and the armor. When they are created, the knowledge in regards to using them slowly melds into his mind over time, so figuring out their use wasn’t much of an issue.
He knew Limos was capable of absorbing any form of energy and using it as an attack or something beneficial to Avrin, though it had its limits. Its full power was as strong as an Ancient Deity. He didn’t want to fight against something on a higher realm than that using just one fragment.
This armor in particular had an interesting ability, though it required a large amount of energy consumption from him at this stage. He knew if he focused carefully, what he wanted to achieve would be done in time. He couldn’t afford to screw up or let the other gods know. It would put him in a bad position.
“Sarcanus...” God, who was beside Avrin, said. It made Avrin, who felt a little more at ease, turn towards him. “Sarcanus?” Avrin asked in confusion. God nodded with a smile. “The armor you have on. Call it Sarcanus.” Avrin’s eyes narrowed a little. Why did God decide on a name for his armor? Though before he could ask, God spoke. “When you find out what Sarcanus is, you will understand why I want you to name it as so.” With that said, God vanished, leaving Avrin a little stunned.
“Sarcanus, huh? That’s fine. I couldn’t think of a name for it anyway.” Avrin used his Divine Step again before landing softly on the summit of a snowy mountain. Though the weather did nothing to him, he was now focusing on managing the rods that were imbedded within Seleria.
Avrin knew the gods of Seleria wouldn’t be able to find him so easily, and because this was his planet due to Septim’s deal, he understood they couldn’t care less what Avrin did as long as he kept his end of the bargain.
A soft, excited screech sounded out as Avrin’s palms extended forward, with Limos forming between. Though when Limos appeared, Sarcanus, which was armor on his body, began to stir, as if it didn’t like being around Limos.
Avrin willed it to settle down. “--You’re now a generator....for the next seven months--” Avrin thought with a calm tone. Limos shivered slightly, as if it understood a little of what a generator meant and was displeased. But it didn’t dare refuse. It began to absorb the mana within the air at a rapid pace in a large area, and from there it would convert it into dark matter to store.
Avrin willed Sarcanus off his body and to form around Limos. It seemed to hesitate for a moment, but obeyed Avrin’s orders. There was no real fusion. It was as if a parasite was attached to Limos and it began to absorb the dark matter that Limos converted from mana.
Avrin formed a new set of clothing for himself. He knew he had to think of a way to deal with that issue. He looked at the two pieces of equipment. “--Sarcanus, the dark matter you absorb from Limos, use it to power the rods you sent--”
Avrin spoke using a telepathic link with these objects. He didn’t plan to stay here for seven long, boring months and feed Sarcanus. Everything was fitting in perfectly. Limos could absorb mana and convert it, and Sarcanus had an ability that could affect a planet. And Avrin intended to use it. Avrin already knew that God purposely set all these coincidental things for him to possibly use for this moment in time. It was just another show of God’s omnipotence. Though Avrin wasn’t negative towards it. In fact, he was somewhat afraid in regards to something else.
Extending his Divine Sense, he could see that Kael was leading Amias and Larissa. They were within the southern continent. Avrin knew it had been five months, most likely the three were looking for their families since things have calmed down. Avrin could also feel the Spectrals and the village they had formed on the surface. The village itself was larger than the hidden home they built within the mountain. While looking at them all he shuddered slightly.
“What a disgusting thought..... Spectrals were never meant to spread, but to be raised and bred to become sustenance for this heart? Do not think I will stoop so low. These are people who have given up everything and that are now relying on me. I still do not know as much as I would like to, but I will do my best to make sure I am not as ignorant as I am now  .” He said before sitting cross legged, entering his inner workings again.

chapters.content:
!!!!! Pr Credits To Draconis Von BloodTrap &  Dragonofsomesort  Who Constantly Help With SR chapters, Please take the time to rep them for their work :)
Evening!. So everything has been going smoothly, and i feel as if releasing this would only be fair for you guys. That being said some of you may feel the pacing is a little quick in regards to this, but i have plans to get back to the story of certain individuals as things progress past a certain point.
There isn't much i have to say really, i'm just looking forward to testing myself for when i take that step into the universe with Avrin.
Please enjoy
-------------------
“What is he doing?...He’s been at it for nearly 7 months!” glancing down into the mirror like pool of water Tialoc gave an odd expression as he glanced between Avrin and Limos which was covered by Sarcanus. Beside him Septim and Zephiron also watched curiously. “Possibly something to do with those god essence fragments he formed, just make sure to keep watching every now and then. What happens to this planet is none of our concern anymore, we will soon reap some great rewards” Septim spoke with a heavy, coarse tone that lightened the closer he got to thinking about the end results in regards to Avrin and his deal.
“Pfft...I don't think he can be trusted, his rate of progress is infuriating...” Zephiron muttered out in a near vengeful tone, though Mallaku who had just stepped into the hall had heard it and grinned as he replied, “Sounds to me that you might be jealous....hahaha if it wasn't for me and Tialoc you would have been cut in half, what a sight that would be...” Mallaku these past months had not let Zephiron go in regards to saving him, almost as if he wanted Zephiron to owe him.
“Shut your mouth....he simply snuck up on me!..” Zephiron’s expression twisted a little strangely as the thought of that moment when Avrin almost killed him still made him shiver with fear and anger.
“Enough! Watch, it seems a bug has found its way to him...”
Avrin by now was covered with snow to some degree, he hadn't budged an inch in these past few months, though the moment a snowflake touched the two god essence pieces, it would evaporate and be converted to dark matter. The entire summit of the mountain was now twisted to a small degree, the snow held a glowing purple hue signalling that so much mana had been drawn out and converted it had messed with the very makeup of the summit, to a degree that even purplish veins were forming under the point where Limos was located. These veins pulsed, emitting dark matter that would be absorbed by Sarcanus or dispersed into the surrounding snow.
Though the blizzard-like air soon grew more violent as a sharp sound of wings beating began to approach, a looming white shadow shot towards the mountain before smashing down, nearly dwarfing the summit. The creature that appeared was a large tri-horned dragon, its body was covered with white and blue scales showing this may infact be its habitat.
“Disgusting....to think that I can't sleep properly because someone dares to defile the mana in this area....” the dragon’s voice echoed out causing the summit to tremble, it was at this point that Avrin’s closed eyes slowly opened as he glanced casually at the dragon as if he had just found an ant.
The dragon looked at him then at Limos which it felt held a sort of corruptive look. It snarled at Limos before turning its attention back to Avrin. “You....you dare try to corrupt my land!...This is my territory demon!!! I will be sure to tear you to shreds!!!.”
Avrin grinned before he raised his hand and pointed his index finger towards the dragon, nebula mist softly surged out before forming into a sphere that seemed unstable, this sphere began to condense until it was no longer the size of a large bowling ball but now the size of a tennis ball. Suddenly the sphere began to quiver and the space around it trembling slightly, a ring of jet black dark matter formed around the sphere before Avrin willed it to move.
The dragon, that was carefully watching Avrin’s movements, felt that something was off. Its instincts told it to flee, and that is exactly what it did, not daring to underestimate Avrin, its wings began to beat heavily as it truly became afraid. The strange sphere with a ring of dark matter around it smashed against the chest of the dragon, the rings cutting through its flesh, embedding the sphere in the dragon's chest.
The dragon began to screech in agony as it was stopped from flying and even began to tumble down the summit causing a significantly large avalanche.
The sphere suddenly cracked and tendrils shot out from all sides as they began embedding themselves within its flesh as well as organs. As the tendrils spread, the dragon’s mana began to reform and reshape as it screeched in agony, the ring around the sphere which was used to cut a way in suddenly began to rotate at a rapid pace which caused the space to tremble even further, and soon it even seemed to form its own miniature gravitational field that was absorbing all the mana and flesh of the dragon after the veiny lines had stunned and taken control of it.
Avrin glanced casually in the distance with his divine sense, spreading it out to keep track of the progress of Sarcanus while ignoring the screeches and roars of pain that the dragon issued out. These painful roars and screeches lasted for only a minute before they died down, soon a pebble sized dark core flew up towards Avrin who extended his palm and caught the dark core, then glancing at it.
“-My conversion control is significantly better than before, it should be enough to pull this off. Avrin gave a soft glance, with his divine sense he could see the veins that spread from Sarcanus had completely spread from the lower mantle to the incredibly high temperature of the inner core, remaining completely unaffected by the intense heat.
The veins had also began to pump out excess dark matter that Sarcanus hadn’t absorbed. “It's almost time...” Avrin again spread his divine sense outward, he spotted everything, from the spectrals to Abbadon and his angels, from Syrana and Myra who were back in the south helping the humans, to Lilia and Driada who were currently visiting their father's gravestone carved from granite paying their respects.
He also spotted Kael and Amias as well as Larissa who had managed to find their families. Avrin was relieved to know that Gregson was alive, and Shimaru at the least was missing an arm most likely from a battle. He noted how Kael was currently glancing at a small makeshift estate within a city filled with humans. With Avrin’s strength and improvement it was easy for him to see that Kael was glancing from an alley and into a window, to look at his father and family.
Kael was currently covered from head to toe in simple black robes with a hood over his head, he had a strange, calm expression as he looked at the man that was his father, as well as his brother and sister.
He was within the southern port city, and the houses these nobles could get could only be so large as to fit everyone, the city itself had to house at least 60 million humans when its capacity was at most 20 million. One could tell in an instant that there would be many homeless individuals and the expense of things would be huge.
Kael looked to see his father's haggard, pale look, while his brother who appeared a little like him but more noble and prideful was arguing with his father. His sister who was somewhat beautiful wore a simple red dress as she had her hands in her lap, her shoulder length hair which was in a ponytail was as still as a rock showing she hadn't budged an inch.
Kael grinded his teeth a little as he wasn't sure what he should do, this was because he was currently listening to a conversation to do with him. “Father....please this is enough...I want to go find him myself...there is a chance he may still be alive....” Kael’s brother called Ashton spoke in an angry tone showing his dissatisfaction.
“Enough! I told you once and I'll tell you again...the situation is not as simple as you think!!....There are millions dead....and where would you even go to look!!” his father responded as he had truly neared his limits.
“It doesn't matter where I go....it's our fault that we have been so persistent in neglecting him...family is still family...I need to make things right especially in this situation.” Ashton calmed down which gave his sister Tessa time to speak.
“Father, elder brother is right, right now our family can no longer be considered noble...The king is dead and we have been drastically weakened, if we have any hope of recovering some status we need all the strength we could muster, from what you told us both years ago, Kael has grown quite strong due to his master, if this is truly the case then we need that strength..”
Sient, Kael's father, was pondering the matter, he stood up and walked over towards the table. Right now this house could be considered barely above average, they didn't have any guards of the sort as the price for this house alone was astronomical, even some nobles were homeless showing how dire humanity was.
Sient reached over towards a bottle of wine before reaching for a barely decent glass, he began to pour himself a cup before he found that the wine remaining was only enough for a quarter. He simply sighed as he felt his heart tighten with regret. “Our actions and arrogance have left us to suffer like this...everything taken away in an instant....our nobility, our home, our kingdom....the maid servant that helped raise you, Valina...” Sient truly would never forget the day when his head maid servant died due to a disease. She had given so much to his family though she and many hundreds of thousands were inflicted with on their travels, how could nobles who were pampered and always in high areas have resistance to dangerous diseases. They didn't even have enough to hire a healer to help cure her, and by the time they reached the aid of the elves Sient remembered his valina was already covered and wrapped in a shroud ready for burial.
Kael who was listening clenched his hand, his heart tightened as a tear rolled down his cheek, “Valina...please forgive me....if...if I was there sooner I could have saved you all and protected not just you but many others...”
Kael clenched his teeth as he glanced over at his family, his father truly looked as if he were on the verge of having a heart attack, though Kael truly wanted to convert his family, he knew Avrin imposed restrictions. Kael looked outside of the alley spotting many thousands of homeless lining the streets and corners, children crying and steam rising from pots that contained scraps of food and even some inedible things.
Kael glanced up and spoke softly. “Master.....these people need us....we can't let them suffer....the gods have abandoned them.....please let me help them!..” He truly hoped Avrin was listening, Kael understood how powerful Avrin’s divine sense had become but wasn't certain if it was spread or not, so the gamble was based on emotions pushing him to speak. Though Avrin was indeed listening, being able to hear conversations from not just Kael but everyone within his divine sense, he was currently stunned and shocked as this was something new to him, millions of voices resounding in his head, men, women, children, the elderly, the crying of babies, the crying of parents burying their children.
These people were in the past well off, but now their situation was even worse than the spectrals that he had converted. He was somewhat reluctant, right now was not a situation where he could save people freely, none of it wouldn't matter if Orphelium arrives and destroys everything in a heartbeat.
Avrin was quite unsure, there were 3 days before Orphelium entered this system, and it wouldn't take long for him to arrive to this planet, in his dark matter core, the green hue of light began to shine as if it had understood what Avrin was capable of, and what he needed to do. The green hue began to absorb dark matter and grow at a rapid pace, Avrin slowly opened his eyes as he felt this change.
This story is posted elsewhere by the author. Help them out by reading the authentic version.
2 days ago he had finally achieved perfection with 100% in both c.particle and normal particles in type 12, his power had again boosted, and he had spent a majority of his time improving his conversion ability, he had faith he could achieve this, but he wasn't sure if this would cause a backlash. With every second he spent thinking, a second would continue on with many hundreds or thousands dying. Could he truly abandon these people, and if he converted them wouldn't he have to live knowing they were meant to be resources, wasn’t it leaving one’s fate of death and living a potential lie of a life?
Avrin took a deep breath in as he felt that green matter around his dark core engulf around it, “So this is what hope looks like...” He clenched his teeth before his eyes began to shine, both pupils covered with a green and purple light.
Soon his divine sense had been activated to its maximum efficiency forming small specks of purple light, though it wasn't strong enough still, it had engulfed the entire planet. The green matter within his dark core began to go crazy as if it wanted to assist, the purple specks suddenly began to grow and strengthen as they were empowered by a green hue of light that empowered Avrin’s divine sense.
The gods above Seleria, who were currently within their palace now on the moon, were truly were stunned, they were gazing down in shock as they saw that a purple light with a green mist like hue had engulfed the entire planet. “W...what is he planning to do!...” Ishana had rushed over to the viewing pool after feeling something was wrong, the other gods were already glancing down in surprise.
“-This Avrin....isn't he only as strong as a new deity?...How is he able to cause a planetary scale change?!!-” Septim thought in his mind, he was truly worried that Avrin would convert the entire planet and absorb it, god knows how Septim would be able to stop him then.
Zephiron began to shiver again as he felt that Avrin had gotten stronger, and that he had already offended him by killing Azrael. “Not good...” he muttered under his breath.” The same reactions were felt across seleria.
People were gazing up, some with fear and some with hope that the gods had felt their plight. Many began to fall to their knees and pray to the gods, though never could they know that their gods had indeed abandoned them, and the one who was about to offer hope would be seen as a demon in their eyes.
Avrin felt his body become unsteady as if the particles loosened, drips of blue blood began to run down his nose lips and even his eyes, a sign showing just how much of a toll on his body this was, though if Avrin was to use the dark matter pumped into the planet by Sarcanus, then it would make things easier, he had a different plan for that mass of dark matter.
Ignoring the ramblings and shouts of fear and prayers that these people were speaking that was all clear in Avrin’s mind, he suddenly spoke using his divine sense as a conduit. “--Those that want to live, will need to sacrifice their mortality and become something else, whether you are human or not, I offer you a chance to live, and save your dying loved ones. I will only offer this once, for those that accept, extend your hands out and devour what I give you.--”
The entirety of seleria was in uproar, from all continents everyone was stunned in regards to these words, though Erebus who was within the northern continent was shivering with excitement and anticipation, the spectrals were glancing around in confusion before Erebus who was standing near the square called out. “Watch as our Lord Monarch gives hope to those who are suffering, soon we will have new brothers and sisters, we won't need to feel fear or hide!! This planet will be safe for our kin!”
Eitri held his hammer which was slumped over his shoulder, he simply snickered as he spoke quietly, “Those old bastards who chased me out, hahaha I hope some of them accept so I can boss them around, then I could die happily!”
Asura was a little indifferent, he glanced at Shandian which looked dumb as it was jumping about, Asura suddenly smacked it on the head. “Damnit sit down!...Do you think this is good?...Now I have to deal with possibly more people to steal my food!..”
Shandian though frowned and responded with annoyance. “You big bastard, when master come back I'm going to tell on you!” Asura shuddered, he knew Avrin, although he didn't show it, favoured Shandian somewhat.
Abbadon was currently seated on a stone chair, his people's homes had been ruined and they had to move and rebuild, although the process was not complete, it still brought order. Right now he knew this voice belonged to Avrin, how could he forget it at all. Abbadon glanced around seeing his people some were miserable and even looked as if they were contemplating it. He suddenly shouted out. “Do not be fooled by this demon! He is no god, infact he is an enemy to our gods. If you give in then you will be no better than that damn Orochi! Those who accept this demon’s offer I will personally kill!”
Though Abbadon and the other sigil wielders had long lost their weapons and were weakened, that wasn't to say they were not the most powerful individuals around even if the dragons were now ahead.
The eastern continent, Giron had a strange expression as he was seated with his arms crossed, “Hmm I know that voice from somewhere...” he had a haggard look, having lost his sigil weapon although he was the strongest among the beastmen his status wasnt so solid anymore should someone challenge him.
Lilia and Driada were gazing up as they were making their way down from the hill which their father was buried upon. “That voice..” Driada’s eyebrows furrowed as she spoke, Lilia had a faint smile. “Avrin!..”
Though her excitement wasn't as shared as it was within the elven forest of the southern continent, Myra was currently trying to keep the elves calm as they thought that a demon was about to corrupt the world. Syrana, who after returning had locked herself away to train and regain her calm and composed aura felt herself grumble. “Just what are you planning, though I guess it makes finding you simpler” speaking in a manner in which she still had plans to track Avrin down again once she was sure her current self was suitable for travel.
The central continent where humans were slowly returning, two robed individuals were seated in a tavern eating simple meals, the originally active tavern had gone silent the moment the divine sense had become visible for them, but now they were whispering with worry and confusion in what was going on. One of the hooded individuals raised her head to reveal her beautiful eyes that seemed as if they could cause conflicts, she lowered her makeshift mouth cover and gave a soft tone while speaking. “That voice...it has to be him, I will never forget it.” This was none other than Izanami who seemed quite excited, almost immediately she was tempted to raise her hands out if it meant she would be given a chance to see Avrin, but before she could, she felt an arm reach out and stop her, she turned to see Ayame with a cautious calm expression.
“Sister...what if it isn't him?....It could be a trap?” Ayame had matured carefully and had grown cautious, when her and Izanami had split up with Syrana, they had gotten a clue from the mayor of the port city but the dragons soon after attacked and they had to go into hiding to not be involved in the conflict. Their lives had been hardened by the fact that they had to live on edge while glancing at the sky hoping to not see a looming shadow which represented their death.
“There is that...” Izanami had also gotten cautious, she was unsure, but she clenched her hands and freed her arms from Ayame. “But it is a risk I'll take for him....to see him again...” Izanami had truly not only felt that her love for Avrin had grown, but if this was truly him doing this to help people, then her opinion of him could only rise, she raised her hands out and within moments the dark matter containing purple specks with green hues began to gather in her palm and form a small conversion core.
This attracted the attention of the other tavern goers who also one by one followed suite fueled by curiosity. This scene played out all over seleria, with people in dire need being the ones take up this offer the most.
Kael glanced around stunned by what he was seeing, he watched as the conversion cores were formed in the palms of not tens or hundreds but thousands of people who were nearing death. He quickly turned towards a direction and his eyes widened with newfound hope, he watched as his father had seemingly extended his hands out to form a conversion core, much to the surprise of his brother and sister who followed afterwards.
“Master...thank you, I truly thank you!” Kael spoke out loudly with no hint in hiding himself, he truly felt no need as if he were free and was soon to be among his people, that wasn't to say that everyone accepted the offer, some were cautious and didn't dare extend their hands out saying it was the work of a demon or a trick to steal their souls.
As joyus as this seemed to those who were feeling newfound hope, when they touched these conversion cores they received a simple phrase that entered their mind, “Devour this core, and enter a sleep in which once you wake up, you will be reborn as my kind.” Avrin was not sure how to properly word this message, but he did so as he tried to play to the beliefs of these people.
Avrin looked incredibly exhausted as his body distorted to a degree, he couldn't even absorb the dark matter which made his blood blue. He was only thankful for two facts, one was that he had focused on improving his conversion skills, the other was that these conversion cores were not directly tied to being a pureblood, he lowered the quality so that all these individuals would have blood equal to that of a spectral ranked as squire. This was the most that he could achieve right now, but it was enough to save those who needed it.
Avrin maintained his current state for a few minutes, as he wanted to make sure that people had a little time to ponder carefully, his main targets were those who wanted to be saved, and more or less he had indeed achieved it, so when he finally dispersed his divine sense, he felt as if his head had split open and truly wanted to vomit, the pain he experienced was one he hadn't felt in a long time.
“Th...that is something I don't...want to do for awhile..” He panted heavily as he struggled to stand up, he reached up to his mouth and swallowed the dark core he had formed from the dragon, he wasn't sure which sort of individuals had accepted his offer but weeds could be pulled out when he needed, It wasn't as if he was worried, not only did he have the ability of being a progenitor but he was powerful enough to put up a fight and even had a fair chance of winning against Septim.
Avrin glanced at Limos and Sarcanus, and soon he sat back down after stretching, tomorrow would be the day that he initiates his plan, he had a general idea of how long it would take, but he also wanted to be sure and prepare himself for the worst.
“Orphelium, just wait until i have enough strength to deal with you in the future, someone like you will never leave me alone after being converted. You surely will try and kill me afterwards to steal the fragment.” A cautious look appeared within Avrin’s eyes.
------------

chapters.title: Not A chapter - Important Please Read. + Small Questions answered
chapters.content:
Hello! firstly sorry that this isn't a chapter, secondly  it's that time of the year where i kindly ask my readers to update their reviews, remember though what i do love most are reviews with a bit more effort in them, please do not simply put "this fiction is the best" or "this fiction sucks" as an author this is often a bit iffy for me to read.
To my new readers, every now and then when spectral regalia has progressed i will nicely ask you all to re do your review to see how you feel about it, i want your honest feelings whether they are up votes or down votes. I usually use this to help me judge the current state of my story instead of letting those old reviews stay with a new one coming in every now and then, so please if you have time and you are readers who love or hate spectral regalia, go ahead and update your review, it means a lot to me.Questions I cant always answer my pms as well as questions posted in threads, usually i'm really busy irl, or the questions are usually so good i cant think of proper answers at that time, so i will try to answer a few of the common ones i have seen.1- (Q) When is Ethereal Sovereign being written again. (A) the next almost done, i'm just trying to find my mojo in finishing it off
2- (Q) Is ES and SR's universe connected? (A)
Spoiler
:
Its hard to explain but the stories are connected so a half yes
3- (Q) What sort of upbringing will the spectral's have, (A) i have my own system i want to put in play for their form of government i drew inspiration from Ancient Rome
This story is posted elsewhere by the author. Help them out by reading the authentic version.
4- (Q) Where is the romance? (A) you know when i first started writing i looked at the tags and said to myself "piece of cake" now i understand how wrong i was, writing isn't easy In fact its frustrating and works your mind mentally, but its worth it. I do plan for romance and i have Avrins future partner all ready thought up, what i can tell you is a few things in this spoiler tag for those who want it a surprise.
Spoiler
:
She is from the second universe, and has to do with the fragment of immortality gods body.
5- (Q)Where is the harem? (A) just like romance this is a case of me wanting to use what i know readers love, thankfully this isn't a regret because i can use this to tie in emotions and use it to improve upon Avrins character, i know to my more careful readers they do not like forced harems, and i do know to my more free readers that they love this sort of thing, so its not easy thinking of a compromise but in the end i'm going with what i feel is right as an author that loves his story.
If any of you have questions please post them here since it is an updated thread, i will do my best to answer them but please know i will not give away major spoilers, also please refrain from spoiling things for others in the comment section.

I'v decided to release 136 as  special chapter on its own. Meaning 137 will be a regular release this week.
Spoiler

"--Little did everyone know, the real reason for this release was Zephon  is afraid because of the cliffhanger. For this chapter was enough to prepare pitchforks. Who would truly wait a week more for a new chapter.--"
Please know i do not mind people sharing my story at all on different websites, or even using the artwork for their own OC story. It's when someone profits off of someones else's hard work where an issue arises. :D-----------------Avrin, after spending a day recovering his strength, noticed that millions of people had accepted his offer and were slumbering. He couldn’t control the situation they were in and could only rely on others to look after them. At this current stage, he had bigger problems. It was time for him to speed things up and engage in the second phase of his plan. This was also the perfect opportunity for him to do so.With a thought, he reclaimed both Sarcanus and Limos, which returned to storing themselves within him. “--Kael, Erebus, in a few moments I’m going to be converting everything into a single dark core. In a couple of days, a creature will be arriving from space and I won’t be its match. I have a way to avoid it and keep as many people as I can safe and this planet intact, but to do so I need you to make sure no one resists this conversion, or they will die--”Avrin didn’t sugarcoat his words. Erebus and Kael, who had received this message, felt their hearts clench. They weren’t sure what to think of what Avrin said, but in the end he was the one that gave them a new life and way to live. They didn’t dare disobey. “--Lord Monarch, I will alert our kin in the north--” Erebus replied with no more than a second of hesitation. “--Master, I’m not sure if people here will all listen. I can only hope that they do. What about the ones in the process of being converted?--”As Kael spoke, he looked around, seeing the slumbering bodies of those who had accepted Avrin’s offer. There were some who didn’t take it and had quickly left the scene, thinking it was an ill omen, and there were also others who took the time to loot, while some even had thoughts of killing people.“You traitors!!!” A man in a light grey robe with a pendant around him roared out. He had several other people by his side and they all held strange symbols. These were the worshipers of the gods of Seleria. They were true fanatics. They all held knives, swords, and even butcher cleavers.“Kill them all! Do not let any one of these heretics survive!!” The man in the center ordered. The robed fanatics charged forward and entered the street where those being converted were located, though before they could get far, a figure appeared from purple ash in front of them and gazed with a straight expression. This was Kael, who would not allow any harm to come to these people.“You want to hurt my kind?” Kael spoke disdainfully. Though his appearance shocked the fanatics for a moment, the man leading them spoke. “Do not feel fear!! He is a demon sent to protect these treacherous heretics! Kill him and you will be rewarded by our gods!!” One could see each of these fanatics had crazed looks. Kael knew arguing with them would be pointless. He smirked before a look of bloodlust covered his face.His hands tensed and he shot forward like a bullet. In but a few seconds, screams and shouts could be heard from that location, and moments later it had become dyed with blood as the fanatics had been slaughtered by Kael. He was not one to feel any mercy anymore towards those who want to do harm to his people or loved ones. He knew it would simply bring more pain if he left them be.The head fanatic, who was the only one left, quivered with fear as he raised the pendant he had and brought it up to face Kael. “D...demon… If...you dare attack me, the gods will-” Kael had augmented his index finger and slashed it towards the man. In a swift moment, the fanatic collapsed to his knees and clutched his throat as it bled like a flowing river.“Your gods?.. Well then, when you see them, tell them I said hi.” Kael turned to leave as the fanatic’s eyes quivered with fear before he fell limp onto the ground.Abbadon’s face was dark. He was currently covered in blood. Around him, several corpses were splayed on the floor. “I.....I told you...all that I would kill anyone who accepts!.... The gods...have deemed this heresy!!”A dozen bodies lay on the ground, each were angels that had raised their hands and taken the conversion cores, not even having time to devour them. They were angels who felt that the gods had abandoned them and they didn’t want to die, but in the end they hadn’t even found a place to hide before they were spotted and executed by Abbadon.“--I save you and this is how you thank me?--” Avrin’s voice echoed in Abbadon’s mind. He, of course, had heard from Myra in regards to Avrin saving him, but he didn’t think much of it. But Avrin had seen what Abbadon did.Abbadon glanced around. He saw how his fellow angels looked at him silently. Before long, he found that they had surrounded him.“L..Lord Abbadon, please calm down...” One angel spoke, and another followed suit, “There aren’t many of us and yet your slaying your own kin!’ With Abbadon losing his Sigil weapon, there were people wanting to usurp his rule.Abbadon clenched his fists as he raised his right hand and began to form a bolt of mana. “Avrin!!! This is your doing… You try to turn my people against the gods and against me!! I don't know what you’re planning, but I won’t let you get away with this!!!” Abbadon had nearly gone mad. Ever since he lost his Sigil weapon, he pleaded again and again in secret to Septim to receive a new one, but no matter what, he didn’t get an answer. Deep inside, he knew the gods abandoned them, but he didn’t want to believe it.“--Noisy buffoon!--” Avrin’s voice echoed in his mind again. The air above Abbadon suddenly began to twist and distort. A purple hue covered the sky somewhat, but it was not a significant size, only a length of twenty meters. Dark matter began to form and take shape in that part. Avrin clearly wanted to deal with Abbadon before things got too out of hand.“Avrin!!” Abbadon pointed his right hand upward before several seals appeared around his hand. These seals began to form into the sphere of light in his hand, before firing a beam of white and yellow light towards what Avrin had been doing.But in a few more moments, the purple colored portion of the sky suddenly creaked and screeched and emitted a heavy glow and then pulsed out. From the center, several layers of purple light began to swirl around like a cyclone before a purple pillar of light shot down towards Abbadon. It engulfed his attack and with barely any resistance absorbed it and continued down, surrounding Abbadon.The angels had backed away in fear and Abbadon’s eyes widened before he felt the light engulf him. He roared out in pain and his body shrunk. In a few moments, he had been converted into a dark core that rolled along the ground before resting against a loosened tile.Back at the mountain summit, Avrin frowned a little. “You are truly annoying. Stay there for awhile.” Avrin spoke soundly before his body vanished. A second later, he was past all the atmospheric layers of Seleria and was in space, looking down at the jewel-like planet.Avrin turned to look behind him. Of course, he couldn’t see Orphelium, but he could feel that in the direction he gazed a faint ripple of mana was present. Avrin raised both his hands and shut his eyes. His focus was completely on the planet.“--Those of you on Seleria, in two days, a catastrophe will wipe out this planet. Whether you despise me or are with me, if you want to live, do not resist the feeling of pressure or you will die--” Avrin didn’t want to waste too much time. He had now just warned the entire planet. Whether they choose to believe him or not was up to them.Because the people that accepted his offer were in a slumber, it wouldn’t be an issue. His voice caused a commotion to occur around the planet again. Some people were cursing his words, and others said that doom was approaching and the end was nigh.Avrin showed no real interest. This was because the people that were not in a slumber were those borderline fanatics who didn’t believe him, as well as a handful of people who needed a bit more of a nudge.Taking in a deep breath, Avrin wasn’t worried for those who didn’t want to be converted, but also didn’t want to resist. After all, they didn’t need to become a Spectral to survive this. That was reserved only for those who felt they had lost all hope after the dragons attacked.“Sarcanus,“ Avrin spoke softly, and a few moments later the rods that hadn’t returned and were embedded inside the planet began to glow a deep purple. The entire mass of dark matter that had been hidden away in the planet suddenly began to stir. A pulse of purple light shot out from the core of the planet, and soon the sky turned jet black with not even the clouds being visible.Everyone awake was feeling worry. Erebus had calmed those in the north, and they all relaxed their bodies. In several moments, the entire surface of Seleria began to glow a soft purple. The Spectrals in the north all suddenly felt their bodies feel light, then they felt tired, and in moments they turned into small dark cores that were absorbed into the planet’s surface.Avrin’s focus was completely on this. He could only hope that the gods located on the moon don’t interfere, as it would cause things to be a bit trickier. He would not have been able to do this had it not been for the dark matter he had prepared beforehand. And even then, it was putting a toll on his mind and body.Kael looked around. Around him were the bodies of others who intended to harm the slumbering soon-to-be Spectrals. He suddenly saw how the bodies of the dead were absorbed violently into the surface, and he eased his body, not resisting at all. The entire city emitted a sharp bright purple glow. Everything was soon absorbed into the planet.This scene played out across the entire planet, with creatures from the size of rabbits to the grass and trees, it was all shrinking and being converted into dark cores of all shapes and sizes and then being absorbed into the surface of light that engulfed the planet.On the eastern continent, Giron was a little reluctant, but a servant of his had screeched in pain as he felt his body be violently dragged down into the surface. He then remembered Avrin’s words, which made his face pale. He quickly relaxed his body after roaring out towards all his people to not think of resisting or they will really die. He was not one to see his own kind perish.Not too far from the city Kael was in that had been absorbed, Shimaru was relaxing. Around him were the remnants of the White Dragon clan. He was smoking a pipe with his remaining arm. He looked worse for wear, but he felt at ease. Next to him was Amias, who seemed a little worried. He held out the conversion core that he had been given before.“Grandfather...what will happen to us?...” Amias worryingly spoke. Though they were in a makeshift village with wooden houses that were roughly built, the remaining thirty members of the White Dragon clan, including the current clan leader and his wife, seemed to be better off than those in the city. This was related to their skills and survivability. “Like Avrin said, simply relax.” Shimaru’s words were quiet, but one could see he was a little conflicted. He had seen his kinsmen perish under the assault of the dragons, and it was a miracle they survived at all.“Father..” The one who spoke this was Shimaru’s son and the current clan leader. Shimaru glanced over and nodded, and the clan leader nodded back. He stood up and left the small wooden house that contained no real furniture.The clan leader, after going out in the open, knew that nod from Shimaru was confirmation of them to trust Avrin. “All of you, do not even think of resisting. If you do, you truly will perish!” Calias’ voice resounded. This made those who were sitting outside looking nervous and worried to ease up a bit.This content has been unlawfully taken from ; report any instances of this story if found elsewhere.Almost as if on queue, the energy engulfed that area as well. The sky darkened and the ground began to glow. They all felt a tinge of fear and immediately relaxed. Soon, they all felt themselves shift and turn and in moments they were absorbed into the surface.Inside the building, the wooden floor was emitting a purple glow. “G..Grandfather!” Amias called out worryingly. Shimaru simply laughed. “It’s fine. When this is over, eat that core you have there. I have a feeling your path will lead to bigger things.”When Shimaru spoke, he suddenly felt his body emit a glow before he shut his eyes, and in a flash he was absorbed into the surface energy engulfing the planet. Amias felt a little worried after seeing this, but he too relaxed and then felt himself and the conversion core enter that surface of energy.Avrin was feeling around the entire planet, as if he could pick up on every speck and detail. It was an amazingly euphoric feeling, but at the same time it made him feel sick and exhausted. It was as if at this current time the positives and the negatives of this feeling were perfectly balanced.Avrin knew that those who didn’t resist would shift into dark cores that would be stored within the dark core that would be formed from the planet. Because they didn’t resist, they would be able to be reconverted into their original forms. He understood thanks to the information God had given him in return for a favor, that the matter formed by hope was considered the matter of life and was the key to this reconversion, but it would take a larger toll on his body to do this, thus he planned to use his last favor from God to return everyone to their former state.Avrin didn’t feel any worry, though he knew he still had to confront Orphelium. That being said, Avrin also knew that there were people who continued to resist, and those people would have their bodies distorted before turning into dark cores. These people would already be dead the moment they were converted. He would have to handle this matter later on, which is something he understood.Avrin now focused his attention on the rest of the southern continent. He felt quite nostalgic while glancing at the Sylph forest. He watched as the trees shined with the purple glow of dark matter before they were absorbed.When he turned to look over the Sylph city, he felt that none of them resisted. This was most likely because of Myra’s persuasion. Although she was sketchy in regards to trusting him, she probably gave up in the end.He had watched as the entire population had shifted and were converted, though as his focus was fixed upon a certain portion he spotted the mana trace of a powerful figure looking up at him. His expression twisted a little. He knew who this figure was. It was Syrana. Myra had already been absorbed, but Syrana seemed to resist a bit.Though at that moment, she suddenly called out as she watched the jet black sky. “You said you would come back and give me an answer!! I refuse unless you promise to keep your word after all this!!”Avrin’s expression changed slightly. He looked at her and watched as she even went as far as to cause all her mana to burst out to try and fight back Avrin’s pressure, but even that was slowly being absorbed. It would only be a minute at most before she would be killed.“-This woman...-” Avrin stopped and remained quiet for a moment. He owed her an explanation, but he knew he was in the wrong. He decided to suck up his pride and agree, though he wasn’t sure why he showed such care. He assumed it to be a fix of his emotions.“--Fine. I promise, you crazed loon--” He spoke to her reluctantly. Although Syrana frowned a little after hearing Avrin’s words she suddenly gave a soft yet cheeky smile. She relaxed her body and soon, as if like a torrent of built up energy was waiting, she was converted in a near instant.Avrin quickly moved on. It had taken him a full day to convert everything, and right now Seleria was no longer a blue and green jewel, but a deep purple and black crystal. It was also no longer the size of its former self, but had shrunk down significantly until it was around the size of the central continent.“If you let him absorb that, we are doomed!” Of course, not everyone was accepting. Within the palace on Seleria’s moon that was now in a freed orbit, Zephiron was pleading with Septim to intervene and stop Avrin.“Be quiet… A deal is a deal. Besides, if he thinks of betraying us, then I’ll just inform the king of his presence and how he ruined our mission. It’s no loss for us. In fact, we may even be rewarded if we tell him he is capable of forging God Essence.”Septim didn’t seem very frustrated. Although he knew Avrin held a majority of the cards, Septim could always give this info away and make Avrin’s life a living hell with the possibility of him being hunted down.Nefria was silent as she looked at Septim’s expression. She had been married to him long enough to tell when he was taking a risk. She wasn’t sure herself in regards to the details, she was simply informed by him that this was their lucky break. Though she had faith in Septim, she still needed to be cautious. She wanted to start her own legacy. During their conception, since they had been taken in under their king’s wing, they hadn’t had time to do as they pleased. But they hoped when this task ended it would all change.“What do you think of this?” Mallaku cautiously spoke to Ishana, who kept a calm expression on her face, though her lips moved in reply. “I have to take Zephiron’s side on this. That man is dangerous... At his current strength, I don’t think any of us but Septim could take him on. He advances too quick.”Tialoc overheard this and simply laughed before speaking. “Advances too quick? Isn't it normal? After all, we live an existence where beings are born with the power to devour galaxies in only a few thousand years.Gravuna puffed her cheeks, feeling a little jealousy as she watched Avrin carefully, fueled by Tialoc’s words. “This brat isn’t anything special! We were born deities, after all. His advancement should end real soon, right?”She wasn’t the brightest of the bunch and her words seemed to dawn on nearly all of them as their faces paled. What they were thinking was that she was wrong and that Avrin didn’t seem to have an end in sight.The surface of the continental sized pearl that marked Seleria had a glossy appearance, yet seemed to also appear metallic. Avrin had found the hard part of the conversion process was over, and it was now simply using that raw energy and finish the completion by shrinking it as much as he could.7,000,000 square kilometers, down to 1,000,000 then down to 200,000. Space seemed to distort the more the energy was condensed, though the more Avrin glanced at it and saw how much energy was compacted within, he began to subconsciously salivate somewhat. His eyes twitched a little and his heart began to beat quicker. 100,000 kilometers, then 50,000, then 10,000. The energy was compacting more and more, but it didn’t seem to struggle at all. In fact, it seemed as if it was fitting in perfectly until it was significantly smaller than it should be.Avrin clenched his teeth a little as he felt God’s Heart, the dark matter core, quiver with excitement. Apparently it assumed Avrin intended to absorb this. Avrin could feel its desire. “-Don’t even dare-” He simply willed towards his heart, which reluctantly screeched before going quiet. Though this gave a bit of worry towards its nature.Five more hours had passed and the beautiful blue and green planet was finishing its conversion shrinking at a rapid pace from the size of a small house until it stopped at a final width and length resembling a basket ball. It would not shrink any more, but the color it held was remarkable. Some people would see this as a beautiful, priceless jewel. Though to Avrin, he was fighting back a hunger that welled up within himself. When he glanced at this dark core, its scent was the most delicious thing he had ever smelt in his life. Even more so because he was in space with no air. It was as if the dark core itself was trying to entice him by somehow emitting this strange scent.Giving a soft sigh, Avrin managed to calm himself down. This basket ball sized dark core contained those who trusted him and held hope towards him. At the center of the dark core, a golf ball sized green matter core was present. This was all the hope gathered from those who decided to entrust their lives with Avrin. He wouldn’t betray them.“It’s done.” His voice sounded out strangely, as if despite the void of space, he could still speak with no interference. He placed his hand onto the dark core and gave it a soft push. In a moment, it seemed to pass through a ripple of space before vanishing in a distortion. Avrin carefully stored it within his dark space.With the light of the dark core gone, Avrin suddenly realised how gloomy the atmosphere seemed. He glanced around and felt excitement well up within him. Right now he was casually standing in space without dying, and he was considered a god. A newly established god, but a god nonetheless.Avrin remained still as he carefully thought about some personal matters. Though the gods within the palace gazed at him. “What is he standing around for?” Mallaku curiously asked, feeling somewhat confused. “Your guess is as good as mine. To think a planet could be done in like that... Did he absorb it?” Tialoc replied with his own question.“-If this is part of some unique ability he has, then it makes him even more dangerous. Turning planets into energy, and one that doesn’t resemble mana... Just who is he-” The one thinking this was Ishana. She seemed to be more perceptive than Zephiron, who simply feared being killed by Avrin.“What’s done is done. Now that it’s settled and that matter is out of the way, he can keep his side of the bargain.” Septim gleefully smiled, his hands twitching a little as if he wanted to rub them together, but he wanted to maintain his dignified look, thus he didn’t.Zephiron was quiet. He looked at the pool that reflected the still Avrin. Whatever chance he felt he had in the past was now gone. If Avrin absorbed Seleria then he would possibly be stronger than Septim. If worse comes to worst, they could always activate the Return Rune that King Lestyn had given them. But it could only be used when they finished their task. Zephiron would rather the punishment from him than to die and possibly be devoured by Avrin.With several more hours passing by, their discussion suddenly came to a halt as they all felt their bodies shake with unfathomable fear. They turned to glance in a direction. Avrin himself tensed up, his eyes twitching nervously. He glanced behind him, into the depths of space. “He’s here... Damnit, so quick. There was still a day left!”In the distance, the large, leviathan-like figure of Orphelium was skimming across space. He had a near crazed look as his eyes pierced through space. His mouth opened up as he gave an elliptical roar. This roar itself caused the entire system to quiver somewhat and even shine with a greyish hue to a small degree, showing just how powerful Orphelium was.Orphelium’s large figure remained still for a moment as he looked into the distance. He spotted the moon with the gods on it, but paid no attention to them. He then looked in the direction that God had promised him his evolution could be achieved in. It was as if a marker was in his head with a large arrow pointing directly overhead of Avrin. Glancing at Avrin the veins in Orphelium’s eyes swelled to a degree as a look of excitement appeared.“I’VE FOUND YOU!!!” The words seemingly echoed across the vastness of the system. Avrin, despite having stored Seleria, knew that if he was late in converting Seleria he would have failed in protecting these people. Right now, his position could be said to be good. His life was guaranteed to be saved, but he couldn’t help but tremble in the presence of Orphelium. This was a being that had reached the door to becoming a Cosmic Entity and simply needed a key.And this key just so happened to be Avrin.-------------Avrin's Inner Workings Status

chapters.content:
