So i'v decided to release a special release for you guys, strangely im in a good mood even though with this new beta update my stories rank has gone to  70 something o.o i wont let it get me down like i'v said i'v had my reader base and regardless at this point i can only grow il leave the rankings to the others.(:( yeah yeah im a little salty about it leave me alone!)
Some more good news, the artwork should be done pretty soon i got the 3rd copies of the drafts and i'm liking how they are looking right now. i don't mind the appearance for limos and god at this stage, limos isn't completed and with each new fragment given it will change so i'm not overly worried about the reception for the picture when received by you guys.I'v found Two Prs for Ethereal sovereign and tonight i sent the Raw copy off to the shop to get fixed if you catch my drift. When its done and i'm satisfied with it not just in Pring but with changes i may make to my previous writing, i'l send it to be released. to those i havent replied to who have offered i truly apologize, o.o some interesting offers to say the least.
Some other things Gods heart/Dark Matter core/Dark heart. take your pick, or Avrins heart. Some of you may have forgotten but Dark matter is creation. I feel i haven't touched upon this aspect enough so in the next few chapters you will see me tinkering with this to progress Avrin as a character and the story.
People don't like what they don't understand or things they aren't used to, Spectral Regalia isn't a story that follows all common cliches and story lines, my main intention is to give everything more freedom and expansion. With 5 universes i don't plan to cut anything short.
I truly hope you guys like these next few chapters i'm putting 110% effort into improving myself and i like to think i'm improving at a decent pace.
If i have any hopeful authors who want to or plan to write a story that read this, i can tell you this as advice. do not flood your beggining with to much content, settle your start and slowly progress things, draft out the first few chapters and write down general plot ideas before writing/typing, it really helps. its taken me 2 years or so to realize my mistake and comparing quality now to my first volume, its the distance between heaven and earth? i believe they say.
So on an ending note, i'v added a poll in regards to an idea someone pmed me awhile ago. Please feel free to vote or not, also i hope to see more random guests register and comment about how they feel about the chapter or discuss it a bit. :)Regardless enjoy.
-------------
A look of surprise followed by excitement could be seen on Calomia’s face. She could tell at first glance Avrin wasn’t simple. Anyone who lost their legs and an arm would all but give up hope and live the life of a homeless person where every second was a struggle to live, but as she looked at Avrin, from the second they met she could see he didn’t pay too much attention to it, as if he was 100% certain that he would grow his limbs back.
She quickly moved her hands around a small satchel at her waist before pulling out a four pinky nail sized pieces of crystal that seemed to have a small, very transparent blue mist that was barely noticeable within the crystal’s center.
“These....these are me and little Ilisia’s life savings that I have gathered over the past eight years...” Calomia, holding those lucent crystals, saw that Avrin extended his hand over to her as if he wanted to take a look. “Mm...” she quietly murmured, somewhat reluctant. “I won’t take them… Look at me. It’s not as if I can run.” he joked to reassure her.
Calomia was in dire straits. Lately, life for her and Ilisia had become tougher. The villagers were more aggressive and it was becoming harder for her to get work because of the war. Despite it being beyond the borders of the city, many men had gone off to draft themselves, leaving their families to fend for themselves. This meant that women and children would need to work and do tasks, and why would the villagers pick Calomia over friends and family who could do the tasks instead of her and Ilisia, who they disliked to begin with. The choice made was quite easy in their eyes.
She composed herself and handed Avrin one of the lucent crystals, still feeling a bit nervous. She didn’t hand him any more and even carefully watched him from only a couple of steps away.
Avrin ignored her as he took the crystal and held it up in front of his eyes. “-Incredible...-” Avrin was shocked at what he was seeing. These crystals were clearly identical to something he knew too well. “-A faint trace of mist that is made from mana within the crystal. It’s as if I am gazing at the mana equivalent of a dark core… Could these...there is no way in my current state I would be able to replicate this. The only option is to profit, but the energy within these crystals is definitely pure mana-”
Avrin looked at Calomia and gave a forced smile. “Calomia, please forgive me...” Calomia blinked, her old, withered skin quivering a little in confusion, but she had an odd feeling. “Forgive you? What do you mea-” she didn’t finish, as her mouth opened in a slackjaw manner. This was because she saw Avrin open his mouth and place the lucent crystal within, swallowing it.
Her hair stood on end as her old legs trembled, her eyes seemingly wanted to cry but it was as if the tears had dried up. She could only point her boney finger towards you. “You....you!”
Avrin closed his eyes for a second and the moment the lucent crystal entered his stomach the dark matter pounced at it, causing the crystal to dissolve as if it were being burnt away by molten lava. The mana within it was cleanly converted to dark matter that was used on Avrin’s body. Avrin felt a little relief before giving an odd smile. “-More... I need more… If I can find a good source of these crystals, I should be able to kickstart my body-”
Avrin then turned to look at Calomia, who looked as if she was a ghost. Though he knew why she was looking like this. “Don’t fret. Give me some time and I’ll repay you back a million times more.”
Calomia calmed down in a near instant, because the thought of being repaid with such an amount was the perfect medicine. “Avrin, was it! You need to promise and swear by the Four Heavens that you will keep your word!”
Avrin looked at her oddly. “-Four Heavens?-” Though he disregarded this and spoke solemnly. “You have my word, under the Four Heavens, that I will repay you with one million of these lucent cryst-” he was suddenly interrupted by Calomia, who grunted and quickly spoke.
“No no no!! If you can promise me a million Haze lucent crystals, what am I going to do with all that! Where would I store them? Just promise to get me one Azure lucent crystal and this debt will be done. This way I can improve little Ilisia’s life.”
Avrin listened and then spoke as he found this a little bothersome but entertaining nonetheless. “I promise under the Four Heavens that I will repay what you have given me with an Azure Lucent Crystal.”
When Avrin spoke, Calomia seemed to ease up somewhat. She then ‘hmphed’ and slammed the point of her walking cane onto the wooden floor. She was about to speak, but Avrin had done so first. “By the way, what is an Azure lucent crystal?”
Calomia’s face paled and her eyebrows began to twitch rapidly. Several hours later, after berating Avrin in regards to making a promise for an item he didn’t know about, she explained everything to him about the types of lucent crystals and their values and who may have them, and even talked to him about profitable methods and profitable jobs. Her knowledge in this field was quite good. Avrin assumed she must have worked hard to find a way to sustain herself and Ilisia that she had no choice but to try and research many things.
After she was done, Ilisia returned with some fruit, wild vegetables some bird eggs that she definitely had a hard time obtaining. One could tell by the dirt on her face and the dirt on her white dress that she was crawling around and climbing a tree.
“You naughty child! How many times have I told you to not dirty and ruin your dress! You only have that one dress. Ah, why do you wear it so much!” Calomia shook her head as she began to look over the goods that Ilisia obtain. Ilisia pouted and frowned. “Grandma, I can wear what I want. I love this dress and I don’t like the other rough clothes we have, they look funny and are itchy!”
Avrin was sitting on a chair at an uneven table. The chair itself was made roughly and seemed as if it would break, its legs were made uneven with some being too thin and one being incredibly thick, as if it were just mashed together with random sticks.
He was using a flat, thin piece of bark to act as parchment and used ink made from a variety of flowers and common minerals. He was listing some things and drawing some diagrams.
“-Haze is one, Unclouded is one-hundred, Luminous would be one-thousand, Cored is ten-thousand, Crystalline is one-hundred-thousand, and Azure is one-million. Calomia said she knew that above Azure was Radiant, but she was unsure of the equal value. But above Radiant there were more. Very interesting. These lucent crystals are quite strange. They are almost certainly the mana equivalent of dark cores, but they seem natural compared to mine-”
Avrin was quietly thinking as he listed the values and names of the crystals mentioned so far. He found that if he was thinking too hard in his current state it would exhaust him somewhat, so he asked Calomia for this wooden bark to use as parchment and she happily agreed. He didn’t think she would be so willing, but knew he owed her an Azure lucent crystal which was most likely the reason she was a bit more friendly.
Avrin, focused, suddenly stopped as a strange looking object was placed in between him and the wooden parchment. “Hmm?” he turned to see Ilisia giving a cheeky grin and laughing. “Mister Avrin, you will like this! It’s called Bellybush Root. It’s yummy and is a little savory like meat. It’s really a rare thing to find, but I think you deserve it!”
Avrin glanced at the Bellybush Root which was somewhat similar to how ginger is shaped, except the outer skin looked more like a lemon. It had an orange color with some brown patches, but one could see it had been cleaned. It didn’t look appealing at all, but Avrin happily grabbed it and took a bite. The texture was crisp like a carrot, but as for it being savory, it was nearly non existent. Avrin turned to look at Ilisia, who had a somewhat nervous smile that seemed a little sad.
“-This is savory?-” Avrin felt bad. He had only taken one bite before giving it back to Ilisia. “Actually, you can have it. How about I treat you to a proper meal when I get better?” Ilisia was about to refuse, but she saw Avrin’s serious look and could only accept. Yet inside she was overjoyed. She loved the taste of the root. “A proper meal? You mean meat and side dishes?” she asked in a confused manner.
“Indeed. Until you feel as if you will explode.” he smiled warmly. He felt pity for her. He realised that she had very, very rarely eaten good food, including proper meat, that this bland, nearly tasteless root was considered a rare delicacy that was like meat to her. He also owed her a lot because she helped him.
“Ahh, meat and side dishes!!! You have to promise this to me, Mister Avrin!” Her eyes widened and she gave a serious expression while looking at Avrin, her little body shaking with eagerness, and she was drooling a little. “I promise. Now go help your grandmother.“ Ilisia jumped for joy. It would be a wonderful sight had it not been for her dirt covered appearance and near ruined dress. She rushed outside while eating the Bellybush Root as she went to go fetch some water.
Avrin looked at the parchment again. He had listed several things and even crossed out some. The names that were crossed out were alchemy, blacksmithing, mercenary, adventurer, fishermen, builder, and soldier. He had many reasons for doing this. These all had their ups and downs. Alchemy and blacksmithing were crossed out because they would make to much of an impact at this stage, but he decided once he gathered enough funds and a better understanding of the world he was in, he would revisit these options in the future. 
Support the author by searching for the original publication of this novel.
This was something he wanted to do, mainly with alchemy. He had a feeling that he could do something amazing with lucent crystals, but for now would put it off. Mercenary and adventurer would be something that was based on time and risk for profit. The risk part he didn’t mind. He knew that on this world it would probably be very rare to find someone who could give him a good fight, even in a weakened state.
Mercenary was something that would put him in the spotlight if he did the job. This was because he knew he would be doing good and it would draw attention from people who would want to hire him. A soldier was the same deal. He didn’t want that path, as it would build up connections he didn’t want and give him a sort of obligation.
The name that wasn’t crossed out was interesting. “-A vendor. Basically a merchant, huh. I guess it’s not so bad. I would be working on my own terms, and it would allow me the sort of connections that I would need to get information. But like a soldier, it would leave me with the risk of building unwanted connections that always pose a risk of trouble, but at the same time it is also an interesting job.
Though I shouldn’t need to worry about this, there are always many risks and advantages and nothing in the past went my way. If I do well, what’s to say I can’t build a network of information spanning a galaxy. But if things go badly, I may be permanently on the run. For now, I’ll play it safe and gain experience. I know where to start-”
Avrin used the thin, makeshift feather pen to circle around the word vendor. A smile crept onto his face. He thought of a rough set of goals. One was to establish himself on this planet, the next would be to find where Seleria was placed. But this was not a real issue for him, because he knew due to his specifics when speaking to God it would be a place no one but him would be able to visit unless someone used a fragment to trade, which was highly unlikely due to the incredible rarity those possessed. They could not even be tracked unless an Inheritor made it known.
“Boy, come eat!” Calomia’s words rang out. Avrin frowned before muttering to himself. “I would gladly do so if I had legs...” he sighed before smiling faintly.
Time passed, and Avrin had spent nearly a month under Ilisia’s and Calomia’s care. Both his legs had grown back and he had some strength, but it was nothing special.
Avrin’s body had healed in a strange manner. It stored dark matter within both stumps and in one night had regrown both his legs. The next day, when Calomia saw Avrin had regrown his legs, she nearly had a heart attack. Ilisia had taken it much better and was excited and awed, even asking if Avrin could teach her how to do that.
Though Avrin was also feeling happy because he was now out and about. He loved being able to walk on his own without having to be cared for like a baby, though he was truly grateful to both of these two. Despite having just about nothing other than a run down home with barely scraps of food, they still treated him good and took him in with no ill intentions.
Avrin, despite still missing an arm, was quite happy, even going as far as to accompany Ilisia on a foraging trip. The two of them were currently exploring the forest not too far from where she found him.
“Mister Avrin, this is great, this is great!! Look, it’s a Popper mushroom!” Ilisia nearly went wild as she pointed to a mushroom that was half the size of an average umbrella. It had several white lines but looked like an overgrown Shiitake mushroom in shape, but the color resembled a simple white mushroom.
“That’s quite big,“ Avrin said with curiosity as he looked around. Right now, he could feel the mass of dark matter within the stump of his missing arm. Once that was healed, his body would focus on healing the rest and improving the state of his dark matter heart, which seemed dormant. Avrin couldn’t even feel the energy of any of his Skymetal equipment, which left him quite cautious.
“Mister Avrin, tonight we can have mushroom stew! We have some left over vegetables, this will be a great treat.” Ilisia showed more excitement as she took out a wooden knife and began to cut some pieces off the large mushroom.
While Ilisia was tending to that, Avrin suddenly winced slightly. His nose twitched a little, and his pointed ears also twitched. Despite being weakened greatly, his body still had its sensitive traits. He could hear the faint sound of rustling and also smelt something familiar. “Blood… Should be about one-hundred meters from here.“ Avrin turned to look in the direction where the smell and sound came from. He turned to look at Ilisia and spoke.
“I’ll be back, you can return without me.” Hearing Avrin, Ilisia’s mouth opened to reply, but as she turned around to look at him, she saw he was already gone. Although Avrin was wearing his half complete black clothes, he still looked like a dark ghost, carefully making his way across the outer forrest, nearing the inner parts without making a sound. Every branch and every twig as well as anything that could be stepped on and crushed to make a sound was avoided without slowing him down in the least, as if it were natural for him to do this.
He didn’t even need to look, as his enigmatic eyes were focused towards the source of the bloody scent. The smell of this blood was obviously from a beast, yet Avrin felt strange. He didn’t feel interest, what he felt was his dark matter and particles jumping around, not with excitement but with hunger, as if they were waiting for their parent to feed them.
Avrin was careful. The closer he got, the stronger the scent became. It had gotten to the point where he found traces of thick, gooey blood and broken branches. “-A wounded beast? Perfect-”
Avrin approached an open area and cautiously hid himself behind a tree. He regulated his breath to help keep it controlled and soon turned his head around the corner to peek and see what was over there. What he saw wasn’t anything uncommon within the laws of nature, but it piqued his interest.
The corpse of a creature no larger than a deer but with crocodile-like scales and a lizard-like head was being eaten by an armless, furred creature with a large bone horn that emitted a soft blue light. The furred creature resembled a sort of fat hippo crossed with a sloth. It was not appealing, but Avrin didn’t care much. He bared his teeth. He was gazing at the corpse, the hunger that usually was constantly fed and suppressed began to rise and an aura of bloodlust surged out.
The furred creature, which was chewing mouthfulls of meat, stopped for a moment and turned around in surprise, quivering slightly. Avrin saw that it only had one eye, almost like a cyclops. As it gazed in Avrin’s direction, he knew its senses were sharp. Avrin didn’t feel the need to hide. He stepped into the open and smiled at it.
“Hey buddy. You don’t mind sharing, do you?” Avrin smiled coldly at the furred creature which cautiously looked back. As if understanding Avrin’s intention was to steal its meal, it roared almost like a small lion, with bits of meat shooting flying onto the ground.
Avrin bared his seemingly perfect set of teeth and his smile widened to show a near crazed look. “Oh, that’s fine. I’ll just eat you instead.” He dashed towards the creature. Despite being weakened, he had regained some strength. After all, he was a being that could match up to a High Deity.
The creature quickly felt something ominous and turned its horn to face Avrin. The horn began to emit static, which shot towards Avrin, who seemed as if he misjudged the creature. The lightning bolt hit his chest and he was pushed back several meters. As his feet slid across the ground, a small patch on his chest was burning and the clothing was destroyed. The creature began to roar as it charged towards Avrin with the intention to impale him with its horn. Its fury surged out and its worry was gone, replaced by anger towards this pitiful looking individual who interrupted its meal and tried to steal from it. But as it grew close, Avrin lifted his head and gave a twisted smile.
“How about an Umbral Cirrus,” he spoke softly. The stump on his arm suddenly surged with dark matter before it exploded outward towards the creature with hundreds of tendril-like appendages. The creature was stunned, but it was to late to stop, it could only continue with its attack reluctantly.
The tendrils formed from the gathered dark matter suddenly swapped from whip-like appendages to sharp spikes. Avrin simply willed them forward and the spikes smashed against the charging creature, skewering it in a near instant. It was almost too gruesome to see, as it was turned into a shish kebab. Even as it was raised up by the tendriled spikes formed from the dark matter that had gathered at Avrin’s stump of an arm, it didn’t seem to way too heavily on him.
The tendrils suddenly reverted back and began to expand and contract. At the same time, this happened the creature’s body was being covered in dark veins and it began to wither and grow smaller, as it was being converted and devoured. Avrin sighed in relief. This was not a waste of energy at all. He risked it, but it had paid off. This had sped up his recovery. To him, this creature, although not as pure as the lucent crystal, its mass of mana was enough to count for ten Haze ones.
The process of absorbing the creature took no more than a minute, and when it was done the tendrils formed under Avrin’s attack, Umbral Cirrus, returned and suddenly began to coil together near the stump. In a few seconds, they formed the shape of an arm, and a dozen seconds after that, Avrin was complete. He was no longer missing any limbs and even had a bit of energy to add to his reserve.
“Perfect.” He glanced over towards the corpse of the crocodile-like dear and began to walk towards it. He knew if it remained here for long it would attract more creatures, and he knew if he dragged its corpse while it was like this then they would follow its scent. He simply reached over with his arm and ripped off one of its meaty, scaled back legs before he turned to leave. Almost at the same time, many roars and howls of creatures getting nearer sounded out.
Back at the cottage, Ilisia was sitting at the table with a sad look. “Grandma, do you think he will come back?” Ilisia seemed to be worried and afraid. This was because she had someone else to treat as a friend other than her grandma.
“Him? He sure as hell better. He still owes me!” Calomia also had a sort of worried expression. It had been nearly an hour since Avrin left Ilisia, who returned and told Calomia about what happened. Though right after Calomia spoke, another voice sounded out. “Didn’t I promise under the four or something heavens that I’d pay you back? I said I would keep my word.” Avrin approached and opened the door that seemed as if every time it was used it would break off.
“Mister Avrin, you’re back!” Ilisia jumped up happily and approached. “What’s that?” She stopped and looked at what Avrin was holding. Calomia turned to look at what Avrin had after hearing her granddaughters words, though the moment she saw it her eyes bulged slightly and her prune-like lips were covered in saliva. “T...that’s!”
Avrin looked at her and walked over, placing the scaled leg onto the table and gave a simple reply as if he didn’t consider what he did as anything special. Even more so, he considered it bad because he wanted to bring the entire body but couldn’t due to safety issues at this moment “Hmm? Oh, this is dinner.”

A half hour later, a soft humming sound could be heard within the small, run down kitchen. Soon, a voice was heard. “It’s ready!” Calomia had a happy expression with a wide smile. Of course, because of her age, it would surely be a face that would make one who didn’t know her keep away.
“Yayaya!” Ilisia’s excited voice could be heard as she slapped the table with both her hands while seated on the chair. Her little feet were kicking in the air, as she wasn’t tall enough to touch the ground. Then again, it was an issue with the table not being well made.
Calomia came over with a cracked, old looking iron pot with a hearty looking stew filled with meat chunks, an assortment of greens and other edible food. She placed it on the table and began to give Ilisia her share.
“Avrin, you were lucky to find a half eaten body and get out unharmed. The creatures in this forest are very aggressive and won't simply let someone take their meal. Are you sure you don’t want me to give you some?” Avrin was reading a book Calomia had given him. Although the book was torn, in some places it listed creatures, herbs, and an assortment of things that could be found in the wild that held value. Calomia, being such a cheap old woman, would have to have some general knowledge and keep a book like this with her just in case one day she struck the jackpot with something that could be sold. That being said, the book itself was incomplete, but for Avrin it didn’t matter.
“-A spark brute, huh. It seems the horn is deemed valuable. Three Haze lucent crystals just for that piece of junk? It can only be considered a barely common material, then again these are prices from ten years ago-” Thinking about this, Avrin carefully summarized some things.
Because of the information God had given him in return for a favor was considered general knowledge with a few beneficial points, he was given quite a load to think on. He knew that the system of item ranking was not developed by the gods of Seleria, but was a universal standard. He also came to know that spirit stones are not a commonplace thing. This was because a Deity would have no need for one and it was considered by them as a weaklings way to tell one's own affinity.
Avrin glanced over towards the shabby table to see Calomia and Ilisia eating their meals. Although Calomia was quite old, with her teeth seemingly about to fall out, she had no problem devouring everything with barely any chewing. Ilisia was even more so surprising, as if she had never eaten before one would think she didn’t want to share by the speed at which she ate.
“Tomorrow morning I’ll be going to the village to trade some items. I may be late in returning.” Avrin would have headed out now, but by the time he would reach it, night would have fallen and his lack of money meant he couldn’t rent a room at the inn. Lower than lucent crystals was common currency, but this was a primitive method used simply for meals and the like, meaning a currency for the lowliest of the low, and even then Calomia barely had a few bent copper pieces. It made Avrin cringe somewhat at how bad her luck was. He truly felt sorry for these two.
“What?!“ Calomia stopped eating and looked at Avrin with her eyebrow raised. “Why are you going to that place? And what do you have to trade?!” Calomia, after recounting Avrin’s words, grew curious.
“Nothing yet, which is why tonight I’ll be heading out to gather some raw materials to sell.” Avrin didn’t seem stressed by this fact. He came to know that the creature he butchered was a peak Beginner level creature using his Divine Sense, and going by the book he had read and Calomia’s knowledge, the strongest creature in the outer forest that one could stumble upon would be at the level of a trained person. Avrin had nothing to fear. In fact, he was quite eager to bring himself up from his current circumstances.
“Hmm! How do I know you won’t skip out on our deal, ay boy?!” Calomia raised the wooden spoon and pointed it at him. Avrin looked at her and smiled. “You don’t, but I swore upon the heavens or whatever you made me say. That should be enough. In any case, I don’t see any downside to taking both of you with me when I head to the village. You told me there is a designated market for vendors to set up shop, if I choose to wander off and explore I will need someone to keep an eye out for me.”
Calomia’s face paled somewhat as she grunted, which almost seemed like a low pitched death throw. “Nonsense, not me or little Ilisia will be going there tomorrow. Besides, if they see you with us, it won’t be good for your image....”
Hearing this, Avrin realized that Calomia was trying to spare him some ridicule from the villagers, who may see him as an easy target. He then glanced at Ilisia, who had stopped eating and was forcing a smile as she spoke. “Mister Avrin, it’s fine. I don’t like being hit. I don’t want to go to that place, but could you bring some more meat when you come back?” Ilisia’s stomach rumbled at that moment and she gave a shy look before digging into her food again.
“Of course.” Avrin spoke. When Avrin arrived earlier with his previously missing arm now present, Calomia truly wanted to laugh. She wasn’t sure what to make about the situation, but it hadn’t surprised her as much because she knew Avrin had regrown his legs. She had expected his arm to regrow as well. Ilisia was still amazed and was circling Avrin like a hungry pigeon waiting for him to bring her something good to eat again. Being someone disliked, she didn’t have any friends and another reason she hung around Avrin was simply for the sake of it.
Avrin’s arm having returned, Calomia took this as a chance to make him work. She had gotten him to work the small 4x4 meter farm with some wilted crops growing, and got him to help her in drying the pieces of scrap meat she had set aside from the chunk he had gotten earlier.
Avrin could see their life was hard but it was something he was used to. Back in his universe, he had been to a mining planet that had been abandoned after the materials mined had run out. The government didn’t show much care for helping those people move and they were left to fend for themselves against the creatures of the planet. Avrin had led his crew to pass by on a scouting mission and had seen their situation on a holo screen, but he followed rules that had been set and didn’t pay them any attention. It was ironic that now he was in the same situation, if not worse. At least then they had each other to hunt and organise.
When, after fourteen straight hours of labor, Avrin realised Calomia’s and Ilisia’s struggle every day, not one task could be missed or it would set them back. It made him contemplate some things, but night had already fallen and it was currently 10:00pm. One could hear the soft roars and growls of the creatures within the forest. Calomia and Ilisia took a large risk by living here and it was no short of a miracle that they had survived without being attacked.
Avrin had taken a small, makeshift, stitched sack Calomia had made earlier in the day on Avrin’s request while he tended to the chores. It gave her time for a breather. Ilisia, by this time, was fast asleep and Calomia was tucking her in. Avrin stood at the doorway and looked over towards the dark forest. “Hah, when night falls people don’t dream of heading to the forest at night because of how dangerous it is, but you, boy, don’t seem to care one bit.” Calomia walked over with her makeshift wooden cane as she glanced in the direction Avrin looked towards.
“Why don’t you stop me?” Avrin curiously spoke. Calomia gave a haggled laugh and replied cautiously. “Nonsense. Me, stop you? I already know you’re capable. I know for a fact that no creature would leave a kill unguarded. You must have used some method to scare it away so I’ll just take this as having a bit of confidence in you. But be careful. At night, more creatures will be around and you won’t have an easy time!”
Avrin began to walk out of the small home and simply waved while walking off. “I’ll be heading straight to the village to save some time.” With this said, he vanished into the night and Calomia gave a soft warm smile.
“Mm, fearless. He reminds me of her..” Heading back inside, Calomia threw another small log into the fire pit before sitting on chair and shutting her eyes to rest. With that said and done, Avrin wasted no more time as he dashed forward to the forest. He could already smell blood coming from the forest. It seems the creatures had wasted no time hunting prey and even each other. It made the particles inside his body quiver with hunger and excitement, as if they wanted to be nurtured back to health.
The forest at night was nearly pitch black. Even with the moon being full, it wasn’t able to penetrate through the tree line and shine within. Avrin had to take note that the creatures most likely saw well at night. He soon dashed into the tree line while holding the empty sack on his back. He stopped. When his arm had healed he set aside some energy to use as an attack and with the amount he had stored it wouldn’t be any trouble.
He shut his eyes as he carefully used his body’s keen sense of hearing and the smell of blood to detect his prey. “-There!-” He suddenly vanished as he quietly dashed forward to the left. The foliage was quite thick and small rays of moonlight were barely able to shine in some areas. Avrin’s eyes began to twist and turn as a small thin coat of dark matter covered them. He wasn’t able to fully augment them, but all he needed was the aspect of night vision, and right now things were clear to him to a degree.
He had been running for five minutes before encountering his first target. A small, four eyed chimp with a round pebble-like crystal on its forehead was currently fighting with another chimp. Avrin, going by what he knew about animals, figured it was either a territorial dispute or a fight for a female.
“Leaf Crystal Ape.” Avrin quietly spoke, but this was enough for the already cautious chimps to quickly glance in his direction. They were engaged in conflict with one another, but they were not dumb. If they knew a predator or someone came they would band together to fight him off.
One chimp hissed and growled at him while another picked up a small rock and threw it at Avrin. “Little bastard...” Avrin revealed a wicked smile before he dashed forward after grabbing the rock that had been thrown towards him. His speed surprised the cautious chimps and the one on the left charged at him with its hands pointed out with the small claws ready to tear at him.
Support creative writers by reading their stories on , not stolen versions.
The claws all stabbed forward, showing the chimp had no real method to utilize combat abilities and wasted an advantage, but Avrin, who had side stepped, used his momentum to curve his body until he was behind it. He glared at the chimp that slowly turned to face him, but when it did, a large crashing sound with bones breaking sounded out. The chimp’s head exploded into bits of flesh and gore with pieces of its brain splattering on the trees behind it.
Avrin had used the thrown rock to smash its head into bits. But the chimps head was quite hard and the stone had cracked and become useless, so he dropped it and picked up the small crystal that was embedded in its forehead. The crystal itself was like a symbol of pride for these creatures. It allowed them to gather a little mana which could be used as a trigger to learn some wild magic. Of course, right now, it had become an item ready to be sold by Avrin.
The chimp that remained and saw Avrin take care of its former competitor had its mouth open with shock, and its instincts had told it to run but it had not gotten far before Avrin rushed towards it. His speed had increased due to his small recovery. He appeared behind the chimp with commendable speed and gripped it by the back of the neck before raising it up into the air with ease and breaking its neck killing it instantly. Nebula Mist surged out and began to devour the corpse. Of course, Avrin recovered the leaf crystal beforehand. He didn’t want to torture these creatures. It was simply survival of the fittest, and he was not here to hunt for fun, but to survive.
After he had converted both these creatures into Nebula Mist he was a little disappointed by the amount of dark matter they had given him. Right now, he didn’t dare simply convert raw dark matter. This was because newly converted dark matter held unstable impurities and was not pure enough for him anymore.
He simply converted these creatures to Nebula Mist first and condensed the dark matter to be as small as possible. By doing this, he would be able to stabilize it and make the most out of it instead of letting the raw impure mass remain. It wouldn't help him recover as quick as he wanted, even if it could be purified within his body.
Avrin had shut his eyes again to focus. He was currently standing still and a soft breeze began to flow about the forest, causing the branches of the trees to sway. He could hear the low roars and sounds of creatures who had come out to hunt. Any normal human would hide and cower in fear, but to Avrin, this was an exhilarating experience. Due to his current handicap, this situation made his heart beat quickly with anticipation. It reminded him of when he first came to Seleria and had to survive.
Suddenly, Avrin’s pointed ears twitched slightly. He heard the sound of a bush rustling very faintly behind him followed by a low humming sound that was barely audible even to him at this stage. Avrin didn’t move and decided to put on the act of a clueless man as he stood still.
And at that moment, the humming sound shot up to a high pitched one and a flying figure shot towards him. This creature was a four winged Drill Bee. These creatures would live a solitary life and make nests at the top of trees. They were shaped more like wasps than bees but had green and black stripes, making them hard to spot at night as their dark colors blended well with the trees and bushes.
They had several large eyeballs that were split like a fly’s, though the most discerning feature was their drill shaped stinger, and they were considered a Beginner level creature that ambushes it’s prey. These creatures first stab their prey and inject a special enzyme that would liquefy their prey's insides, much like a spider, before using their mouths to drink the insides after piercing the skin with their hook-like fangs.
“Too slow!” Avrin used a simple sidestep before he engulfed his right hand in dark matter and straightened his palm, slashing down at a near exact moment and cutting the creature in half,  causing green colored blood to spew out as its momentum in the air went for a bit before its halved corpse rolled on the ground. Avrin wasted no time before he used what he knew to scavenge the creature. He took the somewhat sturdy drill from it. The drill itself could be straightened and crafted into an arrow that was worth one Haze crystal. To Avrin, it was better than nothing.
After converting the creature’s body into dark matter, Avrin turned and shot off. He headed towards a small, rocky outcrop that was within the forest. This would be an appealing area for some creatures to lay about and make a home, but right now it was a battlefield.
The sounds of bones cracking and flesh being ripped sounded out. A large creature that resembled a lion but with five small, ten inch bone-like plates on its back emitting a faint red glow with a soft red hue as well as a blue body with a deep red mane that had been dyed by blood was currently gorging itself on one of several dozen corpses of a small band of creatures that had stumbled upon its territory.
This marvel of disaster was known as a Flame Plate Fury. This creature could be said to be a king of the outer forest and was three meters in length while being nearly two meters tall. It’s most notable aspect was not its fearful appearance, but the fact that it could absorb mana from the corpses and flesh of creatures it ate and store it within its bony plates and use a low level magic to engulf its body in a faint layer of flame and use this to attack with a fierce fury.
Avrin was currently eyeing the creature from a distance, carefully observing it and going over what he knew about it. Avrin could see the bony plates on its back were giving off a dim red light with some smoke emitting from them. This symbolized that it had activated its magic. After doing so, it needed five minutes after dispersing it to gather mana again. “-Not long should have passed judging by the freshness of the bodies… But it makes no difference-”
Avrin raised his right hand and dark matter began to gather. A small, two foot long weapon took shape. Although it was roughly made its strength was no less than an Uncommon level weapon. Avrin had formed a tomahawk with the back end of it had a curved blade like a sickle. The dark matter weapon gave off a purple glow, and it was because of this glow that the lion-like creature’s eyes turned to look towards him. Avrin had already dashed towards it after leaving the small sack on the ground.
The Fury’s eyes widened with surprise. It would have never thought a simple looking human would try and attack it alone, but as it saw how fast he came towards it, it figured he was not simple at all. It let out a roar before rushing towards Avrin with its blood stained teeth ready to bite down on him.
“You’re all the same! Hahaha!” Avrin found this funny. These creatures’ methods of attack seemed the same as they went head on first. Avrin didn’t dodge or act until the final moment. He simply jumped up and onto the back of the creature, using his hands to grab its mane. He skillfully used the sickle part of the weapon to cleanly cut across the base of the bone plates. He met with a little resistance, but he didn’t hold back and right as the Fury turned to look at its back its eyes bulged to see its plates were removed. It felt its body tremble with pain and anger as veins surged within its eyes. It madly began to struggle on the ground.
Avrin quickly collected the plates before he kicked his feet off the lion and jumped several meters to the side. He glanced at them with a smile, but his eyes widened as he saw the Fury had charged at him at a fast pace. Just as he threw the plates onto the ground the Fury jump at him and bite down on his shoulder. The force of its charge and weight pushed him back a bit and blood was drawn. Though Avrin’s body had natural durability, the Fury still held sharp teeth. Right now, in Avrin’s state, his body couldn’t match its previous durability and the Fury’s teeth sunk in nearly a full inch, with several teeth crushing down on his shoulder.
“I....guess I owe you this one....but,” As the fury felt satisfied with its bite its eyes turned to look at Avrin’s face, expecting to see fear, but what it saw was that dark veins surged near his eyes as his lips curved into a smile, revealing a sharp set of teeth. Avrin felt agitated. He raised his right hand and dark matter surged around it before his muscles bulged.
He then smashed down onto the creature’s backside, causing its organs to ripple, before the force of the attack made the creature’s insides explode out. Avrin had wasted 5% of the dark matter he had gathered from this night but he felt it was a worthy sacrifice. The Fury still had a shocked look on its face even as its body was blown to bits.
After Avrin turned the corpse as it was into Nebula Mist, his wounds began to slowly heal using the newly acquired energy. He then went over and grabbed the five plates from the ground and carefully examined them. “Uncommon ranked plates. Enough of these would make a set of scaled armor worth five Unclouded crystals, but the price should be two Haze crystals a plate.”
Avrin had spent the entire time hunting creatures and re-honing his combat abilities and what he could do at this stage. He had faced a large cyclops after he ventured a bit deeper into the forest that was at the mid trained level. It’s eye was considered valuable and a good magical medicine. The eye was worth three Haze crystals itself, and because the cyclops was no larger than a normal man Avrin had no issue dispatching it.
Avrin had felt a bit more gutsy and wanted to end his little hunt soon. He was walking back from the outer edges of the inner forest. He didn’t dare venture deeper, and right now his sack was filled with materials that would make any normal hunting group look with greed.
Avrin was casually whistling a small tune he had enjoyed within his former world. He was pleased with tonight. Right now, apart from gathering a potential total of sixty-eight Haze crystals he had absorbed a good amount of creatures to heal himself. Though as he walked, he suddenly stopped in an open area where a ray of moonlight shined down. He carefully looked around as the forest had seemingly gone silent.
“Hmm?” He felt his body shudder as the air grew colder. He quickly tilted his head to the left and just at the right moment, because right after a ray of silver light shot towards where his head had been. Of course, because there was nothing there, the ray of light shot forward and pierced into a tree leaving a clean hole going right through.
“You little....” Avrin gave a taunting glare. He felt his blood surge again, because as he glanced at the creature he knew he was going to get an even better profit tonight.
The creature made its way towards Avrin in the open. It had deer-like antlers but had the body and scales of a snake. It’s head looked like an eagle. It opened its mouth and gave off a wraith-like screech, as if it were angered that it had missed it’s attack.
This creature was an early Intermediate level creature known as Silver Scale Beaker. Though it didn’t seem daunting at first glance, this creature’s beak was quite hard. That being said, it’s most useful aspect was not that it had any useful materials but that it would make a beautiful scarf when dealt with.
Due to this, the creature had been hunted down until its numbers dwindled and it was considered a rare specimen. One left captured and intact would be worth four Unclouded crystals. This was because people would breed them together to make more. Of course, this was very risky and most people would die in the process. But this just meant the demand was higher.

God Orochi Limos
The Artwork will be updated in the main artwork thread soon.
--------------
Avrin placed the sack down and frowned as he looked at the beast. It had almost pierced through his head which would have killed him in an instant and he was not going to let it get away especially since it was worth quite a bit. Though looking at it he saw the moonlight sparkle across its scales, yet its screeching like a harpy was enough to make one no longer admire its beauty and simply want to stomp it to death.
Avrin didn't move but he took a defensive stance, this stance was commonplace within the white dragon clan. Avrin could not simply attack it as he wanted to catch it alive. While he took his defensive stance he began to gather dark matter under his feet and into the ground.
The Silver Scaled Beaker carefully began to pace back and forth causing its body to wiggle almost like a worm. Two minutes had gone by and yet Avrin had not moved an inch. The creature was beginning to grow hungry and impatient, it no longer wanted to wait and shot towards Avrin again intending to go for his legs this time to cut off his retreat and gain a level advantage, its small arms, despite their size, were quite strong as it let the creature dig its claws in and then shoot like a miniature rocket while spiraling towards Avrin.
Dirt kicked up behind the creature as it fired its body towards him like an arrow, though Avrin simply glanced with some disdain as he curved his right foot downward before swiftly kicking with a controlled amount of force upward. The kick smacked the bottom of the creature's jaw, the vibration caused by the attack rattled its mind a bit and the power of the kick also launched several meters. All of this was done precisely from an onlookers perspective.
But Avrin was not done, he waved his hand as nebula mist surged from it and soon the ground split as a large mist shot upward and engulfed the creature that began to wriggle around in fright and anger. Despite how much it struggled it was not able to free itself in mid air, this allowed the nebula mist around it to take shape, and soon a large glowing purple cage was formed around it. The creature began to smack against the cage but it was small enough to not allow it to build momentum. Avrin knew it would be troublesome if he gave it room.
The creature began to screech with anger, as it opened its beak and began to gnaw on the cage. “Will you shut up...” Avrin reached up and grabbed the ring holder at the top of the cage and started shaking the cage until the creature grew quiet and dizzy, no longer daring to make a sound.
Avrin then turned and walked back a step before reaching down to grab the sack filled with materials, he then turned and looked up, at this time it was nearing 5 in the morning. Calculating his time to reach the village from here he would be there by 8 or 9 which could be considered perfect for most merchants to open up shop. He soon left and began to make his way towards the direction of the village while following his hearing, though this led him to take a small detour.
By now he had enough dark matter to fully reform his attire, and his hood was covering his head. He didn't expect to meet people here and was grateful because converting his body at this point would use a bit of dark matter and was dangerous due to the recovery and inexperience.
Avrin quietly sat down on a small boulder as he shut his eyes for a moment to see how his recovery was fairing, though he couldn't enter his inner workings still. “-Perfect, I should be able to reach a preferable state in no time if I continue this up. My physical strength should be as strong as someone at the Master level, but this is just external, my particles still need to recover all their energy. At that point I should be able to reach the Sage level in both ability and strength and after that I will be back to my original strength in no time at all. Though why do I feel as if something has changed, I feel lighter and stronger than I was at the Master level, interesting-”
Avrin suddenly turned his head in the direction left of him and spotted several orange lights making their way in this direction, his eyes narrowed, but nebula mist covered his face before it reformed into the shape of a plain mask with durability no less than iron yet was as light as plastic, it perfectly fit over his face and covered it well with the cloak.
At that moment a group of 10 individuals came out from the bushes in a bunch, consisting of 3 girls and 7 males. “Big brother I told you it's strange...we haven't found anything for awhile and you want us to go near the inner parts? It's too strange and we shouldn't go there.” a soft sweet sounding voice from a short haired green female wearing simple leather attire with a short sword on her waist spoke with some dissatisfaction and a pouty face.
Though as they were walking, the male she spoke to had a serious expression as if he were contemplating something, he seemed to be in his early 30’s with a short black beard and combed black hair as well as a scar across the bridge of his nose. His attire consisted of some plate and chain with the remainder being leather, he had a longsword on his back and was holding up a torch.
The rest of the people following close behind and chatting also wore similar attire and seemed at ease while some at the flank and rear of the group seemed on watch and looked with caution. The man holding the torch and the brother of the female who had seemed dissatisfied suddenly stopped as he quickly held his torch forward, he spotted a dark figure several meters in front and entered a battle stance as he spoke.
“Show yourself!” in a quick moment everyone grew tense as they knew this forest was dangerous. They quickly unsheathed their weapons and got in a formation known to them, 2 of the females as well as a male stood in the back and held out their hands at the same time runic circles began to hover across their wrists as if they were preparing to attack.
“Hmm.” Avrin raised his head and glanced at the man in front carefully eyeing them curiously. Both sides were silent, it was only when the silver scaled beaker began to screech and try to move about in the cage that Avrin turned to look at it and gave the cage a soft kick. “I said shut up...” At this point the female by her brother’s side gazed with awe. “T...that’s a Silver Scaled Beaker!! Brother that's exactly what Lady Missla wanted!” speaking as if the creature was already hers she wiggled a bit causing her fairly proportional bust to jiggle slightly.
The man eyed Avrin for a few more moments, he saw that avrin was alone yet still managed to capture a silver scaled beaker which would pose a great risk for even them. He released his grip on the long sword that remained on his back and then showed a tough smile as he looked at Avrin.
“Sorry about that friend, I thought you were something else.” the man seemed oddly friendly all of a sudden but Avrin knew from the words of the girl this creature was something they wanted so he didn't bother to incline in small chat. “Make an offer.” he spoke a simple phrase.
“Offer?” the girl tilted her head a little confused, and the others behind her seemed to look confused as well as they looked at each other. The man at the front stood clueless for a moment before he gave a heavy laugh. “Ah, mister you seem to have keen foresight, ok since we are in a rush for a gift how about 1 unclouded crystal?”
Avrin snickered behind his mask. “I would have settled for 3 but because you tried to rip me off so badly I want 5 now..” Avrin showed no mercy as he still casually sat on the rock, of course the creature in the cage was afraid Avrin would shake it again so it didn't dare speak make a sound.
Though hearing Avrin’s offer the man felt a little miserable as he was about to speak one of the girls from the back who seemed to be a mage felt anger in her heart and roared out towards avrin. “You!! How dare you, you are speaking to a captain of the Anzazia Mercenary Group!! Now show him some face and take captain Lev’s offer!”
Avrin raised up both hands and and held up six fingers. “Give face? What the hell is that? It sounds perverted, regardless thank blabbermouth over there because I want 6 now!”. A small commotion broke out in the group and Lev felt his face pale a little, a tall man behind him who looked like a rogue whispered among the group. “I say we just beat him to a pulp and take it...”
Lev hearing this took a deep breath. “Mister, I apologize for my subordinates words and my attempts at swindling you. I'll be honest with you, I have a total of 8 unclouded crystals with me, I hope that by telling you this it shows my honesty towards you and that you will give me a fair price.”
Avrin smiled, he could demand it all but he knew the man didn't take uneccesary action, looking at them all Avrin felt their strengths their levels ranged from beginner to a few being trained. As for Lev, Avrin felt his mana matched that of a mid level trained individual nearing the peak, but he could tell by a glance this man had battle instinct and most likely feared avrin because of his ability to capture a silver scaled beaker on his own without assistance.
“Do you have any information books?” Avrin suddenly spoke, Lev suddenly spoke after hearing Avrin. “Lisa” his sister who was seemingly excited yet nervous quickly rushed to the back of the group where an individual was carrying a large backpack, she shuffled through it before pulling out 8 books and returning in confusion, she stood beside Lev as she held the books. “Mister I'm not sure why you need books but I have 8 as you can see, they range from a creature encyclopedia describing those from the trained level to the master level. I also have some common reading material about our country and also a book that describes, Sigil Crafting.”
Almost immediately after hearing the final word Avrin quickly spoke. “Give me 3 unclouded crystals and give me the books and you can have this thing” Avrin softly kicked the cage again which made the beaker screech silently.
Lev sighed in relief before nodding, after a few moments Avrin was going over the book describing sigil crafting while Lev’s sister Lisa was holding and glancing at the beaker which was gnawing on one of the dark matter bars. “After 10 more hours the magic holding the cage will vanish,” Avrin spoke before he placed the books in the sack and placed it over his shoulder.
Lev glanced at Avrin and stepped in front of him before extending his hand out. “Friend I didn't get your name, anyone who can handle a Silver Scale on their own definitely has some metal of worth, what is your name?”
Avrin looked at his hand and then extended his own before clasping onto Lev’s hand, though the others were gazing at the Beaker some were glancing at Lev and Avrin with curiosity though if they looked closely several veins around Lev’s arms and forehead bulged as he tried to grip around Avrin’s hand with all his strength but he felt as if he couldn't make him budge at all, as if he were attempting to forcefully crush a steel ingot it was simply impossible with his strength.
The author's content has been appropriated; report any instances of this story on Amazon.
“-Strong...-” Lev thought as he smiled, Avrin simply glanced through the eye holes of the mask with indifference to him Lev’s grip was simply a firm handshake and he didn't even know he was attempting to test his strength until he saw his expression.
“Avrin.” he spoke. Lev then let go of Avrin’s hand and nodded. “Avrin hopefully we can encounter each other again, you gave me a good deal today” he then turned to head towards his group. Lisa glanced at Avrin and looked at him curiously she could see his eyes were glowing blue, and she wasn't sure why but she felt her soul shake and body quiver faintly. It made her turn a soft shade of red before turning around and walking off to follow the rest of the group that intended to go forward.
Avrin didn't linger around anymore as he still had things to sell, he held his hand out and had 3 index finger nail sized crystals, these looked like haze crystals but these crystals had more mist inside of them and were somewhat clearer. Avrin continued to walk and placed one in his mouth and swallowed it.
As soon as it slid down his throat his body couldn't wait and the crystal wasn't even able to enter his stomach before it was melted down and converted into dark matter that was absorbed into the walls of his esophagus.
Avrin felt a fresh feeling and gave a soft breath that was cold enough to cause a mist to appear, “Strangely leaves a sweet minty aftertaste.“ Avrin felt that this crystal was significantly more appealing than the haze crystals it made him wonder about the higher ranked crystals if they tasted this fresh and appealing he may simply devour these things. Even though he doesn't need to eat it made his tastebuds tingle.
Several hours later as Avrin left he noticed more and more groups of adventurers making their way inside the forest as well as some who had already begun to set up a small camp. Avrin figured at this time many would start their day by preparing to hunt beasts to sell at the villages special trade market where lucent crystals were used as currency instead of coins.
Some gazed strangely at the black cloaked avrin who with one hand held a full stitched bag on his back while with the other was holding a book to do with sigil crafting. “-It seems it's not anything special nor unique to them. The method of creating this seems simple enough, but something like this is definitely interesting. Sigil crafting is simply an emblem etched with countless runes and symbols to form a sigil, though each set of symbols and rune engravings represents a certain equipment ranging from amulets, armor and weapons. Mmm again it needs mana? Nonsense, it shouldn't be an issue for me to mimic it with dark matter, this could be a good step for me to begin until I have a source of lucent crystals.-”
As Avrin walked out of the forest he followed a set path, he shut the book and glanced forward, from this area he was able to see the open area even better than at Calomia’s home. He could see merchant caravans going back and forth from a small outpost just outside of the forest heading towards the direction of the village, Avrin ignored this and simply went on his way.
The landscape could be said to be quite pristine, open plains with farmland as well as wooden palisades spanning around a soft perimeter around a bit of the forest to keep certain areas free from creatures. Of course this place seemed to be big for people to make money from so it meant that food needed to be acquired which brought a need for farms to be made closer.
As Avrin continued down the path he felt a little nostalgia, he remembered when he broke out of the sylph forest and explored out to his first town, the current feeling was as if he were redoing that journey but he no longer feared being threatened by anyone. He doubted there was anyone around here at the high god level or above, to his knowledge this part of the landmass was a backwater area.
Avrin was tinkering around with a small mass of dark matter in his hand, it was shaped like an octagon and he willed random runes to be etched into it to form what was needed, right now he was carefully willing the dark matter and giving it orders. He was now able to communicate with the particles of dark matter formed by energy outside of his body and not just inside, making things much more useful for him. He held the 2 inch wide and 2 inch tall octagon that was as thick as a thumb he carefully examined it, right now it was simply using his will to program the dark matter but it wouldn't mean much if only he could use it.
Right now the sigil he had created was quite simple, it had an obsidian look to it and seemed quite sturdy, though since he intended to sell these he would need a symbol. He began to tinker around with the makeshift sigil and had formed a rough eight-pointed star with the inside being a soft shade of purple while it was outlined by a black color. Using dark matter, he had a circle made around it that was dotted precisely every few centimeters, and from there he took inspiration from his dark matter cores’ surroundings. He had a large sphere in the middle of the symbol, and connected to that sphere were four lines that connected to two medium sized spheres and two smaller sized spheres which had three dots lined in front of them.
(A.N: Please refer to Spectral Regalias cover, the symbol on the mask is the symbol used on the sigil )
Avrin had a simple solution for the issue regarding dark matter not being able to be felt by anyone other than Spectrals. He pulled out an unclouded lucent crystal and within moments the sigil shot sharp veins towards the crystal and impaled it; however, it didn't devour it. Soon the sigil began to draw in mana, seemingly pumping it from the crystal. Finally, the crystal was then swallowed by the sigil to become the core. Now when Avrin looked at the sigil he created, it looked like a genuine sigil. The sigil would slowly feed from the crystal, only enough to keep itself sustained. As a safeguard, the moment someone tries to tinker with it or extract the crystal Avrin had ordered the particles to simply self destruct.
“Trigger” he spoke and in a moment the sigil morphed in his hand and formed into a foot long dagger. It took the shape of a dark matter weapon with the lucent crystal encrusted within its hilt. “Trigger necklace” he spoke again and the weapon condensed and reformed back into a necklace with the lucent crystal set in the pendant. “Trigger ring” the sigil once more transformed, this time into a ring with the crystal set at the top like an overgrown diamond with a few dark veins to bind it in place.
“That should be it for now.” Avrin at first silently questioned his ability to easily recreate something like this. He remembered God speaking about his god’s heart and its powers of creation.. When Avrin pondered on that piece of information, it didn't seem so surprising. He knew that he had a lot to learn, and that he wasn't able to recreate different types of energy, mana for instance, but he was satisfied for now. He stowed the sigil and stopped where a bend in the road and a break in the trees allowed him to overlook the village ahead. Of Course this also had the potential to cause issues in the future.
The village of Roth was established along a broad river that spanned hundreds of miles in either direction, connecting the ocean to the large lake of the city that could be seen at the edge of the horizon. The village was neither rich nor poor and was fairly average with a population of a couple thousand. Its houses were built from wood and stone and included some fairly common shops such as butchers and small book shops. The village was divided into several sections. The southern portion of the village was the poorer part of the village with homes built simply from wood, and was the section Calomia had previously made a living in helping.
The northern section, which contained a larger bulk of buildings, were all made out of carved stone, and were decently made with more care. The paths leading across the village were well maintained gravel, likely left over from carving the stones for the houses.
Connected to the northern section was a walled-off elliptical section that was over 400 meters long and 100 meters wide. The walls around this area were all higher than even those protecting the village, they manned by guards adorned in scaled uniform armor with a simple grey shield emblazoned with two swords crossed under a shield. Each guard had a careful look, as if they didn't dare not be cautious.
This heavily guarded section was the market.  The houses near the market section were all small mansions, and each one well made. In this village being closer to the marketplace was seen as a sign of prosperity and riches.
The market’s main entrance was marked by heavy gates, rich adornments, and the long line of buyers waiting to pass inspection. Away from the main entrance, a wider, less fanciful gate was manned with several more guards who were currently inspecting carriages of merchants wanting to sell their wares and peddle goods.
The merchant line was more efficient, and the line contained only three people, one with a carriage and two others who were carrying backpacks filled with goods. The guard inspecting a parchment containing a list of the goods furrowed his brow, he had a ragged, gritty look with a shaven face but a serious expression, the guard scratched his head and spoke after rolling up the parchment.
“You're all clear, pay the fee of 2 haze crystals or something of equal value and then enter.” The merchant didn't bother to linger as he led the small, 3-horned, bull-like creature (that was nearly double the size of a normal bull) to continue on in with the small carriage that definitely had a fair amount of goods within.
Avrin had arrived on time and was silently waiting in line, with his mask on, and the sack slung over his right shoulder. “-The price seems fair-” he spoke. The guard continued and faced the two individuals who were next and spoke. “List your category of goods or hand me a manifest” his answer seemed generic but it was spoken as if he had done it thousands of times. The two people simply handed the guard a parchment, and after some time the guard rolled the parchment and handed it back then repeated the same words he spoke to the merchant with the small carriage.
Soon as the two peddlers entered after paying the fee Avrin walked up and the guard who seemed bored glanced at him, though the moment he looked at Avrin he felt his body quiver a little. He was not sure why but he felt an urge to be somewhat more respectful. “Morning sir, list your category of goods or allow me to see a manifest.”
Avrin didn't bother wasting time and spoke. “Creature materials as well as a sigil.” The guard was a little stunned, a sigil could only be made by people who not only had a special talent for controlling mana but learnt a special magic that allowed them to combine the mana with materials to create a sigil, the materials varied depending on the sigil needed.
“Very good sir, usually merchants have manifests but by seeing you don’t I’m assuming your new? Hehe for a small price I’m willing to share some information if you are willing?” Avrin smirked silently behind his mask this guard. Of course he wouldn't leave a chance to make a small profit.
Avrin brought the sack out and pulled out one of the materials he had obtained from a creature. “I don't have any lucent crystals but will monster materials do?” Avrin pulled out one of the small leaf crystals he had taken from one of the creatures he killed earlier.
“Of course!” the guard happily accepted it and then looked around, he glanced at one of his fellow guards who then approached and handed a small booklet that had seemingly been prepared before. The guard handed it to Avrin and began to speak. “Since you are new I will explain some unspoken rules, the upper sections of the market are usually reserved for those merchants with more reputation than others, despite being a small village we have some shops from the three big players in this country, although they are minor minor branches they are still something; the Spring Institute, Artificer Consortium and the Highland Syndicate.”
Avrin was a little confused “I'm not from this region, can you tell me about these three establishments?” the guard in charge of things was stunned. He had never in his 30 years as a guard, and even 20 years as chief inspector,, seen nor heard of anyone who didn't know of these powerhouses.
