Since that day a full six months had passed. Things had gotten increasingly busy for Avrin so much so that he had formed a deal with Calomia. Calomia, at first, was quite reluctant to accept too much from Avrin. Because he was staying at her home him giving her some gifts and food could be considered as payment and she refused to simply rely on him, especially with Ilisia as she wanted to teach her a walk of life.
Avrin asked for her and Ilisia to help take orders and payment and describe what he was selling. In return, he would give payment to her and Ilisia. He also said this would teach Ilisia responsibility as he didn't want to simply gift her. In this regard, he agreed with Calomia that spoiling her too much would be bad.
The first day they had helped Avrin they were simply watching him handle things. Ilisia was extremely excited, she had never before been in a strange building like this, her body was constantly trembling as she was full of energy. Had it not been for Calomia she would have most likely run around the entire building exploring.
Calomia was a bit more wary of the situation. She had a few secrets in regards to her past and knew what a Sigil weapon was, but when she saw the Sigil weapons Avrin was creating she couldn't help but be surprised. This raised his position in her mind to a different level.
While Avrin had been receiving customer’s requests and payments he had to cycle between showing every new customer his Sigil weapons and what they could do. Explaining this took time that he wanted to use to make Sigil weapons. After all, despite his ability it still required some time, especially when within six months you have anywhere from a dozen to a hundred people interested in products.
The adventurers that had come the first time were newly registered and didn't have much to spend. Avrin felt a little pity for them and decided to use the situation for his and their advantage in a fair trade. He gave every member of that group two Sigil weapons each, he only asked that if they had a chance to promote him to do so and if they ever decided to sell or give away the second Sigil weapon to tell whoever it was of Avrin’s shop.
They were all over the moon after Avrin recommended this, even more so when he showcased the product and showed how durable and strong it was. Since then, with the help of the promotional parchment he had selectively given to adventurer and mercenary groups, things had gotten quite busy.
Though not all of it was positive. If Avrin was to calculate things carefully, around thirty out of one hundred of the promotional posters were taken seriously and about fifteen of that thirty were of people who made purchases, but one may think he was being negligent in regards to it. Though to him, it was no real matter because things were still on track. In fact, he was somewhat worried that he wouldn't be able to keep his promise of speed to people because of how popular he had become.
Calomia and Ilisia had started helping Avrin on the second month. Calomia was tasked to act as the receptionist and to help with showcasing products, and Ilisia was given an easier task because she was still young. All she needed to do was take the enchanted sack Avrin had given her with each customer's payment and order prepared inside, and then after it was done she would come back and give the small chest Avrin formed along with the order to Calomia who finalised everything.
Calomia’s energy didn't suit her age. She was incredibly efficient, like a machine, as she had easily memorised what Avrin had told her and was able to boast about the Sigil weapons, though with her own hidden past she understood some knowledge of Sigil weapons and she herself was quite surprised as to how Avrin’s products blew the same level of competition away.
Over the months, the shop’s design began to change, with tinkering done to make it seem cosier and full. Potted plants were added by Avrin who could make the pots but had to buy the plants, he made furniture and tables, carpet and even bought other things such as paintings.
The bare interior was now much more full and comfortable. Avrin also adopted a strategy from his old universe, a ticket system, which would kill the need for lines and would allow people to sit down and relax as they waited for their turn. The ticket dispenser was a simple one, powered by dark matter that formed a ticket from Nebula Mist. This only required a control particle to remember the tickets dispensed and the number would reset every day.
The interior near the reception had turned from a wide hall to a lobby. There were four large areas for sitting. People who entered here the first time would feel as if they had entered a different world. It was uncomfortable, but after coming here a few times they had gotten used to it.
Avrin was always thinking of ways to improve what he could. Previously he didn't have lights, but he developed a method to use dark matter orbs to act as solar panels and trap light within and then slowly dispense it out to light up the area. This was not without issue. It meant he needed a sunroof. That would be a bit strange, but it was nothing to him. Right under the sunroof, on the floor it was over, Avrin had changed that tiled area and added a small man-made pond filled with crystal clear water and a small fountain. He didn't need to purchase any fish or flowers as he simply Divine Stepped to find a similar pond and just took what he wanted from it.
The light glistening off the water gave the atmosphere a more refreshing feeling, though Avrin’s current customers consisted only of adventurers and mercenaries who dealt with life and death battles they felt a little at ease in such a location.
Avrin’s success was starting to get the notice of those from the market bazaar, especially the Artificer Consortium that found it had lost quite a few customers. How would they know that because of Avrin’s smooth talking and marketing that he had formed verbal contracts with other mercenary groups similar to the one he made with Urkan and the Anzazia group? The Artificer Consortium building’s interior was inferior to Avrin’s, it was rough and cold. It had several rooms where Sigil craftsmen would start their work. One could feel mana of all sorts of elements resonating around, assistants would be carrying trays of materials to each room as requested by those inside.
The finished products were marked and then sent off. The service was quiet and somewhat rude. It was as if the shop's staff only wanted Lucent crystals and when it was given, they were shooed away. Though within the largest room the same elderly man that had gone to see Urkan with the middle aged women was currently sitting on a thick mat with an assortment of brewed tea on a tray placed on a carved stone table.
“Are you sure about this?” The man brought down a cup of herbal tea from his lips, placing it back on the tray. He glanced over at a group of three people, the middle aged women he had gone with before included, standing in the middle.
“Yes, Grandfather ... I wasn't sure what was going on at first, but we were able to identify the cause of our and the Highland Syndicate's business slowing down.” The old man's pupils contracted. His face was somewhat pale and he hadn't been able to sleep in the past six months. At first, they thought nothing of the situation when a few of their regulars didn't show up to view new products and have their weapons repaired, but they had lost 15% of their business within the months and it was increasing.
“Well what is it…which scum dares steal our work.” The old man frowned as his heart was beating with anger, his aura began to surge. One could see he was at the peak Master level and already past his prime, but scary nonetheless to those weaker.
“G...Grandfather...remember those strange parchments that some of our trusted customers brought in and showed us? The one's we were unable to discern.” The women felt some fear but spoke. The two beside her were even more frightened.
“Yes... what was it again... this Shaded Moon shop, wasn't it a scam?” The old man spoke, then thought for a moment before speaking again. “No... do not tell me that it’s a real business!?” The man was worried and as his granddaughter looked at him and nodded he felt his body tense up. “This is our damned fault... we should have taken this seriously…” The man smashed the back of his right hand against the stone table, sending it crashing against the wall and shattering into bits along with the special porcelain teapot and cups.
“To think someone who isn't the Highland Syndicate dares to make a move on our lifeblood... what else do you know about this Shaded Moon business, who runs it? Who do we need to remove.” On the outside, the old man seemed quiet and calm, but on the inside, he kept the fierce reputation of the Artificer Consortium true. He was quite vicious and didn't think twice about removing obstacles. The Highland Syndicate was large and him making a move would cause issues, but who would care about a business cutting in on their pie. In fact, he felt that the Highland Syndicate should be thanking him for this.
“Grandfather, this past month I did some digging. This is everything I've managed to find and compile... it took some coercing and payment but I managed to find out quite a bit and also this.”
The middle-aged women may also seem a bit vicious but unlike her grandfather, she was more scheming and thoughtful. She walked over and pulled out a small, fur skinned book that contained all she knew about the situation. Inside the book was also one of the dark Sigil weapons in the form of a ring that she purchased from someone.
The old man ignored the ring for a moment as he read the first few pages of the book. “The land the Anzazia group obtained the deed to, at first I thought they wanted it to use as a bartering tool with us, who would have thought that devious bastard Urkan gave it to this Avrin fellow for him to build a shop, no doubt they have a deal made…..his side is obvious, from here on make note that anyone apart or related to the Anzazia group will not be allowed to purchase any items from us or any stores affiliated to us, we will let them feel the pain from this.” The old man spoke towards one of the well-dressed men on the right who bowed respectfully and left to carry out the order.
A case of content theft: this narrative is not rightfully on Amazon; if you spot it, report the violation.
The old man then picked up the strange ring that was placed on the page that listed the commands to activate it. “Trigger sword…” the old man spoke curiously, and when the dark matter within twisted and turned he jumped from fright, dropping it onto the ground. Yet the moment it hit the ground it had already turned into a short sword.
The scene didn't shock the remaining man and the old man's granddaughter as they had already experienced the shock, yet in their eyes was a strange hint of curiosity and eagerness to understand how the weapon is able to do that.
The old man who had jumped back two feet glanced silently at the short sword before stepping over and picking it up. “Strange….and the quality of this specific Sigil weapon is Common?”
Asking this the remaining man who was the one who obtained it for the middle-aged women nodded. “Yes senior, the man I purchased it from I tasked with going undercover to purchase this. The cost was four Haze crystals.”
The old man scoffed after hearing this. “Four Haze crystals?... is it made from shit?! So cheap... well then let's see.” The old man reached to his side and pulled out a similar sized short sword from his own enchanted sack. He now wielded a blade in both hands as he eyed them both carefully.
“Look carefully the two of you, the difference in quality is obvious. How can our products be inferior to a cheap imitation!” With that, he smashed the two blades against each other with no mercy, yet a cracking shattering sound of metal rung out, but it was not from the blade he expected.
The middle-aged women and the man to her side were slack-jawed and looking with horror as they saw that in the old man's hands the Dark Sigil weapon with a purple metallic lustre was fine as if nothing happened, yet the Uncommon quality blade made by her own grandfather was shattered to bits.
The old man was silent, his eyes moving from the Dark Sigil weapon and the Sigil weapon he had made before. When he realised what happened, fear came to his mind. Fear that in this area he was no longer the best, fear that his shop would lose all its business, fear that he would be reprimanded by the main headquarters for allowing someone to beat them like a dead dog.
“Grandfather….” The woman finally built up the courage to speak and break the silence, though when she glanced at the old man, she felt a little worried for him. But when his lips moved her worry was gone. “Go inform Lord Malvin and his disciple Lord Galum that I request their presence….I think this issue should be cut at the root before it grows too large…”
Back within Shaded Moon, Avrin was underground. The area was different from before. A second staircase near the one that led up to his office had been made. This one led down to a hall that led to another staircase that ran down into the expansive underground room. Within this room there was a five meter wide and long platform that had a single step on each side that led to it.
On top of that platform, Avrin was sitting cross-legged with a pile of Haze crystals and several open parchments detailing orders. Around him were many chests of varying sizes, each of these chests were made from mahogany wood with a coating of dark matter as well as the Shaded Moon emblem on the front section. Mahogany wood was not a material that could be found in this region to Avrin’s knowledge. He doubted it could be found in this universe unless a God liked it and brought it with him.
“Mister Avrin!” Ilisia came running down the steps with a handful of rolled up order parchments. She rushed towards Avrin with an excited look. She wore a beautiful white, long-sleeved dress with white dress shoes. Avrin made it carefully to Ilisia’s liking and so that also when she ran around she wouldn't trip and the dress wouldn't cause issues.
As for Calomia, Avrin wasn't sure what to make her so to avoid any issues it gave him the idea for another product he wasn't selling at the moment. He had given Calomia a small, flat, bendable piece of dark matter. All she needed to do was think and imagine what sort of attire she wanted and the piece of dark matter would surge and from that piece for her to wear.
“How many?” Avrin spoke soundly while continuing his work. Ilisia rushed over, climbed the step and placed the pile of rolled up orders beside him. “Ummm, Grandma said today was busier than normal. Eight different mercenary people came in and two adventurer people as well. Poor Mister Avrin, you're really busy, hehe!”
Ilisia wasn't sure how to refer to the customers yet and she couldn't really tell who was who at the moment. Avrin also heard that she was teasing him a bit. “Hmph…” he uttered before stopping his work for a moment. Her words had made him come to a realisation. “-You're right... this has become too easy for me, why do I need to waste time doing this... I have a better idea. I have the Fragment of Creation and have seen humans create machines to mass produce... why don't I simply find a solution-”
Avrin stood up and Ilisia watched him carefully. “Step a few meters back Ilisia.” Avrin said cautiously. Ilisia was not a stranger to Avrin’s abilities, she knew he had strange magic that let him do a lot of amazing things.
Avrin shut his eyes as he began to think carefully. Very carefully he began to put several concepts together in his mind, many different concepts. Some looked good but worked badly, others looked bad but worked well. He needed something that would be the most efficient but also not an issue. He understood his body and his capabilities. He again had to thank the information God had given him as well as the book in his consciousness. He could do so much with dark matter that it made him worry about what powerful beings would do if they found out that he had it.
“There it is….” Avrin’s eyes shot open and he raised his hands up, both facing  each other. “What's there, Mister Avrin?” Ilisia tilted her head in confusion. She had been much more relaxed and happy lately, mainly because she had a neat pile of Lucent crystals for herself. Though  Calomia and herself had been unable to spend any of them because they were too worried to go to Roth, whenever they needed something Avrin simply formed it for them, free of charge.
At the tip of every one of Avrin’s fingers, drops of blue blood seeped out before shooting towards the centre of the space between where his palms were facing each other. Avrin began to carefully will the blood together. This was pure blood, good enough to make a Spectral as pure as Asura and the others. Though when the blood congealed to a fleshy, jelly-like substance and dark matter was being fed to it, it began to pulse and expand and contracted before sparks of purple lightning flickered around, it began to emit a heavy pulse.
Avrin’s eyes narrowed before he moved his palms quickly over the congealed sphere, cupping it. Moments later, a slight booming sound echoed between his palms as he moved them away. The skin and flesh of his hands had been burnt and mangled to such a degree that his bones were visible. Obviously, he had underestimated himself and this was the result. Had he let that congealed blood explode. It would cause the room to be damaged and more importantly Ilisia to face danger. “Ahh!!“ Ilisia screamed as she looked at Avrin’s hands and ran over towards him. Her face paled and she looked like she was about to cry. “What do we do!! You’re hurt!! Grandm-” Avrin spoke quickly so that she didn't make a big deal out of it. “This is nothing. Don't you remember I can heal my limbs? What would a silly wound like this do to me.”
The dark matter began to converge around his hands, forming a thin coating to act as skin until his wounds could heal. “This should only take a few minutes at most….you should go back to check on your grandma. Oh yes, tomorrow will be Shaded Moon’s official first day off. I think it would be good to go to the market for you and her to buy some things.”
Ilisia frowned and looked somewhat worried at Avrin as he seemed to show not much care towards his damaged hands, though when he brought up that he would take her and Calomia to the market her heart skipped a beat. She felt a conflicted feeling. To them she was strange because of her eyes, she was considered bad luck.
“Mm…I don't want to go…” Avrin glanced at her as he sat back down and continued to make Sigil weapons. “Because they will tease you and your grandma? You're both rich now, I don't see why you should care about what they think. In fact, take it as a chance to show off a little. I guarantee the way they look at you and treat you will change when they see you have Lucent crystals to spend.”
Ilisia listened and began to think for a few moments. She wasn't sure how to respond, she was still quite little after all. She simply ran off quietly without giving a reply to Avrin. Avrin was a little disappointed. He wondered what he had done wrong in regards to the object he wanted to create. “-This makes no sense...control should have been easy to maintain but it reacted oddly. To think my blood can be so volatile. It would be too easy if everything went my way. I will try again later-”
Avrin smirked to himself as he began thinking on another subject. “-It's been a long while since I've recovered my peak strength, tonight I will step towards Type 13 particles. I've long since amassed the required energy...hmm?-”
Avrin stopped for a moment and turned to look several dozen meters away as the ground in that spot was cracking slightly. His Divine Sense extended out underground and his right eye twitched slightly. “I completely forgot about them…” he gave a rare embarrassed look as he watched the ground crack open and a large hand reached out and clutched onto the edge of the hole causing the ground to crack under the pressure and grip.

chapters.title: V6: Chapter 154 The Ant Ailirion & The Visit From The Consortium.
chapters.content:
!!!!! Pr Credits To Draconis Von BloodTrap &  Peter1765 Who Help With SR chapters, Please take the time to rep them for their work :) Sponsored Release
Special thanks to SR's DonatorTobias Klauke For sponsoring this release!
Here is 154 after i came back from work i didnt even wash up and came straight to prepare and release it for you guys!.Just some news since a majority of you dont follow me on twitter. Draconis is taking a small vacation so me and Peter/Utibe need to be a bit more cautious and careful with checking the chapters which may mean a slight delay until Draconis gets back.---------The large hand tensed up slightly before a blurry shadow shot up from the hole, landing beside it. There stood a creature that towered like a giant. As it looked around, its breath emitted an intense heat from its nostrils causing steam to form with each breath. The most notable aspect of this creature was the large, spiky crystal mass on its back emitting a heavy purple hue and glow.“Massterr!!...” the creature shouted out towards Avrin, causing the ground to faintly vibrate at its voice. This creature was Tardiff’maras. Avrin glanced at a little ashamed because he had forgotten about it. He intended to visit them after some time passed but because his progress was quite efficient and he was too busy with his tasks and looking for ways to create and change things it was pushed out of his mind.Though the sound of footsteps sounded out as Ilisia came down the steps calling out with surprise. “Mister Avrin, what was that….AHH MONSTER!!” She looked at Tardiff and screamed. Tardiff glanced back at her and frowned, he felt somewhat hurt at being called a monster.“Noot….monster!!...” he shouted, his body tensed up slightly before he flickered and vanished with such speed it was astonishing for someone of his size. He appeared behind Ilisia who looked up at him. She was so frightened her little face paled and she fainted on the spot. Tardiff reached down towards her.“What do you think you're doing?...” Avrin’s voice caused the entire space to tremble and Tardiff froze. He glanced at Avrin seeing a single right eye glancing at him through the eye hole of the mask. Around Avrin, Nebula Mist surging somewhat like a fire so hot it caused a ripple.“Ahn..thiis….master’s frieendd...sorry….” Tardiff quickly stepped back. It didn't intend to hurt Ilisia, it was just a bit hurt that it was called a monster. Avrin stood up and appeared next to Ilisia as he reached down and carried her in his arms. He walked over as Nebula Mist formed around the ground into a large pillow that he laid her on. He then turned to look at Tardiff who trembled and was poking his fingers together.“Treat this girl and her grandmother upstairs well. In fact, treat every person you see well unless I say otherwise. You need to learn to control yourself.” Avrin couldn't blame Tardiff and didn't want to hurt him. It was now part of his race and it didn't know any better. It hadn't gotten much smarter by the looks of it, this worried Avrin more than Ilisia fainting.“Foorgivee….” Tardiff spoke before sitting on its butt and gave an excited look as it glanced around. “Maaster’s hoome?...” it spoke out. Avrin was glancing down at the ground. His Divine Sense had extended for a monstrous 50,000 kilometres. Avrin had previously been able to extend his Divine Sense across the entirety of Seleria, but this was the first time since regaining his full power that he extended it out as far as he could. He wasn't sure what to think of the situation, he wanted to laugh. This was because his Divine Sense was probably just under 9.8% of this planet's entire circumference, it made him wonder just how large planets could be. Each universe had a different set of laws and energy so he had already mentally prepared himself to see planets as large as the sun. Then again, he felt it shouldn't be a surprise because he had seen how large Orphelium was.Avrin could see the entire tunnel that Tardiff had gone through. In fact, Avrin could see thousands of other creatures within the tunnel. Avrin’s expression changed as he carefully looked at these creatures’ details. They were no doubt the ant things that he had seen before, but their body structure had changed somewhat. They seemed more humanoid. Their legs were only slightly bent and they boasted a carapace on the outside in the shape of a more humanoid body. Their arms were somewhat thicker and more human-like but had several spikes sticking out. And each arm had a long blade-like appendage where Nebula Mist was surging out from towards the ground causing it to disintegrate, they have clearly adapted their method of digging.“-One….two…. six-hundred-thousand of them…..all converted….-” Avrin felt his body tremble to a degree. He could feel the underground system and the complex array of tunnel systems that led incredibly deep. Truthfully, Avrin couldn't completely feel the depth of the planet. His Divine Sense stopped at thirty-thousand below as he couldn't bring it down anymore but he knew this planet's depth was most likely between seventy-thousand or eighty-thousand kilometres, yet these converted ants had actually managed to reach a depth of four hundred kilometres. The tunnels themselves were somewhat interestingly maintained. These ants, after digging through, would coat the walls of the tunnel in a liquid substance that was dark matter yet it would solidify like metal. It helped keep the tunnel stable.“This time was my fault Tardiff, but you all have done well. Your task was successful by the looks of it. The resistance you met must have been quite large if only six-hundred-thousand of them remain.” Avrin said. Tardiff tilted his head. He remembered it clearly, it truly was a battle. Yet with him on the spectral side he decimated all of them and not only did the ants at the main nest want to attack him they wanted to eat him alive, though the elderly ant that had been converted told Tardiff that if the queen was converted or perished then the rest of the nest will crumble.Leading a small group of these ants towards the queen's nest was easier said than done for Tardiff. He had to constantly keep on his feet and keep killing those that attacked them until they finally reached the lowest part of the nest. The queen herself was as large as him and an ugly creature.She could not be convinced by the elderly ant, this was because as the queen she had only the most basic of instincts and lacked most intelligence. She only needed to be fed and to make more ants. She considered anything else as hostile forces and even treated Tardiff and the converted ants as food.Tardiff didn't bother holding back, he completely destroyed the area and not even the queen was able to stand up to him. When he made his way over to her she intended to spray him with an acid but he simply punched her head causing it to explode and that was the instant the rest of the near mindless ants were shocked and unsure what to do. The elderly ant took advantage of the situation to rally them all together.When Tardiff finished explaining what had happened, it began to think. “Mmm….something else…..forgot…...found something…..” Tardiff began rubbing his head as he tried to remember, Avrin glancing at Tardiff suddenly turned to look at the hole he came from and then spoke towards it. “Stop hiding yourself and tell me what is it you both found…” Avrin’s voice echoed within the lit chamber.Another shadow shot up with incredible speed towards Avrin before landing several meters in front of him. This ant’s appearance was different to the others, it's entire humanoid body was a full metallic carapace with a purple and black lustre. It even had detailing such as abs and biceps. The creature's head had four winged horns, two punishing to the front and two pushing back. On its forehead, two long, black antennae scuttled about. The ant itself also had black, shoulder-length hair. Its face was incredibly human-like, with only the parts where the flesh connected to the carapace head portion looking a bit odd.The creature's eyes were also identical to a human’s except there were no pupils, just two glowing purple orbs. The creature's arms were both a meter long and somewhat thick. It had two large claw-like hands, and it's legs were human except curved somewhat. It also retained that bottom ant bump on it's lower backside and it had two half meter lumps on it's back with darkened slits. If one looked closely they would see the faint edge of a pair of thin folded insect wings. The creature also had a long black beard and an aged look yet still retained a dangerous appearance. It was kneeling in front of Avrin with great respect.“Great one….” It spoke with as much respect as it could in its heavy tone. It was speaking in clear English, the reason being that it was much simpler than the other languages that it was given in the Sphere of Knowledge.Avrin glanced at the creature carefully and then noticed the staff in its hand. This was the same one the elderly ant had before he converted it. “Oh, it's you. It seems your conversion was smooth. Do you have a name?”The ant looking at Avrin felt deeply nervous. It was quite strong already, it was at the early Master level and definitely needed some work. The first month where it and Tardiff were rampaging throughout the ant nest to get to the main chamber of the queen they took the ant had been the one responsible for converting all the other ants to the specifics Avrin had given it in the Sphere of Knowledge, it needed to maintain order and was more intelligent than Tardiff.It had made sure to convert four other ants to a position equivalent to the Baron title in the Spectral rankings. It then made ten ants with the rankings of Arch Knights and then went ahead and made conversion cores enough for one-thousand Knight Spectrals. The rest were all Squires.It didn't dare convert anything else other that, that was because it knew of the restriction placed on conversion, but he had restricted conversion greatly. The only Spectrals that could freely convert were Avrin himself, Tardiff and this ant.  “Ailirion….mighty great one...my name is Ailirion.”“Good...I guess I need to make a gift as a welcoming present for you. That being said, let me handle some things first.” Avrin raised his finger towards Ailirion and the Spectral ant’s body trembled slightly as it's particles were shifted and changing with a sort of lock. It knew that from here on out it would no longer be able to convert.“You truly went all out, though I hope you won't hate me for locking conversion. It once caused a great catastrophe to my….well, to our people.” Avrin spoke in a straightforward manner. His reason for doing this was for their own good. “Great one...this lowly ant understands…”Avrin frowned a little. He felt Ailirion may have a sort of inferiority complex, this wasn't good, though as he was about to speak Tardiff said “Maaster….I ….deservee….giifft...too?..” Avrin glanced at Tardiff who tried his best to look miserable to get some sympathy from Avrin.“You scared my little friend, so no there will be no gift for you..” Avrin teased the giant somewhat. Follow me both of you. Avrin walked back over to the platform as he began to create sigil weapons again, though this time he took 5 unclouded crystals and glanced at them carefully, Dark matter began to surge out from Avrin's right hand towards the 5 unclouded crystals, they began to form and congeal around them before covering them completely, the dark matter then shot upward and downwards from above and below the points of where these crystals were covered, the surge was neat in a cylindrical shape, from there it began to form two blade heads one at the top of the shape and one at the bottom, the entire form of dark matter began to shift and turn as it was being changed at every second.This tale has been pilfered from . If found on Amazon, kindly file a report.Tardiff and Ailirion were glancing with reverence towards Avrin, they didn't know what he was doing but they felt the amount of energy in the dark matter he had formed, it was so much so that if they were to combine both their energies together they would only be able to amount to 10% of it.Avrin's expression of course flickered faintly this would be the strongest sigil weapon he formed, the reason he used 5 unclouded crystals was because he wanted to see this weapon improve, and it would also test himself, he had almost lost control a few times as the crystals were almost devoured by the dark matter which would make its evolution progress much slower, though this weapon was a simple placeholder for Ailirion, when he had the time he would have another one made. Avrin looked forward to giving the sigil creation method to Eitri he felt that with that dwarves skill and talent he could figure out a much more efficient and better way of forming sigil weapons. The process had taken 5 minutes but when the residue of the dark matter dissipated a double sided glaive was hovering in the air, both the blade heads were transparent and somewhat crystal clear, they radiated a faint aura of dark matter, and in the middle section of the glaives shaft all 5 of the unclouded crystals were barely visible, there were also two grips for Ailirion to hold the glaive, the weapon was quite long and with Ailirion's height and reach it should be great for him.“Great one…” Ailirion quickly knelt down as he felt incredibly happy as he knew this weapon was made for him. Tardiff, of course, glanced over somewhat jealous. “Give….weapon for mee….” Tardiff uttered.Ailirion glanced behind towards him with a frown. “Greedy creature…..you want a weapon after devouring so many ores and minerals! Go bash your head against the enemy it's surely as solid as a hammer!” Tardiff's body trembled from anger at being teased but when it remembered all the ores and crystals it had eaten as well as the many many corpses of the ants it had converted into dark matter, it gave a somewhat weird giddy look.“Have you found any lucent crystal deposits yet?.” Avrin spoke. Ailirion and Tardiff both glanced at him, the glaive hovered down towards Avrin's hands to which he began to weigh it and test it in a slow manner. “Great one….this ant has already failed you….we have not found anything that resembles a lucent crystal deposit….we lack knowledge on where they may form…”Avrin gave a calm expression, he already knew where several deposits were after he's thousand of kilometre divine sense scan, he would have gone himself but they were not in tunnels and were quite literally buried surrounded by dirt, Avrin  opened his hand as a small sphere of knowledge began to form, it contained coordinates to the closest lucent crystal mines around them, he casually tossed the sphere to Ailirion who knew what it was. Ailirion didn't hesitate before his mouth opened to reveal sharpened mandible like teeth and in one go he swallowed the sphere of knowledge, his body trembled for a moment before the information came to his mind.“It will be done great one…” with the sphere of knowledge Avrin simply detailed which one's he wanted to be mined first, and he ordered that the ores at the rare and high-quality level were not to be devoured but stockpiled for him.“Good, Tardiff you're task is a bit different, the lucent crystals mined from these deposits, I want you to create sigil weapons, have a few thousand of your brethren assist you. I want as many of you armed as possible.” Avrin again formed another sphere of knowledge detailing the best and most efficient ways he knew of to form sigil weapons; When he tossed it towards Tardiff, the big creature moved its head and in one go, gulped it down before giving a slight burp, but when the information came to its head it frowned a little.“Boooring!!...” it argued. Avrin also frowned as he looked at it. “That matters not to me, oh yes, any lucent crystals higher than unclouded are to be stockpiled as well, I do not want any devoured, in fact, Tardiff you're banned from where these materials will be stockpiled you eat as much as that buffoon Asura.”Tardiff was a little disappointed being compared to Asura as he felt he was much stronger and could eat more. “Hmmmmm….not dumb lion thing…” it mumbled to itself before standing up and walking towards the giant hole it made.“Ailirion, keep an eye on him and when enough has been gathered simply have it all delivered into this chamber. “ Avrin passed the dark matter sigil glaive to Ailirion who graciously accepted it.“Mr….Avrin?...” Ilisia leaned up as she was rubbing her eyes. “You better go” Avrin spoke to Ailirion who nodded before turning into a flicker of darkness before he vanished back into the hole.“I'm here...” Avrin spoke as he glanced at Ilisia with a thoughtful expression, Ilisia who had woken up suddenly remembered the giant creature, she looked around quickly as if to find it she had an urgent worrying look. “Huh?....w..where's the monster?...”  her words seemed to contain a full trace of fear, Avrin knew eventually she would find out about them so he didn't bother to hide much. “That wasn't a monster, he was one of my followers, he was a little hurt that you called him a monster, but don't worry he won't harm you, he went back to go continue his work, so remember the next time you see him or others with him, try to be polite”Ilisia looked at Avrin from where she was seated on the large pillow, she had an odd look. “Mr. Avrin can make things like that his followers?....so cool…I wonder when I can learn amazing magic like you.”She realised where she was sitting and that she had fainted her cheeks reddened as she felt a little embarrassment, she hopped to her feet and looked at Avrin who was speeding up the sigil creation process as he had fallen behind somewhat. “We will see…” he wasn't sure at all what to do when it came to Ilisia, Calomia's words were still in his mind, he treated her more delicately than Kael. But, Kael wanted to get stronger and made sacrifices and pursued it to change himself, Ilisia, on the other hand, was more fragile and didn't know much about the world, he would prefer until she understood more before doing so after all to his knowledge once one was converted there was no way to convert them back.A sudden sound of footsteps came down as Calomia appeared with a frown on her face she began to call out. “Little troublemaker hurry up I need your help..” she glanced at Ilisia than at Avrin before shaking her head, she noticed the hole in the ground but thought nothing of it other than thinking Avrin may be renovating a bit again.“Yes grandma…” Ilisia sighed and then ran back up to follow Calomia. Outside of shaded moon was much tidier than before, Avrin had made a path that went from the entrance to the main dirt road and even placed a metal signboard stating what the large building was. Several carriages could be seen carrying mercenaries and excited adventurers who had heard about shaded moon from their comrades or by word of mouth, some were on their way to pick up their goods others were here to look at what was the talk about or to make first time orders.A dozen or so individuals could be seen going back and forth carrying small chests that contained their goods. And if one thought carefully about it the situation seemed a bit too innocent for a place that sold weaponry and a device that could explode out with a large spike to kill a creature or person.Avrin had a lot to think about. Tonight he would finally take the step forward and use his amassed energy to upgrade his particles, and then he would have to figure out a way to create the object that would help him to mass produce sigil weapons. If he could figure this out, then he would have a lot more time to spend on different matters.A few hours later within the large lobby area of the shaded moon, Calomia was currently looking at many parchments that littered her desk while speaking to a few customers. She used the kindest tone she could, as to not scare them off. Then again, she was at ease, because no one here seemed to cause trouble especially since they offered prices cheaper than other establishments and the product quality was even better.“Perfect, the order of 2 unclouded sigil weapons and 4 haze crystal sigil weapons should be completed after tomorrow in the morning, the price comes to…” While she was speaking to the customer, three figures came inside the building. One was the old man who was in charge of the Artificer Consortium branch, another was Galum who was wearing a set of clothing similar to the other man who had a clean shaven face with brown hair with a small ponytail. This man had eagle-like eyes, and his strength was quite fierce, he was a mid-level grandmaster and also Galum's teacher.“I... isn't that Artificer Meutin… what is he doing here?...” one of the people noticed the three of them and finally spoke to another, of course, their voices were heard and now many people were looking and recognising them“Oh... boy this won't end well I'm telling you…” a brawny man laughed quietly as he folded his arms while speaking to his comrades, he could tell something was going to go down by the cold angered expression on Meutin the old man's face.Calomia raised her head and noticed the talk and commotion. When she looked at the three she cringed slightly as the words artificer came to her ear. “-that boy Avrin predicted that these people would come eventually, it's a bit later than he thought they must have finally gotten stung hehehe-” she though referring to the fact that their business had taken somewhat of a hit.“Grandma what's an arti...ficer?..” Ilisia who carried several parchments was glancing at Calomia with a curious expression she clearly had no knowledge of who the three were. Calomia looked at Ilisia and reached over to gently pat her head, “go tell Avrin that three people from the Artificer Consortium are here and by the looks of it don't mean well”Ilisia gave a stern expression as she nodded before rushing off with the parchments in hand, Meutin, Galum, and his mentor were walking towards the reception desk, no one dared to get in their way so much so that the customers who were already there were scared stiff and stepped aside, meutin than glanced at Calomia with a cold look. “So this is the shaded moon, I must say I'm a little impressed such an interesting design very very good, though I'm a little disappointed it seems to lack the essence and character of a crafting place for sigils...it has no soul...as expected of a place where cheap imitations are made…”“Cheap imitations?..” one person spoke while another also asked in surprise. “What does he mean?..are these things real or fakes?...” Calomia's brows furrowed, she knew Meutin was sowing seeds of doubt to try and ruin them.----------Avrin's Inner Workings Status ]Dark Stage Control Particles Type 12 100% Dark Stage Particles Type 12 100% God Essence Weapons Astaroth-Scythe Limos-Vajra God Essence Equipment Sarcanus-Armor

chapters.title: V6: Chapter 155 Shaded Moon Vs The Artificer Consortium's Branch.
chapters.content:
!!!!! Pr Credits To  [Peter1765
 Who Help With SR chapters, Please take the time to rep them for their work :) This chapter was pred by peter alone i simply gave it a gloss over, so go easy on the guy as well as me :( that being said any mistakes that ruin the story please pm/comment below.
i'm incredibly tired right now and its only 11:00pm the joys of a sleep schedule. regarding people Pming me i will take a look when i'm not so tired.
Off to bed p.s i'l have 156/157 ready by the end of the weekend to finally clear the queue . ---------------
“If you’re here to cause trouble I will have to ask you to leave quietly…” Calomia didn't want to make things worse or cause trouble for Avrin so she spoke in a not so friendly yet not offensive tone. Meutin glanced at her carefully and gave a rigid hmph! Galum's eyes narrowed somewhat as he softly laughed before shrugging and replying; “Trouble? No trouble we were just stating the truth, we of the Artificer Consortium have been affected by your business’s cheap imitations... is it fine for us who are in the right, who put our heart and soul into a product, to simply sit by and let those people who create fakes and worthless pieces of trash ruin our line of work?”
Calomia's heart stirred with anger, her wrinkled face narrowed as her right hand tightening on the head of the cane Avrin had given her. When it came to this she didn't have much knowledge about the subject but than again she also wasn't dumb, she glanced around to notice the sceptical worried looks from the new customers that had come in and had been waiting for quite awhile, the customers who had been with them for several months knew that their products were the real deal but no one dared to speak out and make an enemy of the Artificer Consortium, especially considering Galum and he's mentor were present.
“Do you have proof that our products are cheap imitations and worthless?” Calomia thought of a simple method, though she never expected that Meutin would softly laugh he's beard shaking slightly as he pulled out the dagger Avrin had given him, it was broken in two pieces with cracks that looked like it had been smashed against a tougher blade, the broken blade head was emitting a weak glow of the same metallic lustre as well as the bottom half of the remaining blade portion and the hilt giving the same weakened glow.
“I myself was quite fascinated with your store's products and decided to test it against one of my own. As you can see the result was not so good....but I'm sure everyone here may have some doubts, so lord Malvin if you will...”
Malvin the man who was Galum's teacher gave no expression as he reached out and pulled out a second dark sigil ring they had managed to coerce someone into selling, he then spoke. “Trigger short sword.” With that, the ring emitted a faint pulse before reforming into a short sword identical to the others that people purchase, everyone wasn't sure what was going on but they knew it was the Artificer Consortium's way of ruining the reputation of a small-time rival.
Malvin then reached into his side and unsheathed a blade no smaller than the dark matter short sword, while holding it up he spoke out. “Ladies and gentlemen as you can see this product is one of our specialities the Zircon silver blade, an uncommon level weapon matched with another uncommon weapon that comes from this store, of course, it would be impossible to mimic this stores methods of creating a sigil weapon by the looks of it, meaning that creating a fake would also be impossible!”
Calomia shook with anger as she glanced at them silently. “-these bastards...they are using Avrin's unique method against him...they must have planned well...such snakes..-”
Malvin then grinned before his arms tensed, with  a quick motion he skillfully crisscrossed slashed the two blades against each other both colliding the collision causing the air to split and crack before the sound of metal shattering echoed across the hall. Shards of dark matter spread out across the room some even hitting people, though Malvin was quick to speak. “Please remain calm! As you can see this weapon from shaded moon is quite volatile and unsafe...it seems once it's broken which can be done so easily it will explode into shards that can damage your allies around you....if you want to be mad at someone well you are in the culprits home base...they are selling you a product that is very dangerous....”
Meutin gave a grin as he listened to Malvin speak, of course they couldn't fault the dark frost mine enough to make it bad for The Shaded Moon, but they could do their best at to ruin their reputation when it came to sigil weapons, he had felt it would be enough to get them away from that business and even ruin their reputation, it may even possibly lead Meutin to a good chance to force the method of creation from Avrin or incite violence.
Calomia backed away as she gave an aged shout from pain, several of the shards had hit her face and she tumbled back weakly and fell to the floor. When she managed to stand up again feeling her entire body was sore she could see the looks of The Shaded Moon's so-called customers, of course, what she didn't expect was that some of these people were planted by the consortium.
“D..damn you Shaded Moon bastards... are you trying to sell us weapons or tickets to hell!...” one of the Consortium's agents spoke while another frowned and replied. “I agree!! And to think I was going to buy a few weapons from you using my hard earned lucent crystals...how can you lot have the heart to treat us hard working adventurers so badly!”
With a few more speaking the entire lobby was in a slight uproar, people began to stand up and prepare to leave. Of course, the smarter customers simply did nothing but enjoy the show or inwardly curse at the Consortium for trying to ruin their chances at being big. After all, it wasn't a secret anymore that they picked The Shaded Moon over the Consortium. If The Shaded Moon did badly, then when they went out of business it would make transitioning to the Consortium much more difficult and they would probably have to pay much more.
“Y..you!!...” Calomia was shaking with anger her body hurt and her heart was filled with fury, her face was bleeding from the shards that had hit her they didn't even bother to warn her, of course for Galum and Meutin the shards were not a big deal at their level.
“Grandma you're bleeding!!” Ilisia came running back up the steps and rushed over worryingly to Calomia glancing at her with a heavy look of worry. “Who hurt you!!” her eyes were filled with tears as her anger grew; She glanced around before looking at the three in front of the desk. “Was it you three?... I'll kill you!!!”
Ilisia truly felt an attachment to her grandma that had raised her since she was a baby; She didn't have anyone but her even more then Avrin who she hadn't known as long, she pulled out one of the sigil rings and roared out. “Trigger dagger!!” while the dagger formed in her hand she rushed towards Malvin who was now 2 meters away and stabbed forward. Of Course, to Malvin her movements were quite slow, so he quickly spoke out.
“You all see this I am just defending myself!” he said as he raised his right hand and punched towards her with no intention of holding back, she was his Consortium's enemy and therefore his enemy, mercy wouldn't be given.
“Stupid child get back!!” Calomia screamed out in fear as she saw Malvin about to punch forward. Ilisia trembled as she had a terrible feeling she stopped a meter away but Malvin simply grinned before punching forward like a mini rocket causing the air to tremble.
The onlookers were truly stunned the child clearly stopped but he intended to still punch forward they all felt this was a disgusting act for someone on his level. “Defending yourself is fine, but trying to kill a child who simply acted on instinct with no mercy given...your quite shameful”
A thump sounded out as Malvin's fist collided against the stomach of a figure, the figure didn't budge an inch as if he were an immovable object, though the sound of bones cracking could be heard between the three as well as Ilisia and the figure that appeared, Malvin suddenly roared out in pain as he pulled his fist back and stumbled backwards, his entire right fist was broken, the situation would be a normal human punching a rock the outcome would not be good.
The figure he had punched was, of course, Avrin. Although Avrin wanted nothing more than to kill these three but he knew it would do more harm than good. So he deciding to control himself, he remained calm. Y..you... how dare you attack me!!” Malvin spoke as he glanced at Avrin with eyes full of rage.
Avrin simply shrugged with his hands somewhat extended, one couldn't see his expression behind the mask he wore. “Attack you?... I simply stood here and your fist hit me, I didn't do anything, it isn't my fault you’re so damn weak, who exactly is attacking who?”
The commotion that occurred made those who were about to leave suddenly stay and look with shock and awe at the situation going down. Meutin seeing Avrin furrowed his brows. “Are you trying to pick a fight with our Consortium... who are you?...”
Avrin turned to glance at Meutin then at Galum who was currently pale with fright and trembling with fear. He ignored Meutin and pointed to Galum. “I'm quite sure you told me that I was not going to see you again. Maybe I was to lenient... as for who I am, I'm the owner of Shaded Moon the business you three are slandering with false evidence!.”
Meutin was stunned as he was ignored so easily by Avrin, though when he looked at Galum and saw his frightful look and how casually Avrin was speaking to him, Meutin felt things weren't as they seemed, he had a bad feeling about this, though he couldn't give up. Since the boss of Shaded Moon was here he needed to make the best out of the situation. “False evidence... how dare you!... in front of everyone we showed how flimsy your product is and how volatile it is!!”
“Flimsy?...” Avrin grinned and looked at Avrin with a soft chuckled before walking away from the small group ignoring Malvin who held his fist and was exercising control with a deep hatred for Avrin and caution. “Ladies and gentlemen. “ Avrin spoke just like Malvin had before. “Since the first sale of my sigil weapon until now, not one has been returned for repairs... that is evidence towards its durability... secondly this allows me the chance to show you all a feature...
Avrin walked over and picked up one of the shards of dark matter as he glanced at it, he smirked and spoke. “Trigger re-forge.” with that the shard pulsed, this pulse caused every other shard that had broken apart to tremble and turn to ash before shooting towards that one shard.
This scene was remarkable in the way that no one knew what was going on, once a weapon was broken it was useless for anything but scrap metal, but right now something astounding was happening, Meutin who was glancing at this was not sure what to think of the situation but he had a bad feeling.
After a few moments, a mass of dark matter was condensing in Avrin's hand formed from the shards that had been broken and spread from Malvin breaking the weapon. The mass of dark matter soon condensed into the shape of a ring, of course within the centre was the haze crystal, lucent crystals themselves were incredibly tough and durable nearly impossible to break. Only someone at the mythical level and higher could break lucent crystals.
With the ring reforged in front of everyone who gazed dumbfoundedly, Avrin spoke. “Trigger short sword.” the ring reshaped into the same weapon  that Malvin had broken before it looked as if it were in perfect shape, of course, the repair would need quite a bit of dark matter which in turn needed mana.
“Reforging a broken dark sigil weapon requires a bit of patience and mana, of course because of my level I can feed it my own to speed up the process, though for others it may take a few hours or a day at most, it surely beats spending more on repairs and sending it off when you need it most...as for the durability...it seems that earlier this weapon was tampered with... it was on the verge of breaking. Most likely it underwent harsh treatment before a final blow broke it...the only thing that could do this would be a weapon of a higher level.”
People began to speak again, they truly were confused as to what to think of the situation, on one side Meutin said Avrin's products were flimsy on the other Avrin clearly showed the weapon could reforge itself after being broken which meant flimsy or not it didn't make a difference.
“You....are you saying that we did something to your weapon?...in front of everyone's eyes we used a weapon of equal rarity against it and your cheap product lost out...how can you even have the guts to speak out after this!!”  Meutin shouted out and pointed at Avrin.
“Equal rarity?....very well since you tested your product against yours... wouldn't it be fair that in front of everyone I test my product against yours this time? Surely you wouldn't find this any issue. In fact, if the same situation repeats itself I will refund everyone's lucent crystals and shut down The Shaded Moon, I will bet everything on this.”
The tale has been taken without authorization; if you see it on Amazon, report the incident.
Meutin frowned and was about to speak but when he looked at everyone glancing at him he knew he needed to be careful, there were many people here who had connections if he said no it meant he would have done something to it and they wouldn't believe him. He clenched his aged teeth, he tried to think of a way out of this. “Such nerve! You still doubt our Artificer Consortium's reputation!! We have existed for many years and built up a high standard, do you think we enjoy seeing others try and steal our work with fakes?”
Avrin smirked before glancing at everyone present. “Clearly, they are worried about being proven wrong surely the mighty consortium will humour me. After all, I am gambling my life while they think they have the right to come here and slander me before leaving...”
Some of the tougher mercenaries couldn't take it anymore one short haired muscular one resembling a barbarian stood up and shouted out. “Just go with the damn test!!! Can't you see the man is risking his life's work on this!! And you Consortium bastards won't do this small task?!!”
Another mercenary an average looking female with a few scars on her face and a band around her head shouted out as well. “We are the customers and we demand to see both sides given a fair view! Let the man do his test!! We deserve the best prices and treatment I would die before going to the Artificer Consortium's branch again without seeing all the evidence first!!”
She roared out, she herself was gambling on this. Many more started to rise up and shout out in agreement. In the end, Malvin's face twisted as his aura surged out, he was much stronger than the rest and when they all felt it they trembled and remained quiet. “All of you watch....” Malvin spoke as he used his uninjured hand to pull out the zircon silver short sword. “Our Artificer Consortium boasts quality and assurance...how can a fake withstand our products!!”
Galum nervously looked at Malvin and spoke. “Lord mentor...please reconsider this....it's a bad idea...that man is dangerous his the...” Galum was interrupted by Meutin who spoke without a hushed tone. “Very well...you want to have a test very well....lord Malvin will attack you...and you will attack him...the superior product will always make its wielder the superior warrior...” Meutin's sense of view in regards to combat surely was twisted it made Avrin cringe somewhat but he did not decline.
“Very well... make your move child beater..” Avrin taunted with a smug grin on his face, his provocation of Malvin was simple and effective, Malvin had been building up the silent anger in his heart for his fist breaking against Avrin, he felt it was a trick or method and he wanted a chance to redeem this stain he felt was made, unable to control himself anymore he dashed forward causing the tile he was under to crack and smash apart as he dashed forward like a taunted lion towards Avrin with the same zircon silver blade he had used to break the dark matter sigil weapon. “Look carefully everyone....see for yourself if this is fake.” Avrin gripped the dark matter sigil weapon in his hand, and as Malvin slashed down towards Avrin not even bothering to go for the weapon he had but for Avrin himself with intent to kill Avrin's sword hand flickered for an instant.
There was no sound of shattering or anything of the like, only a moment went by before the sound of metal clanging against the floor as if it were drop could be heard, a perfectly cut blade head was flat on the surface of the tiles with the end bit cut perfectly.
Malvin's hand was holding the hilt of his weapon as his motion showed his hand and the blade pointed towards the ground after his slash motion, of course when he glanced at his weapon he saw it was missing half of the blade, he  was stunned and glanced at the blade for a moment. The entire lobby area was quiet no one was sure what had happened, they simply just saw Malvin slash down towards Avrin and the blade suddenly losing half of its length.
Malvin glanced at Avrin on instinct and saw the glowing blue eyes behind the mask glance back at him, not filled with disdain but the desire to simply kill him, Malvin felt this intent to kill it made him tremble, it was as if he was caught in an ocean's current during a storm and was unable to surface, he dropped to his knees as he began to sweat.
Of Course, Avrin who expected this was the calmest. “Well... we were planning to test weapons... but it seems the consortium's weapons themselves are so flimsy they can't even take a swing hahahaha...” Avrin's words set off a reaction, the mercenary leaders who had went all in with him also quickly went in on this. “Look at you Consortium freaks... how can you say that shaded moons weapons are of bad quality when it's as Mr. Avrin said... your weapons can't handle a simple swing!” the large barbarian like mercenary called out.
Many others began to speak out while the ones hired by the consortium tried to quickly think of a way to refute this. “You... we aren't done yet... you used a trick... our weapons are of the highest quality! Lord Malvin stop messing about if you please!” Meutin shouted out his old vocal cords sounding broken.
Malvin who felt Avrin's intent vanish trembled with anger, he had never been so humiliated before in his life. “You... think you're superior to us...!! ...than me?!!” he shouted out before he quickly unsheathed another weapon, this weapon was of higher quality it was a rare weapon the Consortium specially designed for high paying buyers, the blade was curved slightly and was a misty green colour,  on the back of the blade it had a leather sort of covering, the materials used for this were a special nature attuned metal that started off as an acorn within a special rare tree from their headquarters the acorn would then be placed inside another tree to which it would absorb the nature energy until the tree died, from there it would be moved from tree to tree until the centre of the acorn formed a clump of metal from the accumulated energy. The leathery part was made from the hide of a bull creature that appeared like a lizard a grandmaster creature the woodland impaler.
Avrin knew this level of weapon was the only legitimate way it could cause trouble for his uncommon level sigil weapons, he knew that before they had weakened his blade through by cheap methods before bringing it to The Shaded Moon to break, he simply frowned he didn't want to go too far and repeat the same method before, this time as Malvin glanced at him with red eyes of hatred and moved forward with no intention of holding back, as he clearly wanted to butcher Avrin. Avrin's hand moved again. But this time, it was visible enough for everyone to see so no doubts would be given.
The blades collided with several sparks shooting out, Avrin wanted everyone to clearly see his weapon was capable. “Incredible...if I recall correctly Malvin's weapon is one of the Consortium's rare products a nature scimitar... such a bizarre scene, that the dark sigil weapon that Mr. Avrin reforged is able to hold it off... lord Malvin is a grand master... surely his strength with a rare quality weapon would break a weapon of lower quality... but it seems as if the weapon quality of lord Avrin's is no less....”
One of the mercenary leaders who was quiet before finally spoke out, he wanted to take a neutral stance until now that is, as he glanced at the scene he was dumbfounded yet excited because Meutin's claims about Shaded Moon were put to rest.
“That isn't all... look at Mr. Avrin!... he isn't breaking a sweat at all he hasn't budged a bit since clashing against lord Malvin... his strength must truly be something... it's as if he is treating lord Malvin like a child!” the female mercenary leader spoke up again with fascination.
Meutin's wooden stave like cane was clutched tightly within his wrinkled right hand to the point where the hand was pale from him clutching it too tightly. “This is impossible...” Meutin was stunned as he glanced at Malvin slash away towards Avrin like an angered infant having a tantrum, it didn't matter what skill or ability he used to try and attack Avrin's open guard, every time his blade neared it would be deflected or blocked by Avrin's dark matter sigil weapon with no effort at all.
“Why won't you die!!” Malvin roared out to Avrin, who loved these situations the most because it meant he could take control. “While this young man runs out of steam... I  hope you all can see that my weapons ability is no less than that of the Consortium's. In fact, it seems they are going as far as to use a rare weapon against my weapon of uncommon quality and I am still able to easily hold out... this is evidence that they must have used some dirty method to weaken my product beforehand... how would I dare sell cheap products to everyone... wouldn't that mean that all my effort in establishing a name for myself in the future would be in vain?”
Avrin did his best to speak in a clear concise manner with words that made sense. Of course, that he was fighting while speaking in a casual manner stunned many spectators; Because, wasn't he fighting an individual who was a renown lord and grandmaster that wanted to kill him? Yet he could easily block and parry as well as think carefully on his words.
“Amazing!” one mercenary laughed out, and another, of course, followed suit. “I knew Mr. Avrin's products were of high quality... I have to thank these Consortium fellows if it wasn't for today I wouldn't have known that with a simple word we could reforge our broken dark sigil weapons as well as see with our own eyes that Mr. Avrin's weapons can match up against a rare quality weapon of theirs!”
Everyone speaking were those leaders of the groups who either took a neutral stance or who sided with Avrin and would lose a lot if the Consortium gained this victory. Eventually, Malvin jumped back as he panted for breath glancing at Avrin with no more anger but a worrying fear, he felt Avrin could kill him whenever yet he treated him as such.
Meutin glanced at Malvin and then at Avrin. “This... you dare to make a mockery out of our Consortium!.” Meutin seemed to be quite angry himself, his plans that he carefully plotted had gone down the drain and now Avrin had so effortlessly turned them into the villains.
“If you three are done, you can leave now. Also never return....you are not welcome in this store as well as my land anymore...” Avrin's words were like hot steel being smacked against Malvin and Meutin's faces, red with anger and being made a show of Meutin was going to speak but Galum walked closer to him and whispered.
“Senior Meutin... I ... I believe we should be careful... this Avrin fellow can surely kill us... not even my master could hold up to him... maybe its best if we leave...” Galum who experienced Avrin's ferocity before didn't want to take a chance especially since he told Avrin they wouldn't meet again.
“Are you siding with him now?... hmph... though... this matter seems larger than I thought... hmph!... Malvin... let's... return..” Meutin spoke his sentence reluctantly as he was grinding his teeth together.
Malvin of course who was exhausted and experiencing many dangerous emotions as well as had a broken hand was trembling with anger and fear as he looked at Avrin glance casually at him. “This isn't over...” he mumbled before sheathing his weapon he turned and walked over towards Meutin who glanced around at everyone here it seemed he had one more plan install.
“Those of you who follow me now regardless if you had joined this Shaded Moon or not in the past, follow me now and not only will you be forgiven....you will be given a permanent 40% off all purchases otherwise those who don't will be banned permanently from any Consortium branch and affiliated stores!”
Avrin's eyes narrowed as he smirked. “-sly old dog-” he thought. He could see Meutin wanted to salvage the situation, and as he saw the three walk out he spotted several reluctant and happy mercenaries who were definitely hired by him follow Meutin, Malvin and Galum out, a total of 16 people left leaving Avrin with this situation.
“-you made me your public enemy, I no longer need to hold back...watch me run you out of this region-” Avrin was concocting up a scheme to ruin the Consortium's branch within this region, to him they only did harm with no good.

chapters.title: Chapter 166: Temporary Break.
chapters.content:
IMPORTANT! Hey Guys firstly sorry this isn't a new chapter, basically i'm going to be taking a break from writing hopefully spanning a few weeks. The reason being i wasn't satisfied with my past job as i was getting tired easy and lacked stamina. So i decided to work with my brother as a tradesman, to work on improving my health. I felt hard labour would help me out, and it definitely has i can see the difference in nearly 2 months. Though i'm still not used to it yet i come home physically exhausted which affects my writing ability i'm to tired to think. i just need time off to focus on my job for now  that being said i don't have writers block at all i just need to ease up and get a proper amount of rest until i'm satisfied with myself adapting to the job.
If you discover this narrative on Amazon, be aware that it has been stolen. Please report the violation.
that being said if i have spare time i will definitely be writing down plot ideas in a personal document i keep for myself so when i go back to writing i can smoothly clear that queue and more when i return. i'm hoping to come back in 1 month and hopefully surprise you all with a few releases and that artwork piece i'm having done.
i look forward to writing for you guys "hopefully" within a month. i hope you all understand my position not even i am free from the burdens of life.P.S to the people who pmed me i apologise i wasn't able to reply just yet atm i'm incredibly tired still not used to that 7-3:30 + 7 days a week schedule but its definitely enjoying.
P.S.S by habit i spent 15 mins going over this after finishing typing but i realised i don't need to post anything else hahaha.
