Amias glanced with surprise before dashing back and making some space between him and Avrin. He entered a combat stance while looking at Avrin as if he were a monster. “I don’t need handouts, and I don’t need your help. No, especially because it’s you!!” he spoke in a loud tone. His words seemed to trigger something, as the daggers reformed in his hand. He dashed towards Avrin while swinging the daggers, causing purple lines to form in the air as he slashed towards Avrin.
“Everyone seems to like me a bit too much or hate me...” he frowned before raising his finger. As Amias barraged him with well aimed and timed slashes, Avrin’s right arm and hand blurred as his finger perfectly blocked each attack whether it was from the front, sides or the back.
“Hate you? You’re the one who hates me. What are you talking about!” Amias grew madder as a frenzied look appeared on his face. His speed began to pick up and he grew faster and faster.
Avrin’s brows furrowed with curiosity and amazement. “-How is he getting faster?-” Avrin managed to keep up with his pace, but when glancing at Amias he felt a familiar yet strange feeling of dark matter. “I don’t hate you. Or maybe you’re referring to the time where you tried to befriend me. I admit I did treat you coldly. I won’t deny I did wrong. But you have to know I was in no position to have anyone close to me.”
“Shut up with your excuse...” Amias’ lips curled into a crazed smile as his eyes darkened. His skin began to emit a faint orange mist as he had gotten even faster, his daggers slashing about like typhoons.
Izanami was shocked and stunned. She had never seen Amias like this and she couldn’t even see his movements clearly. Avrin, of course, matched his speed. Avrin seemed to be focusing on Amias carefully. “-This little guy actually managed to figure out Frenzied matter? What a monster...-” Avrin was a little envious of Amias’ ability to figure out the Frenzied matter, but he also knew just how angry one had to be to obtain it. He felt guilty because he also knew he was the reason. He wondered just how long it had lingered in Amias’ mind. “Fine,” Avrin spoke as he no longer blocked. It was then that Amias gave a quick stab towards Avrin’s chest, the blade slashing in several inches as Avrin had purposely weakened his body’s durability with his mastery over his own particles.
“I know I wronged you. I wronged many people on this planet, but how do you expect to get over it if you don’t let me make up for things. I’m offering you a way to improve yourself. I don’t plan to give you handouts, I won’t accept those into my race who think it is a free ticket to luxury without at least putting some effort in.“
Seeing his blade enter Avrin, the orange glow around Amias trembled before dissipating. This was because Avrin’s actions to let him stab him as well as his words had finally gotten to him. Amias pulled the dark matter dagger out of Avrin’s chest and watched as the wound healed in seconds.
“I don’t know...” he spoke. If it had been the old him he would have taken him up in an instant, but things still couldn’t be fixed so easily, he wanted time to think about it. “I understand, take your time. I will be returning to Seleria every now and then so you have plenty of time.”
Amias blinked as he heard something of interest. He raised his head and spoke. “Returning to Seleria? What do you mean by that?” Avrin gave a slight grin and shrugged. “Did you really think Seleria is the only planet that is inhabited? There are billions upon billions of planets with life, and that is only a drop in an ocean. I plan to increase my own strength and my race’s strength so one day we can proudly travel without fear of being attacked. Finding many interesting things and improving our strength, one day there may be even another god born within our race beside me.”
Avrin hadn’t hesitated a moment to take advantage of Amias’ curiosity. He could see the same interest in the boy's eyes as when he had first met him. Amias looked surprised and began to daydream a little about what he could accomplish. “I accept!!” he quickly spoke up.

chapters.title: V6: Chapter 170 An Empowering Plan
chapters.content:
“--All of you, gather--” Avrin's words echoed within the minds of all the pure-bloods. While some shivered, others jumped in excitement, however, they all made their way towards city's main area, where the largest structure within the Spectral city stood.
After Amias accepted Avrin's deal, along with Izanami, they all began to talk about past events, using the opportunity to bring each other up to date. Although Izanami was not a pure blood he knew her personally; not to mention her information collecting skills would be valuable if the time called for it. However, there was a lot for Avrin to learn about Amias. After their conversation, Avrin divine stepped both of them to the tower peak where he introduced them to the others.
With Izanami at his left and Amias standing on his right with a curious and stoic expression. The pure-bloods began to appear after reaching the distance for their Divine Sense to allow them to divine step. Meanwhile, Avrin had to personally divine step Tardiff and Ailirion as they had not reached that level yet.
“Master, you have been calling us quite...ooh?...” Asura was ready to complain as he had been watching a sparring match between two Spectrals while chewing on some meat but when he glanced at Izanami he made a sound that wasn't befitting of him and was more fitting for a stunned monkey.
His body trembled and he froze for a moment. He felt as if the whole world froze. In that moment, not even Avrin who was beside her was visible, only she was. He had never felt like this before; Izanami to him was simply too incredibly attractive. “Mua....wiauas...nawua...”
As Asura stood slightly hunched over, with his jaw dropped revealing the chunks of flesh between his teeth, Eitri, who walked by him, glanced with a strange look. “Stupid beast, are you sick or something? Out of the way. Hey, Avrin, this creature needs to be put down... hehe.” Eitri gave a cruel remark before standing a small distance from Asura's side.
Tardiff passed by him with a silent groan as he looked around and reached up to scratch his head. “Nmmmm.....” Seeing that there was no seat big enough for him, he leaned back and sat on his butt, causing the room to shake a little.
“Lord Monarch, is everything alright?” Erebus, who had been the first to arrive, asked. To his side, also a distance away, Ailirion kept silent, as if he knew Avrin would speak when ready.
“Master? Who are these two?” asked Kael who had arrived last. Dressed in azure blue silk and linen attire, he looked at Izanami who seemed to be glancing at everyone while trying to ignore Asura's gaze as if she felt like he was thinking lesser thoughts. Then she glanced at Kael and seeing that he resembled Amias’ age, she gave a cute wave towards him.
Kael's cheeks reddened as he reached up, covering his mouth as he cleared his throat. He could feel that Izanami was somehow different from the Spectrals he had met here. Meanwhile, he noticed a piercing glance aimed at himself. Turning, he fixed his gaze onto Amias, who was looking at Kael carefully as if he were sizing him up.
Both of the two boys felt their eyes twitch, as if static was in the air. It as if some sort of rivalry had just been born. “Good! You are all here. I won't waste time, but I want to introduce you all to Izanami and Amias. Both of them are from backgrounds that specialize in hand to hand combat or as you know from my Sphere of Knowledge, martial arts. Izanami is quite good at retrieving information and while I believe she can improve; in combat, she is currently better than any of you without the use of powers. She is not a pure blood.”
Erebus frowned a little as he looked at Izanami. “-Who is this woman?... Obtaining information? Better than any of us? Hah, I don't believe that-” of course Erebus kept his thoughts to himself, not daring to speak out of character.
Ailirion, of course, was more subtle with his words and instead chose to voice them. “Great One, I do not doubt your words, but when will there ever be a need to retrieve information? I believe that with our strength, we will reach a point where no one will be a threat to us as long as we keep ourselves out of the public eye for an extended period of time.”
Avrin listened carefully to Ailirion. Out of all of them, he seemed to be the best listener and most respectful towards him, followed very closely by Erebus. “Your point is valid Ailirion, you would be very surprised to know just how powerful some individuals are out there. I want you to remember this, in fact, all of you remember this. There are other creatures and people out there that have been living for many millions and even billions of years, lurking in the depths of existence. Do not think that if we hide and strengthen ourselves for a few hundred or a thousand years that we can come close to matching them.”
Izanami and Amias stood stunned and confused as they listened to Avrin's words. This information was somewhat new to them. Beings that lived for so long were unimaginable to them, how would something bare to live for so long, would they accomplish everything? That was one of their thoughts as they pondered carefully.
“I understand Great One. Thank you for enlightening this humble servant.” Ailirion bowed with his right arm across his chest. The other pure-bloods watched silently. Even Asura had broken out of his stupor and focused even though he still gave Izanami side glances, trying to be as inconspicuous as he could be. Nevertheless, the Spectrals thought on Avrin's words.
“Next is her younger brother, Amias. I'm sure some of you have seen or met him since that incident, this young man is quite impressive. His strength is already at the mid-expert level by Seleria's standards and he hasn't even begun training his particles yet. Not only that, but he is an Enigma ability user.“
Avrin carefully watched their reactions but his gaze focused upon Kael. His words were targeted towards him, as he felt this was a perfect opportunity for a rivalry that would set off improvement. Kael, of course, trembled slightly, his fists clenching only a little as they remained behind his back. He kept a calm look while looking at Avrin, yet he decided to speak, not daring to be a coward in this moment as he had changed from his past self.
“Master, I am not a fool. If you want to spark a rivalry between us I do not mind improving myself but....he...he isn't even as strong as me, let alone a pure blood. When you brought him to us he was at the level of early trained by our judgements before he suddenly left and, yes, after a few years he is now an expert...but I trained hard as well and made more improvements!”
Amias’ expression darkened somewhat but he kept calm and then looked to Avrin, whose lips had curved into a rare grin. “Dear Kael, you have indeed changed to speak to me like that, very good! In fact, you’re right and you’re wrong. Right that I want to use this as an opportunity to make you improve, but not just you, the others as well.”
When Avrin spoke the other pure-bloods all gave curious expressions and they paid more attention. “You see,” Avrin pointed towards a small, makeshift necklace hanging around Amias' neck. It was made with simple materials with a small purple sphere as the main attraction.
“A pure-blood conversion core.” this time it was Erebus who carefully spoke those words. They all glanced at him for a moment before looking at Amias carefully. “It is, from that day I brought him back from the Deities of Seleria. I gave that conversion core to Erebus to give to Amias, but...Amias chose to not absorb it and convert. Not yet of course.”
Avrin glanced at him carefully. Avrin had talked to Amias about this when he asked him about the conversion core, thinking Erebus had forgotten it, but Amias pulled it out from under his training attire and showed it to Avrin.
--Flashback---
Within the open area, Izanami was carefully glancing with her petite hands behind her as she leaned over to peek at the conversion core Amias was showing Avrin, listening to her brother's words with a hint of jealousy and admiration in her eyes.
“Why I didn't absorb it then?....well I hadn't made up my mind. It hadn't taken me long to find Grandfather and the others as there is a set location we have for emergencies, in this case when the dragons attacked. Grandfather told me to devour the conversion core after the rebirth, every Spectral calls it?...uhh, but after the rebirth....I felt...I felt as if I needed to challenge myself, and that's exactly what I did. As I said, I don't want easy handouts. This thing makes me more pure right? Stronger? I find it a bit unfair. I won't need it, not yet.”
Avrin couldn't help but glance with admiration and approval, in fact, he wished the other pure-bloods had this sort of mindset, as they would all be stronger as a result of this. “Well said.” Avrin couldn't help but say. It reminded him of several soldiers that had shown great discipline.
----Flashback end----
“I see Amias as having a lot of potential. Kael, I told you before that being a pure-blood doesn't guarantee you will be at the peak. Amias is a good example of this. Although he hasn't reached that peak yet, given sufficient time he will be on par with all of you. So I recommend taking the time to train when possible. I understand that I have given you all tasks to handle, but in between there is quite a bit of free time. Kael and Asura, of course, you both will have an advantage once we go to Shaded Moon as there are many more high-quality Lucent crystals. That being said, be sure to make the best of that advantage.”
Stolen from its rightful place, this narrative is not meant to be on Amazon; report any sightings.
Kael trembled slightly and gave things a second thought before nodding. “Yes, Master.” Asura also nodded and said the same thing. “Later today I will go collect every single piece of dark matter crystal and store it here. When the vault is completed, Erebus and Ailirion, you are both in charge of storing it there.”
“Yes Lord Monarch.” Erebus spoke while Ailirion followed suite. “As you wish Great One.” Avrin looked at Izanami and spoke. “Will you be fine here or did you prefer I take you back to the south?”
Izanami thought carefully before speaking. “I would prefer to go back to the south and help where I can. I think Amias should remain here and train.” Avrin glanced over to Amias who didn't seem bothered where he got to stay as long as it didn't negatively impact his training.
“Very well, Amias here.” Avrin extended his hand, causing a small patch of nebula mist to form in the air then reform into a small Sphere of Knowledge containing some basic information as well as how to train one's particles and eventually the dark space.
“This contains what you need to know. As talented as you are, without a path you're going to stagnate. The rest of you are all dismissed except Asura. You are going to show Amias around. Afterward, prepare to leave tomorrow morning.” Avrin glanced at Asura who looked as if he was wronged.
“Nmmmnm...Fine...” he hesitantly spoke before glancing at Amias cautiously. “Eitri, before you go, you also need to prepare some things for tomorrow morning. I will most likely need your help with handling Sigil requests at the Shaded Moon, it will give me more free time to handle other matters.”
Eitri nodded without disagreeing and soon most of pure-bloods departed, including Amias who went with Asura. However, there were a few that remained; Tardiff, Ailirion, Izanami, and Avrin. Avrin glanced over at Ailirion carefully before using a divine sense link. “--Is something wrong?--” Avrin spoke, Ailirion immediately replied. “--Please reconsider your decision in putting Erebus in charge of the dark matter crystals with me, I do not trust him...--” Ailirion was quite blunt with it.
Avrin gave a sudden faint smile. Izanami glanced at him and then Ailirion. She could tell quickly that they were speaking privately so she didn't interfere. “--Ailirion, I will just say this, don't think I would leave a small pot of honey within a bee hive without reason. I could simply store it all away within my dark space and be done, but sometimes it's best to check which are the bees...and which are the wasps--”
Avrin's reasoning was simple. When he had absorbed their memories before, he had felt something strange, as if some things were not real and seemed synthetic. He couldn't tell who it was from, the feeling was like comparing a real fleshy steak to a foam steak that looked identical. You couldn't tell the difference and Avrin wasn't skilled enough just yet to be able to get closer and touch both steaks to see the difference, so this was the next solution. A bit rushed, but it would do.
This way by gathering all the dark matter crystals from the world it would avoid conflict with anyone else on the outside and contain it here. Avrin wouldn't keep things too unprotected but he also felt it would be good to at least allow the pure-bloods a chance to see if they can figure out the mystery behind the dark matter crystals.
“--Yes Great One, I trust in your words and I will take my leave--” Ailirion bowed again before turning around and leaving. Tardiff finally glanced at Avrin with a quiet pondering look. “Uhh...” he muttered out before Avrin glanced at him.
“Oh, I almost forgot. Tardiff, do your best to train your particles. The sooner you open your dark space the better.” with that said Avrin divine stepped him from the tower’s peak back to his previous location. After that he glanced at Izanami. “I have my own matters to tend to, give my regards to your grandfather.”
“Of course,” she replied with a soft smile, and within moments Avrin divine stepped her away. Avrin was then left by himself in the tower's peak. His face darkened for a moment before he vanished then reappeared nearly two-hundred kilometers in the sky within the orbit of Seleria.
He glanced down at the planet and suddenly his body shook for a moment before an invisible tidal wave of energy surged out from him and washed over Seleria from top to bottom, inside and out.
His focus was careful when controlling this. It was his Divine Sense. While he was more serious, right now he could detect many things. He could sense the smallest of pebbles to chunks of ore, he couldn't help but sigh as he spotted many legendary pieces of ore but he chose to leave those alone. He felt a little regret for Seleria and felt maybe someone would discover them after he left. He wouldn't steal from the planet anymore and would just take what needed to be taken. A total of one-thousand-three-hundred and eighty-four sources of dark matter crystals scattered around Seleria, Avrin was fascinated at the fact that there were never dark matter crystals buried too deeply, they all seemed to remain within the upper or mid-crust area, the deepest simply being within the edge of the lithosphere and the crust area.
With a thought, each of those dark matter crystals, enormous or insignificant, trembled before vanishing. Within moments, just like before, the crystals were all above Avrin and were being clumped together by him. They spanned nearly one-hundred meters high while being twenty meters wide. Avrin was simply amazed now that he saw it with his eyes.
“-I could become incredibly powerful very quickly if I....no...-” he snapped out of his thoughts before raising his right hand. Dark matter trickled out and formed into a dense Nebula Mist-like spray that covered the entirety of the dark matter crystals, forming into a rigid dark purple rock-like shell with only a small arm’s length area opened to expose the crystals. This was where the purebloods would obtain the dark matter crystals for examining.
Avrin vanished, taking the large covered clump of dark matter crystals with him. When he reappeared he was within a small cave formation. The clump appeared with him and caused the small cave to shake and crack slightly. Avrin glanced around and then looked up. “This is deep enough.” With that said, Nebula Mist surged out of him like a deathly aura that formed into the shape of a square. It then began to expand out upward and sideways. Everything that was touched was absorbed and neatly turned to ash. The ground was seemingly kept flat so perfectly it seemed like it was waxed despite being dirt and rock.
Within moments the small cave formation was turned into a square shaped room just large enough to fit this clump of dark matter crystals. With the creation of the room done, Avrin raised his hand and began forming a very strange mass of dark matter. It began to stir and move as if it were alive.
Avrin had placed several particles and control particles in this from his own body as well as a special surprise for whoever was going to betray him. He pointed the mass towards the covered clump of dark matter crystals and it flew over like a bullet crashing into the shell and digging in before the energy of the mass spread out, causing blue veins of energy to form around that shell that began pulsing as they gathered dark matter from the surroundings at a fair pace, only enough to sustain itself.
Avrin lowered his hand and looked around, this would be where the vault would be made. He had done the hard part of making it wide and long enough in a few seconds which would have taken over a hundred Spectrals a few days to do the same. “--Erebus, Ailirion--” Avrin contacted them with his Divine Sense and began to explain where the entirety of the clump was. After which they told him they would handle the rest.
Avrin soon vanished. When he reappeared he was not on Seleria but outside it, just at the edge of the aura-like sphere where it was easier for him to divine step. From there he entered the Spectral domain and glanced around carefully. He looked around and then his body tensed up before the space around him trembled for a moment. His Divine Sense surged out at its maximum capacity and strength stretching on and on. It was not fifty-thousand kilometers anymore but a massive one-hundred-thousand, showing his advancement had affected it greatly.
Within that one-hundred-thousand he found nothing different or odd. He couldn't detect any life, but what he did feel was mana, a lot of mana. The Spectral domain of this universe was made of mana, and now Avrin felt he could absorb freely without impacting anyone.
“Limos.” Avrin extended his right hand and soon the Vajra God Essence weapon appeared. The moment it did, an eye formed within its core that glanced around before looking at Avrin.
Avrin then shot forward with his entire strength. He seemed like a shooting star, especially when considering the space under his feet rippled from the energy. He had only stopped when he was sixty-thousand kilometers away, a fair distance, and even when he expanded his Divine Sense again he felt nothing.
“Let's begin. I have the remainder of the day to get as much as I can. Do your best, Limos.” As Avrin sat cross-legged while holding Limos in his lap, the space underneath him trembled as if it were solid.
“Sarcanus.” the God Essence armor immediately reacted to Avrin's words, engulfing him in a white mist before his armor was formed along with the bone-like wing structure with the rod ends.
Soon those very rods split off from the rest and shot forward several meters. Limos followed suit. Avrin wasn't 100% proficient with controlling Limos and he didn't trust the weapon very much, however, Sarcanus seemed to be quite affectionate towards Avrin.
The rod ends began to connect together to form a long, pillar-like rod that pressed against the chest plate of the armor on Avrin's chest, vein-like lines embedding themselves within as if they were grafted there.
The top end of the rod repeated the same thing but this time to Limos, which, despite looking about strangely with its eye, didn't do anything. From there, Limos trembled before the top of the Vajra began to emit a strange dark light. A crack seemingly began to form that expanded outwards and began to swirl almost like a vortex. The moment this vortex appeared, mana began to gather from the area around it, then into it, and from there it would siphon down the pillar-like rod formed by Sarcanus and into Avrin.
“More....expand much more...is this all you can do?” Avrin's eyes opened as he glanced at Limos’ eye. The eye glanced back and trembled before it let out a shriek. The vortex suddenly cracked and ripped apart before reforming and expanding not a few feet but this time it had started off several dozens of meters and kept expanding at a rapid pace.
“Nnm....” Avrin was a little stunned as he felt the mana enter Limos, then become converted to dark matter and then siphon into him. Almost immediately he began to will his body into overdrive. He had obtained this idea when he felt the effects of the dark matter crystal. In the sense, it was simply dark matter that was very compact, but with a strange negative addiction as a side effect. But what if he could repeat it and surpass that compact energy without the side effect?
He then remembered the domain. The sight was something to behold, it was like a mini whirlpool in space that spanned several hundred meters, absorbing mana at such a rapid pace that blue streams of it began to form as it entered the vortex.
The rod-like pillar connecting Limos to Avrin was emitting a heavy purple light as it was siphoned to Avrin. “-I'm not greedy...your strength is my strength....-” Avrin then began to feed his ravenous particles to increase them, after which he willed the dark matter to feed his God Essence equipment, which would empower them, although slightly, was still a difference. He still had enough spare to store in his dark space. This was because Limos kept expanding. The edge of the whirlpool-like vortex emitted crackling sparks of purple electricity.
“I hold God’s Heart the Fragment of creation...if I cannot construct a way to empower myself at a rapid pace then who can?” Avrin spoke in a rare form of self-flattery as he thought this was an incredible idea.
His particles were no longer limited to constraining themselves on rationed dark matter. They were devouring at such a rate that each one emitted a purple hue of light which in turn affected Avrin's exterior appearance. He was emitting that same purple hue, as it seemed small sparks of light flickered about him.
“--Limos, stop at one-thousand meters. If I can keep this up for the remainder of the day it seems I can strengthen myself enough to maybe reach the peak of the Void stage, but the Rift stage...what exactly is it...--”
Avrin knew it didn't matter if he kept absorbing power. In the end, if he didn't understand how to progress, the amount of energy his body had wouldn’t matter. It was like having a device and then plugging in a charge that gave it triple the amount of power it needed to work. It would not make the device faster and might very well ruin it over time.
When Avrin's thought reached Limos, the vortex suddenly halted, but by now it was like a small hole in space and from a distance quite terrifying. The Spectral domain was an incredible space and contained more mana than the outside, this was because there was such a lack of lifeforms in here that the mana would gather in abundance without any use, making it quite a hub for Avrin.
Avrin's teeth clenched as his body tensed up. He felt exhilarated and refreshed, as if he could do anything. The feeling in itself was exciting, as if he was constantly being pumped with adrenaline. Little did he know that from a distance of several million miles away there was a small moon, and within this moon it was completely hollowed out leaving only a deadly darkness that could affect one's soul.
Within this darkness a glowing purple eye formed and then more began to form in near instants, until several hundreds upon thousands of large eyes had formed. These eyes all resembled that of Spectrals, all of which were looking towards a direction, towards Avrin.

chapters.title: V6: Chapter 171 Escape!.
chapters.content:
“-Incredible I can't believe how perfect this place is for increasing my strength, my control particles have already reached 80% completion whilst my normal particles have reached 20% completion, with the mana amassed in this domain I won't have to worry about the risk of failing to reach type 14 particles.-”
As more mana was sucked into the vortex, Avrin's absorption limit steadily increased with the strength of his particles. Meanwhile blue and purple charges of static were skidding across Limos as well as the rods that siphoned the mana to Avrin formed by Sarcanus.
“-with the mana gathered in this domain I wonder how far I can reach, obligations though truly are a bothersome thing, for now, though I’ll just..-” Avrin blinked as he felt something strange as if the pool of dark matter and mana had suddenly decreased and was being drained even further.
Opening his eyes he gasped in surprise because surrounding the vortex were strange apparitions that seemed transparent with no real physical feature except for the single glowing purple eye on the center of the forehead that had glowing veined lines that stretched around their bodies.
“-what the hell are those things?-” Avrin was at a loss for words as he watched them, but he suddenly came to a realization that these wraith-like creatures were absorbing the mana and even the dark matter that Limos was gathering, Limos was screeching as it was surrounded by those creatures that latched onto it.
Streams of the two energies were being drawn into the glowing purple eyes. “Hey....HEY! THAT’S MINE! YOU VULTURES!!” emitting a heavy phantom pulse every single wraith-like creature was pushed several hundred meters away and space rippled from the change in gravity. However, the creatures did not appear to be harmed at all, they began to gather again and even more began pouring out and started to appear within Avrin's divine sense. They came from asteroids and other celestial bodies but the main point of origin seemed to be a single hollowed out moon.
“My dark matter!!” Avrin wanted to cry out at the unfairness of it all, he removed the rod from the chest plate of Sarcanus and vanished with great speed appearing next to one wraith he glared at it but it seemed to ignore him.
He formed a void sphere in his hand and fired it towards the creature in disgust. But the moment the void sphere neared the wraith it trembled before it was instantly absorbed into the glowing purple eye.
“.....” Avrin backed away a little, he didn't dare to use his hists after seeing what had happened, instead, he thought of another plan. “Astaroth.” the moment the god essence weapon appeared a heavy surge of bloodlust and killing intent seeped out of it engulfing a large portion of the area, this was not unnoticed by the creatures that suddenly glanced at Avrin.
There was an eerie silence for a few seconds that made Avrin's body tense, he quickly got into a defensive stance and moments afterward the creatures shot towards Avrin like stars skimming across the night sky.
Entering a battle stance, Avrin brandished Astaroth with great skill; using the scythe to slash through space cutting several wraiths in half.
However, their bodies simply flew apart for a few moments, before the two halves would give an electrical current that would fuse the two halves back together. After which, the wraith would appear a bit smaller.
Avrin gave a slight grunt as he smirked. “All of you bastards, keep coming, I'm going to take back what you stole from me!” Avrin was not going to let these things go, right now he simply willed Limos to absorb as much as it could from the space. While he fought off these wraiths, he fount it funny that occasionally one of these wraith-like creatures would be a bit too greedy and would get too close to the vortex causing it to be nearly devoured as it's energy was quickly drained after which it would flee for safety.
To Avrin it was like a swarm was attacking him from all sides. Surrounding himself with his phantom pulse, he kept attacking with Astaroth. Meanwhile, the wraith creatures unable to penetrate his defenses, gradually became weaker as they were repeatedly cut in half.
This had lasted for several minutes before they all stopped attacking and simply surrounded Avrin. As he glanced around, he grew a bit nervous as he realized that these creatures numbered not in the thousands but hundreds of thousands and they stared at him with their glowing purple eyes that although strange were oddly familiar. Yet he didn't dare let his guard down especially when a moment later a wraith emitted a deep vocal echo and then the others followed suite.
When hundreds of thousands of these creatures emitted such a chilling sound it was bound to make one tremble. Avrin felt a heavy tinge of danger as the wraith creatures all shot towards one location and began to fuse into a large mass of energy, as this mass of energy grew larger it eventually began to take shape.
Avrin wanted to tell what sort of energy these creatures were made off but it was hard for him to do so, they weren't mana or qi, in fact, the closest thing they resembled was dark matter, a very odd dark matter that wasn't dark matter at all.
“.LIMOS!!” Avrin felt a great very dangerous feeling, Limos suddenly broke out of the vortex before it reappeared in front of Avrin, the moment it did, the creature had formed, Avrin was stunned and nearly afraid of how strong it felt, he could feel how powerful the energy was despite not being able to tell what it was. By Avrin's estimation, this strange wraith-like apparition had an energy mass at the middle supreme deity level. The creature formed from this fusion of hundreds of thousands of wraiths was simply a featureless face that emitted a chilling transparent white aura the face had lips that gave neither smile nor grin, it was simply a straight face, the eyelids were closed, and the most chilling thing was the enormous purple eye on its forehead there were veined lines stretching across the face connected to this eye.
What frightened Avrin the most about this eye was that its pupil was identical to his, it was a double sided “”T”” the eye pulsed for a moment before two sparks of light entered the middle section of the top and bottom of this “”T”” which then began to rotate clockwise, it began to become faster and faster until it formed a full circle from the afterimage it formed. Avrin's dark matter heart began to suddenly beat quickly as if it was warning him of a danger,
Avrin felt that it was not a good idea to be here even though he was planning to use Limos to defend himself. “Fucking shit...” he clenched his teeth before grasping Limos in his hand as well as the rod Sarcanus had formed, the moment he did he froze for a moment before his eyes widened, he quickly focused all of his strength and energy into a divine step despite it being incredibly hard, the spinning “”T”” of the creatures pupil suddenly stopped which caused the surrounding space within the domain to crack somewhat, on the opposite side of the domain within the real space one would notice many cracks and fragments of space forming.
The two specks of energy within both sides of the “”T”” were forced to smash against each other within the middle of the “”T”” causing a tyrannical mass of energy to pulse outward, Avrin was frightened even more so than when he had faced Orphelium, he quickly divine stepped 30,000 kilometers away.
From a distance he could see simply a bright flash before a ray of light that resembled a pulse-like wave of energy shot across space causing it to rip and shred for several hundred thousand kilometers the energy seemed to have a strange effect on space as it caused it to rip and crack, this energy had even struck several asteroids that would disintegrate as if their particles were picked apart and turned into nothingness.
Avrin's lips trembled as he looked at this scene from a distance. “What a frightening power...that thing is more dangerous than Orphelium was when I fought him...if I got hit by that I would have been done for...”
Avrin didn't plan to stay a moment longer as he retreated back to Seleria, his face was pale and beads of sweat were running down it, he had just realized how insignificant he truly was compared to many beings out there, he had no idea what those wraith things were but it was a good thing he had gotten out of there, not only would that strange attack have ended him in one hit he had a very strange feeling that the creature was missing something as if it were injured greatly and not at full power.
This book's true home is on another platform. Check it out there for the real experience.
When he returned to Seleria he decided to meditate within the orbit of the planet away from everything, he had a flash of insight especially in regards to the creature’s pupil. “-the same shape as mine, very strange, this is the Spectral domain it's related to my race and only a handful outside of my race can access it, could it be related to someone on the outside or possibly even the Spectrals? That being said, if that thing can do that, then why can’t I! I’ll simply find a way to mimic it! Avrin was not simply just stunned and somewhat afraid but a little thankful, this was because he had learnt a possibly powerful attack from the creature, if something at the supreme deity level had an attack that could outmatch a primordial entity then if he learnt something like that it would benefit him as well against individuals a step above him.
Entering his inner workings whilst still grasping Limos he began to siphon the mana from it into his body, since Limos wasn't in a vortex like state it would be less dangerous for him to grasp it like this.
Back on the planet outside of the Spectral domain, Ilisia and Calomia were sitting within a room, this room was similar to a cell but was quite fancy for one, it showed that the deity who had captured them did not want to rough them up just in case there was a possibility that if they were hurt or injured things would go sour even though he was confident in threatening whoever it was that owned shaded moon.
Ilisia was frowning as she sat huddled up in a corner, ignoring the somewhat lavish seats and food on the table. “Grandma....Mr. Avrin gave us that thing....can't we just use it?...” Calomia was seated next to Ilisia with a book in her hand, she quietly responded. “We don't seem to be in any danger for now....besides it’s better like this...”
Ilisia pouted and raised her head, one could see the dried trails of tears on her face. “How is it better? Mr. Avrin is going to be very worried when we aren't there!” Ilisia felt it was a bad thing to remain here, of course, Calomia simply laughed. “Careless child, when he is worried he will come to look for us...and when he finds us he will definitely punish that man...”
Before Ilisia could respond a voice echoed throughout the room. “Punish me?...hahaha! I truly fail to understand how a mortal is going to fight a deity, do not think this is some fairy tale cooked up in a book for children I am a true mage deity....you should grovel before me and feel proud to be in my presence...even more so that I am being so hospitable to you both!”
The deity who had captured both Ilisia and Calomia was standing outside of the cell with his hands behind his back, it was impossible to see the expression on his face due to the faceplate he wore that resembled an open tome, of course, one could guess by his words that he was looking down on them.
Calomia glanced at him carefully before giving a quiet laugh. “-Artificer consortium...you made a big mistake kidnapping us...-” Calomia was no fool she understood Avrin was not normal and had always been hiding his strength, she herself had a strange background and understood Avrin was hiding a lot more than it seemed. The deity no longer wasted his time and soon left. When he stepped outside of the prison area he trembled slightly and quickly glanced to the side to see another figure, this female figure was dressed in gold and white attire that fitted well to her body, she retained the look of a mage by the robe like attire that also seemed for agile movement, but still kept a feminine charm by revealing a bit of her thighs as well as her fairly well endowed bust to a degree, she also wore a faceplate but this faceplate was not a simple open tome, this tome seemed as if it were alive with strange golden bronze like roses growing out of it emitting a strange light. She took a step forward causing her shoulder length blonde hair to sway slightly as she took a step forward.
The deity with the normal tome took a step back away from here before calling out. “W...what are you doing here Blood Rose!!...” when the spoke out that title the female stopped for a moment before she trembled a little. “You know....I hate that name...” an aura began to slowly seep out of her yet this was not a normal aura, this aura was truly fitting of the 5th universe and was an aura of runes, “Velethia!..” suddenly a voice called out, from the end of the hall the sound of footsteps began to echo, with each footstep taken the mana lights hanging from the walls would dim and then flair up, a male figure began to make his way forward with his arms at his side, he also wore an agile mage like robe but this one was emitting a strange runic light despite also being gold and white.
His tome like face plate was strange as if it were alive, it would show the images of strange runic incantations and often reveal strange images, yet in his presence and to his words Velethia the female, as well as the grand forerunner, didn't dare show disrespect, the grand forerunner, of course, knelt down in respect. “This one greets Vice Magister Elorin...” he quickly showed his greeting, of course, Velethia simply folded her arms while glancing in disgust towards the grand forerunner.
“Tyron it was reported that you captured two individuals yesterday and didn't report it.” the man named Elorin spoke while glancing down at Tyron who was the grand forerunner.
“Indeed...may I ask if something is wrong?...” Tyron spoke carefully and did his best to show no disrespect. Elorin thought for a moment before speaking. “No...nothing wrong...it's just a bit strange that a deity of our great artificer consortium would capture an old lady and a young girl...”
Velethia scoffed for a moment and chuckled before speaking. “Strange?...I’d say it was more towards weird and disgusting...” when her words sounded out Tyron’s face under his faceplate trembled and paled with anger yet he didn't dare say anything, Velethia was a rank above him and Elorin was two ranks about him. “It doesn't matter what his purpose for capturing them are....but do not try to bite off more than you can chew. Tyron your fellow deities aren't stupid, if you have found something valuable to the consortium, then don't you dare use it to gain prestige...you may obtain a bit of title....but the greedy will not be let off easy, in the end you're simply a new deity...speaking to those mortals....to me you're not different than a bug..” Elorin spoke with a casual matter. “Velethia we are leaving, my words have gotten across..” this was because Elorin could tell Tyron was trembling slightly, Velethia glanced down at him before grunting and walking away with Elorin.
Of course, Tyron was clenching his teeth, he was indeed afraid but also angry. “-you fucking bastard....you and this consortium....once I obtain that technique who gives a shit about any of you....I’ll go find a major power and trade it for resources and safety....then we will see if you short sighted mules will dare to harm me!...-”
When Avrin had finished stabilizing his body he returned to the Spectral city and searched around using his divine sense. The dragons within the southern continents sylph forest were chased off because he didn't feel the need to convert them since he felt that there would likely be stronger creatures out there that would make better Spectrals, the dragons of Seleria were too arrogant and haughty, he didn't want any of that as a Spectral.
He also saw that Ailirion was leading a large group of Spectrals to properly make a way down to the dark matter crystal vault area where they could construct a proper structure around it, since Ailirion had been handling this matter Avrin tasked Erebus with bringing together a few Spectrals to prepare more resources that would be taken and prepared for Myra to help the move to the sylph forest,
Kael was handling the situation with organizing the tournament with other Spectrals, the event had caused a great stir as well as increase in Spectrals who wanted to train, this had an effect on Asura who was now very busy with teaching a lot more, this also meant that the more Spectrals who were learning how to fight needed more proper weapons, Eitri who had prepared his things had a bit more time before he and Asura would leave with Avrin, he was helping Tardiff with sigil weapons as well as crafting weaponry for those Spectrals.
As Avrin glanced around the streets lining around the city, he noticed something strange. The only places that seemed like shops were those places that handed out equipment that was forged, apparently Spectrals would place their orders and would then return with a receipt like ticket and pick up their order and leave, there was no currency at all everything was done to help each other out, Avrin liked this method a lot.
It was Spectrals helping Spectrals, but he also worried as to how far this method could go, he pondered that when his race has many millions and even billions of individuals in the future if they reach the first universe how would supply keep up with demand, at the same time he was also a bit cautious about using currency because he understood that although money was good at keeping balance it also bred greed and evil for many individuals, he didn't feel rushed for a solution right now, after all, he understood everything now was temporary even their stay on Seleria.
“--Myra...--” Avrin in the past had been able to use his divine sense to communicate to non spectrals, thanks to his current state the range and clarity was much more powerful. His c.particles were now 95% complete while his normal particles were 45% complete, thinking about the situation still made him bitter. “--Avrin?...where are you?--” Myra was confused as she glanced around but couldn't find him. “--I’m speaking to you using...well let’s just call it divine link for now, I wanted to ask you how you are faring with preparations to move?--”
Myra was silent for a few moments before she replied. “--Syrana is quite mad and a few support her anger but my people, as well as many humans and beastkin, want to move to somewhere with a healthier atmosphere and look so they are greatly in support of it. You know Avrin because of you, Syrana hasn't talked to me after we argued!--”
Avrin frowned a little to himself “--that can't be helped, she is a bit stubborn but I’m sure over time she will forgive and forget, once things are handled Seleria will be restored and there won't be a Spectral left on this planet to worry about, you will all have your home back and without worrying about gods--”
Myra was quite curious in regards to Avrin's words, she pondered for a few moments before speaking. “--tomorrow we will begin sending several groups over to start taking materials over, will your people be helping?--”
“--when you all reach there, you will find many crates filled with what you need, so don't feel the need to overburden yourselves, it would be better to simply take more people and food to eat along the way--” Avrin responded.
Myra soon replied. “--good, that will save a lot of effort. Avrin there is something I've been meaning to ask you.--”  Avrin was a little surprised, Myra wasn't ever the type to ask him something out of curiosity without worrying about him bringing destruction. “--what is it?--” he himself was quite curious.
“--what’s...it like out there?...--” Myra’s words held no real reference but Avrin knew what she was talking about “--its...well....it doesn't let your imaginations down, there is a lot to see and experience but there is also a lot of danger.--”
Myra didn't respond but because Avrin's divine sense encompassed the entire planet he could see she was sitting quietly as if she were thinking, after a few moments Avrin retracted his divine sense until it covered just his city.
He was eager to see how his people would expand out in the future but he also pondered about a few things, he understood that the past two inheritors of the dark matter heart were much more powerful than him, he wondered about the meaning of his people, how they were simply to feed him, “-did they ever devour them?...they must have been quite evil-” Avrin wasn't sure what else to think, to devour a race you created would be like devouring your own children which was clearly a case of one being evil.
After pushing the thought aside he divine linked with Eitri and Asura. “The two of you, come to me and bring your things, it’s time to leave, Eitri, I understand you will be quite busy at Shaded Moon, I want you to bring an assistant with you, I apologize for the short notice.”
Avrin was quite pleased with himself, he couldn't wait to return to The Shaded Moon to begin the next phase in his plans, and of course he had no idea that when he returned it would be a situation that would keep him on edge.

chapters.title: V6: Chapter 172 Returning To Tya’shara.
chapters.content:
On the outskirts of the aura barrier that concealed and protected Seleria from the outside three figures suddenly appeared out of thin air as it seemed to the naked eye. “Whoa! I can’t believe this, we are actually in space?” this voice belonged to Eitri, who struggled to gain footing as he floated, unable to gain balance. Of course, being a Spectral, his body was quite durable and didn’t need oxygen so being in space was fine. Asura, who was flailing around, finally managed to stand straight before glancing over at Seleria.
“Ooo....”
he let out a strange sound while looking over at it with fascination. Avrin, of course, had a slightly nervous look that he concealed quickly. He spoke to the two. “Both of you don’t move from here.” Avrin didn’t wait any longer as he moved slowly and carefully out of the aura boundary, entering the Spectral domain. He cautiously glanced around, his Divine Sense having extended to its full extent.
He couldn’t feel anything living or moving, not a sign of that strange entity or any wraiths. “-It doesn’t seem to be patient...good...-”Moving back in, Avrin reached over and grabbed both Eitri and Asura by the shoulders before exiting the boundary, “Hey, why do you look troubled?” Eitri noticed Avrin acting a little strange and decided to ask.
“It’s nothing, let me focus for a second.” shutting his eyes, Avrin engulfed them in his Divine Sense before Divine Stepping with them both. Of course, because he wasn’t used to the Spectral domain yet and was taking two Spectrals with him the maximum distance he could reach was several thousand kilometers but it was enough to reach the surface of the planet.
Asura and Eitri trembled, feeling their bodies quiver. Of course, Divine Stepping would be different in the Spectral domain. However, it was more the shock that came from arriving at a strange twisted looking planet.
“Huh? Master, this place...” Asura frowned a little as he looked around, seemingly not impressed. Eitri too didn’t seem happy. “Well, that kills the excitement! Avrin, boy, did you trick us? Damn, I should have stayed behind.” giving a sigh Eitri frowned.
Avrin gave a sigh of relief that he had managed to reach the planet safely. He wouldn’t want to encounter that creature again with his current strength. That being said, he turned to glance at the two. “Heh, pay attention and watch.” with that said an aura of dark matter pulsed and engulfed him and the other two.
Out of the Spectral domain, within the same location of the planet, space began to twist as static began to gather and slight rips in space formed with a strange energy seeping through and reforming into the three of figures.
“Gwuah...” Asura quickly dropped to his knees and held his stomach and mouth as he wanted to vomit. Eitri was no better as he fell on his butt holding both sides of his head with his hands as he had a splitting headache.
“It’s an aftereffect, it won’t happen again. That being said, welcome to our second temporary home.” Avrin casually glanced around, his Divine Sense extending a bit to see if anyone was within the vicinity. “Good, it doesn’t seem like anyone is close. Eitri.”
Eitri, hearing his name, grumbled before managing to slowly stand up, but not before giving a glare at Avrin. “Shit...you could have warned me beforehand. My head...hurts damn it...” the dwarven Spectral took several deep breaths by habit, hoping it would help.
Asura was willing dark matter within his stomach to help ease it. “Master...please let me go back...I don’t like this place.” Asura was simply a halfwit in Avrin’s eyes. He didn’t like to be around Avrin, but Avrin didn’t really care. He had some use for him and he wouldn’t leave him to his own machinations just yet.
“Asura, you can pick one of two tasks. One is to assist Shaded Moon and guard over the store, the second, you can go train the Spectral ants on this planet. Eitri, your task isn’t hard either, just like I said back on Seleria. I trust that you will improve upon Sigil crafting as well as forging somehow, and the best place right now to do it is on this planet with a richer variety of resources.”
“Ah good! I’ve been meaning to examine things a bit more carefully, I believe I can find a medium between both forging and Sigil crafting, but I just lacked quality material that could last. Just send me where I need to go and I’ll get started.”
Avrin glanced curiously at him. “Are you sure it was wise for you to not choose an assistant? You may need the help.” Eitri responded. “None of them were proficient enough in Sigil crafting and all of them would just get in my way. I also need them to make sure supply of equipment is kept in line. There are many of us and me leaving is already a hit on it. Right now I need to focus my efforts on not only training these new Spectrals but also improving my skills.”
“Good! “ Avrin’s Divine Sense extended out and engulfed the entire underground Spectral colony, his voice transmitting to all the high ranking Spectral ants. “--Listen carefully all of you. I’m sending a pure blood to help teach you another method of creating equipment.
His orders are no less than Ailirion’s, so do well to learn as much as you can--” Avrin didn’t seem to look around much, the underground colony had been improved to a decent degree. Many of them had begun to reform their homes so that they were less dirt shacks and more proper, using the home Avrin created as a source of inspiration.
The architecture, though, was a bit strange, but amazing in its own right. It resembled a mix of layered bricking and columns with layered roofing along with carvings. Each home had different carvings, as if it were a sign of who lived within.
The Spectrals that had received the divine link had all responded in greeting and acceptance as they all knew Avrin’s voice. After giving them a location, Avrin glanced at Eitri and nodded. Eitri prepared himself before he was Divine Stepped many kilometers away to the second Spectral city.
“Asura, have you made a decision?” Avrin understood time right now was quite valuable, but he wanted to be somewhat fair and gave Asura some time. “Hmnn...” Asura pictured Ailirion and cringed slightly as he imagined a whole colony of Spectrals that appeared as mysterious as him.
“-Ahh, damn it, why couldn’t I stay on Seleria. At least then I could have befriended Izanami! -” he gave a pitiful yet conflicted look before sighing and speaking. “I...I’ll help guard the store, Master...” Avrin nodded and glanced at him for a moment.
“Asura, you need to understand that it does not matter to me whether you hate me or not, what I am doing right now is for the benefit of our race. It wouldn’t be hard for me to simply leave you all to your own lives, but right now none of you are powerful enough to protect each other. When that day comes then what you all do is not my problem, I am simply helping the process along.”
Of course, Avrin wanted to give Asura the notion that once things are settled he will be done and go, but deep inside Avrin had a strange soft spot for his race. It irritated him a little but also made him happy, as it was a sign that he still had some humanity left.
“Mnm...” Asura grumbled in a conflicted manner before nodding. He would treat it as him and Avrin traveling again. He had gotten used to being the boss, but now he was simply a minion so to speak.
Avrin gave a soft smile before nodding. Without another thought, he Divine Stepped Asura and himself away before reappearing within the Shaded Moon interior. Avrin’s attention was diverted to the Spectral colony beneath the ground, looking carefully to notice Eitri was already ordering around the Spectrals as if he knew what to do.
“-It seems he wants them to show him what ores they have. It’s a good thing those were stockpiled. If I left Tardiff here they would probably all be devoured. Why do I get the ones that eat too much-” Avrin frowned a little.
Asura curiously glanced around with awe at the interior of the store. “Incredible...” his jaw dropped somewhat, revealing his sharpened teeth. “Master, is this really the store? It looks so strange...is this how buildings on this planet look? The surroundings looked like Seleria a little bit and I paid no attention...damn I was wrong...”
Asura had gotten over his small fit quite quickly as his mood was easily affected, though his attention was fixed on the architecture of the building with fascination.
“If you want to stand out and grab attention from potential buyers you need to take advantage of everything that can change it. When we get more popularity I have more plans, but yes this is Shaded Moon and where you will be making sure no troublemakers cause issues when I need to handle other matters. Of course, you also need to...huh?”
While Avrin was talking he searched Shaded Moon with his Divine Sense. He couldn’t find Calomia or Ilisia and thought they were outside gathering or doing something and he kept expanding it. After expanding it for forty-thousand kilometers he still couldn't find them, a monstrous forty-thousand.
Ensure your favorite authors get the support they deserve. Read this novel on .
He quickly became quiet and expanded it to the maximum range of eighty-thousand kilometers, but still couldn’t find them. He gave a solemn expression. What he did notice though were the mercenaries who were supposed to be keeping an eye on Shaded Moon looking around the forest area as if they were searching for something. They all seemed haggard and tired.
Avrin’s face twisted a little before he spoke. “Wait here till I get back.” with that said he vanished. A fair distance away from Shaded Moon, Urkan was within the Anzazia mercenary home base. He was holding one hand against his head while glancing over a map with circles.
He looked tired and nervous. Right now several people were around him. “This is ridiculous!!! How can you not find any traces of them....just who is it that attacked!!...Shit!!” Urkan gripped the ink pen tightly, snapping it and throwing it against the floor before standing up.
“C-Commander, we have already spent quite a few resources and used all our connections, but not a word. All that we know is the same time they disappeared several of our men on usual patrol around Shaded Moon were knocked unconscious, and when they woke up they found that other creatures were also in the same state. Whoever it is that is responsible most likely is powerful and has some conflict with Shaded Moon. I suggest we keep out of this.” this was one of the other lower leaders of Anzazia who was sweating bullets while speaking. Urkan clenched his teeth.
“You damned...” Urkan stopped as he glanced over at his underlings seeing pale looks of fear as they trembled. He raised his brow before one of them slowly pointed behind Urkan.
Urkan’s eyes widened before turning around to look behind him. He spotted Avrin with the hood over his head, and his face changed.
“I see...so that’s what’s going on huh...” Urkan froze as if he were a statue. He wasn’t sure what to say to Avrin. His heart was feeling an intense fright, he had gotten used to Avrin’s mysterious aura-less presence but for some odd reason, he sensed a deep danger.
“Mister...Mister Avrin, welcome back...but...since you have heard everything it seems....the only culprits we can think of is the Artificer Consortium. They took a hit not too long ago but quickly recovered soon after and are doing even better than before.”
Avrin tilted his head and gave a thoughtful look. He didn’t want to jump to conclusions and lose his patience. Whoever was the culprit most likely took Calomia and Ilisia with them to use as some sort of leverage to scare Avrin. If they wanted something from Avrin then they wouldn’t harm them, though that was just his belief.
“Stop your search, it’s pointless. I’ll handle the issue. I’ll contact you when I’m done, thank you for the assistance.” Avrin then vanished in a haze of ash right in front of their eyes.
Urkan dropped back into his seat as he gave a heavy sigh. “What a dangerous individual...heh...the Artificer Consortium branch really messed up if they were behind it all.”
Within the village of Roth, trade was booming as shops and stalls were open with vendors selling their wares to adventurers who were eager to upgrade. Of course, right now there was one place that was busier than the rest, this was the Artificer Consortium branch that had somehow shot up with the items they were creating in a single day.
The Highland Syndicate store was only half as busy, showing just how much the difference was.Within the branch of the consortium, Meutin was sitting in his office with a wide grin on his face as he was reading profit reports. Beside him was a female assistant who was holding documents and would every now and then take the one Meutin was reading after he used an ink stamp on the piece of paper.
“-Good. If we can keep up this pace we can restore all connections that those bastards at Shaded Moon destroyed and profit even more. Eventually we can even run those Highland Syndicate fools out of here. Hehe, the Four Heavens must love me if fate has sent a Grand Forerunner to handle the pests-”
Of course, Meutin should have known that fate was not one to choose sides. His words spoken to himself were truly wrong. The entire room trembled for a moment, Meutin quickly looked up feeling something was wrong. He was just about to stand up but felt a heavy pressure on him. A surge of Nebula Mist engulfed him and the assistant before a Phantom Pulse pressed over the Nebula Mist, locking them in place.
Forming from dark matter, Avrin’s figure was revealed. He glanced at Meutin and spoke. “Ten seconds. Tell me who is responsible for attacking Shaded Moon. Otherwise, the moments after these ten seconds will be excruciatingly painful for everyone within this building. Man or woman, it makes no difference to me.”
Meutin glanced at Avrin with a trace of shock as he struggled with fear. He looked from the corner of his eyes to see his assistant doing the same thing. She was just about to scream but Avrin’s Phantom Pulse extended over to her lips, causing them to shut. She began to mumble and squirm.
“Ten...nine...eight...seven...six...” Avrin began a countdown. Meutin simply laughed as he spoke with pride and caution. “It makes no difference!! You shouldn’t have made an enemy of the Artificer Consortium. You attracted the attention and anger of a Grand Forerunner! Hahaha, if I were you I would pack up and leave....in fact, never return!!”
Avrin thought for a moment before speaking. “Where does this Grand Forerunner live?” Meutin blinked with surprise before bursting out in laughter. “HAHAHA! Y...you actually think it makes a difference!! The only reason I’m telling you is because it doesn’t matter who you are.
You can’t hurt a being that is a God!! But I’ll humor you. Not too far from the province of Lav’Faliva is where the Artificer Consortium’s headquarters is located, a place of unimaginable magnificence and prosperity, ruled by gods and children smiled upon by the Four Heavens. Do you think a little worm like y-?”
Avrin gave an expressionless look before he willed the Nebula Mist into action. Almost in a near instant, Meutin was disintegrated. Avrin would not bother converting such trash into a Dark Core, it would leave a bad taste in his mouth as if he were absorbing some of his stupidity. Avrin was quite irritated with this branch of the Artificer Consortium, for now, he would leave it and handle the main issue at hand.
He still had time to tie loose ends.
Avrin had read about the province of Lav’Faliva in a book he purchased in Roth and understood its size which exceeded the scope of his Divine Sense for now. It took a single Divine Step before appearing in the grassy mountainous plains that were also being used to herd a special kind of animal. Ignoring the inhabitants, Avrin focused his Divine Sense again.
This time he got results. Though he was a bit at a loss what to think. He wondered why Calomia hadn’t used the object he gave her but also felt it was a good decision. If she used it she would most likely have been found. Avrin could sense the massive castle that was the headquarters of the Artificer Consortium.
Within it were thousands of individuals of varying strength, including six new Deities, three high Deities, and one Elder Deity. None of which had noticed Avrin’s Divine Sense. Avrin felt the small device Calomia kept on her which was dark matter allowing him to pinpoint them in an instant. He found them behind bars in a cell, which made him frown.
Avrin waved his hand as if to try and Divine Step them out, but the moment dark matter began to form around them the cell emitted a rune that sent out a pulse that dispersed the dark matter.
Calomia and Ilisia, who were inside the cell, were frightened by what was going on but looked around with curiosity. “Grandma?” Ilisia spoke with uncertainty. Calomia nodded. “He’s here.”
The moment the cell emitted that rune, Tyron was instantly alerted. He snickered before he used his finger to form an aqua colored rune. The moment the rune was formed it expanded and engulfed Tyron.
Within the prison, in the corner of Calomia and Ilisia’s cell, the ground lit up with that same rune and expanded upward to show Tyron had teleported there. He didn’t waste time before rushing over and snickering. He reached up and grabbed Ilisia by her hair and raised her up.
“AHH!..” Ilisia let out a scream “STOP!” Calomia shouted out and rushed over to try and rescue Ilisia, but was kicked to the side by Tyron. Of course, he controlled his strength. “Scram, withered husk.” he cursed at her somewhat before speaking up in laughter. “Hahaha...don’t try and trick me. Owner of Shaded Moon, was it? I know you’re he-”
Tyron felt his mind twist and tremble as his vision faded into darkness. The moment this happened the entire castle shook, causing some of the towers to crack and even fall apart. This alerted the other Deities in the Artificer Consortium.
“What was that? It came from the dungeon.” a Deity with a black fitted leather robes with chain straps spoke. The tome on his face reflected two moons that emitted a faint glow. This was one of the high Deities that were within a large chamber. Beside him was Vice Magister Elorin, who had a bitter look. “That’s the dungeon Tyron is presiding over. That fool is up to no good. Arch Thero’lizer, I will handle this issue.”
Seated on a small flat stool was an individual wearing a deep azure robe that covered their entire figure. Not moving an inch, they gave no response. Their right hand was waved up to the right as if giving acceptance to Elorin’s words. Elorin nodded with a snicker under his tome mask.
Within the dungeon chamber, a crack in the ground was formed as a figure was lying motionlessly. Avrin was knelt over with his right hand grasping the head of Tyron who he had smashed into the ground and defeated with one anger filled move. Avrin’s right hand was missing the leather covering, showing that the force he put into that hit was more than his clothes could handle.
Avrin’s face was darkened, he knew things would get dangerous and immediately Divine Stepped Calomia and Ilisia away. With this point blank distance it was not interrupted at all.
Avrin then casually raised Tyron up by his head. Tyron’s face was bloodied and his body trembling. His tome mask was cracked and shattered to reveal his bloodied face. Despite that, Avrin glanced to see that a metallic like aura reflecting runes was emitting around Tyron’s skin.
“Hmm...So this is the strength of a High Magus.” Avrin spoke with a casual expression. Tyron was badly bruised, despite having a fortified layer of magical protection it was nearly completely shattered. Under Avrin’s strength, Tyron’s entire mana pool within his mana core was depleted. Another attack from Avrin would surely end him.
Avrin gave a crude grin, revealing his pearl white set of teeth. He glanced at Tyron not as if he were a living being but as if he were a resource. “You’re going to make a fine Dark Core. “
Avrin raised his left hand with Nebula Mist gathering, preparing to engulf Tyron. But at that moment his eyes turned to the right as he felt a hand on his shoulder. Elorin was behind Avrin with a cautious stance. “Friend, to have defeated Grand forerunner Tyron you must be quite strong, but you have made a very very big mistake attacking our Artificer Consortium. Do you have any idea who we are? No Deity on Tya’shara is clueless about the Second Heaven alliance. Who the hell do you think you are?!!”
Elorin was a high Deity with a sense of superiority even among Deities. He saw new Deities as weak. Of course, he couldn’t feel Avrin’s strength, but it was nothing new for a mage to hide one’s power. Elorin looked at Avrin carefully, ready to attack if he made a move on Tyron. Of course, what he saw was Avrin turn his hood covered head to face him.
Elorin felt a dangerous sense of urgency as he spotted a malicious grin on Avrin’s face.
Elorin raised his left hand on instinct and spoke out. “Epitaph of Protection.” a flood of runes surged out from Elorin’s hand, converging in front of him. But at that moment, Avrin unleashed a powerful Phantom Pulse that smashed right against the shield.
The force of the attack caused a sonic boom as Elorin was blown away like a ragdoll. Whenever he bounced on the ground, a flash of greyish light would form right under the part of his body that would be hit, protecting him from the damage.
After being knocked away several dozens of meters, Elorin began to get up on his knees with a sense of surprise. Around him, the ceiling of the dungeon was crumbling from the sonic boom and force formed from Avrin’s Phantom Pulse hitting his shield.
Elorin was stunned. From the side of his lips, blood was leaking out. He could feel his organs were shaken and injured somewhat. He clenched his teeth and spat out a small mouthful of blood.
He raised his right hand and a four meter long staff that was half a foot thick except for the part it was held was revealed. The shaft of the staff was a strange brown wood that emitted a living sort of reflection, almost like a dirty mirror. At the tip of the staff was a round black orb with an orange aura around it. It gave off a chilling mana, one could tell this weapon was not normal.
“H...how dare you!!” Avrin ignored Elorin and focused on Tyron again. He was just about to start again, but Elorin acted before him. “Shadow Epitaph: Chaos Entangle!” as Elorin spoke he drew runes with his left hand which moved at a quick speed. The runes drawn emitted a dark mana aura.
The moment he finished the runes clumped up together and began to form a sphere of darkness. Elorin raised the enormous staff in his hand and tapped the end onto the ground, sending a heavy pulse. The orb on the staff tip emitted a dark light that affected Elorin’s spell.
The strange spell began to twist and form before static formed around it. A beam of dark light shot into the sky and almost immediately clouds began to gather around it almost like a vortex. The center of this vortex was an ominous black.

chapters.title: V6: Chapter 173 A sudden Agreement?
chapters.content:
Avrin calmed himself down. He had never battled with a mage of the Fifth universe on the Deity level and couldn’t be careless. It was also a learning experience. “The vortex’s center suddenly shot a ray of dark light that engulfed Avrin who threw Tyron to the side. Avrin quickly dashed to the side and just as the ray of light was about to hit where he was it changed direction and followed him.
“Oh?” Avrin was a little impressed. He opened his palm and shot a Void Sphere towards the ray. The ray was slowed for a moment before the Void Sphere was turned into nothingness.
“Don’t bother trying to escape, we mages may not excel at physical strength but our magical abilities make up for it!” Elorin spoke with pride. From what he’d seen, Avrin wasn’t a Deity who used magic.
Avrin listened for a moment, but as he glanced at Elorin he noticed the orb on his staff was emitting a strange pulse. It reflected the image of the ray of light and Avrin. Avrin then glanced at Elorin and noticed that his eyes were also emitting the same strange sort of mana trace.
“You shouldn’t hold back.” Avrin understood that Elorin was holding his strength back mainly because they were on his home ground, but in the end, they had aggravated Avrin and he didn’t really care. He needed to deal with the consortium and had tried to do so in a discreet, fair manner, but they provoked him at every turn and resulted in violence and even went as far as to capture those he cared about.
Avrin wasn’t willing to wait until help arrived for Elorin. He casually Divine Stepped and appeared in front of him. Elorin was stunned with fright. Teleportation magic that didn’t require a conduit or an action was something incredibly rare only those at the top of the food chain of existence knew, but for Avrin to use an ability similar or even identical was out of his expectation. All he could do was prepare himself.
“Epitaph Ward of-” Avrin’s right hand flashed like a bolt of lightning before Elorin could finish his incantation. Avrin grabbed his staff and kicked towards Elorin’s stomach with heavy force.
The smash pummeled into Elorin’s stomach and the shock of the attack caused an aftershock of energy to smash against the walls of the dungeon and beyond and cause them to blow apart. There were people already scrambling for safety. No one in the Artificer Consortium headquarters was overly weak, but the debris formed from the aftershock was enough to cause large chunks of rubble to injure and even kill a few unlucky individuals.
Avrin’s eyebrows narrowed as he noticed Elorin hadn’t loosened his grip on his staff. The force had caused him to skid several meters back and Avrin had been pulled along. Elorin began to spit out more blood as he raised his head to reveal that his skin was engulfed in the same runic barrier as Tyron. Elorin, of course, looked extremely mad.
“You...dare try to take MY STAFF!” he gave a maddened look as mana began to surge around him, causing the air to grow thicker and heavier. “-No kidding. Good thing I have some information from God. You mages may not excel at physical abilities but this mana barrier is a form of protection-”
Avrin thought to himself. Elorin’s left hand flashed like a knife through the air forming a line of runic engravings, “Epitaph Chaos Wave!” the runes crumbled together and were absorbed into Elorin. His body began to radiate a dark mana before a pulse of dark energy surged out. Avrin quickly let go of the staff but was caught up in the energy as he was knocked back several dozen meters. The attack was quite powerful and stunned Avrin.
The crazy thing was that another wave was sent outwards in all directions causing everything it touched to be pushed back. Every second, a wave of energy was being sent out, but while this occurred, Elorin raised his staff again and tapped the end onto the ground
The Dark mana of Elorin’s chaos wave suddenly strengthened. It emitted a heavy droning sound as it also grew faster. Avrin was fascinated by magic and was a little conflicted. This was because of several things. He wanted to get revenge on Tyron, he wanted to see more of Elorin’s magic, but he also wanted to end this battle and get his point across.
“-That Elder Deity is surely watching, I’ve no choice but to handle this quickly-” Avrin raised his right hand and began forming a very thick mass of dark matter that caused space to twist a little. Of course, Elorin wasn’t idle. The chaos wave was meant to keep distance between him and an enemy with physical prowess. Meanwhile, he finished another set of runic engravings in the air and roared out. “Epitaph Doom Light!!”
A mass of black energy surged around from the engravings. Again he tapped the end of the staff, empowering his spell. It was almost as if it were living black lightning that formed into a sphere of energy that radiated a chilling aura.
Elorin was infuriated and filled with anger. “DIE!!!” the thought of someone touching his staff maddened him. Right now, he showed no more care for holding back. The sphere of energy suddenly caused the ground to tremble before a massive beam of light shot towards Avrin.
Avrin snickered. He couldn’t Divine Step carelessly near Elorin as he would get caught up in that wave of energy, but it didn’t matter. This was still an easy fight in his opinion. “Good!! “ Avrin spoke out. The moment the ray of dark light neared Avrin he raised the mass of dark matter in his hand. “Stygian Bacillus.”
The mass of dark matter, as if it were alive, began to surge and expanded out several hundred meters wide and caught the entirety of the ray of dark light almost like a net. It began to fill up the dark matter. This lasted for several moments to Elorin’s horror and amazement. Once his attack concluded, in front of him was a large mass of dark matter that was somewhat transparent.
It emitted a static dark light, yet inside was Elorin’s attack. “You...what foul abilities you use!! Which alliance are you from!!” Elorin roared out. “Alliance? Remember the name Shaded Moon...and also remember never to provoke it again!!”
The large bubble-like net of dark matter containing Elorin’s attack twisted and turned before it opened up, facing toward Elorin. The moment it did, the ray of light that was contained shot outward, this time not towards Avrin but towards Elorin.
Elorin gave a frustrated look and raised his hand to for incantation, but Avrin was done playing with him. He emitted a Phantom Pulse and increased the weight of his left hand, disabling him. To Elorin’s horror, the ray of light smashed against him. Of course, the mana pool of a high Deity was nothing to scoff at, the attack was strong and knocked Elorin away, and dispersed the chaos wave he had in place but not before a last wave smashed against the ground.
